title: Bruce Arians says he wants to be a head coach in the NFL next season
summary: Bruce Arians is thinking about coming out of retirement.
full_text: Bruce Arians is thinking about coming out of retirement. Again. Arians told Jordan Schultz that when he announced his retirement from the Buccaneers in March of 2022, it was because of health problems that have since been resolved, and he now wants to coach again. "I had torn my Achilles early in that season, and I was wearing these prosthetic high heels, and it threw my back out, and I couldn't stand on the sideline for four hours anymore without a lot of pain," Arians said. "I was also monitoring an aneurysm on my heart, so I had some health issues. We did everything we thought we could do in Tampa after winning the Super Bowl, trying to get two, and then it was time to give it to Todd [Bowles]. Now that I'm all healthy again, I got the itch again. So, we'll see." If Arians does come back next year, he'll be the oldest head coach in NFL history. That distinction currently belongs to Pete Carroll, who was 74 when he coached the Raiders last season. Arians will turn 75 next season. Arians' first retirement announcement came from the Steelers after they did not renew his contract as their offensive coordinator following the 2011 season, but Arians later said he was forced out and didn't want to retire. He then took a job as offensive coordinator of the Colts in 2012, and was their interim head coach for most of that season while Chuck Pagano battled leukemia. Arians coached so well that he was named the NFL's Coach of the Year. Once Pagano returned to the Colts, Arians became head coach of the Cardinals, and he won a second Coach of the Year award. He announced his retirement following the 2017 season, after five years as head coach of the Cardinals. But in 2019 he came out of retirement to become head coach of the Buccaneers. He won a Super Bowl in Tampa Bay, then retired after three seasons. Arians thought that was it, but he said that his son is now coaching high school football, and in talking to his son about the job he realized how much he misses it himself. "Another fire got lit," Arians said. "I had no desire to go back, and I was still fighting some health issues, but now after the open heart surgery I've got so much more energy, it's amazing." Arians may find, like Bill Belichick before him, that all the accomplishments in the world don't guarantee an NFL head-coaching job. Or perhaps he'll convince some owner to give the oldest coach ever a chance to do what he's done three times before, and turn a franchise around.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Luke McCaffrey knew the rules and made a heads-up play, causing a kickoff out of bounds
summary: Commanders kickoff returner Luke McCaffrey made the smartest play of the game by not returning a kick in Thursday night's win over the Giants.
full_text: Commanders kickoff returner Luke McCaffrey made the smartest play of the game by not returning a kick in Thursday night's win over the Giants. With McCaffrey back to field a Giants kickoff, the ball landed near the sideline at the 5-yard line. The kick stayed in bounds, and some returners would have grabbed the ball and started running. But McCaffrey let the ball bounce, then stepped out of bounds, and then grabbed the ball with his feet down on the sideline. By rule, the ball is out of bounds if it touches a player who is out of bounds, even if the ball actually stays in bounds. By touching the ball while his feet were out of bounds, McCaffrey forced a kickoff out of bounds penalty on the Giants, putting the ball on the 40-yard line for the Commanders. "I thought Luke McCaffrey made a really smart play that won't show up on the stat sheet," Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said. "That's a difficult play. Is it out of bounds? Is it not? I was nervous about it, that's one of the ones where you hold your breath." Every kickoff returner needs to know that rule, but knowing the rule is easier than having the quick-thinking ability to do what McCaffrey did, in the fourth quarter with the game on the line. It was among the smartest football plays you'll see.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Quinn: We needed that, we needed every bit of it
summary: After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants.
full_text: The Commanders headed into Thursday night's game against the Giants desperately needing to win, if they wanted to have any chance of competing in the NFC East. After their 24-21 win, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was a combination of exuberant and relieved. "We needed that. We needed every bit of it," Quinn said. "This is one we had to have, and our guys make sure we have it." After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants, and the Commanders now own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants. Quinn's team is still a long shot to win the NFC East, but given the state of that division, it's not unreasonable to think the Commanders can compete. And compete is what they did on Thursday night, in a game that went down to the final minute, just as Quinn said the Commanders expected. "Going into it, we thought this is going to be all four quarters," Quinn said. "It felt like the most adversity, but also the most belief. It was a balance of both, and we definitely needed that."
author: Michael David Smith

title: John Harbaugh expresses confidence in K Dominic Zvada
summary: Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games.
full_text: Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games. He missed another on Thursday night, a 33-yarder. While it happened in the first quarter and not on the final play, it stands out in a game that was decided by three points. After New York's 24-21 loss to the Commanders, Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked about his level of confidence in Zvada. " Yeah, we’re confident ," Harbaugh said. "You know, you can't — as soon as a guy doesn't make a play, I mean, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who's a rookie. So I'm confident that he's gonna become a good kicker. I mean, if at some point in time, it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. "But I'm not gonna panic, you know, halfway through the season when the guy who's made a bunch of kicks, if that's what you're inferring we should be doing. So, you know, I mean, we're just not gonna knee-jerk it like that. He's gonna make kicks. He's gonna make a lot of kicks, I believe in him. I think he's really good, really talented. And we're gonna give him an opportunity to do it. It's up to him to do it." That's a fair assessment of a player who's still new to the NFL. But a kicker has one job. If he can't do it (especially from distances that should be automatic), at some point tough questions need to be asked. Basically, how much time will Zvada get before Harbaugh decides it's not going to happen? That remains to be seen, if Zvada keeps missing kicks he should be making.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Stefon Diggs' late TD gives Commanders 24-21 win
summary: The wide receiver caught a 32-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 57 seconds left.
full_text: With 3:27 remaining in Thursday's game, the Giants lined up with Jameis Winston under center on fourth-and-1 from their own 11. The team's backup quarterback, who runs the team's quarterback sneaks, yelled, "Hut One. Hut Two. Hut Three. Who let the dogs out? Who, who, who, who?" The Giants took a delay of game and then punted. The Commanders got the last laugh, winning 24-21 on Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The Commanders are 3-5-1 and the Giants 5-3-1. In an entertaining second half, the teams traded the lead four times. The Giants took a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left on Isaiah Likely's 66-yard catch-and-run. The Giants then had back-to-back interceptions of Jayden Daniels. Safety Jevon Holland, who is having an All-Pro season, took the ball away from Chig Okonkwo at the 2-yard line with the Commanders on the Giants 24 with 5:27 left, and Ar'Darius Washington stepped in front of Okonkwo on fourth-and-2 at the Washington 45 with 2:15 left. The Giants, though, couldn't run out the clock, and the Commanders made the most of it. They needed only three plays to go 71 yards thanks to a questionable 33-yard pass interference penalty on Deonte Banks, who was covering Treylon Burks. Three plays later, Diggs scored. The Giants reached the Washington 48 on their final drive, but J.J. McCarthy's deep throw to Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas with 25 seconds left to end it. The Giants outgained the Commanders 399 to 340, but missed a field goal and had two turnovers. Daniels was 23-of-33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Rachaad White ran for 47 yards on 11 carries, and Diggs caught six passes for 83 yards. Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott each caught a touchdown pass. McCarthy was 23-of-36 for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Cam Skattebo had 18 carries for 78 yards and two touchdowns and caught three passes for 44 yards, and Likely had nine receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Aaron Donald on having no sacks: "They come in bunches"
summary: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has played seven games this season.
full_text: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has played seven games this season. He has no sacks. “Sacks come in bunches," Donald told reporters on Thursday. "It's going to come. Just keep playing ball and keep finding ways to win. That's the most important thing is winning. No pressure, I'm not worried about it. I've been playing football since I was five, six years old. They come in bunches. They'll come eventually so just keep doing what I need to do to help this team. When they present themselves, hopefully hold the ball and take advantage of it.” On Sunday, Donald finally played with Myles Garrett, the player whose arrival in June sparked Donald's decision to return after two years of retirement. Garrett, in his first game since Week 1, had 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble. Regardless, the Rams won, pushing themselves above .500 for the first time this year. On Sunday at Arizona, they have a chance to win their fourth in a row. And Donald has another chance to get his first sack since he returned from retirement.
author: Mike Florio

title: Isaiah Likely's 66-yard TD has Giants leading, puts him over 100 yards
summary: Isaiah Likely has a career high, with 127 yards on nine catches.
full_text: Isaiah Likely has a career high, with 127 yards on nine catches. McCarthy had Nick Cross in his face when he found Likely with a perfect throw. McCarthy is 22-of-32 for 272 yards and a touchdown.

title: Justin Jefferson: It's a joy to see Kirk Cousins take over as a leader
summary: Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and perhaps no one is more excited about that than Justin Jefferson.
full_text: Kirk Cousins is back in Minnesota, and perhaps no one is more excited about that than Justin Jefferson. The wide receiver had career highs in catches (128) and yards (1,809) and earned the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year award in Cousins' last full season with the Vikings in 2022. Jefferson, though, said he has "no expectations." "It's really just going out there and just executing our plays ," Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN. "It's not really getting too juiced up about him being here or anybody being back there. It's just all about understanding the plays that are being called, understanding the jobs that we have and executing our responsibilities. And just the plays that are there, and the plays that could be made, we just need to continue to just make those type of plays. And I'm pretty sure that the results would be a lot better. "He just understands the game. He's a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throw those type of plays, but he also doesn't force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me." Jefferson said it was "a joy to hear [Cousins] just take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field." "He's being vocal," Jefferson said. "Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he's talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he's just making sure that everybody's on the same page. So it's definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that's pretty normal from him. So it's definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking that control."
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Rex Ryan incident was captured on camera
summary: The recent news that Rex Ryan, of all people, allegedly ran over, of all the things, the feet of a pair of pedestrians in Nashville seems too crazy to be true, absent visual evidence.
full_text: The recent news that Rex Ryan, of all people, allegedly ran over, of all the things, the feet of a pair of pedestrians in Nashville seems too crazy to be true, absent visual evidence. Apparently, there is visual evidence. Via TMZ.com, the incident " was captured on camera ." The video has not yet surfaced, but it presumably will at some point. Ryan was arrested on six misdemeanor charges arising from the allegation that he ran over the feet of two people while driving a pickup truck on November 12. ESPN hasn't said much about the situation. From a one-line statement issued on Wednesday: “We are aware and are in touch with Rex." It's unclear whether he'll appear on Sunday morning's ESPN pregame show, or whether he'll make any appearances while the criminal case is pending. Ryan, who coached the Jets and the Bills before pivoting to TV, is scheduled to appear in court next month.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Commanders lead Giants 10-7 at halftime
summary: Ben Sinnott caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 5 seconds remaining in the first half.
full_text: The Giants and Commanders played a first half fitting the weather. On a cold, rainy night, the Commanders lead the Giants 10-7 at halftime. Ben Sinnott caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 5 seconds remaining in the first half. It completed a nine-play, 67-yard drive. Washington also had an 11-play, 49-yard drive that ended with Drew Stevens' 46-yard field goal. Daniels was 11-of-15 for 112 yards and a touchdown in the first half. Rachaad White had six carries for 20 yards, and Stefon Diggs caught two passes for 34 yards. The Giants outgained the Commanders 152 to 143 and had 12 first downs and a 17:18 to 12:42 advantage in time of possession. Cam Skattebo ran for a 1-yard touchdown with 2:35 remaining in the second quarter, giving New York its first lead at 7-3. It capped a 16-play, 72-yard drive. The Giants punted after reaching the Washington 37 on their first drive, and Dominic Zvada missed a 33-yard field goal after the Giants stalled at the Washington 15 on the second drive. Skattebo had 35 yards and a touchdown on eight carries and two catches for 37 yards. J.J. McCarthy went 12-of-19 for 92 yards and rushed for 30 yards on four carries. Isaiah Likely had five catches for 39 yards. Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo (back) is questionable to return.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams place WR Puka Nacua on IR
summary: Nacua injured the MCL and PCL in his knee and has turf toe.
full_text: A day after Sean McVay said the Rams wouldn’t place Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the wide receiver went on IR. McVay said “roster semantics” would keep Nacua on the 53-man roster, with every team getting only eight designated-to-return slots during the season. The Rams have used three of their designations and have Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson and now Nacua on IR with hopes of returning. But with Nacua set to miss "extended time," as McVay said Wednesday, with MCL and PCL sprains in his knee and turf toe, the Rams opted to move him to the IR list. Nacua will miss at least the next four games, with the Cowboys game on Dec. 20 the earliest he can return by rule. The Rams signed wide receiver Brennan Presley to take Nacua's roster spot and added wide receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: DeMarvion Overshown didn't know inactive players couldn't celebrate on the field
summary: The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts.
full_text: The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts. One of them was called unacceptable and undisciplined by Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive and dressed in street clothes, came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, "After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We have non-uniformed player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That's a 15-yard penalty." Overshown apologized to head coach Brian Schottenheimer and his teammates. “At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it," Overshown said Thursday, via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News . "I apologized about it. It was definitely in the moment, but earlier I had said that as a defense, we're going to start celebrating more, getting takeaways. And I was just caught in the moment. So you can laugh at it now, because we won the game, but in the moment, fourth quarter, tied ball game or close ball game, you don't want a 15-yard penalty from a guy, especially that's not even playing. So that's a lesson learned.” Overshown said he didn't know the rule until linebacker Dee Winters started yelling at him, which should prompt questions about why Overshown didn't know the rule. But he defended Schottenheimer and said he accepted his "butt chewing." “It’s not an indictment on Schotty. It’s on me as a player. I own it,” he said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Knoxville, Chattanooga Fox affiliates pass on Titans game, for now
summary: The Tennessee Titans apparently need an asterisk on their name.
full_text: The Tennessee Titans apparently need an asterisk on their name. At least two TV markets in the state for which the team is named have passed on televising their Week 10 game against the Jaguars. Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing explains that 506sports.com coverage map shows that the Knoxville and Chattanooga Fox affiliates will not televise the Jaguars-Titans game . Instead, Vikings-Packers will be shown in the 1:00 p.m. ET window. It's a preliminary map, as Lerner notes. The Fox affiliates in Knoxville and Chattanooga, the third- and fourth-largest cities in the league by way of population, could change their minds. Making the situation even more unusual is the fact that Fox won't get many Titans games, because they're usually on CBS. The obvious takeaway is that the Fox affiliates in Knoxville and Chattanooga believe that more people will watch Packers-Vikings than will watch Jaguars-Titans. It's not personal, it's business. And the affiliates think they're business interests are best served by showing Packers-Vikings not Jaguars-Titans.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jim Harbaugh: Broncos took advantage of a loophole the NFL should not allow
summary: The Chargers' head coach is not happy with the Broncos trying to renegotiate the trade for Daiyan Henley after the deadline, or with the NFL allowing it.
full_text: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is not happy with the way the Broncos backed out of a trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, or with the NFL rules that allowed them to do so. After agreeing to trade a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Henley, the Broncos told Chargers GM Joe Hortiz they couldn't go through with it because Henley's physical revealed concerns about his knee. The Broncos were still willing to trade for Henley, but wanted to give up less. Harbaugh believes physical exams should only be to determine whether or not the player is healthy, not to renegotiate trade terms. "What happened with the trade? Here's what I know, from talking to Joe: The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn't and we didn't," Harbaugh said. "In my opinion it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into, because it sets a bad precedent." Asked if it's permitted for teams to renegotiate trades after the trade deadline, Harbaugh answered, "It shouldn't be, but apparently it is. That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that." Harbaugh said the Broncos offered to say Henley passed his physical, but only if the Chargers would take something less than the fifth-round pick the Broncos had agreed to. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass-fail for a medical grade, and they told us they weren't going to pass him if it's a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon — they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a fill in the blank. I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is," Harbaugh said. Harbaugh is right that the NFL has set a bad precedent. By allowing teams to renegotiate trade terms after the deadline, the NFL is incentivizing teams to engage in chicanery on physical exams to squeeze their trade partners into taking less favorable deals. The Chargers refused to budge, but the NFL rules shouldn't have put the Chargers in a position where they had to make that decision.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Joey Porter Jr.: Injuries keeping me off field, not my contract situation
summary: Porter missed practice again on Thursday with an ankle injury.
full_text: Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. remained out of practice on Thursday and said that his ankle injury is the only reason he isn't on the field. Porter insisted that isn't the case. "I don't even know where that narrative come from," Porter said, via Todd Archer of ESPN.com. "I get it. It's the internet, but I really don't pay no attention to that or really care for that. My goal is to win games and play football, and that's what I want to do. So if there's any chance I could get on the field, I'm going to get on the field and do what I do best." Porter joined the Cowboys in a late September trade with the Steelers and has appeared in four games with the team. title: Patrick Mahomes on Josh Downs: You can tell the intellect, how he can pick things up
summary: The Chiefs brought in a receiver at the trading deadline, acquiring Josh Downs from the Colts.
full_text: The Chiefs brought in a receiver at the trading deadline, acquiring Josh Downs from the Colts. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that he's excited to get going with the wideout. “I think you can tell just the intellect and how he's able to pick stuff up and that he's a professional, that he knows what he's doing and he wants to come in and just compete and to have success, and he wants to win. And so, I'm excited for that,” Mahomes said, via transcript from the team. “And then you can just see him interacting with the other receivers in the room. You can tell that there’s going to be a great cohesion there, and that's the type of guys you want on the team, that want to compete and that want to win.” Mahomes noted he’s impressed with the way Downs can win his one-on-one matchups. “He runs routes really well,” Mahomes said. “He sets them up really well where he will run a route early in the game that he sets up for another one later in the game. And then he has really good feel, you can tell, obviously, playing in the system that he has, he has a lot of read-type routes, and you can tell he knows how to get himself open, settle in the right zones, and win versus man [coverage] when he can. “And so, I think it will be an easy transition for him to kind of do that stuff in our offense. Then, with how we do things, he can play a lot of different positions as we move receivers and tight ends around.” The quarterback also sees it as realistic for Downs to play and contribute early on in his tenure with Kansas City. While that begins with plenty of reps at practice, Mahomes and the rest of the offense can direct Downs to where he needs to be during games if necessary. “[W]e do a great job of kind of moving guys in and out of every single position, and so guys know the entire concepts of the plays,” Mahomes said. “We're very detailed with how we call the plays in the huddle, which will help him out a ton. “Then when he doesn't know, being able to talk to me in the huddle or talk to the guys as they're breaking the huddle, and that usually helps when the guys like each other. And so, it's good to have a guy that you can tell everybody's going to like, and that he has his head on the right way, and he's going to make sure that he's going to do whatever it takes to win.” In nine games with the Colts this year, Downs caught 33 passes for 354 yards with one touchdown.

title: Cardinals name Carson Beck starting QB: Rookie faces Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett in NFL debut
summary: Gardner Minshew's season-ending injury opens the door for Beck, whose first assignment comes against one of the NFL's most accomplished pass-rushing duos
full_text:
If the 2026 NFL season feels like an unprecedented year for unheralded rookie quarterbacks, that's because it is.
With the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) announcing Carson Beck as their starting quarterback for Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams (5-4), he will now be the third rookie quarterback drafted outside of the first two rounds to start a game this season. The other two were undrafted rookies -- Jalon Daniels of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Joe Fagnano of the Baltimore Ravens . That hasn't happened since 1987.
"You never really know until you get to the live bullets on Sunday, but just the way he goes about his business, whether it's been from OTAs through training camp before he got hurt, seeing him operate in that first half," coach Mike LaFleur said. "Plus, the one possession there in the second half, so obviously we'll know more come next Sunday, but we have all the confidence he's ready to roll."
Beck started the season low on the depth chart, and reflected on how it feels to move so far up in the same year.
"Obviously, having gone from the emergency quarterback at the beginning of the season to last week being the backup to now being the starter, it's been a crazy season," Beck said. "It's really been a welcome to the NFL season, just getting introduced to what the league is and what it can be, but I'm super excited for the opportunity and to have the chance to go play with these guys."
Jacoby Brissett started the year as the starter, was then benched, and was eventually traded to the Baltimore Ravens. Gardner Minshew took over as QB1 was Brissett was demoted and at that time, Beck was promoted from emergency third quarterback to backup. The Minshew injury now leaves Beck to take over after spending the first half of the season learning from his predecessors.
"I think the biggest thing is just watching those two and how they carry themselves and how they handle themselves not only in the meeting room around the coaches, but during the walkthrough, during practice, and during the game," Beck said. "I think that's the biggest thing that you can learn from those guys, of everybody's looking at you as a quarterback, and your attitude has to be right each and every day. The moxie going out there, having confidence, and making everyone around you better."
That "confidence" is not something Beck is worried about. He believes that "confidence is a choice" and having it makes everyone around you better as well.
"When you can choose that, again, you just have to go out there and execute," he said. "You have to go out there and do your thing and you have to go out there and be confident, have swag, and have moxie. Regardless of the circumstances, regardless of anything going on around you, regardless of maybe what happened the play before or maybe thinking about what's going to happen the next play. You have to be in the present moment and that's really all you can do and control."
To kick off the 2026 preseason, Beck completed 15 of his 19 throws for 188 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers . Beck will also become the fifth quarterback to make his first career start against a duo of pass rushers with 100-plus sacks each when he faces the Rams' duo of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett .
"Who do they got?" LaFleur said jokingly. "I got no expectations for him except to go out and play his game one play at a time. Go let it rip, go have some fun. Have some fun with your guys."
A depleted group represents Beck's supporting cast, with Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) out for the season and Marvin Harrison Jr . traded to the Houston Texans . Fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil , undrafted veteran Simi Fehoko and Pro Bowl return man Devin Duvernay are the projected starters.
Fortunately, Beck also has the 2025 first-team All-Pro tight end at his disposal in Trey McBride . McBride leads the NFL with 73 catches through Week 9, and he has 11 consecutive games with at least seven catches. Beck also knows a thing or two about feeding his superstar tight end after his years teaming with Brock Bowers at Georgia.

full_text:
In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning.
Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here.
Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down.
Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble.
The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run.
In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season.
Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside.
Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays.
The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games.
They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media.
But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media.
The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night.
When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields.
Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross .
The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays.
Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy.
I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night.
Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14

title: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh implores NFL to investigate 'loophole' that nixed Daiyan Henley trade
summary: The Broncos and Chargers called off their agreed-upon trade following Henley's physical
full_text:
The trade that was supposed to send Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos is off. When the Broncos announced that the deal would not be finalized , they did not disclose the reason why the agreement fell apart. But Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh pulled back the curtain and shed light on the negotiations, calling upon the NFL to look into a "loophole" that caused the trade to crumble.
Although both teams announced the deal ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, both noted that it was contingent upon Henley completing a physical. It was that examination that led to the trade being called off. According to ESPN , the physical raised concerns inside the Broncos' front office about Henley's knee.
Harbaugh said the Broncos used their findings to negotiate trade compensation after the deadline passed. This is permitted, as long as the teams do not add other players to the trade package. The initial deal called for the Broncos to send a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers in exchange for Henley.
"The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation," Harbaugh said on Thursday after the deal collapsed. "We wouldn't, and we didn't. In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into, because it sets a bad precedent and continues to set a bad precedent."
Henley has only missed three games in his NFL career and just two (in 2023) due to injury. He was on the injury report in Week 6 with a knee issue but practiced in a limited fashion all three days and participated in that week's game. He appeared again on last week's injury report, but it was due to a shoulder problem rather than another knee ailment, and he practiced in full on Thursday and Friday.
Harbaugh said that teams "shouldn't be" allowed to renegotiate trade terms after the deadline regardless of what does or does not come up in physical examinations.
"That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."
The picture Harbaugh painted is one where the Broncos were still open to giving up the 2027 fourth-round pick but wanted to reduce the value of the second pick. According to ESPN, Denver proposed a counteroffer of a fourth-rounder and seventh-rounder or a fourth-rounder and a pick swap. The Broncos still reportedly wanted Henley but not at the agreed-upon price.
"Medical grades should be based on pass/fail, what the medical grade is, not being used by an organization to get less compensation for a trade that was agreed upon," Harbaugh said.
Henley was set for a team upgrade himself, as the trade would have sent him from the NFL's only winless squad to the AFC West leader. He has shined individually despite the Chargers' woes and is the team leader in tackles (51) and fumble recoveries (2) and posted two tackles for loss and an interception across his first eight games of the year. Since he joined the starting lineup in 2024, he has been a perennial 100-tackle linebacker and is on pace to cross that threshold again this season.
The Broncos' starting lineup is already set at the inside linebacker spots with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad occupying the middle of the stout defense, so Henley would have likely arrived as a premier depth option.
Henley is in the final year of his rookie contract and will be an unrestricted free agent at the end of the season.

title: NFL nightmare: How a six-win NFC East team could end up making the playoffs if Commanders beat the Giants
summary: This would be the NFL's worst nightmare
full_text:
The second half of the NFL season kicks off Thursday night, with the New York Giants hosting the Washington Commanders in an NFC East showdown.
With Washington sitting at 2-5-1, this might not seem like a big game, but you could argue that it's actually huge. If Washington pulls off the upset, that will throw a wrench into the NFC East race, because it will leave the Commanders just two games back of the Giants (5-2-1).
A Commanders win could also cause some serious chaos in the division, because it could potentially lead to a situation where a SIX-WIN team wins the NFC East. Now, that probably won't happen, but we're still going to look at this somewhat realistic scenario, since it would be the first time in NFL history that a team has won its division with just six wins.
Here's what would have to happen down the stretch with the Cowboys, Commanders and Giants (For the sake of this exercise, we're not going to worry about the Eagles).
Week 10: at Giants (WIN) Week 11: Bengals (LOSS) Week 12: at Cardinals (WIN) Week 13: at Titans (WIN) Week 14: Texans (LOSS) Week 15: Falcons (LOSS) Week 16: at Vikings (LOSS) Week 17: at Jaguars (LOSS) Week 18: Cowboys (WIN) Breakdown: If the Commanders pull off the upset on Thursday night, it wouldn't be surprising at all to see their schedule play out like this. We have them beating the Cardinals and Titans in two very winnable games and then dropping four in a row and there's a good chance that they'll be the underdog in each of those games.
Week 10: Commanders (LOSS) Week 11: Jaguars (LOSS) Week 12: at Colts (LOSS) Week 13: 49ers (LOSS) Week 14: at Seahawks (LOSS) Week 15: Browns (LOSS) Week 16: at Lions (LOSS) Week 17: at Cowboys (LOSS) Week 18: Eagles (WIN) Breakdown: The biggest stretch on this list is definitely the loss to the Colts in Week 12, but it's easy to see how Indy could potentially pull off an upset. The Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per game and you could see a situation where Jonathan Taylor goes off while leading Indy to a shocking win. As for the other losses, the Giants will probably be an underdog in at least five of their seven games from Week 11 thru Week 17.
Week 10: 49ers  (LOSS) Week 11: Titans (LOSS) Week 12: Eagles (WIN) Week 13: at Seahawks (LOSS) Week 14: BYE Week 15: at Rams (LOSS) Week 16: Jaguars (LOSS) Week 17: Giants (WIN) Week 18: at Commanders (LOSS) Breakdown: The Cowboys still have to play the 49ers, Rams and Seahawks and there's a good chance they'll be a huge underdog in all three of those games. The only game here that would he hard to see happening is the Titans winning in Dallas, but let's not rule it out. Five of Tennessee's seven losses have come by one score and they just took the Bengals to overtime in Week 8.
You essentially have two games here that feel like a stretch -- Titans over Cowboys, Colts over Giants -- but everything else seems somewhat plausible.
If all of this happens, that would set the stage for the NFL's nightmare scenario: A six-win team taking home the NFC East title.
If the schedule plays out this way, the final standings in the division would look like this:
NFC EAST FINAL STANDINGS 1. Commanders: 6-10-1 2. Giants: 6-10-1 3. Cowboys: 6-11
Under this scenario, the Commanders would win the division thanks to their better head-to-head record against the Giants, going 1-0-1.
Not counting strike years, only three teams have ever won their division with seven wins (2010 Seahawks, 2014 Panthers and 2020 Commanders), but no team has ever won it with six wins. Considering the Commanders were the last team to get in with seven wins, it would almost be fitting if they were to break new ground by making the playoffs with six wins.
As a division winner, the six-win Commanders would get to host a game in the wild-card round of the playoffs, and based on how things are playing out in the NFC North right now, they could be playing a team that has TWICE as many wins as them.
If a six-win team ends up hosting a game, the NFL might have to go back to the drawing board with its playoff format. In early 2025, the Lions offered a proposal to change the seeding in the playoffs and if that had gone through, the seeding would have been based on each team's final record.
All four division winners would still have gotten in under this proposal, but they wouldn't have been guaranteed a home game. If the NFC East or NFC South (or both) produce a six-win champion, the league might have to revisit the proposal during the upcoming offseason.

title: Broncos announce trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley falls through, 'will not be finalized'
summary: Henley will return to the Chargers after an initial agreement was reached on Tuesday to send him to Denver
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will not be upgrading their linebacker room after all. The Broncos announced on social media late Wednesday night that "[t]he proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized."
Denver had agreed to send a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Los Angeles in exchange for Henley on deadline day. The Broncos did not provide a reason why the trade is not being finalized.
According to ESPN , Denver had concerns about Henley following his physical. When the trade was initially announced, the Broncos said it was "pending a physical." Even after said physical, per ESPN, the Broncos wanted the trade to go through and discussed revised terms with the Chargers, but no agreement was reached.
Henley has played all eight games for the Chargers this season, recording 51 tackles, two tackles for loss, three quarterback hits, half a sack, two passes defensed, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. He's in the final season of his rookie contract and set to become an unrestricted free agent in 2027.
The Broncos will move forward with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad as their primary linebackers, as they have been for the entire season to date. They still have one of the top defenses in the NFL, and they're still in first place in the AFC West. But they will not get the lift in the middle of their defense that they expected to get when they agreed to this trade in the first place.
On deadline day, CBS Sports gave the Broncos an 'A-' for this deal, given the help Henley would provide. Here's what writer Zachary Pereles initially said:
"The Broncos quietly made a helpful deal, acquiring Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a couple of mid-round picks. Henley has plateaued a bit the past couple of seasons after a strong start, but he's an impressive athlete who could benefit from a change of scenery. Vance Joseph has gotten the most out of lots of players, and Henley has the tools to be next in line."

title: 2026 NFL midseason awards: Expert picks for Super Bowl winner, MVP, Coach of the Year, OPOY and more
summary: The CBS Sports NFL staff predicts winners at the halfway point
full_text:
The NFL season is halfway through, with the Giants and Commanders kicking off Week 10 of the 18-week schedule Thursday night.
As per usual, the first half of the season had plenty of surprises. The Rams entered the year as clear Super Bowl favorites but are now clinging to the outside of the playoff hunt while dealing with a bevy of injuries. The Giants lead the NFC East despite already using three different starting quarterbacks. The Chargers -- an 11-win team in back-to-back seasons -- are the league's only winless team.
So, to recalibrate where things stand, we asked our NFL staff -- writers, editors and CBS Sports HQ analysts -- for their updated award picks plus playoff and Super Bowl projections. Here's what they said:
Voters: Tyler Sullivan, JP Acosta, Josh Edwards, Leger Douzable, Michael Renner, Zach Pereles, R.J. White, John Breech, Garrett Podell, Jordan Dajani, Jared Dubin, Carter Bahns, Pete Prisco, Bryan DeArdo, Kevin Steimle
1. Bengals QB Joe Burrow (11 votes) 2. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence (2 votes) T3. 49ers QB Brock Purdy , Packers QB Jordan Love (1 vote)
Burrow is the clear choice here after a marvelous first half of the season that included at least four total touchdowns in each of his past four games. He leads the NFL in completion percentage (74%), passing touchdowns (23) and passer rating (114.8).
1. Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (6 votes) T2. Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs , Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III (4) 3. Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase (1)
Smith-Njigba is the pick, but it's a close race. In his quest to become the first wide receiver to ever win Offensive Player of the Year twice, the Seahawks star leads the NFL in receiving yards (1,036) and receiving touchdowns (9) and is second in receptions (71). But Gibbs, who leads the NFL with 1,132 scrimmage yards and Walker, who is fourth in that category, are not far behind in our experts' eyes.
1. Texans EDGE Will Anderson Jr . (6 votes) 2. 49ers LB Fred Warner (5 votes) 3. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons (3 votes) 4. Bengals DT Dexter Lawrence (1 vote)
Anderson leads the NFL with 9.5 sacks, and his 12 tackles for loss rank second. After a runner-up finish last year, he's in strong position to earn his first Defensive Player of the Year, but he has some strong competition to hold off. Warner is tied for the NFL lead with five forced fumbles, and his 77 tackles are tied for eighth-most this season.
1. Browns WR Denzel Boston (7 votes) 2. Broncos RB Jonah Coleman (3) T3. Titans WR Carnell Tate , Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza (2) 5. Browns WR KC Concepcion (1)
Boston leads all rookies in receiving yards (507) and receiving touchdowns (3), while Concepcion is tied for the rookie lead in receptions (37), giving the Browns two strong candidates. Mendoza could be the wild card here as he takes over as the Raiders' starter after Kirk Cousins got traded to Minnesota.
1. Giants LB Arvell Reese (9 votes) 2. Jets EDGE David Bailey (6 votes)
This race is truly neck-and-neck and could stay that way throughout the season. Reese is coming off a three-sack game, becoming the youngest player ever with a three-sack game. He's also the only player with 65 tackles, eight tackles for loss and an interception this year. Bailey, meanwhile, leads all rookies with 7.5 sacks and 31 pressures. His five forced fumbles are tied for the league lead as well.
1. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (9 votes) 2. 49ers LB Fred Warner (4) T3. Bengals QB Joe Burrow, Texans WR Tank Dell (1)
Mahomes made it back for Week 1 after tearing his ACL and LCL in December 2025. The Chiefs star ranks top-10 in completion percentage, yards per attemp, touchdown-to-interception rate and passer rating.
1. Lions T Penei Sewell (12 votes) 2. 49ers T Trent Williams (2) 3. Bengals T Amarius Mims (1)
Sewell has made the transition from right tackle to left tackle almost seamlessly. In 298 pass-blocking snaps, he has allowed just one sack and three quarterback hits, and he remains a mauler in the run game. Pro Football Focus has him as the No. 1-graded tackle both overall and in run blocking; he is fourth in pass blocking.
1. Bears WR Luther Burden III (2 votes) T2. 49ers QB Brock Purdy, Texans QB C.J. Stroud , Bears QB Caleb Williams , Packers WR Christian Watson , Bills DL Deone Walker , Packers S Evan Williams , Bills EDGE Greg Rousseau , Buccaneers CB Jacob Parrish , Steelers RB Jaylen Warren , Packers QB Jordan Love, Packers WR Matthew Golden , Bengals WR Tee Higgins , Vikings QB Kirk Cousins (1)
If there's one consensus here, it's that there are a ton of options. Though "Most Improved Player" is not an award handed out by the Associated Press like MVP and most of the other major awards are, it is given out by Pro Football Writers of America. Each of the least four winners have been a quarterback, but in the history of the award dating back to 2000, there have been winners from nearly every.
1. Giants coach John Harbaugh (7 votes) 2. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan (4) 3. Bears coach Ben Johnson (2) T4. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell, Jaguars coach Liam Coen (1)
In his first year in New York, Harbaugh has the 5-2-1 Giants on course for the playoffs, even after losing Jaxson Dart for the season in Week 2. His playing a big role in acquiring J.J. McCarthy certainly helps his candidacy. He has won the award once, back in 2019.
1. Vikings DC Brian Flores (11 votes) 2. 49ers DC Raheem Morris (2 votes) T3. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon, Steelers DC Patrick Graham (1)
Flores dominates this vote, and for good reason. The Vikings are second in yards per game and yards per play, and first in sack rate and red-zone efficiency. Minnesota's 14.5 points per game allowed is also best in the league.
1. Jaguars GM James Gladstone (7 votes) 2. Bears GM Ryan Poles (6) 3. Browns GM Andrew Berry (2)
Gladstone's bold trade-deadline deals for defensive lineman Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III could be what push the Jaguars to the top of the AFC, if not beyond. Poles, meanwhile, swung the biggest deal of the year, sending two first-round picks to the Titans for Jeffery Simmons. Both Gladstone and Poles lead teams that lead their divisions.
1. Jaguars (4 votes) 2. 49ers (3) T3. Bears, Bengals, Broncos (2) T6. Packers, Bills (1)

title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Was Arvell Reese a luxury for Giants? Has Francis Mauigoa turned a corner?
summary: New York's top-10 investments are already fueling a 5-2-1 start, with a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate emerging on defense and a reshaped offensive line
full_text:
The New York Giants ushered in a new era with head coach John Harbaugh and immediately introduced a new way of thinking. Leading into Thursday night of the draft, New York had been linked to Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love , Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate and a variety of offensive linemen, but the availability of Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese presented a new wrinkle in the decision-making. In the past, New York may have gone with a bigger position of need rather than best player available. The selection of Reese breathed new life into the building and inspired hope for the future.
New York has overcome the loss of quarterback Jaxson Dart to sprint out to a 5-2-1 record. The process is paying dividends in the Big Apple, but were those the correct first-round selections long-term?
Removing the positional value of quarterback from the picture, Reese was the top prospect available in the 2026 NFL Draft . Many did not immediately associate the former Buckeye with the New York team, because they are chock full with pass rushers and linebacker is not typically a position taken Top-5 overall. Recognizing the potential of Reese and making that selection when bigger needs were present illustrated discipline and sound decision-making of which the franchise had not been associated over the prior half decade.
Through Week 9, Reese has expressed that potential in all facets of the game. In the run game, he plays square to the line of scrimmage and shows an ability to slip blocks to make a tackle in the gap. As a coverage defender, he shows the range and top end speed to effectively trail leaks out of the backfield or a tight end escaping into a route. As a pass rusher, he sets up moves well and exploits oversetting linemen with his quickness. According to TruMedia, he has converted 85 pass rush snaps into 4.5 sacks (all of which have come over the last four games).
In Week 9, he strengthened his case for Defensive Rookie of the Year with three sacks. There is still room for improvement as Reese can do a better job not getting sucked down into the box and trusting his eyes more to make those impactful plays in the backfield, but the early returns have been impressive.
After trading All-Pro defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati, New York was positioned to make two selections in the Top-10 overall. Harbaugh had premier assets with which to construct the next iteration of the Giants franchise.
After selecting Reese, there was dialogue about which position the team might target next. Would they draft a wide receiver to pair with Malik Nabers ? Is Caleb Downs the Kyle Hamilton-type eraser at safety? With Ohio State's Carnell Tate and Arizona State's Jordyn Tyson off the board, the choice seemingly came down to building through the trenches or Downs.
The only offensive lineman drafted prior to New York's selection was Utah's Spencer Fano . Harbaugh deployed a strategy to fortify the offensive line to support young quarterback Jaxson Dart. Six other offensive linemen were taken in the next 16 selections.
A former right tackle at Miami, Mauigoa has transitioned to right guard. Jermaine Eluemunor had earned an extended opportunity to stick at right tackle. Eluemunor turns 32 next month, and there is an off-ramp from his contract following the 2027 campaign. Could a return to his former position be on the horizon for Mauigoa?
Mauigoa had been a sturdy presence for the Hurricanes, so a move to offensive guard seemed natural. He has been inconsistent. Ironically, his best game was against the vaunted Texans pass rush. The Samoan displayed independent hand usage to better sustain blocks and did a good job angling blocks to seal run lanes for Cam Skattebo .
Other times, block sustainment has been an issue because he does not bring his hands along with his feet. He occasionally loses depth in the pocket, and his eyes are not always in the right place to pick up stunts. The bull rush has given him some problems, resulting in 4 sacks and 14 pressures allowed this season, according to TruMedia.
Aspects of his game will improve with more repetitions at guard, but it also feels as though he is missing the edge with which he played in Coral Gables.
There is a world where Reese is not the best prospect to come out of this draft class, but the odds of him being anything less than just a good player are slim to none. New York made the correct decision at No. 5 overall. He already looks like one of the better linebackers in the NFL and his value could rise even more if the team elects to utilize him more as a pass rusher.
If New York plans to move Mauigoa back to tackle, then the decision to take him at No. 10 overall was likely well-founded. If they intend to keep him at right guard, they would have been better served taking the player who had already spent considerable time there (Vega Ioane). The jury is out on his ceiling in the NFL, but Mauigoa quickly filled one of the five starting offensive line positions, which is valuable.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Why Kirk Cousins made decision to return to Minnesota, reunite with Vikings
summary: Cousins said one phone call on Tuesday helped him make his decision
full_text:
Maybe the most consequential trade of deadline day in the NFL wasn't actually made by a front office executive. Instead, the lone player in the deal gave it the final go-ahead.
In the final hours before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline, the Minnesota Vikings pulled off a trade for Kirk Cousins , sending the Las Vegas Raiders a 2027 third-round pick to reunite with their former quarterback. Before ultimately agreeing to the deal, however, the Raiders put the ball in Cousins' court, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . Las Vegas gave Cousins the chance to decide whether he'd like to leave the organization and head back to Minnesota or stay with the club he had started the first nine games of the 2026 season for. A big reason he decided to head to the Vikings was head coach Kevin O'Connell.
"Kevin knows me. Kevin knows what I do well. Kevin knows what I don't do well," Cousins said on Wednesday. "Kevin knows what I can handle. Kevin knows what I can't handle. And I think that helps."
Cousins said he was eating breakfast with his Raiders teammates when he got a call from Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak informing him he was being traded. After talking with his family, agent Mike McCartney, and O'Connell, Cousins made up his mind by midday Tuesday and ultimately informed Raiders GM John Spytek that he wanted to return to Minnesota. Thus, the trade was made.
Part of the calculus in Cousins' decision to opt for a return to the Vikings was the presence of Fernando Mendoza . Cousins seemed to know it was only a matter of time before the Raiders turned the keys to the franchise over to the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, so his status as QB1 was fleeting.
But Cousins has such a strong familiarity with O'Connell and the Vikings that made the move easier. He believes it will help them down the stretch.
"Not just that [O'Connell] knows your strengths, but that he knows your weaknesses," Cousins said. "And that as a result, he's going to try to protect you and not have you do things that he knows, 'You know what? That's not how Kirk functions. That's not his best chance of success.'
"I think the fact he knows me well, the good about me and the bad about me, I think that should help us."
Cousins was a name thrown around during the trade deadline, but he said he wasn't necessarily interested in just going to any team. The fit had to make sense for him and his success, and it made sense with the Vikings.
"I'm not too interested in completely starting over," Cousins said when asked about potentially being traded elsewhere. "I want to play with … you've got to play off reaction and instinct. And if you're thinking, I don't think you can quite be the player that you otherwise could be. So to me, it's important to be able to be at a place that you feel you at least have the potential to do that."
Even with that familiarity, joining a new team and starting for them in the same week is no easy feat, even for a veteran. O'Connell said the goal would be for Cousins to start in their high-stakes divisional game against the Packers on Sunday, but added that he wants to "be fair to Kirk and make sure he feels good about it going into Lambeau Field."
The last game Cousins played in a Vikings uniform was at Lambeau Field in 2023, when the QB tore his Achilles and his season was declared over.
"To be back there wearing purple and gold, it has meaning," Cousins said about the significance of his return with the Vikings happening in the same spot as his injury. "But you have to go make it mean something with the way you play."
When asked if he feels he has unfinished business, he said, "I think my whole career's felt like unfinished business."
With an opportunity to go back and help a Vikings team he spent six years with and won the NFC North with in 2022, the proper pieces fell into place to give the deal the green light. This is also a pretty unprecedented move, as Cousins has the most single-season passing touchdowns (20) — as well as career passing touchdowns (318) — by any quarterback changing teams midseason in NFL history.
During his first six-season stint with the Vikings, Cousins was second in the league in completion percentage (67.9%), fourth in passing yards (23,265), and third in passing touchdowns (171) among all quarterbacks over that span with at least 50 starts. He also reunites with wide receiver Justin Jefferson , who averaged 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins — an NFL record for most receiving yards by a quarterback-receiver duo over at least 50 games.
While the 15-year veteran is now returning at 38, the hope is that he can come close to that production and give an offense tied for the fewest offensive touchdowns (11) in the NFL this season a boost. Cousins is focused on maintaining "joy" in a job where comparisons can steal it. While that can be a challenge, he said he looks forward to embracing it in the coming weeks.

title: NFL MVP odds: Joe Burrow surpasses Josh Allen for top spot entering Week 10
summary: There's a new leader in the MVP conversation with nine weeks to go in the NFL regular season
full_text:
Once again, the race to win NFL MVP has become a literal arms race. While Kenneth Walker III was an early favorite, the current front-runners to win the award are quarterbacks, which shouldn't come as a surprise, as a quarterback has won the award each year since 2013. Unless Walker or Jaxon Smith-Njigba go on a ridiculous run over the season's final two months, the NFL's most prestigious individual honor will once again be given to a quarterback.
There's a very good chance that the next NFL MVP will ultimately be one of the following five quarterbacks who currently have the highest odds to win the award. There's also a decent chance that this year's winner will be a first-time recipient, although Josh Allen may have something to say about that.
Gibbs currently has the best chance of any non-quarterback to win league MVP. If that happened, Gibbs would be the first running back to win MVP since Adrian Peterson did so back in 2012.
In addition to being third in the NFL in rushing and tied for second in touchdown runs, Gibbs paces the league in rushes and first-down runs (55). Gibbs is currently on pace to rush for 1,800 yards, which would be the third-most prolific rushing season in Lions history behind only Barry Sanders' 1997 and 1994 campaigns.
So far, Maye's season hasn't lived up to last year's MVP runner-up campaign. He's currently tied with Justin Herbert for interceptions thrown after Maye threw three interceptions during last Sunday's lopsided loss to the Green Bay Packers .
While he currently has decent odds of winning MVP, something drastic would have to happen for Maye to actually become the first Patriots player to win the award since Tom Brady .
For whatever reason, Goff's name is often overlooked in discussions regarding the league's top quarterbacks. That might change, however, if Goff and the Lions continue at their current pace.
After a 2-2 start, the Lions have ripped off four straight wins and have gotten to within a half-game of first-place Chicago in the NFC North. Goff, who oddly threw for just 170 and 176 yards in Detroit's last two wins, can strengthen his MVP argument with a winning performance this weekend against Maye's Patriots. It's safe to wonder, however, if Gibbs could cancel Goff out in terms of MVP votes, and vice versa.
The two-time league MVP, in addition to having Walker and Travis Kelce at his disposal, will now have Josh Downs to throw to after the Chiefs acquired the former Colts wideout before the trade deadline. That addition should help Mahomes' MVP odds moving forward.
While he doesn't lead the NFL in any major statistic, Mahomes is nonetheless in the middle of the MVP conversation again, and for good reason. He's once again the catalyst of the Chiefs ' offense and is playing his best football of the season.
In Week 7, Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns (while completing 73.2% of his passes) in a close loss to the Broncos . Last Sunday, Mahomes completed a whopping 74.2% of his throws while throwing two touchdowns in a rout of the Jets .
Williams' injury (which sidelined him for three games) hurt his MVP case. His four interceptions in last Sunday's overtime win over the Buccaneers didn't help, either.
Despite those warts, Williams still has a puncher's chance at joining Walter Payton as the only Bears player to win MVP. It will likely come down to how successful Williams is from a win-loss standpoint. If Williams plays well down the stretch and helps lead the Bears to a division title (and a possible No. 1 seed), he should have a pretty strong MVP case.
While they didn't acquire any offensive players, the Jaguars loaded up on defense before the trade deadline by acquiring safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux . Those additions should obviously make the Jaguars even better, which in turn should help Lawrence's MVP chances.
No Jaguars player has ever won the league MVP, but that could soon change. It would probably take the Jaguars winning the AFC's No. 1 seed, though, which is possible given their transactions before the trade deadline.
Lawrence has been incredibly efficient this season. Eight percent of his attempts have been touchdowns (an NFL high). He also leads the league in average yards gained per pass attempt and yards gained per pass completion. Lawrence is doing all this while also taking care of the ball.
Three weeks into the season, the Packers were 1-2, and there were rumblings about Matt LaFleur's job security. That's a distant memory now as Green Bay currently sits at 6-3 following Sunday's convincing win over the Patriots.
Love's play since Week 3 has been the biggest reason for Green Bay's resurgence . No one has thrown for more yards this season than Love, who could join fellow Packer quarterbacks Bart Starr, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers as a league MVP.
Love is taking advantage of an emerging receiving corps that is quickly becoming one of the league's best. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson (whose 17.9 average yards-per-catch leads the NFL) have become a formidable duo, while Tucker Kraft is showing no ill effects from last year's season-ending knee injury.
Somehow, the former Mr. Irrelevant continues to be overlooked. For all of his success since becoming the 49ers' starting quarterback, Purdy still isn't usually put in the same stratosphere as some of the league's other top-tier quarterbacks. That will have to change if Purdy continues to play well and the 49ers keep winning games.
Some of the hesitancy to anoint Purdy as an elite quarterback may stem from the narrative that he plays with so many talented players. While that is true, it's also true that Purdy has often had to play without many of those players due to injuries. He's recently been without wideouts Mike Evans , Christian Kirk and Deebo Samuel .
Purdy has been one of the main constants this season for the 49ers, who would be the NFC's top seed if the playoffs started this week. He'll need more of his wideouts to get healthy, however, if he wants to keep pace in the MVP race. Purdy has thrown four touchdowns and three interceptions in the 49ers' last three games, which is a byproduct of the team's injuries at receiver.
The 2024 league MVP, Allen was the front-runner for the first half of the regular season. And while he no longer has the top spot, Allen still has a very good shot at winning his second MVP in three years.
Buffalo's success as a team — they are 7-1 and would be the top seed in the AFC if the playoffs started today — and Allen's prowess as a runner should keep him in the MVP race until the very end. Bears running back D'Andre Swift is the only player with more rushing touchdowns this season than Allen's nine.
Allen's passing touchdown total, however, could be the main reason why he doesn't win league MVP. His 12 touchdown passes are currently tied with Geno Smith for the 15th highest total in the NFL. Allen has thrown 11 fewer touchdown passes than the player that has supplanted him as the MVP front-runner.
Burrow could have won league MVP in 2024, but the award ultimately went to Allen largely because of team success, or lack thereof. The Bills went 13-4 during the regular season and came within a game of the Super Bowl . The Bengals missed the playoffs with a 9-8 record despite Burrow leading the league in both passing yards and touchdown passes.
Defense was Cincinnati's Achilles heel then, but their current unit has helped the Bengals get off to a 6-2 start and have put Burrow in position to possibly win his first league MVP.
It also helps that Burrow has elite connections with wideouts Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The trio has been torching opposing defenses on a weekly basis. Burrow, in particular, has been on fire, as he currently leads the NFL in completion percentage (74%) and touchdown passes (23).
Cincinnati's offensive line has also undergone a rapid improvement. Burrow no longer has to pick himself up off the ground after seemingly every…

title: Super Bowl odds: How title odds have changed in nine weeks since the start of the season
summary: The 49ers have surged into the top spot while the Bears and Jaguars make dramatic leaps into the top four, leaving preseason darling Los Angeles searching for answers
full_text:
The 2026 NFL regular season is officially halfway through, and it's about time we start paying attention to these division races and the competition for the first-round byes in each conference. The NFC North is completely loaded with every team having at least six wins, while the NFC South features four teams with exactly three victories. The quality of play may be different, but these races will be fierce nonetheless.
What about the Super Bowl favorites? The San Francisco 49ers look like the top dog in the NFC, while the one-loss Buffalo Bills are maintaining pace in the AFC. Let's take a look at the current Super Bowl LXI odds for the teams in the top half of the league, and examine how they've changed from the preseason.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Hindsight is 20/20, but the 49ers may have always been the play in the NFC West and were a good value Super Bowl bet. In a division featuring the reigning Super Bowl champions and an alleged "Super Team," there sat the seemingly-always competitive 49ers. Believe it or not, there were TEN teams that had shorter odds than the 49ers to win the Super Bowl preseason. They were listed at +1900 and are now the favorites at +540.
Through nine weeks, the 49ers are the lone one-loss team in the conference and hold the No. 1 seed. This is San Francisco's best eight-game start since 2019, when they also made the Super Bowl. Brock Purdy ranks top three in completion percentage, yards per attempt and passer rating this year despite the 49ers having the most games missed due to injury among wide receivers (39), according to CBS Sports Research. Injuries are again a concern with the 49ers, as they also have the most games missed due to injury overall with 159. John Lynch added defensive lineman DeForest Buckner and wide receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline to fill some holes and should return players like Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel and CJ West soon.
Two teams made massive jumps into the top four: the Bears and Jaguars.
The Bears have gone from +2400 to +850 to win the Super Bowl this year. Chicago was coming off a season in which it went 11-6, clinched the NFC North for the first time since 2018 and won its first playoff game since 2011. It certainly looked like Caleb Williams had found his footing in the league, but the Bears were projected to have the hardest strength of schedule in the NFL this season. Each of the past nine teams to enter a season with the hardest strength of schedule failed to win a playoff game. Many saw the Bears regressing in 2026, but they may be even better this season. The Bears are off to their best nine-game start to a season since 2012, boast the No. 3 offense in the NFL and have a rejuvenated defense with the arrival of Jeffery Simmons . The Bears may be the best team in the best division.
The Jaguars, on the other hand, have seen their odds shift from +3000 to +750. Jacksonville is running away with the AFC South, as its six wins this season are as many as the rest of the division combined. The Jaguars are an NFL-best 14-2 over the past 16 games dating back to last year, while Trevor Lawrence leads all quarterbacks in total touchdowns in that timeframe with 42. With the No. 1 seed in the conference in reach, general manager James Gladstone went out and acquired defensive tackle Jordan Davis , defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III at the trade deadline.
What I will say about the Jaguars is that there are not many impressive wins on their schedule. In Week 3, they blew out the Patriots, who have taken a step back from last year, and beat Joe Burrow and the Bengals in Cincinnati in Week 4. If you were curious, the Jaguars' two losses this season came to the Broncos and Texans. They have an interesting stretch on their schedule from Weeks 13-15, where they play at the Bears, vs. the Steelers and at the Texans.
Since the NFL expanded to 32 teams in 2002, this year marked just the fifth time that we've seen an overwhelming preseason Super Bowl favorite with odds under +1000. The Rams were listed at +550 after loading up on big names like Aaron Donald , Myles Garrett , Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson , but now own the seventh-shortest odds at +1300.
The Rams are 5-4, and one reason is injuries. Donald and Garrett played together for just the first time this past week, while Matthew Stafford's two star wideouts in Davante Adams (hamstring) and Puka Nacua (knee, turf toe) are now sidelined. Kobie Turner (groin) is on injured reserve, Poona Ford (triceps) and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) are out for the year, and Steve Avila (hamstring) is now expected to miss several weeks.
Even when the Rams were relatively healthy, they haven't looked like the team they were in 2025. To be honest, LA holding +1300 odds at this point is surprising. I would rather place money on the Broncos, Lions, Packers or even Vikings.
