title: NFL Week 10 picks: Our experts face off on Commanders at Giants, Vikings at Packers and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run?
This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset.  … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20
Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night.  … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14
Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back.
When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20
Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late.  … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21
Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21
Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16
Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17
Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game.  … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14
Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26
Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense.  … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23
Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Week 10 Super Bowl stock report: Jaguars go all-in at trade deadline, injuries ravage Patriots offense
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 9 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
At the NFL trade deadline , many of the league's fiercest Super Bowl contenders made moves to separate themselves from the pack . The midseason point and the personnel changes that come with it are often a fulcrum upon which the championship race hinges, and that may be the case again in 2026. Teams like the Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears are pushing their chips forward, and non-competitive teams are feeding them star players in exchange for draft capital.
Some postseason hopefuls were eerily quiet at the deadline, though. Why did the Los Angeles Rams not make a play for a wide receiver? How come the New England Patriots sat on their hands while their offense battles the injury bug? Time will tell whether the decisions to stand pat hurt those teams and others.
Week 10 offers a first look at many players on their new teams, which adds intrigue to a schedule that already includes a couple of massive divisional clashes and an important international matchup.
Here are the latest trends in the Super Bowl race coming out of the trade deadline and heading into Week 10.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
James Gladstone had a field day a day before the deadline. The wunderkind general manager pulled off three trades on Nov. 9, which was tied for the most in the league . All of them project to make the Jaguars noticeably better in the immediate future, and one of them, the blockbuster deal for Jordan Davis , added another cornerstone standout to the roster for the long term. Gladstone parted with a first-round pick, two second-rounders and a pair of Day 3 selections to bolster a defense that already ranks second in scoring. That shows a commitment to winning now at the highest level.
Davis and Godchaux will shore up and likely even improve upon the run-stopping efforts while DaVon Hamilton watches the rest of the season from the sidelines with a torn quad. Bates is a plug-and-play replacement for Eric Murray at safety who brings All-Pro-caliber production to the pass defense. The Jaguars filled a couple of lineup holes in an emphatic fashion.
2027 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pick
2027 second-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick
Conditional 2028 sixth-round pick
These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence , somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place.
An easy-peasy schedule over the second half of the season paves the way for the Jaguars to contend for the AFC's No. 1 seed. They face the one-win Tennessee Titans twice in the next three weeks, have matchups with three teams from the downtrodden NFC East and close the campaign with a trip to face the rebuilding Indianapolis Colts . The only real test that lies ahead is a Dec. 6 battle with the Bears. That might be a Super Bowl preview.
Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins . The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl.
Making matters more challenging is the decimation that occurred on the offensive side of the ball over the last couple of weeks. The Patriots will be without their top two running backs for the foreseeable future as Rhamondre Stevenson battles a knee injury and TreVeyon Henderson manages a mysterious illness. At wide receiver, Romeo Doubs remains on injured reserve, and A.J. Brown cannot seem to get quite right due to his ankle sprain and knee condition. Alijah Vera-Tucker is on IR, too, and represents a key missing piece on the offensive line.
All of those issues undoubtedly contributed to Drake Maye reverting to his early-season tendencies in Week 9. He is back in a tie for the league lead in turnovers on the heels of his three-interception disaster in the blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers .
Because of all these injuries, things might get worse before they get better. If and when the offense gets closer to full strength, time will be of the essence as New England seeks to lock up a playoff berth.
Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix.
Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. He continues to play the best football of his career and is not even remotely the reason why the Texans are still two games under .500. Tank Dell's return to the wide receiver group and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s addition about a month ago also gave him a deep stable of pass-catchers to target, and he is cashing in.
Nobody expected the story of the Texans' season to be the offense carrying the defense, but here they are. The defense has to click eventually, right? It is bizarre to watch Will Anderson Jr . lead the league in sacks and play at a Defensive Player of the Year level yet have the rest of the defense fail him. There are plenty of opportunities for that group to right itself against middling opponents in the weeks to come.
Sunday, 1 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo (try for free)
Losses are rare in the NFC North. At least one team has to add one to their tally in Week 10, though. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason . They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. But they will have to do so against a Vikings offense that should be far better the rest of the season now that Kirk Cousins is in at quarterback.
Sunday, 9:30 a.m., NFL Network
Considering all of the Patriots' offensive deficiencies, there is a world in which the Detroit Lions post a number New England simply cannot match. But maybe this is the right kind of opponent for Mike Vrabel's squad at this juncture: One with a porous defense that they can move the ball against even when they are not at full strength. Detroit is squarely in the aforementioned NFC North battle and needs a win here, as it does every week, to keep up with the rest of the pack.
Sunday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo (try for free)
Someone's four-game winning streak has to end on "Sunday Night Football." The victor between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will secure sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers got the job done in the first meeting, which was a hotly contested 30-27 clash in Pittsburgh. Home-field advantage means a heck of a lot in this division and could lead to the opposite result this time around. Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level helps quite a lot, too.
author: Carter Bahns

title: It wouldn't shock me if ... NFL Week 10: Fernando Mendoza struggles in first start, new Chiefs WR dominates
summary: The No. 1 overall pick doesn't have the softest landing spot to make his first start
full_text:
Nine weeks and the trade deadline are now in our rearview mirror. From here on out, it's all gas no brakes through the second half of the regular season as we rocket towards the playoffs down the road to Super Bowl LXI. Of course, plenty will happen between now and when we kick off that championship match from SoFi Stadium, and we'll keep marching on with Week 10 on deck.
As always, unexpected storylines develop over the course of the season and in a given week, and we try to pinpoint some of them for you here before they arrive.
Last week, we highlighted a bounce-back performance from Bijan Robinson , who had 147 scrimmage yards in a loss to Cincinnati in Madrid. While he didn't commit multiple turnovers, we also put you on the scent of Jayden Daniels -- who fumbled -- being a little loose with the football, along with Jonah Coleman continuing to play well enough to soften Denver's need to acquire a back at the deadline.
We'll look to carry that momentum into this week. Below, you can find five storylines and/or individual performances we wouldn't be shocked to see happen in Week 10.
All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
Rather quietly, Zach Charbonnet has looked good in his return from his ACL tear last January. He's played in two games for Seattle and is quickly taking over the backfield.
After a modest six carries in his first game back in Week 8, Charbonnet dominated the backfield touches in Week 9. The veteran back had 16 carries in the win over Arizona, well above Jadarian Price's 9 carries. On top of getting the lion's share of work, Charbonnet is proving to simply be the better back. He's averaging 4.5 yards per carry, far better than Price's 3.7 yards per carry on the season and 2.8 yards per carry since returning from IR in Week 8.
Given the current trajectory of both players, it wouldn't shock me to see Charbonnet continue to see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. If he does, he has a chance to put together his best game so far: the Raiders are allowing 5.0 yards per carry this season, which is tied for the most in the NFL .
In fact, Charbonnet is liable to record just the third 100-yard rushing game of his career in this matchup.
Gambling nugget to note : Zach Charbonnet's rushing yards total for Week 10 is 60.5 (-113 to the Over).
Josh Downs was one of the notable names to be moved on deadline day, and the former Colts receiver suddenly finds himself in NFL nirvana. Not only was his trade request granted, but he was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs , where Patrick Mahomes will be his quarterback. Judging by his immediate reaction to the trade on social media, Downs is clearly happy with how things turned out.
pic.twitter.com/SWGjirDe9N
I expect the Chiefs to see immediate returns from this move, as Downs fits how the offense has run this season perfectly. More than in any other season of his career, Mahomes and the Chiefs have primarily worked the short passing game, as his 5.6 air yards per attempt highlights. Downs is an elite separator. His 3.2 average yards of separation and +24 yards after the catch over expectation are 24th and tied for 24th among 72 qualified receivers, according to NFL Pro. Mahomes will quickly realize and exploit that ability.
Kansas City has desperately been looking for an answer at receiver as the position group is averaging just 117.5 receiving yards per game this season. Not only does that rank 28th in the NFL this season, but it's the fewest in the Mahomes era. Downs may change that overnight.
Atlanta is coming off a loss to the Bengals in Madrid, where the Cincinnati receivers ran wild. While Ja'Marr Chase is in a class of his own, I do believe Downs can have loads of success against this secondary that also just traded away star safety Jessie Bates.
Finally paired with a quarterback that can get him the football, Downs makes his presence felt early for Kansas City.
Gambling nugget to note : Josh Downs' receiving yard total for Week 10 is 30.5 (-109 to the Over).
The Fernando Mendoza era is about to begin in Las Vegas. The No. 1 overall pick is slated to make his first career start on Sunday, after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins (who started the first nine games of the season) to the Minnesota Vikings before Tuesday's deadline.
While anticipation is building for a full look at Mendoza in the NFL, this isn't exactly the softest landing spot for him. The Indiana product will have the luxury of being at home, but at the same time will have the tall task of facing the Seattle Seahawks defense.
The unit is allowing just 244.2 total yards of offense per game, including 155.1 passing yards allowed per game. Both are the fewest in the NFL. On top of that, their 4.1 total yards per play allowed is the lowest by any team through nine games since the 2023 Ravens . They're also surrendering the fewest 20-yard plays (17) through nine games since the 2008 Steelers .
Facing the defending Super Bowl champs presents a tough challenge for Mendoza to come out of the gate firing in his first start. In fact, he's the first quarterback taken No. 1 overall to face the defending champions in his first career start. The five previous first-round rookie quarterbacks to debut against the reigning champs have all lost.
Meanwhile, No. 1 pick quarterbacks are 1-15-1 in their first career starts since 2003. Given that history, it's not worth hitting the panic button even if Mendoza does struggle.
Gambling nugget to note : Fernando Mendoza is -156 to throw an interception in Week 10.
Coming into Week 10, Joe Burrow is the odds-on favorite to win the NFL MVP award at +190. He's followed by Josh Allen , who has +250 odds to win the award for the second time in his career. After that, however, is Brock Purdy at +425. By the end of Week 10, however, it's plausible that Purdy ascends to the top of these odds as the new favorite to win the award.
As I've written about elsewhere this week , I think there's a possibility the Steelers cool down Joe Burrow on "Sunday Night Football." To his credit, Burrow has put up otherworldly numbers, but it's come against subpar competition. He faces a much tougher task against Pittsburgh, who is top five in the NFL in yards per play allowed and points per game allowed. The defense is also tied for the eighth-lowest passer rating allowed. Coming off of their bye, while Cincinnati returns from a game in Spain, there's the potential for him to post a dud in primetime, which will ding his odds.
Meanwhile, Purdy gets an advantageous matchup himself as he and the 49ers will roll into AT&T Stadium to face the Cowboys. Dallas is giving up the third-most total yards per game in the NFL and the third-most yards per play. Moreover, they're giving up 26.2 points per game (bottom 10 in the NFL), opponents are converting 48.31% of their third-down opportunities (highest), and a 99.1 passer rating (eighth-highest).
Purdy is top-three in the NFL in completion percentage, yards per attempt, and passer rating this season and has a history of dominating against the Cowboys. For his career, the 49ers QB is 3-0 against Dallas, averaging 9.2 yards per attempt and a 118.4 passer rating.
The stage is set for another monster outing. If he plays to that level, the MVP chatter surrounding him will only get louder.
Speaking of awards, Will Anderson Jr . is becoming the overwhelming favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year in 2026.
Currently, his odds to win DPOY are down to +150, with Fred Warner the next up behind him at +600. That's thanks to Anderson piling up 9.5 sacks, which are the most in the NFL through nine weeks and the second-most by a Texans player in the first eight games of a season (J.J. Watt with 105 in 2012). Anderson is one of the game's elite pass rushers, and I expect him to only bolster his case to win the award with what could be a career performance on Sunday against the Browns.
Cleveland is set to have Deshaun Watson after the veteran quarterback missed last week's loss to New…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Buyer Beware: 5 NFL deadline trades that could become the next Sauce Gardner bust
summary: Jordan Davis must justify a first-round pick, Kirk Cousins must prove he can elevate Minnesota and three other acquisitions face similarly high stakes
full_text:
As in-season trades become all the more prevalent in the NFL , the risk of overspending also rises. That was most clear in 2025 when the Indianapolis Colts made perhaps the most regrettable trade in league history by sending two first-round picks to the New York Jets in exchange for cornerback Sauce Gardner . Those draft picks are golden with the Colts entering a deep rebuild, while Gardner has played the worst football of his career since landing in Indianapolis.
When teams pulled off 18 deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, they did so hoping to avoid the disaster that was the Colts' acquisition of Gardner. Chances are high that none of this year's trades will be as lopsided as that one, but it is far too soon to rule it out.
Only one transaction this year included two first-round picks, and it is already paying dividends for the purchasing side. And only one other included a single first-rounder. That does not mean that all of the teams involved are out of the woods just yet, though.
Here are the 2026 in-season trades with the greatest potential to go down as busts.
The trade that most resembles the infamous Sauce Gardner deal is the one that moved Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears . The Tennessee Titans secured two first-round picks in the swap. There will always be long-term risks (most notably regarding injury), but Simmons has already delivered, in a small sample size, everything the Bears could have asked of him. The superstar defensive tackle notched a sack and pass breakup in both of his first two games and logged an additional tackle for loss in his debut and elevated the entire unit around him in the process. It is far too soon to close the book on this trade, but all indications suggest it is a slam dunk for the Super Bowl-contending Bears.
Many elements of the Jordan Davis trade make sense for the Jacksonville Jaguars as they pursue the first Super Bowl in franchise history. The most obvious of them is that Davis fills an immediate need that arose when DaVon Hamilton went down with a season-ending torn quad muscle. But there is a great deal of inherent risk that comes with moving a 2027 first-round pick and 2029 second-rounder to land him. It is an all-in move that will either pay tremendous dividends or go down as an overpay. There is very little middle ground when it comes to these kinds of blockbuster trades.
Davis has to be a difference-maker from the jump. The Jaguars are in play for the AFC's No. 1 seed and will battle until season's end to secure it. More importantly, this trade will be judged in the context of what Davis delivers in the postseason. Anything short of a Super Bowl run is suddenly a disappointment, and Davis needs to play a major role in their championship pursuit.
From a run-stopping standpoint, Davis should give the Jaguars everything they lost from Hamilton and more. For the price they paid, it would be preferable if Davis were more of a threat as a pass rusher, however. He has never logged more than 4.5 sacks in a season. If offenses have to take blockers away from other players to account for him, then perhaps the added pocket disruption from the edges will make up for his lack of havoc creation.
The 2023 Biletnikoff Award winner is already a bust of a No. 4 overall draft pick. Will his trade from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans be a bust, too? Unless Marvin Harrison Jr.'s new team can tap back into the production that made him a promising rookie two years ago, the investment of a second-round pick to acquire him will go down as a steep price to pay for no more than a tertiary option in a deep receiving corps.
With time, Harrison's reunion with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud , may prove fruitful. It would be unfair to ask those two to hit the ground running as a prolific tandem considering their time apart and the amount of time it takes to settle into a new system, but over the long term (and there is a long term here with Harrison under contract through 2027 and potentially into 2028) it is a reasonable expectation. Harrison is still a talented player, and Stroud is rounding into a standout franchise quarterback this season. On paper, those two things should mesh well.
There are warning signs about Harrison's future as a viable NFL starter, though, most notably in the form of his questionable effort in Arizona. And while he does have a touchdown already in Houston, he has not caught more than three passes in a game since joining the Texans and has only run 29 routes over three games. All three of his appearances came off the bench, too.
The modest playing time could be a result of Houston easing him into action until he gets a firm grasp on the playbook and rebuilds his connection with Stroud, but it may also indicate that he is not a top option in what has quickly become a crowded wide receiver group. Stroud has to battle each of these players for targets:
That is not to mention tight end Dalton Schultz , who leads all Texans with 47 targets on the season.
If it pans out, the Kirk Cousins move could be the most impactful in-season trade of them all and spark a Super Bowl run for the Minnesota Vikings . His potential to elevate the offense and maximize the team's potential with its otherworldly defense is real. But there is also a risk that Cousins cannot replicate what he did with the Las Vegas Raiders over the first half of the season, and the Vikings give up a third-round pick for a lateral move at quarterback rather than an upgrade over Kyler Murray .
Cousins was rejuvenated in Sin City and played his best version of football since his first stint in Minnesota. He is even on pace to flirt with the first 40-touchdown season of his career. The 38-year-old who fell out of favor with the Atlanta Falcons turned himself back into a starter and a highly productive one at that. But that came in an immensely quarterback-friendly system that coach Klint Kubiak has proven can turn middle-of-the-road passers into standouts. What happens when he leaves that scheme?
The last time Cousins played for Kevin O'Connell, he made the Pro Bowl. His fit in the Vikings' offense may be just as ideal as the one he displayed in Las Vegas. The numbers, in fact, suggest it could be even better.
But the last time Cousins played for the Minnesota Timberwolves was when he was 35, before he tore his Achilles. This is a different quarterback than the one who won 13 games in his last 17-game season in 2022.
The Dallas Cowboys have only gotten one game of full-strength Joey Porter Jr . despite trading for him all the way back on Oct. 1. He did not record a statistic in that debut. Since then, Porter missed a game due to illness, missed another with an ankle injury, and played through the ankle issue in two other games. It remains to be seen whether he will return to the lineup in Week 10 after he missed last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts.
When he is on the field, Porter is a lockdown cornerback. He allowed no better than a minuscule 47.9 passer rating in any of his first three games with the Cowboys across 10 targets. He still has permitted just one touchdown in his career and has gone 1,570 coverage snaps since then, according to Next Gen Stats. But if he cannot stay in the lineup, he will not be worth the 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-rounder the Cowboys gave up to acquire him from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Especially if he leaves in free agency.
That is the next major question in this marriage between Porter and Dallas. Will he stick around beyond this year? The Steelers were unwilling to meet his reported demands to make him one of the highest-paid cornerbacks in the NFL, and Jerry Jones does not exactly have a history of paying players what they ask for, either. This could turn out to be a one-year rental for a player who has already missed time.
Plus, it is not like the Cowboys' defense at large has taken any major steps forward since Porter joined the unit. The NFL's third-worst group in…
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 10 upset alert: Why the red-hot Bengals are in danger on 'Sunday Night Football'
summary: Pittsburgh's rest advantage and formidable defense could end Cincinnati's winning streak, while Kirk Cousins gives Minnesota new life against Green Bay
full_text:
It was a bad week to be an underdog in the NFL . Over the course of the Week 9 slate, favorites went 14-1 straight-up, with the lone upset coming from the Packers as they took down the Patriots in Foxborough.
Naturally, with favorites dominating the day, it wasn't a banner showing from us in last week's column. That said, we did correctly pinpoint New England as a prime upset candidate to Green Bay, so we'll take the win when we can get it.
With favorites finding so much success last week, however, it should heighten their concern heading into Week 10, as the pendulum could swing in the other direction to even things up. And there are several games to choose from this weekend for potential upsets, including a "Sunday Night Football" showdown between two AFC North rivals. So, let's get right to it and identify five favorites who are on upset alert.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The last time these two NFC East rivals faced one another, it was a calamity that resulted in a 27-27 tie. That said, I do think Washington is catching New York at the right time in this Thursday night matchup to begin Week 10.
Giants starter J.J. McCarthy was in and out of the lineup last week after suffering a hip pointer injury against the Eagles , but is expected to play in this game. Before going down, McCarthy seemed more like his Minnesota self than the quarterback who completed 20-of-28 in a win over the Texans before their bye. McCarthy threw for 127 yards on 12-of-19 passing in the win over Philly, with his yards per attempt (6.7) taking a noticeable dip from his first two appearances. He also took five sacks.
If that continues on Thursday against a Commanders defense that is allowing just 15.0 points per game over the past two games, Washington's offense may not have to do too much heavy lifting. Meanwhile, Jayden Daniels has largely had success against New York, coming into this game with a 3-0-1 record against his division foe. He's also totaled five touchdowns and zero turnovers in those games. Daniels has largely protected the ball this season as well and has yet to throw an interception.
So, the recipe for Washington here is for Daniels to keep a clean sheet in the turnover margin, and for McCarthy to come back down to earth.
Maybe a trip across the Atlantic snaps the Patriots back into form after an abysmal loss to the Packers at home in Week 9. One of the biggest issues for New England's offense this season has been turnovers, committing one on 19.4% of drives. While that's hardly going to instill much confidence in anyone backing the Patriots in Week 10, it is worth noting that Detroit hasn't exactly been known to create turnovers on defense. Entering this international game in Germany, the Lions have eight turnovers this season, which is tied for the fourth-fewest in the NFL. When you compare that to Green Bay's 19 total turnovers (second-best), the Patriots should get some reprieve in that department.
Meanwhile, Jared Goff hasn't looked as lights-out as he did over the first five games of the season when he was an early MVP candidate. Even amid this winning streak, Goff's numbers have dipped.
He's still playing at a high level, but it's not otherworldly, which could help New England's defense -- particularly the secondary --  put together a bounce-back performance.
Minnesota has the disadvantage of being on the road against a division rival and being on a short week after playing on Monday night, but they do get a huge boost on offense for this game. Before Tuesday's trade deadline, the Vikings pulled off a trade to acquire Kirk Cousins from the Raiders , which should elevate the offense to a more respectable level.
Coming into the week and pre-Cousins, Minnesota ranks 31st in passing yards per game (160.8) and is tied with the winless Chargers for the fewest offensive touchdowns (11) in the NFL this season. Despite all that, they're 6-2, which is thanks to their top-flight defense. Now that they have an offense that can not only complement them, but sustain drives to give them more rest on the sideline, Minnesota should be taken more seriously.
The defense will have its hands full against Green Bay's prolific passing attack, but they do have the personnel to contain them. That's especially true in the aftermath of Josh Jacobs (broken finger) being ruled out for this game, further limiting an already anemic ground game.
The Packers have also struggled in this spot. The club is 1-5 in its past six games against division opponents (including playoffs) and are 1-8 in its last nine games against teams entering the matchup four or more games over .500.
With the shot in the arm on offense with Cousins' arrival, the Vikings are live at Lambeau.
Carolina is in the midst of a three-game losing streak, which has brought Bryce Young's play into focus. Over the last three games, the Panthers quarterback has averaged 216 passing yards per game, has five passing touchdowns and four interceptions. While that's not great, context is key. Young and the Panthers have squared off against the Buccaneers , Packers (road), and Broncos during the skid, all of which are among the top defenses in the league right now. New Orleans is not that.
The Saints secondary has allowed 7.3 yards per attempt so far this season (tied for the fifth-highest in the league) along with a 99.5 passer rating allowed (seventh-highest). Meanwhile, Young was solid last week, albeit in defeat. He completed 71.7% of his throws for 276 yards, three touchdowns and a pick. That output should hold up against a weaker defense in New Orleans and should help propel them to snap the losing streak.
That's especially true considering the Saints haven't been a strong team at home so far in 2026. At the Superdome, they are 1-4 and have yet to cover (0-5 ATS).
Whoever constructed the schedule this year did the Bengals dirty for this Week 10 matchup. Not only are they returning from an international game in Madrid last week, but they are hosting a Steelers club that was on the bye in Week 9. That's a massive rest disadvantage for Cincinnati, which could rear its head in this matchup.
So far, Joe Burrow has been the talk of the NFL as he's leaped to the top of the MVP conversation after a sensational run over the Bengals' four-game winning streak. He has the offense averaging over 35 points per game and has 18 total touchdowns with a 132.0 passer rating. While those are video-game-like numbers, the competition he's been slicing up hasn't exactly been the Legion of Boom. Over the streak, Cincinnati has beaten up on the Dolphins , Ravens (no Lamar Jackson ), Titans and Falcons .
The Steelers pose a much tougher challenge, especially on defense. Pittsburgh is tied for the fifth-lowest yards per play average (5.0), tied for the fourth-lowest points per game allowed (18.0), and tied for the eighth-lowest passer rating allowed (83.3).
Since 2020, the Steelers have also won and covered in each of their six games coming off the bye.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Predicting full 14-team NFL playoff bracket after trade deadline: Entire NFC North makes postseason
summary: For the first time in NFL history, all four teams from the same division make it to the postseason, and one team makes a run
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline was Tuesday, and no one made a bigger move than the Minnesota Vikings . With their season hanging in the balance, the Vikings decided to make a trade for Kirk Cousins .
Thanks to the move, the Vikings are expected to coast into the playoffs along with EVERY OTHER TEAM in the NFC North. That's right, in our latest projection, we have all four NFC North teams making the postseason. If that happens, it would mark the first time in NFL history that a division has sent all four of its teams to the playoffs in one season.
So who else is projected to get in? Glad you asked.
To help us figure that out, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. There are 136 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project all eight division winners and the 14 playoff teams, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.
With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.
The AFC playoff picture is starting to take shape, and based on our projection, it's starting to feel like the playoff teams in this conference are almost locked in at this point. For the second straight week, not only does our projection have the same seven teams making the playoffs, but they're all seeded in the exact same spot.
Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. Bills (7-1) -- AFC East champion 2. Jaguars (6-2) -- AFC South champion 3. Broncos (7-2) -- AFC West champion 4. Bengals (6-2) -- AFC North champion 5. Chiefs (6-2) 6. Steelers (6-2) 7. Patriots (5-4) JUST MISSED: Texans (3-5), Browns (5-4)
According to our projection, the only real battle will be for the seventh seed. We have the Patriots projected to get the spot right now, but the Texans are nipping at their heels. We have both teams projected to finish the season at 9-8, but the Patriots are sneaking in thanks to a better conference record.
The good news for the Vikings is that adding Kirk Cousins does help: They're now projected to finish with 11 wins — compared to 10 without Cousins — but the problem is that 11 wins won't help them win the division. According to our projection, the Vikings are going to finish THIRD in the NFC North, but that will still be enough to get them in the postseason.
Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record): 1. 49ers (7-1) -- NFC West champion 2. Lions (6-2) -- NFC North champion 3. Giants (5-2-1) -- NFC East champion 4. Buccaneers (3-6) -- NFC South champion 5. Bears (7-2) 6. Vikings (6-2) 7. Packers (6-3) JUST MISSED: Seahawks (5-4), Rams (5-4)
For the first time all season, our model is projecting ALL FOUR NFC North teams to make the playoffs. At this point, it feels like the only way that's not going to happen is if the Rams or Seahawks get to 11 wins, but our computer doesn't see that happening.
Having all four teams from a single division make the postseason in the same year wasn't possible until 2020, when the NFL expanded the playoffs to 14 teams. Since then, there have been several instances where a division has put three teams in, but we still haven't seen a division put all four of its teams in, so this could be a history-making season.
AFC breakdown: Homefield advantage ends up being an actual advantage here, with all three home teams winning in the opening round. With the Patriots and Chiefs going out, they would eliminate the two teams that have represented the AFC in eight of the past nine Super Bowls.
NFC breakdown: The NFC North has been the best division in football all year, and the division makes a statement in the wild-card round by producing three winners. If this happens, we'd get a rarity: The NFC North would become just the fifth division in NFL history to send three teams to the divisional round.
AFC breakdown: If our projection proves correct, earning home-field advantage could be a big deal in the AFC. After watching the home teams sweep through the wild-card round, the run continues with Buffalo and Jacksonville both winning at home. With the win, the Bills advance to their third AFC title game since 2020 while the Jaguars make a return trip to the AFC Championship for the first time since 2017.
NFC breakdown: The Lions beat an NFC North team in the wild-card round, and they continue their postseason run by beating another NFC North team in the divisional round. As for the 49ers, Kyle Shanahan figures out a way to get his offense going against Minnesota's tough defense, propelling his team to a win. This sets up a rematch of the 2023 NFC title game between the Lions and 49ers.
If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Three teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills, Jaguars and Lions) and one team that hasn't won a Super Bowl in over 30 years (the 49ers' last title came in 1994)
We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at the projected Super Bowl each week.
As you can see, the computer has really taken a liking to the Bills, as this marks the third straight week Buffalo is projected to win the Super Bowl. Scratch that, the computer actually loves the Bills: Buffalo has a 16.94% chance of winning it all, which is a huge number when you consider there's only one other team that's even above 10% (the Jaguars are at 10.74%).

title: Former Cardinals great receiver Frank Sanders discusses today’s team
summary: Things aren’t exactly going the way the Arizona Cardinals drew it up before the season began. They are 3-6-0, which means they have equaled last year’s win total. So, there’s that. But injuries have turned this roster from promising to hemorrhaging. This weekend, the offense will start their third quarterback. RELATED: CARDINALS HISTORY: THE RECEIVERS […]
full_text: 8 Oct 2000: Frank Sanders #81 of the Arizona Cardinals races while holding the ball during the game against the Cleveland Browns at the Sun Devil Stadium in Phoenix, Arizona. The Cardinals defeated the Browns 29-21.Mandatory Credit: Donald Miralle /Allsport | Getty Images Things aren’t exactly going the way the Arizona Cardinals drew it up before the season began. They are 3-6-0, which means they have equaled last year’s win total. So, there’s that. But injuries have turned this roster from promising to hemorrhaging. This weekend, the offense will start their third quarterback. RELATED: CARDINALS HISTORY: THE RECEIVERS SINCE 1988 Is this year’s team improving, or imploding? So far, nobody in the media is discussing whether head coach Mike LaFleur should be on the hot seat. He isn’t. And shouldn’t. LaFleur came from successful franchises that know how to win. This just doesn’t happen overnight. You don’t go from driving an F-150 to a Peterbilt 589 with peak torque of 1,450 and 605 HP. And then there is the attrition problem. Last year, it was a laundry list of starters. The same thing is starting to appear this season as well. What is most troublesome is how many are listed at a key position: OT Paris Johnson, WRs Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, and Jalen Brooks, OG Chase Bisontis, QB Gardner Minshew, CB Will Johnson and S Joey Blount, RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner, plus DL Kaleb Proctor and Zachary Carter. 15 players in all. Many can wonder what a full season would be like if you took all of the injured and had them playing instead. Suiting up just the Johnsons – Paris and Will – would change a lot of things on both sides of the ball in every contest. So, what does an insider think of this year’s effort? Former Cardinals WR Frank Sanders was recently interviewed by Cardinals Insider Kyle Odegard. Part of the conversation circled back to this year’s roster. From a former player’s standpoint, what is going on? Odegard wanted to know if Sanders thought maybe LaFleur is out of his league and a bit overwhelmed from being just an OC. Sanders stated: “I love what he’s doing. I love how he’s handling the program, especially considering it’s not one of the easiest programs to run in the National Football League. For a coach coming in that did not bring anybody in, he’s picked up a lot of pieces that were not his pieces. I think he’s done a wonderful job.” It’s one thing to be responsible for the offense and all of those job duties during the week. But LaFleur has to make certain that the defense and special teams are on point every week as well. Preparation is super key going into a game. And Arizona isn’t in some quasi-easy division such as the NFC South where no team is even at .500 yet. The Cardinals would be tied for first place if they were allowed to relocate. Sanders likes what he is seeing from the newbie head coach: “His attitude is on point, his play-calling is solid. I like what he’s doing. Sometimes we just don’t have the athletes to compete.” What a true observation: “just don’t have the athletes to compete.” But with the Cardinals, they just might have all the players and a solid roster. The problem is, a ton of them are gone for the season due to injury. Who projected the third overall draft pick to have ankle problems when he has been durable ever since high school? How do three receivers end up all hurt and gone for the year? A kid drafted high in the draft to come in and cement the guard position and then is out. A drafted defensive tackle that never even saw the field? LINK: ODEGARD’S FULL INTERVIEW WITH SANDERS Odegard shifted his interview and then focused on the team shipping off starting QB Jacoby Brissett, and now the rookie Carson Beck will be given an opportunity to show he belongs. Sanders had his take: “I think (Brissett) will do a wonderful job. You just need players around him. Jacoby doesn’t need a whole bunch of help, but he needs some help. He’s in a solid organization. ” And Beck? “(A team) still needs depth at quarterback. You still need healthy competition. And you need somebody you can rest your hat on. You need some form of stability in that area.” A lot of media outlets have indicated that the Cardinals will need to play Beck in several games in order to get a complete evaluation to see if he is indeed their QB going forward. Sanders doesn’t see that as a necessity. “Winning is the most important part, and (developing) the offense is just as important. For me to be worried about Carson playing? No. I don’t have to see him for another two or three years if Gardner can be that guy. If he can’t? Then we have to make a decision.” Sanders views Minshew as a solid quarterback who might be the better option as Beck develops. He stated he would stick with Minshew indefinitely. “If Gardner Minshew can play okay. I don’t want to see (Beck). I just want to see someone who can get the job done.” For the present, Sanders said he prioritizes winning and developing LaFleur’s offense. After all, it is a new system. Once the offensive line gels, their key receivers and tight ends get back healthy, and the defense gets a few new bodies, this team is being built to compete within the division where all the big boys play. Sanders was a second-round selection of the Cardinals in the 1995 NFL Draft after he was a First-Team All-American and First-Team All-SEC out of Auburn. He played nine seasons in the NFL, eight of which were with Arizona wearing jersey #81. He finished his career playing in 136 NFL games with 120 starts, with 6,749 yards and 24 touchdowns, and a 13.3-yard-per-reception average. In 2013, Sanders was inducted into the “SEC Football Legends.”

title: The one thing the Cardinals and Rams have that no other NFL clubs hold
summary: The National Football League is a collection of sorts. It is comprised of two charter members, nine expansion clubs, and 14 franchises that started in another pro football league, while the remaining teams joined at various intervals or took over an existing franchise. It is now 32 clubs, all wrapped up very tidily into two […]
full_text: 1960: QB Bart Starr #15 quarterback of the Green Bay Packers against the St. Louis Cardinals (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images The National Football League is a collection of sorts. It is comprised of two charter members, nine expansion clubs, and 14 franchises that started in another pro football league, while the remaining teams joined at various intervals or took over an existing franchise. It is now 32 clubs, all wrapped up very tidily into two conferences with four divisions, which house four teams within each division. RELATED: WHEN THE CARDINALS ALMOST MOVED TO EVANSTON, ILLINOIS The Arizona Cardinals are the second oldest pro football team in North America behind the Toronto Argonauts, and the oldest continuous NFL franchise. The team began as a local Chicago entity in an athletic club (now referred to as gyms). The Cardinals play the Los Angeles Rams this weekend, which are both members of the NFC West Division, one of the league’s most competitive. Arizona won their first match 18-16 in Week 6. The Cardinals and the Rams have something in common that no other clubs share: They both called St. Louis, Missouri, home at some juncture, and each team consequently left this Midwestern city for greener pastures. No other NFL club can hold this distinction. Just the Cardinals and the Rams. From Chicago to St. Louis The Cardinals began in 1898 as a gym team in Chicago off of Racine Street, which runs north and south and ends near the Little Calumet River and dumps into Lake Michigan. It is definitely South Chicago. At the time, the game of American Football was in its infancy. The game was mainly inside runs and a lot of violence. The forward pass wasn’t even legal until l906, so the term “three yards and a cloud of dust” originated from this time period. These athletic clubs served men who wanted to remain in shape and still compete in sports. So after a hard day in the courtroom, the pharmacy, the butcher shop, or construction, men would go to their local gym and work out, box, swim, lift weights, and do other assorted physical activities before they headed home. Almost every gym had a baseball team and played against other athletic clubs. And because Chicago was so large, there were so many teams that were either formed in the local athletic clubs or were formed as neighborhood teams. During this time period, everyone loved baseball, everyone played baseball as a kid, and everyone went to see the hometown Cubs or White Sox. This union of playing other neighborhood baseball teams became the basis of a loose entity commonly called the “Chicago Football League” once the sport of American Football began to take hold. It was a sport for the more rugged individual, the ones who liked contact and wanted to do a bit more athletically than stroke a ball and run bases. Over the years, this league saw around 150 teams come and go and had different divisions based on the weight of their roster members, similar to what boxing offers. Coming from athletic clubs, this made sense. Because this athletic club had a baseball team, they now offered a football team. And the same opponents each club or neighborhood had already been playing made scheduling games easier. Local house painter Chris O’Brien and his brother Pat formed the “Morgan Athletic Club” football team. They played their games at a nearby private park called “Normal Park,” which had wooden bleachers built for baseball games. It was just a matter of stripping off a gridiron for football contests. Because it wasn’t a city-owned facility, O’Brien could charge admission. The majority of these teams were named after streets, gyms, or neighborhoods, such as the Standards, Alpins, Cornell Athletic Club, the Ripmores, the Hamburgs, Ragen’s Colts, the Friars, the Iroquois Athletic Club, and the Young Royals, to name a few. The O’Brien’s team was often referred to as “The Morgans.” They then became known as the “Racine Normals,” which designated a street and ballpark. At some point, nearby University of Chicago Maroons were buying new uniforms for their football squad, and O’Brien offered to purchase the outgoing unies. He mentioned that the maroon uniforms were now faded a bit, and he called them “Cardinal red.” So, beginning in 1901, the Normals became the “Racine Cardinals.” When the NFL began in 1920 as the “American Professional Football Association,” there were 19 clubs, all in the Midwest and along the Eastern Seaboard. As O’Brien was about to enter his Cardinals into this new venture, there was another team from Racine, Wisconsin, called the “Racine Legion.” To avoid confusion, O’Brien changed his club’s moniker to the “Chicago Cardinals.” The Cardinals were purchased by Dr. David Jones in 1929, who sold the team to Charlie “Blue Shirt” Bidwill in 1932 on Bidwill’s fancy yacht. After Bidwill passed away prior to the 1947 NFL season, in which the Cardinals won the league championship, his wife Violet took over ownership. She remarried several years later to Walter Wolfner, who was a St. Louis businessman and became the team’s managing director. In 1954, Wolfner organized an annual preseason game for the Cardinals to be played in St. Louis called the “Cardinal Glennon Charity Game,” which benefited Cardinal Glennon Children’s Hospital and remained a staple of the team’s preseason schedule for over two decades. In 1958, Texas oilman Lamar Hunt tried to buy the Cardinals and relocate the team to his hometown of Dallas. The next year, the Wolfners offered Hunt a 20% stake in the franchise, but the team would remain in Chicago. Instead, Hunt formed the “American Football League” and placed his own team in Dallas. Later, this team relocated to Missouri and became the “Kansas City Chiefs.” The Cardinals played their home games at Comiskey Park, home of the White Sox on Chicago’s south side. It was built in 1909 for baseball games, and by the late 1950s needed a lot of work and enhancements. The White Sox owned the park and balked at expensive repairs and upgrades, so Wolfner looked at other stadium options. In the late 1950s, Wolfner mulled over his idea to seek out a new place for the Cardinals to play, and the franchise could make money and survive. He had roots in St. Louis, where he made his fortune as a coffee broker. All Violet had known was Chicago, and she didn’t want to move anywhere. Dyche Stadium on the campus of Northwestern University had been recently renovated. The advantage of this venue is that it did not have a track that went around the football field, which moved the seats up closer to the action. The university was just 33 minutes north of downtown Chicago. An agreement was made with Northwestern to house the Cardinals on Sundays. However, a document called the “Madison Street Agreement” prevented the move. This agreement was between the owner of the Chicago Bears, George Halas, and former Cardinals owners Dr. Jones and later Bidwill. The league stepped in and nixed the Cardinals move to Dyche Stadium. Because Wolfner had ties to St. Louis, there was an annual preseason game already in place, and the franchise’s inability to find a suitable place for home games, the team relocated to St. Louis beginning with the 1960 season and was christened the “St. Louis Cardinals.” Because there was already a baseball team with the same name, the gridiron team was often referred to as the “St. Louis Football Cardinals,” similar to the situation in New York City and the “New York Football Giants.” Both the baseball and football teams shared Busch Stadium. The Football Cardinals remained in St. Louis until 1987, when they relocated to Arizona and became the “Phoenix Cardinals.” From Los Angeles to St. Louis The Los Angeles Rams began as the Cleveland Rams in 1936, as the second entity named the “American Football League,” often referred to as AFL2. After this league folded, the Rams’ owners petitioned for membership in the NFL and began play in 1937. Cleveland won the NFL…

title: What to know about Falcons – Chiefs in Week 10
summary: The Atlanta Falcons are about to get their bye week, but they have to go through the Kansas City Chiefs first. The difference between rolling into the bye at 3-7 with the Vikings and Lions looming after it and being a 4-6 in the same boat is a potentially significant one, given that the NFC […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 22: Tyler Allgeier #25 of the Atlanta Falcons rushes against Felix Anudike-Uzomah #97 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons are about to get their bye week, but they have to go through the Kansas City Chiefs first. The difference between rolling into the bye at 3-7 with the Vikings and Lions looming after it and being a 4-6 in the same boat is a potentially significant one, given that the NFC South is extremely weak and Atlanta’s final five games are against the Browns, Commanders, and their division rivals. But winning this game is going to be difficult, and more difficult for trading away Jessie Bates. Can our beloved Falcons stop being so thoroughly mediocre and triumph over an AFC juggernaut? For better or worse, we’ll find out. Here’s what you need to know about the Week 10 matchup. Team rankings Team Record Points Scored Yardage Passing Yards Rushing Yards Points Against Yardage Against Passing Yards Against Rushing Yardage Against Turnovers Created Turnovers Surrendered Falcons 3-6 23 21 25 6 20 23 20 17 21 28 Chiefs 6-2 10 2 10 5 3 8 7 10 14 7 That’s a big gulf! The Falcons, by the eye test, the more advanced statistics, and the high level ones I share every week here, are a 3-6 football team that looks like a 3-6 football team. By all those same measures, the Chiefs are one of the ten best teams in football. If this isn’t an ass kicking—and especially if the Falcons actually win—it will be a real triumph. How the Chiefs have changed This team is a diminished version of the Chiefs that briefly ruled the NFL. That’s not to say that Kansas City is not still a contender—they are—or that they aren’t still one of the best teams in the AFC. It is to say that they’re no longer a juggernaut. They did re-imagine the offense by signing Kenneth Walker to a massive free agency deal, and Walker’s been one of the handful of great running backs in the league this year. Before this, the Chiefs had relied on a hodgepodge of lackluster backs, so the lift he’s given them has helped offset a still-frustrating passing game. The team also acquired Justin Fields to back up Patrick Mahomes, and there’s a non-zero chance we’ll see Fields this week with Mahomes banged up. Eric Bieniemy is also back in the offensive coordinator role, and the offense has been noticeably better balanced than it has been in recent years. Their draft has delivered plenty of needed young talent, even if the production has been mixed to this point. Mansoor Delane looks excellent but has only appeared in five games, defensive linemen R Mason Thomas and Peter Woods have real promise even if Woods has largely struggled, Jadon Canady is providing surprisingly strong coverage at cornerback early in his career, and running back Emmett Johnson and wide receiver Cyrus Allen have produced in their limited opportunities to this point. It’s a good class that could pay real dividends down the line. Finally, the Chiefs made a bit of a splash trade, grabbing wide receiver Josh Downs from the selling Colts. Downs is not a standout but has been a consistently productive player on some lousy Colts teams, and is now joining up as a clear top option for Mahomes once he gets his feet under him in Kansas City. Generally, though, you know what this Chiefs team looks like. Andy Reid is the coach, Mahomes is the quarterback, the receivers are all varying degrees of frustrating, and stalwarts like Travis Kelce and Chris Jones are still puttering along at an impressively high level. The Chiefs are still very good because of that, but they’re better health and more cohesion away from being a great team. What to know about Week 10 So much swings on whether the Falcons will see Patrick Mahomes or not. Justin Fields can kill Atlanta with his legs and avoids turnovers, but there’s a massive drop-off from Mahomes to him that will impact an already inconsistent Chiefs passing attack. That’s important because of what Joe Burrow and Caleb Williams have done to the Falcons’ secondary, which is now down a playmaking presence in Bates. Both quarterbacks annihilated Atlanta’s coverage with sharp ball placement, good throws on the move, and effective movement in the face of pressure, and Mahomes can manage all that. The chief (sorry) difference here is that while the Bengals have Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and the Bears brought Colston Loveland, Rome Odunze, and Luther Burden to bear (sorry again), the Chiefs have a much more lackluster collection of playmakers. Their most effective option by far is Rashee Rice, who is always seemingly banged up but is lethal over the middle of the field, and Travis Kelce remains a plodding but useful receiving threat. Downs is an intriguing new addition, but how much time he’ll see less than a week after being traded to Kansas City remains to be seen. If the Falcons can do a reasonable job of bottling those three up, Xavier Worthy is thoroughly mediocre and their fourth best receiving option is probably Walker, who is dangerous in the open field but not a threat downfield. I targeted the passing game first here because of the intrigue around Mahomes vs. Fields, but the single biggest threat in this game is Walker. The Falcons were eaten alive by the Bucccaneers ground game two weeks ago, and Walker is the most dangerous back they’ll face all season. He’s 7th in the NFL in success rate, second behind Bijan Robinson in rushing yards by a measly eight yards, has yet to fumble once, and is averaging more yards per game than any other back in football. Atlanta’s run defense has been exposed as a mediocre one over the past month, and the threat of the Chiefs simply running over this unit can’t be exaggerated. Walker may get 25 carries if he’s rolling, and if he’s rolling, the Falcons are in major trouble. Unfortunately for an Atlanta offense that has been a real puzzle box the past couple of weeks, the Kansas City defense is no pushover, either. They’re doing a nice job of limiting explosive plays and are top ten in counting stats, success rate, and EPA defensively against the pass and the run, underscoring how fundamentally sound they are. A sloppy version of this Falcons offense is going to run into trouble, and a sloppy version of this Falcons offense is all we’ve gotten lately. Your best bet is going to be to run outside where the Chiefs are marginally less stout, and I’m sure Bijan Robinson has no problem with that plan. If everyone’s blocking well, the Falcons should at least be able to get a toehold on the ground. Things through the air are going to be tougher. We don’t know how Corey Levin is going to hold up full-time as the starting center, but we do know it’s a tough matchup against this Kansas City interior, and that Michael Penix Jr. has both struggled under pressure and faced way too many quick pressures in recent weeks. The Chiefs have the talent at every level to punish Penix locked in on receivers, Levin struggling against pressure, and Atlanta’s pass catchers not getting separation. If the past two weeks of woes continue, this one could get out of hand. One item to watch this week if the game is close? Atlanta has a new kicker and the Chiefs are sticking with Harrison Butker, who has been abysmal this season. If Jake Moody can keep rolling, as he has over the past couple of seasons, and Butker struggles, a 3-6 point game could swing on kickers. Overall, though, I’m going to follow my own advice and urge you to do the same: Don’t expect the Falcons to win a game against a superior opponent, and hope for the best.
author: Dave Choate

title: AFC North Week 9 Recap: Joe Burrow strengthens MVP bid
summary: The AFC North standings did not change in Week 9, with only one team getting a win. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) The Steelers enjoyed their bye week at the top of the division. Pittsburgh will now have to defend first place when they return to action in Week 10 against the Bengals. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) Cincinnati […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Joe Burrow of Cincinnati Bengals looks on after the 2026 NFL Madrid Game match between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) | Getty Images The AFC North standings did not change in Week 9, with only one team getting a win. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) The Steelers enjoyed their bye week at the top of the division. Pittsburgh will now have to defend first place when they return to action in Week 10 against the Bengals. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) Cincinnati moved to 6-2 with a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Joe Burrow has firmly planted himself in the MVP race following another strong performance. Against the Falcons, Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns while adding another touchdown on the ground. Over his last four games, Burrow has accounted for 18 touchdowns. Ja’Marr Chase was Burrow’s leading receiver against Atlanta with 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown, while Tee Higgins had a pair of touchdowns to go with 32 yards on five catches. The Bengals defense did not record a sack on quarterback Michael Penix, but the unit did enough to hold the Falcons’ talented offense in check. Barrett Carter had the lone turnover of the game with an interception off Penix. Cincinnati will have the opportunity to challenge for the division lead now in Week 10. Cleveland Browns (5-4) The Browns dropped their second consecutive game with a 23-22 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Shedeur Sanders got the start at quarterback in place of the injured Deshaun Watson in Week 9. Sanders finished the game 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, with another 28 yards on 10 carries. Denzel Boston’s 98 receiving yards on six catches led the offense, while KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. were the recipients of Sanders’ touchdowns. Fannin’s touchdown was particularly impressive as he broke multiple tackles on his way to a 39-yard score in overtime. Cleveland went for the win with a two-point attempt, but Sanders was unable to connect with Boston on the play. The Browns’ defense racked up five sacks on Tyler Shough, with Carson Schwesinger and Myles Harden both finishing with two. Schwesinger had 15 total tackles while also forcing a fumble to go with his pair of sacks. Baltimore Ravens (4-5) The Ravens lost their fourth game in a row with a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano started the game at quarterback on a short week after both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley were injured in the previous game. Fagnano struggled as you would expect, completing 10 of 18 pass attempts for just 60 yards and a pair of interceptions. Justice Hill was the leading rusher with nine carries for 85 yards and a touchdown, with most of the work coming on a 65-yard score in the fourth quarter. Baltimore has since acquired veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, whom they hope can keep their season alive for a potential Jackson return down the road. The Ravens’ defense had a tough hill to climb with little to no help from their own offense, but the unit was supposed to be a strength of the team heading into the season. Instead, Baltimore’s defense has allowed over 30 points in three straight games.

full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon #99 of the Pittsburgh Steelers forces a fumble by quarterback Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game at Acrisure Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game win streak, having exceeded 30+ points in each game, the Bengals will return home for a primetime matchup with the Steelers. In Week 3, the Bengals suffered a 30-27 defeat against Pittsburgh and sit in second place now despite having the same record. Cincinnati’s passing attack has been firing on all cylinders recently and Joe Burrow is hitting his stride. Over the last four games, Burrow has 16 touchdown passes while averaging over 300 passing yards. The Steelers are a Top 3 defense against the run but rank middle-of-the-pack defending the pass. The Bengals continue to struggle running the ball effectively, so they’ll likely attack Pittsburgh’s secondary regularly. Elsewhere, the Bengals’ inconsistent run defense may be tested by Steelers’ rushing attack that has totaled 148 yards and 200 yards on the ground in back-to-back games. The Bengals will need to slow down Jaylen Warren in the backfield, who has been a star this season. If the Bengals can make the Steelers one dimensional offensively, they become a much more beatable team. Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 8:20pm EST Like their divisional counterpart, the Steelers have won their last four games to improve to 6-2, sitting atop the division by virtue of tiebreaker. Prior to last week’s bye break, the Steelers defeated the Browns handedly by 21 points, their most lopsided win of the season and only their second win by more than one possession. Pittsburgh’s momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers’ defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace. On offense, the Steelers continue to long for better production from their pass-catchers to help unlock more downfield plays. Warren has been the team’s only consistent playmaker and Rico Dowdle has ran well over the last two weeks in a complimentary role. However, D.K. Metcalf and company have been up-and-down in the passing game. In order to match Cincinnati’s high-flying offensive attack, the Steelers will likely need to hit on a few explosive passing plays. Cleveland Browns Matchup: vs. Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST The Browns have now lost back-to-back games and are looking to get back on track before their upcoming bye week. In Week 9, they allowed a winnable game to slip through their grasp against the Saints, where they lost by one point in overtime. Shedeur Sanders impressed in his spot-start for Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but the Browns still struggled to run the ball and didn’t start scoring much until the fourth quarter. Watson is set to return from injury to start this week versus his former team. The Texans have underwhelmed defensively this year but still have one of the league’s more talented defenses, which will pose a challenge for the Browns — whose offense has struggled mightily at times this season. Houston has been vulnerable in pass coverage, allowing over 235 passing yards per game, leaving some hope that Watson can hit a downfield shot or two. The Browns will need to connect on some type of explosive plays or find a way to run the ball more effectively. Defensively, the Browns will need to bring their A game, as the Texans have prolific offensively at times in recent weeks. Last Sunday, they scored 44 points and C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes with nearly 400 passing yards. The Browns may be able to afford to sell out against the pass rather than the run, as the Texans rank even worse running the ball than they do. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: vs. Los Angeles Chargers, 8:15pm EST The Ravens were thrashed by the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday night, losing by 20+ points for the third straight game. Baltimore’s offense struggles hit a new low, as the team scored 10 points, gained 10 first downs and totaled just over 200 yards. With a hobbled third-string quarterback under center, the Ravens were no match for a talented Jaguars’ squad. Fortunately, they will get the ultimate potential get-right matchup this coming Monday, taking on a winless Chargers team that is in disarray. Hopes for a potential offensive turnaround lie with new incoming quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens traded for after Week 9. Brissett should provide a significant upgrade over Joe Fagnano as an experienced veteran who has proven, at the bare minimum, he can lead scoring drives and operate an offense at a competent level. Even with Brissett now under center, the Ravens need more consistency from their offensive line and breakthrough performances from veterans like Mark Andrews, Ronnie Stanley and Derrick Henry. Defensively, the Ravens have given up 30+ points in three straight weeks to three of the best offenses and quarterbacks in the NFL. They’ve played good halves and quarters, but the lows have been low. Coverage breakdowns and lack of impact pass rush continue to plague them. If there were ever a spot to have a convincing performance and force turnovers, this would be it. Chargers’ quarterback Justin Herbert leads all quarterbacks in interceptions this season.

It’s safe to say that football fans have had their fill of these teams, of the NFC East, and the NFC in general. At least Week 10 gives us two AFC showdowns. The trouble is that the one on Monday night is about as bad as it gets. There aren’t any rooting interests here as it relates to the Buffalo Bills. You might find yourself cheering for the Commanders just to hand the Giants a loss, or at least see them make good on their horrible decisions that led to the tie in the previous matchup. Depending on how far back your Bills fandom goes, you may find it impossible rooting for an NFC East team (except when they face the New England Patriots, and probably the Kansas City Chiefs). There’s a lot of bad football being trotted out to the masses this season. but this is what you get tonight and you’re probably watching until the end. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 10 of Thursday Night Football. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!
