title: NFL Week 10 power rankings: Bills finally earn one outlet’s respect, but where do the Jets land?
summary: The Buffalo Bills continue to win, and most national analysts agree they’re the team to beat. Following their convincing 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football, Buffalo enters Week 10 ranked No. 1 in five of the eight national power rankings we’ve been tracking throughout the season. The Bills have an average […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills continue to win, and most national analysts agree they’re the team to beat. Following their convincing 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football, Buffalo enters Week 10 ranked No. 1 in five of the eight national power rankings we’ve been tracking throughout the season. The Bills have an average ranking of 1.50, a slight improvement from 1.63 entering Week 9. Their next opponent, the New York Jets, sits near the opposite end of the rankings with an average of 29.00. While most outlets have remained consistent in their assessment of Buffalo, two publications made particularly interesting moves this week. USA Today finally gave the Bills some credit, while Sports Illustrated dropped them two spots despite another convincing victory. Five outlets agree: Buffalo belongs at No. 1 ESPN, CBS Sports, The Athletic, FOX Sports, and Pro Football Talk all rank Buffalo first heading into Week 10. The Bills have now delivered consecutive impressive defensive performances, defeating Baltimore 36-10 before holding Minnesota to just six points. It’s the kind of complementary football Bills fans have been waiting to see. For much of the season, Buffalo’s offense has been expected to compensate for defensive inconsistencies. Over the past two games, however, the defense has demonstrated it can contribute to victories without requiring Josh Allen and the offense to be nearly perfect. Whether that improvement continues against stronger offenses remains to be seen, but the results are encouraging. USA Today finally starts showing Buffalo some respect After weeks of being one of the biggest outliers, USA Today is finally bringing its assessment of the Bills closer to the national consensus. Of all eight outlets, USA Today has consistently been one of the toughest on Buffalo. While several national publications have kept the Bills at or near the top of their rankings, USA Today previously placed Buffalo considerably further down the list. That assessment has gradually started changing. Entering Week 8, USA Today ranked Buffalo ninth. The Bills climbed to sixth heading into Week 9, and following their victory over Minnesota, they jumped another four spots to second. The question now is whether Buffalo can maintain that confidence as the schedule progresses. Sports Illustrated drops Buffalo despite another convincing victory On the opposite end of this week’s movement is Sports Illustrated. Conor Orr dropped Buffalo from No. 1 to No. 3 following its victory over Minnesota, making Sports Illustrated the lowest of our eight rankings for the Bills. What’s particularly interesting is that Orr didn’t criticize Buffalo’s performance. In fact, his assessment of the Bills’ victory was positive, recognizing their ability to wear down Minnesota’s defense and control a difficult matchup. Instead, Orr’s introduction to his Week 10 rankings focused heavily on teams demonstrating urgency and aggression in their pursuit of a championship. He specifically highlighted Jacksonville’s aggressive approach to improving its roster and Chicago’s commitment to building a contender. Jacksonville moved from third to first, Chicago remained second, and Buffalo dropped to third. Orr never explicitly stated that Buffalo deserved to fall two positions. Based on his explanation of the rankings, however, the movement appears to be more about rewarding other contenders than penalizing the Bills for anything they did against Minnesota. It’s an interesting approach, but power rankings are subjective, and this week’s Sports Illustrated rankings demonstrate just how differently analysts can evaluate the same team. The Jets remain near the bottom While Buffalo continues competing for the top spot, the New York Jets are heading in the opposite direction. The Jets enter their Week 10 matchup with Buffalo at 2-7 following a 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Across our eight sources, New York ranks between No. 26 and No. 31, with an average ranking of 29.00. CBS Sports is the most generous, placing the Jets at No. 26. FOX Sports and Pro Football Talk rank them No. 31. NFL.com dropped New York from 29th to 30th, while Sports Illustrated moved the Jets from 28th to 30th. The Jets have struggled to establish consistency on either side of the football, and their four-game losing streak hasn’t given national analysts much reason to reconsider their evaluations. For Buffalo, Sunday’s matchup provides another opportunity to build momentum against an AFC East opponent. But the Bills have already learned this season that divisional matchups shouldn’t be taken lightly. Their lone loss came against the New England Patriots, another division rival, and the Jets will have an opportunity to disrupt Buffalo’s momentum regardless of where the national rankings place them. Final thoughts The Bills have demonstrated they can win games with explosive offensive performances, sustained rushing attacks, and, more recently, dominant defensive efforts. After spending much of the season watching Buffalo’s offense overcome defensive shortcomings, it’s difficult to dismiss consecutive performances in which the defense allowed just 10 points to Baltimore and six to Minnesota. The bigger test will be whether that level of play continues against more productive offenses. Now they need to prove those performances are sustainable. Heading into Week 10 against the Jets, Buffalo has an opportunity to reinforce its position among the NFL’s elite while continuing to build confidence in a defense that has finally started making its presence felt. The rankings may not be unanimous, but the Bills are giving analysts fewer reasons to question whether they belong at the top.
author: Sara Larson

title: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has history with Jets coaches
summary: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets meet Sunday for another round of their twice-a-year AFC East rivalry, and recent history has been pretty kind to Buffalo.  The Bills lead the all-time series 73-58, have won five straight against New York and own a 10-2 record against the Jets since 2020. Buffalo has also kept […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets meet Sunday for another round of their twice-a-year AFC East rivalry, and recent history has been pretty kind to Buffalo. The Bills lead the all-time series 73-58, have won five straight against New York and own a 10-2 record against the Jets since 2020. Buffalo has also kept New York out of the end zone on its opening drive in each of their last 25 meetings. It’s been a while since the Jets have given Bills fans much reason to worry. Of course, when two teams have been playing each other twice a year for decades, there’s only so much history we can dig up before we start telling the same stories. And while we’re always happy to revisit a good Bills win, even our Time Capsule could use a change of scenery. Head coach Aaron Glenn, defensive coordinator Brian Duker and offensive coordinator Frank Reich all have some history with Buffalo. They’ve faced Allen, coached against the Bills and, in Reich’s case, even worn a Buffalo uniform. Glenn already has a season with the Jets under his belt, while Duker and Reich are getting their first taste of this rivalry from New York’s sideline. But none of them is a stranger to Buffalo, and their previous encounters give us a few interesting games to revisit. _____________________________________________________________________________ Aaron Glenn has seen plenty of Josh Allen Aaron Glenn is in his second season as the Jets’ head coach, but his history with Josh Allen goes back to his four seasons as defensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions. And if Glenn was hoping a change of teams would make Allen any easier to deal with, the results so far haven’t offered much encouragement. The two first met on Thanksgiving Day in 2022, when Buffalo traveled to Detroit and came away with a 28-25 victory. Allen threw for 253 yards and two touchdowns, added another 78 yards and a touchdown on the ground, and helped set up Tyler Bass’s game-winning field goal with a 36-yard completion to Stefon Diggs in the final seconds. Their next meeting came in December 2024, and this time Glenn had one of the NFL’s best teams behind him. Detroit entered the game at 12-1, riding an 11-game winning streak and looking every bit like a Super Bowl contender. But Allen wasn’t particularly impressed. He threw for 362 yards and two touchdowns while adding 68 rushing yards and two more scores in Buffalo’s 48-42 win. The Lions failed to sack him, and the Bills piled up 559 yards of total offense. That gave Allen 761 combined passing and rushing yards and seven total touchdowns in two games against Glenn’s Detroit defenses, with the Bills winning both. Glenn got another opportunity when he took over as head coach of the Jets in 2025. Buffalo won their first meeting that September, 30-10, although Allen’s numbers were considerably quieter. He threw for 148 yards, rushed for 59 and didn’t account for a touchdown. The Bills didn’t need a big afternoon from their quarterback to take care of business. Allen sat out the regular-season finale against New York, which Buffalo won 35-8, leaving Glenn still looking for his first victory against Allen as a head coach or defensive coordinator. Three meetings, four if you count Allen handing the ball to James Cook to get his name in the books last January, three (four) Buffalo wins. Glenn has seen Allen put up big numbers, and he’s seen the Bills win without needing him to. Neither scenario has worked particularly well for the Jets’ head coach. _____________________________________________________________________________ Brian Duker knows Josh Allen, too If Aaron Glenn was hoping to find someone who could help him figure out Josh Allen, he certainly didn’t have to spend much time explaining the problem to his new defensive coordinator. Brian Duker worked alongside Glenn in Detroit from 2021 through 2023, serving as the Lions’ safeties coach in 2022 before moving into the defensive backs role in 2023. That means Duker was also on the sideline for Buffalo’s Thanksgiving victory in Detroit, when Allen accounted for three touchdowns and led the Bills to a 28-25 win. But Duker’s experience against Allen doesn’t end there. He spent the next two seasons with the Miami Dolphins as their pass game coordinator and secondary coach, giving him four more opportunities to face Buffalo’s quarterback. The first came in September 2024, when Buffalo rolled to a 31-10 victory in Miami. Allen threw for just 139 yards and one touchdown, but with James Cook scoring three times and the Bills’ defense giving Tua Tagovailoa fits, there wasn’t much reason to ask Allen to do more. The rematch in November was a different story. Allen threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns as Buffalo needed a 61-yard field goal from Bass in the closing seconds to escape with a 30-27 victory. Duker got two more chances in 2025, and this time the Dolphins managed to split the series. Allen threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns in Buffalo’s 31-21 September win, then added 306 passing yards and two touchdowns in the November rematch. But Miami came away with a 30-13 victory, giving Duker something Glenn hasn’t managed in his previous meetings with Allen — a win. Across those four games against Miami’s secondary, Allen completed 93 of 127 passes for 893 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions. Buffalo won three of the four. Now Duker is back alongside Glenn, this time with the title of defensive coordinator. Glenn is handling the defensive play-calling, but Duker brings two seasons of experience preparing Miami’s secondary to face Allen twice a year. Between the two coaches, there’s no shortage of familiarity with Buffalo’s quarterback. Whether that familiarity actually helps them stop him is another question. _____________________________________________________________________________ Frank Reich returns to a familiar rivalry For longtime Bills fans, Frank Reich is a name that needs little introduction. Before Josh Allen was making a habit of pulling off the seemingly impossible, Reich was the quarterback behind one of the greatest comebacks in NFL history. Reich spent 10 seasons in Buffalo as Jim Kelly’s backup, playing a role in the Bills’ four consecutive Super Bowl appearances. But it was January 1993 that secured his place in Buffalo history. With Kelly injured and the Bills trailing the Houston Oilers 35-3 in the third quarter of the Wild Card playoff game, Reich led Buffalo all the way back for a 41-38 overtime win. It’s a game that Bills fans haven’t forgotten, and one that still comes up whenever Buffalo finds itself facing a seemingly impossible deficit. Reich’s playing career eventually took him to New York, where he spent the 1996 season with the Jets. Among his teammates that year was a young cornerback named Aaron Glenn. Thirty years later, the two are reunited, this time with Glenn as head coach and Reich running the Jets’ offense. And unlike Glenn and Duker, Reich isn’t trying to figure out how to stop Josh Allen. His job is to put together an offense capable of keeping up with him, something he’s had some success doing against Buffalo in the past. As head coach of the Indianapolis Colts, Reich faced the Bills three times, including once in the playoffs. His first meeting came in October 2018, when Indianapolis handed Buffalo a 37-5 loss. Of course, Allen was sidelined with an elbow injury for that game, and it was Derek Anderson under center for the Bills. Their next meeting came in January 2021, when Allen and the Bills defeated Reich’s Colts 27-24 in the AFC Wild Card round. Indianapolis put up 472 yards of offense that afternoon, but Buffalo held on for its first playoff victory in 25 years. Reich got some revenge the following November, when the Colts traveled to Buffalo and handed the Bills a 41-15 defeat. Jonathan Taylor ran for 185 yards and four touchdowns, caught another touchdown pass and accounted for five of Indianapolis’ six trips to the end zone. The Colts finished with 370 yards…
author: Rachel Auberger

title: How Amani Hooker fits in Jim Leonhard’s defense alongside Cole Bishop
summary: The Buffalo Bills have a new safety — Amani Hooker. You may have heard. And if you’re wondering how he’ll be deployed in Jim Leonhard’s defense, this article has you covered. Up front, Hooker is at his best in a deep-coverage role. Of course, in the modern NFL, he’s played everywhere in the back seven. […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills have a new safety — Amani Hooker. You may have heard. And if you’re wondering how he’ll be deployed in Jim Leonhard’s defense, this article has you covered. Up front, Hooker is at his best in a deep-coverage role. Of course, in the modern NFL, he’s played everywhere in the back seven. But the film and numbers suggest he’s the most impactful when he can process route concepts, check the quarterback, and range to the football. On 1,172 snaps across the 2020 and 2021 campaigns — his second and third in the NFL — Hooker played 717 snaps as a free safety (61.1%) and rewarded the Titans with a total of five interceptions and 12 pass breakups in 28 games. In those years, Hooker averaged just under 42 snaps per contest. In 2024, when Hooker had five interceptions, he aligned at free safety on 55.9% of his snaps. On this note, here’s how Cole Bishop and Hooker compare in snaps by specific position to date in their NFL careers. Now I think it’s easy to see “free safety” vs. “box” labels and instantly view the difference in safety positioning through the lens of a single-high look. That’s not necessarily the case with those labels. All “free safety” means is that the defender is aligned at a deep safety spot on the field even in a split-field, two-safety look. So both safeties on a specific play can be in a “free safety” spot, an occurrence that happens frequently in the NFL. However, that graphic shows a pretty discernible difference between Hooker and Bishop’s usage in Buffalo and Tennessee respectively to date. Hooker holds a slight edge in free safety snaps, has less frequently been deployed in the box while spending a higher percentage in the slot. And Hooker’s pre-draft workout in 2019 speaks to what has been a more “coverage-based” utilization in his NFL career. In the below graphic, check Hooker’s three-cone drill: I crunched the numbers on Hooker’s three cone at 210 pounds, and it was a reasonably rare feat to be that heavy yet that nimble in that agility drill. Since 2000, of the 248 safeties of 628 combine-attending safeties weighed at least 210 pounds. Of those 248, there were 128 who also recorded a three-cone time. Of those 128 safeties, just 23 managed a three-cone time of 6.85 seconds or faster. Then, reducing further — of those 23 safeties who weighed at least 210 pounds with a sub 6.85 three cone, Hooker is one of just five who also ran under 4.50 in the 40-yard dash and had a vertical of at least 37 inches. In short, he’s a sizable yet very agile and explosive safety with smooth hip flip when changing directions… vital abilities for any defensive back position, which is likely part of the reason he’s spent the largest single share of snaps in a free safety role and almost 20% of his defensive snaps at slot corner (compared to just under 12% for Bishop). For as much as bumping down into the slot has become a key ask for safeties in today’s NFL, it’s not for every safety. In fact, many don’t excel there. Now, in 2026, Hooker had assumed more of a box and slot corner based role. That was likely due to the presence of second-year, former second-round pick Kevin Winston in Tennessee who thrived as a free safety at Penn State, didn’t have sizable experience in the box and even less at slot corner. But based on the scope of Hooker’s utilization throughout his NFL career, while capable as a quasi-linebacker or strong safety inserted into the box, he’s gotten the most reps and been the most productive in a coverage-based, free safety role or when asked to cover the slot… and he has the athletic skill set to do either at a high level. Beyond the physical attributes, Hooker has long demonstrated the keen mental acuity needed to move fluidly toward the football at the right time to disrupt the catch point. At times , Hooker and Bishop will exchange roles on the field. Safeties wear every hat throughout the course of a game. But in Leonhard’s scheme, I expect noticeably defined placements and responsibilities for these two veteran safeties — Hooker in the deeper, coverage-centric role or in the slot with Bishop as the main insert in the box and as the blitzing specialist.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Amani Hooker should boost ailing Buffalo Bills defense
summary: The Buffalo Bills made one move before the trade deadline, a reasonable transaction with the Tennessee Titans to acquire safety Amani Hooker. The move has been widely regarded as a wise one by the Bills. Needing help on a defense that seems destined to eventually cost Buffalo a game, pretty much everyone is of the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills made one move before the trade deadline, a reasonable transaction with the Tennessee Titans to acquire safety Amani Hooker. The move has been widely regarded as a wise one by the Bills. Needing help on a defense that seems destined to eventually cost Buffalo a game, pretty much everyone is of the belief that Hooker will help cover up some flaws with solid defensive back play. Well I have one thing to say to that… Yeah, pretty much. This is a case of everyone being right. I’ll give you my thoughts on the matter with a short highlight reel but this was a great move by Buffalo. Some film and opinions pic.twitter.com/7u5APcB1WN — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) November 12, 2026 What you have there for the video is Amani Hooker’s five interceptions this year. Does that seem like a lot of interceptions in what amounts to half a season? Because it is. Hooker is tied with Green Bay’s Xavier Mckinney for the lead league with that five. In reality though, Hooker should be considered the interception leader so far in 2026. McKinney’s five interceptions come from nine games, and if you like granular assessment he’s played on 604 snaps. That means he has one interception every 121-ish plays. Hooker was out for one game with a concussion and Tennessee was on their bye this week. He’s appeared in just 495 snaps, for an interception rate of one every 99 plays. In the film above, I went with just the interceptions primarily because they’re fun, but there’s plenty to see on them as well. Hooker’s anticipation and ability to read the quarterback is excellent. Over his career that’s led to variable interception totals and being transparent here, 2026 has already tied his career high, achieved in 2024. So really, the ballhawk thing is hopefully a “from now on” kinda deal. I don’t mean to suggest he’s been poor at it, only that this year is very good even for Hooker. The traits that have led to it in 2026 are good signs for all facets of safety play though. Hooker is a heads up defensive back that processes the game with speed and gets into the mix quickly. That’s been interceptions this year, but it also means he’s there for tackles and other support. I don’t want to oversell him either. If you had to choose between Amani Hooker, prime Micah Hyde, or prime Jordan Poyer; Hooker is going to be the third pick for me. Poyer and Hyde both were more confident tacklers and more helpful on blitzes and in general being chaos agents. However, I don’t think I’d say “distant third” either for Hooker. The Bills added a solid veteran presence that communicates what he sees to those around him, has great instinct for the game, and more than adequate athleticism.
author: Skarekrow

title: Given circumstances, Amani Hooker addition was Buffalo Bills best potential move at trade deadline
summary: Nothing happens in a vacuum. Using words like “good” or “bad” inevitably unlocks a more nuanced “good relative to what” or “bad relative to what” conversation. Thus, when the time comes to evaluate the Buffalo Bills’ acquisition of safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans, the question of whether or not the move is good […]
full_text: Nothing happens in a vacuum. Using words like “good” or “bad” inevitably unlocks a more nuanced “good relative to what” or “bad relative to what” conversation. Thus, when the time comes to evaluate the Buffalo Bills’ acquisition of safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans, the question of whether or not the move is good is a very different question than whether or not the move is optimal . “Good” is a value in vs. value out proposition, with the acknowledgement that the concept of value is subjective based upon how someone weights Hooker’s skill, short vs. long term considerations, and financial items. “Optimal” is instead a reflection of the level of “good” achieved from this maneuver compared to the level of “good” that could have hypothetically been achieved through a different maneuver entirely. It’s a question that folds in opportunity cost amongst all potential other maneuvers. In this author’s opinion, the Hooker transaction is both good and optimal. Other content pieces can discuss the “good” part of that statement. Hooker’s skill set, the compensation, the need at safety, the fact that he’s under contract through 2028 with reasonable cap hits…I’ll let other articles and podcasts outline why those factors all come together to form a conclusion that the addition of Hooker is a good one. I’d instead like to make the argument here that not only was the Hooker addition good , it was the most good the team could have done with its resources at the trade deadline and therefore optimal. In order to do that, I will need to discuss two separate items: what the Bills could have spent and what they could have received. Everything in life is a value proposition: what you give vs. what you get. In order to prove that the Hooker trade was optimal, I need to create a clear picture of all the potential combinations of “give” and “get” and when none of them create a better (“more good”) outcome when compared to the Hooker trade, I can then argue that the transaction was optimal. The Bills came into the trade deadline with about $4 million in cap space. In any discussion about the salary cap, it’s important to note that how much current cap space a team has is not as important as how much cap space they can create . Teams have releases and restructures on certain contracts available to them (henceforth called “levers”) that can generate current-year cap space while frequently increasing the cap burden in subsequent years (important note: mid-season veteran releases do not typically create any cap space for the releasing team because veteran salaries become fully guaranteed upon the regular season beginning). Inevitably, conversations come up that include statements like “the (Team) made it fit on their salary cap” while ignoring the fact that a team with X amount in cap space after pulling their levers is very different than a team with that same X amount in cap space before pulling their levers. I say this to say: the Bills had pulled almost all of their levers and still had $4M in cap space. The two main remaining levers to create current year cap space were a trade of wide receiver Josh Palmer (rendered almost impossible by his injury) and a restructure to the contract of left tackle Dion Dawkins (due about $15.5M in salary for the 2026 year that could be converted, in whole or in part, to a signing bonus). The Bills showed that $4M in cap space, but with a full restructure of all of Dawkins’ 2026 salary, they could have theoretically gotten about $14M more for a total of $18m in cap. So we have successfully outlined that the Bills could have reasonably gone shopping with $18m in cap space and their current crop of draft picks. But what could they have gotten with those resources? The only trades we know for certain could have been executed upon were the trades that were actually, you know, executed upon. We could scream into the ether that Brian Thomas Jr., wide receiver for the Jacksonville Jaguars, would have been available for a fourth-round pick, but he wasn’t actually traded, so we don’t know. The Jaguars could have been holding out for a second-round pick and more in the vein of the Marvin Harrison Jr. deal that was made by the Houston Texans or even more, we can create hypothetical trade scenarios in our heads all we want, but they wouldn’t be based in anything factual and shouldn’t be used in evaluation of the merits of decisions that were actually made. Here is a full list of trades that were executed in the lead up to the 2026 NFL trade deadline, per msn.com : Nov. 10 : The Atlanta Falcons traded C Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Nov. 10 : The Indianapolis Colts traded WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick. Nov. 10 : The Los Angeles Chargers traded LB Daiyan Henry to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick. Nov. 10 : The Las Vegas Raiders traded QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick. Nov. 10 : The Tennessee Titans traded S Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills for a second-round pick. Nov. 10 : The Indianapolis Colts traded WR Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Nov. 9: The Philadelphia Eagles traded DT Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick. Nov. 9: The New York Jets traded S Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-round pick. Nov. 9: The New Orleans Saints traded DT Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-round pick. Nov. 9 : The Atlanta Falcons traded S Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. Nov. 4 : The Arizona Cardinals traded QB Jacoby Brissett and a fifth-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a fourth-round pick and a seventh-round pick. Oct. 29 : The Tennessee Titans traded DT Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick. Oct. 27 : The Indianapolis Colts traded DT DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round pick. Oct. 27 : The Indianapolis Colts traded OG Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for third- and fifth-round picks. Oct. 11 : The Arizona Cardinals traded WR Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans for second- and sixth-round picks. Oct. 7 : The Philadelphia Eagles traded OG Cam Jurgens and a seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 fifth-round pick. Sept. 30 : The Pittsburgh Steelers traded CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-round pick. Sept. 28 : The Minnesota Vikings traded QB J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick. Of those trades, we can outline the Simmons, Buckner, Nelson, MHJ, Porter Jr., Davis, Bates, Cisco, Godchaux, Allen, Hooker, Henry, and Downs trades as moves that would have, in a vacuum, have added talent to the Bills roster at positions of at least mild interest or need. The Bills could have traded for Jeffrey Simmons and fit his 2026 salary cap figure ($7.94M) into their current situation with a partial Dawkins restructure. It would have cost them two first round picks to do so and they would have had to make notable 2027 decisions (where they are currently projected to be at least $47M over the 2027 cap limit), but they could have done it this year. I’d make an argument that the Marvin Harrison Jr. deal was a notable overpay by the Texans given his on-field production thus far in his career. Nelson is an expiring contract at a non-problematic position for the Bills despite his excellence. Buckner and Downs are also expiring contracts, though I could make an argument that Downs is exactly the type of man-beater wide receiver the Bills have continually searched for since the departure of Stefon Diggs…

title: Panthers vs Saints: How injuries will dictate this week’s storylines
summary: Hello CSR! We’re on to another game week, which means we can look forward to another game of football to hopefully wipe the slate clean and get Carolina moving in the right direction again. This week, the Panthers will travel to New Orleans to face my personal most hated division rival, the New Orleans Saints. […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Corey Thornton #31 of the Carolina Panthers reacts to his interception against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! We’re on to another game week, which means we can look forward to another game of football to hopefully wipe the slate clean and get Carolina moving in the right direction again. This week, the Panthers will travel to New Orleans to face my personal most hated division rival, the New Orleans Saints. What better way to bounce back from a loss against Sean Payton’s Broncos than defeating his former team? That math maths, right? The Panthers designated RB Jonathon Brooks, WR Xavier Legette, and CB Mike Jackson to return from injured/reserve this week, joining OL Brady Christensen whom they designated to return last week. So the Panthers appear to be finally getting reinforcements soon, which is why I decided to devote this week’s Storylines piece to the Panthers current injury situation on both sides of the ball. The team may not get any of those 4 guys back for this week, that will be dictated by how their practices go over the coming days and how the medical staff evaluates them. So let’s take a look at their current situations on offense and defense. Offense: The Offensive Line is getting healthier, but can they bounce back? On top of the aforementioned Brooks, Christensen, and Legette, OG Damien Lewis practiced in full on Wednesday. He has been the Panthers best offensive linemen when healthy this season, and his presence has been sorely missed. So depending on what happens with Brady Christensen, the Panthers could have two key offensive linemen returning this week. But honestly, the Panthers offensive line wasn’t as bad this past weekend as they have been previously, but they still allowed pressure and sacks leading to turnovers in very key situations. This week, they draw a Saints defense that isn’t the best as far as yardage per game is concerned, but they can pressure the passer. And in recent history, this defense has given Carolina’s offense fits. Of all games to right the trend of losses against New Orleans, this is the week, as Carolina still sits at number one in the NFC South despite their recent string of losses. They need to keep Bryce Young upright to take advantage of the Saints bottom third of the league defense in most statistical categories. Defense: The secondary again a storyline I’m not expecting Mike Jackson to return this week, but him being activated gives the Panthers about 3 weeks to evaluate him and decide if he’s healthy. But, there’s more good news in the secondary as Will Lee III managed a full practice on Wednesday. In addition, the Panthers finally activated Corey Thornton on Sunday, and he managed a really nice interception as the Panthers defense had a relatively okay game. I imagine Marco Wilson might get the call up once again for this secondary as well. They’ll have their work cut out for them, as the Saints have Chris Olave and now first round picks Jordyn Tyson getting more snaps coming off his injuries in the off-season. They’ll need to try their best to match up against these guys without Mike Jack and Jaycee Horn. Bonus Storyline: Looks like they’ll get Jaelan Phillips back The Panthers have spent the last few weeks without their big 2026 free agency signing Jaelan Phillips, which has greatly impacted their pass rush and the setting of the edge in the run game. He appears to be back this week after practicing in full on Wednesday coming off a hamstring injury. Its not a guarantee he will return, as those hammy injuries can pop back up, but at this juncture its promising. Which, having him return will help a defense that might be missing LB Bobby Okereke, who is still nursing the same foot injury that kept him out last week. What storylines are you watching this week, Panthers fans?

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Yhonzae Pierre
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 10: Linebacker Yhonzae Pierre #0 of the Alabama Crimson Tide reacts after a sack against the Georgia Bulldogs during the first half of a game at Bryant Denny Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. Today our profile will focus on Alabama Crimson Tide edge defender Yhonzae Pierre. Bio Pierre (6’3”, 251 lbs.) used his status as a four star recruit in Alabama to earn an All-American Bowl invitation. Despite being offered scholarships to several SEC powerhouses, Pierre chose the home state Crimson Tide. Pierre spent his freshman season in 2023 redshirted before becoming a rotational piece in 2024. While not expected to start last season, injuries to Alabama’s top edges gave Pierre an opportunity, and he never looked back. He ended up leading Alabama with 14.5 tackles for loss and eight sacks. He returned for this year and switched to number zero, taking over Deontae Lawson’s legacy. Pierre has been a bit banged up this year but has 23 tackles with 5.5 for loss and 4.5 sacks through nine games. He even added a pick six for good measure. Strengths/Weaknesses Pierre is a pass rushing producer, again leading Alabama in pressures with 25 so far this season. He plays the run with strength and a solid anchor, holding the point of attack well for his size. Pierre also has a knack for taking over certain games, including six pressures against Florida State this year. He’s able to use his above average athletic ability and strength to win on the outside, making a concerted effort this season of getting his hands up when his pass rush stalls (he has four passes deflected already this year). While his pressure numbers have stayed steady, his inconsistent tackling leads to him not finishing some plays. He also loses his pad level on longer pass rush reps, allowing the offensive lineman to get him off balance. While Pierre is not a small player, he doesn’t have the elite edge defender height and weight, which could affect how he fits into some NFL defensive schemes. Projection Pierre is a hard working, talented edge rusher. He uses his quick start and power to perform well against the run and the pass. He’s a bit hot and cold, with his pressures coming in bunches, but the pass rush prowess is undeniable. Pierre’s ceiling is viewed as a high-end starter if he can finish better at the quarterback. He has plenty of pressures, but his counters are still developing allowing opposing quarterbacks to escape too often. With the Panthers struggling to get to the quarterback, taking an edge rusher isn’t out of the question. The problem with projecting who they might take, however, is not knowing who the long term defensive coordinator will be and what scheme they’ll implement. A 3-4 DC would likely be more open to someone like Pierre, whereas a base 4-3 coach might want someone a bit larger. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Yhonzae Pierre is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: NFL Power Rankings- Midseason Edition
summary: We have hit roughly the midway point of the season. The power rankings look a LOT different than they did the first week of September. Only half the preseason top 10 teams remain in the top 10. One team climbed 18 spots in the power rankings this edition, and one team fell 18 spots as […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 28: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers and Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears shake hands after the game at Levi's Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have hit roughly the midway point of the season. The power rankings look a LOT different than they did the first week of September. Only half the preseason top 10 teams remain in the top 10. One team climbed 18 spots in the power rankings this edition, and one team fell 18 spots as well. As we get a better feel for these teams, hopefully these power rankings more closely reflect what things will look like in January than where we are now in September. Halfway through the season, here’s a look at the power rankings (preseason and quarter pole rankings in parentheses). 1. San Francisco 49ers (6, 1) Definitely could make an argument for the Bears here, but the 49ers have consistently been the league’s best team since week one. 2. Chicago Bears (9, 6) If every team plays their best game, the Bears are the best team. But the Bears showed vs Tampa that they can still win even if they don’t have their A game. 3. Buffalo Bills (3, 3) This feels like a massive year for Josh Allen and needs some postseason success to start cementing a legacy. 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (14, 8) After some aggressive trade deadline moves, might be the best team in the AFC. 5. Green Bay Packers (18, 23) The Packers are not the same team from the start of the season. They have figured things out and look outstanding. Micah Parsons is right around the corner. 6. Kansas City Chiefs (10, 5) The Chiefs keep winning football games, but they rarely look impressive when they do it. 7. Detroit Lions (17, 18) If the Lions’ defense were a little stronger, this team could be truly elite. 8. Minnesota Vikings (15, 10) If Kirk Cousins unlocks Justin Jefferson, the Vikings could be a very tough out. 9. Denver Broncos (5, 11) The Broncos are battle-tested and know how to win close football games. 10. Cincinnati Bengals (16, 12) Joe Burrow is the frontrunner for MVP. How far can he carry this team in the playoffs? 11. Pittsburgh Steelers (19, 22) I wouldn’t say Aaron Rodgers has turned back the clock, but it’s definitely his best season in the last 3 or 4 years. Despite that, their January ceiling is still limited. 12. Seattle Seahawks (1, 2) With a healthier running back room, we will see if they surge back up, but clearly letting Kenneth Walker go was a mistake. 13. New England Patriots (7, 15) This team has been up and down all season long. If the Texans can squeak into the playoffs, it’ll be the Patriots who miss out. 14. LA Rams (2, 7) With Puka and Adams out, this Super Team may just never fire properly this season. 15. Houston Texans (8, 21) CJ Stroud looks the best he has since his rookie season, and the Texans are back on track. Will their September hole be too much to climb out of? 16. New York Giants (22, 19) I would like to see the Giants beat a good team before I believe in them. Right now they have a fluffy record from a very soft schedule. 17. Cleveland Browns (28, 17) The Browns are having a great season based on preseason expectations, but their lack of QB play will still prevent them from any real success. 18. Dallas Cowboys (13, 9) The Cowboys continue to be a lot of hype and no substance. Every year we do the same song and dance. 19. Las Vegas Raiders (26, 14) It’s Mendoza-time in Vegas. Klint Kubiak is off to a great start and looks the part so far. 20. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (21, 28) The Bucs look like the best team in the NFC South. Unfortunately, that’s not much of a compliment. 21. Carolina Panthers (23, 16) The Panthers continue to be the same mediocre football team they’ve been the last couple of years. 22. Baltimore Ravens (4, 4) No Lamar Jackson has completely derailed anything they could hope to do. Jacoby Brissett isn’t saving this season. 23. New Orleans Saints (20, 26) If the Bucs don’t win the South, I think the Saints will. 24. Atlanta Falcons (29, 20) There was hope that Michael Penix could make this team decent, but nope, that was short-lived hope. 25. Washington Commanders (25, 29) This Commanders team is so close to putting it together, but they just keep shooting themselves in the foot. Signs point to coaching. 26. Philadelphia Eagles (12, 13) The Eagles didn’t quite look like a Super Bowl contender to start the year, but now they are getting into the running for the first pick of the draft. 27. Arizona Cardinals (31, 30) After some injuries, the Cardinals might have the worst offense we’ve seen in recent memory. 28. New York Jets (30, 27) The Jets play hard. I’m out of compliments. 29. Indianapolis Colts (24, 25) The only question for the Colts: why are Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones still on your roster? 30. Tennessee Titans (27, 31) The Titans are three years away from being three years away. 31. Miami Dolphins (32, 32) Congratulations, Dolphins, you’ve moved up one spot in the rankings. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (11, 24) Jim Harbaugh is currently doing the worst job of any coach ever in the Super Bowl era.

title: Bears Question of the Day: What adjustment do you want to see after the Bye?
summary: The Chicago Bears are 7-2 after Week 9 and sit atop the NFC North. With all context aside, you couldn’t ask for a better position entering your bye week. While the Bears do have some injuries that will hopefully heal up by Week 11 (namely Kyle Monangai and Luther Burden), the biggest thing the Bears […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Chicago center Logan Jones (54) warms up prior to the start of the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on October 18th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears are 7-2 after Week 9 and sit atop the NFC North. With all context aside, you couldn’t ask for a better position entering your bye week. While the Bears do have some injuries that will hopefully heal up by Week 11 (namely Kyle Monangai and Luther Burden), the biggest thing the Bears can do is make necessary personnel adjustments to set themselves up for a deep playoff run. What adjustment do you want to see the Bears make out of the Bye week? For me, I think it’s time to shuffle out Garrett Bradbury in favor of Logan Jones. While Bradbury has been mostly solid through the first 9 weeks, he’s clearly the weak link on the OL and can lead to devastating results, as in the Bucs game. Pressure up the middle was constant during the Bears’ nail-biting win, and the communication between Thuney, Jackson, and Bradbury is appearing as shaky as ever. Tough for Caleb to do anything here. Bucs confusing the Bears line. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/G5eU80CcBn — Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) November 9, 2026 These types of plays require Bradbury to take authority as the Center and ensure the OL knows their assignments. Each and every week it is clearer that he isn’t up to that task. Beyond the lack of communication, Bradbury seems to lack the lateral quickness and strength at the point of attack to win in run and pass reps. Garrett Bradbury hasn’t been awful and brings a veteran presence to the center position making calls. Every week though there are a number of snaps that are concerning. For the season he’s graded 27th out of 32 centers in pass blocking grade per PFF. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/WPE1rrNApe — Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) November 3, 2026 This assembly of clips shows Bradbury frequently missing free rushers up the middle, getting beat at the point of attack, or lacking the athleticism to win downfield. It’s consistently costing the Bears by forcing Caleb to get immediate pressure in his face, or limiting the effectiveness of the run game. It hasn’t been all bad for Bradbury, who has been a solid addition to a line that lost Drew Dalman to an early retirement. But it’s time to bring in the rookie Logan Jones in relief. Jones, who was selected in the 2nd round of the 2026 NFL draft, is the highest drafted OL for Ryan Poles since Darnell Wright. For a team looking to compete now, the expectation for a 2nd round pick should be for them to contribute sooner rather than later. Fortunately, Jones looked really good in his limited reps earlier this season against the Atlanta Falcons: Logan Jones (54) had some solid snaps yesterday. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/9SZuQvwcSL — Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) October 19, 2026 Seeing him seal off his man downfield and also win a few pass-blocking reps is highly encouraging. However, the rep at the 22 second mark of the link shows that he is still learning and is still prone to mistakes. I am optimistic that if the Bears make this change after Week 11, and with their battering ram in Kyle Monangai returning, that the Bears can return to their elite rushing ways. Now it’s your turn! What adjustment would you like to see the Bears make out of the bye week? Sound off in the comments!

title: Ja’Marr Chase believes the best is yet to come for the Bengals
summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase has been on fire during the past two weeks, catching 21 passes for 296 yards and two touchdowns. But he still believes he and quarterback Joe Burrow have another level to reach. Asked whether this is his best year with Burrow, Chase’s answer went straight back to their national […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase has been on fire during the past two weeks, catching 21 passes for 296 yards and two touchdowns. But he still believes he and quarterback Joe Burrow have another level to reach. Asked whether this is his best year with Burrow, Chase’s answer went straight back to their national championship season at LSU. “Nah, 2019, of course,” Chase said recently. “We haven’t been close. The consistency hasn’t been there. If we played the way we did last week, then yes.” Asked if this is the best year he's had with Joe Burrow, "Nah, 2019, of course…. We haven't been close (this season). The consistency hasn't been there. If we played the way we did last week, then yes." — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) November 12, 2026 This past Sunday in Madrid, the Bengals delivered their best performance of the season against Atlanta. Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns without a turnover, while Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a score in the 34-17 win. The previous week, against Tennessee, Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns, then added an overtime rushing score in Cincinnati’s 43-36 victory. But he also threw three interceptions. Chase finished that day with 11 receptions for 141 yards and a score. So far this season, Chase has compiled 53 receptions, 647 receiving yards, and seven touchdowns. He is currently tied for sixth in total catches and second in touchdown receptions. Those are strong numbers, but still fall far short of the kind of season Chase and Burrow enjoyed during LSU’s championship run in 2019, when Burrow threw 60 touchdown passes, and Chase accounted for 20 of them. He finished that year with 84 catches and 1,780 receiving yards. With Pittsburgh visiting Sunday and first place in the AFC North at stake, the Bengals have an immediate opportunity to build on their performance in Madrid. Chase’s message is clear enough: the ability is there, but he wants the execution to keep matching it.

title: 3 reasons why the Bengals will beat the Steelers on SNF, and 3 reasons they won’t
summary: It’s Week 10, which means we’re halfway through the season. The playoff picture is starting to come into view, and the Cincinnati Bengals are 6-2 with a chance to take a firm grasp of the AFC North. They host the Pittsburgh Steelers, also 6-2, who beat the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27. The […]
full_text: It’s Week 10, which means we’re halfway through the season. The playoff picture is starting to come into view, and the Cincinnati Bengals are 6-2 with a chance to take a firm grasp of the AFC North. They host the Pittsburgh Steelers , also 6-2, who beat the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27. The game will be in front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football under the lights, and the Bengals will wear their “White Bengal” uniform. With the history between these two teams and what’s at stake, this is one of the biggest games played at Paycor Stadium in the last few years. Here are three reasons why the Bengals will beat the Steelers in front of a home crowd on Sunday night (followed by three reasons why they won’t). Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins That’s reason No. 1. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins make up the best quarterback-wide receiver trio in the NFL, and it’s not even close. Burrow and Chase have played football together for the better part of a decade, and Higgins and Burrow have been together their entire NFL careers. And they complement each other perfectly. Chase is a generational talent. He can play on the outside or in the slot or out of the backfield. He can run any route, and he can burn about any defensive back in a footrace. On top of that, when he gets the ball in his hands, he turns into a running back—capable of breaking tackles and turning a five-yard reception into a 60-yard touchdown any time he touches the ball. Tee is a big-bodied receiver—6-foot-4, 220 pounds—but he too can fly. His greatest strength, though, is his literal strength when it comes to catching the ball in traffic. You could make a two-hour movie out of his highlights when it comes to keeping the ball in his hands and defensive backs are draped all over him. The only reason Higgins isn’t WR1 is that Chase is Chase. Bengals Defensive Line The defense is improved. It’s not perfect, but it is better. What makes it better is the defensive line. The Bengals went all in on that one position group. They traded the No. 10 overall pick for Dexter Lawrence, who has been a dominant force in the middle all season long. They also signed Jonathan Allen, who has played extremely well next to Lawrence, and Boye Mafe, who ranks among PFF’s top pass rushers so far this season. On top of the free agent additions, they retained last year’s starters, BJ Hill and TJ Slaton, as well as their 2024 second-round pick, Kris Jenkins Jr. Sprinkle in Myles Murphy, Cedric Johnson, and possibly Shemar Stewart (I know, I know…), and the Bengals have one of the deepest defensive lines in the league. So at the end of the game, when the Steelers’ offensive line is sucking wind, and Aaron Rodgers needs time to find his ogre of a tight end for a first down, maybe they won’t be able to hold off a Lawrence who has just taken a couple plays off on the sideline to catch his breath. Week 10 Offense > Week 3 Offense We’ve seen this story before. The Bengals, though they started the season 2-0, looked weird doing it on offense. They were still in offseason mode, like Burrow and the rest of his offense typically are until late October. Now, the offense is firing on all cylinders. Burrow has thrown for over 1,200 yards, 16 touchdowns, and only three interceptions. If he continues this trend, it would be hard to deny him the MVP. So, if you go back and watch the Bengals lose to the Steelers in Week 3, and then you watch their offense over the last four weeks, you’ll notice they look much better now. Bonus Reason: You This game has potential to be insane. The two teams don’t like each other already, and with what’s at stake, the stadium is going to be LOUD. I’d like to see Rodgers communicate a change to his receivers and offensive line when he can’t even hear himself think. So be loud. ———————————————————————————————————————————— And now, unfortunately, three reasons why the Bengals won’t win on Sunday: The Bengals’ Secondary If the Bengals have a big weakness, it’s their secondary. The front office didn’t address the cornerback position despite the overall lack of quality depth, and now it could come back to bite them. The Steelers don’t boast a receiving corps nearly as good as the Bengals’, but there’s talent there, and Rodgers has spent an entire career making receivers look good. At 42 years old, Rodgers is playing at a high level, and if the Bengals let him run around in the backfield and avoid pressure the way he did in Week 3 again, he will find open receivers and move the ball down the field. The Bengals’ secondary isn’t good enough to lock up receivers for an extended period of time, and Rodgers is perfectly capable of carving them up if he gets the opportunity to do so. Jaylen Warren Rodgers might be the star on the Steelers’ offense, but Warren has been incredible for Pittsburgh. He’s averaging 5.9 yards per carry, which leads the league among running backs with a lot of carries. He averages 88 yards per game, which is more than the Bengals’ offense averages. He’s PFF’s highest-graded running back, and he has more yards and averages more yards after contact per attempt than any other running back in the league with a minimum of 50% of the carries. Lawrence might be really good at stopping the run when the offense tries to run between the tackles, but he can’t be everywhere. And one major weakness of the Bengals’ defense is their ability to stop the run on the outside. One of the best ways for the Steelers to defend against Burrow is to keep him on the sidelines, and one of the best ways to keep him on the sidelines is to let Warren carry the ball and chew clock. The Steelers are coming off a bye; the Bengals are coming off an international game This matters. The Steelers are fully rested and are coming off their bye week. They haven’t played a football game since Nov. 1 and are relatively healthy. The Bengals, on the other hand, not only played on Nov. 8, but they played that game in Madrid, Spain. Then they had to fly back across the planet to Cincinnati and pretend like everything’s normal. They do get the benefit of waiting to play football until Sunday night, but if the NFL wants to continue their international games, they’re going to have to think about giving teams an extra bye week before they have to travel that far. The Bengals had a good trip, but the stress and adjustment to different time zones probably made things a little more difficult than they would have been had they played the Falcons in Atlanta. What do you think will happen on Sunday night?

title: Bengals News: Spain trip strengthened Cincinnati’s locker room
summary: Modern football has become so calculated with analytics — which is great for many reasons — but you can tell fans rely solely on these numbers when talking about the game. The Cincinnati Bengals may have a great example of something that has gotten lost in all this. It is the intangibles of it all, […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver JaMarr Chase (1) and Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5) do a matador celebration after scoring a touchdown during the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, Spain on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Bob Kupbens/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Modern football has become so calculated with analytics — which is great for many reasons — but you can tell fans rely solely on these numbers when talking about the game. The Cincinnati Bengals may have a great example of something that has gotten lost in all this. It is the intangibles of it all , and team chemistry is a big part of that. “I spoke to several people who were on that trip to Madrid, and one thing that really stood out was just how important this past week was for the team above just the football,” Schultz said. “What I mean by that is they arrived; the Bengals did, early in the week in Spain, and something I think fans don’t always see with these international trips is the team bonding that happens when everybody’s together in a different environment. And I was told this was just a major week for the Bengals, not just on the field, but for the entire organization. “The connection from Player 1-to-53 is very strong, and I was told by someone there it’s basically the same as it was during the Super Bowl run several years ago. That’s the type of connection.” It almost sounds like the middle of one of those sports movies like after the team gets arrested in the Replacements and then they all sing a song in jail to gel together and win games. The Bengals are on a four game winning streak, but there are still lingering questions of how far this team can go in the playoffs. Having better chemistry would certainly help. We will see if it helps on Sunday night Football against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Bengals News Quick Hits | Joe Burrow Eyes Drew Brees’ Record Of 74.4%: ‘That Would Be A Fun One To Break’ Burrow has long been recognized for his accuracy, and he is still technically the most accurate quarterback in NFL history based on percentages. It is one of those season stats that would also lead to more wins. The idea of completing three out of every four passes is wild, but that is a number Burrow is maintaining. Bengals call off Arnold Ebiketie trade with Eagles after nearly botching compensatory pick situation The most embarrassing part of this whole thing is Zac Taylor being trotted out there to explain the front office’s mistake. Duke Tobin hiding behind Taylor just makes it look so cowardly. Like when a parent apologizes for a child. Why Bengals-Steelers is the biggest game at Paycor Stadium in years It doesn’t get bigger than two 6-2 division rivals battling for first place in the division while still trying to keep pace for a possible No. 1 seed in the conference. The Steelers won the first time around, and the Bengals will have a chance to show how much they have grown since that game. NFL News Broncos call off trade with Chargers for LB Daiyan Henley Well it appears calling off trades is all the rage now. There is still no reason as of yet. It could be related to his physical as he was at the Broncos facility, but nothing has been made clear other than Henley being stuck on the winless Los Angeles Chargers. NFL Power Rankings, Week 10: Jaguars reach season high; Vikings, Patriots slide after lopsided defeats It is obvious that the top of the AFC is going to be very competitive. The Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs are all in the same group as the Bengals, and it could truthfully come down to matchups and who gets hot once the playoffs start. NFL QB rankings, Week 10: Joe Burrow climbs to No. 1; Caleb Williams slides It has been following this list since the beginning. It always seemed like Burrow would end up near the top after starting off in the second tier. His past few games have propelled him to the peak, and inserted him arguably to the front of the MVP discussion.

title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Steelers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will host the Pittsburgh Steelers in primetime football this week. They face off at Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football with first place on the line in the division. Both teams enter this game at 6-2, with Pittsburgh taking a close win over Cincinnati in Week 3. Let’s look at some of […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will host the Pittsburgh Steelers in primetime football this week. They face off at Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football with first place on the line in the division. Both teams enter this game at 6-2, with Pittsburgh taking a close win over Cincinnati in Week 3. Let’s look at some of the key matchups to watch in this massive AFC North clash. Amarius Mims vs. TJ Watt Amarius Mims has been playing at an All-Pro level all season long. Mims has allowed just five total pressures through eight regular-season games. He is absolutely locking guys down on his side of the line. He is also left on an island more than about any other tackle in the NFL. While he is starting to get more recognition, a primetime matchup for first place in the division against TJ Watt and the Pittsburgh Steelers could really boost his chances for an All-Pro this season. Meanwhile, TJ Watt has already surpassed his sack total from the 2025 season. Watt currently has 7.5 sacks through just eight games played. Last season, he recorded seven sacks during the entire season. Watt is still one of the better defenders in the league, but will certainly have his hands full trying to get around Mt. Mims this week. This is great versus great, and should be a must-see matchup. Amarius Mims has yet to allow a pressure through the first 3 games. He is the only starting tackle in the league to have done so. Mims is Hims. pic.twitter.com/3LzW9PVusO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 29, 2026 Darnell Washington vs. Jordan Battle Tackling Darnell Washington is not a fun task, and the Bengals have been one of the worst teams at trying to do so over the years. Washington had 67 yards against the Bengals during Week 3, including a big rumble down the sideline during the 4th quarter. There was also a play earlier in the game where Jordan Battle tried to come in high on Washington and make the tackle. It won’t be just Battle who has to play well against Washington, but it would be nice to see him learn from his mistakes against him earlier in the season. As for Jordan Battle, it feels like he has started to play some pretty solid football the past few games. His tackling overall has been much more sound, and he made some huge plays against Tennessee in coverage a couple of weeks ago. This past game against Atlanta was the first game of the season that he was not credited with a single missed tackle. Hopefully that is a positive sign for this week, because Washington is a BIG test. Regardless of the angle you see it from, a lot of pathetic effort out there to go and make this play after the Darnell Washington catch. pic.twitter.com/9HKBpp1YMo — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Jaylen Warren vs. Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. Jaylen Warren was incredible in Week 3 against the Bengals, who had a hard time getting him on the ground all day long. Warren had 17 carries for 117 yards rushing. He also added an additional three receptions for another 49 yards. The Bengals will have to keep Warren in check if they want to get the win this week. Two of the main guys responsible for making sure he doesn’t have another game like that will be Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter. While both guys have been okay this year, I wouldn’t call that Pittsburgh game earlier in the year one of their better games. Both guys will need to have a better showing this week at home against the Steelers. Not how you want to start the game pic.twitter.com/SdCNgOqiVe — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 If the Bengals are going to continue having Barrett Carter out there 100% of the snaps (and they likely are) we are going to need him to play better. pic.twitter.com/ao1dBAcJh1 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Chase Brown vs. Pittsburgh Defense The Bengals are always going to be a pass-first team, but that doesn’t mean that Chase Brown cannot have some big rushing performances. This may need to be one of those weeks. Brown had 13 carries for 61 yards during the first matchup against the Steelers. If the Bengals can get some balance with the run game, it will keep Pittsburgh’s pass rush at bay. Brown has been starting to heat up the last couple of weeks as well, and this could be a breakout performance if given the opportunity. One thing I have appreciated all season is his blocking ability in pass protection. He is starting to get more involved in the passing game and showing more elusiveness as a runner in the open field. If Chase Brown can get going against Pittsburgh, I think the Bengals will come out of Sunday Night Football sitting atop the AFC North at 7-2. Chase Brown vs. Pittsburgh The Bengals need to get Chase Brown more carries, but also get him more involved in the passing game. Highly impressed with what he is doing as a blocker this year too. pic.twitter.com/rZ0FZY1VXs — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 2, 2026

title: Best available free agent edge rushers for Bengals to target after failed Arnold Ebiketie trade
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals rarely make a trade at the deadline, which is why it was somewhat surprising that a trade was reported on Tuesday when they (briefly) acquired Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles. However, the trade seems to have dissolved behind the scenes after the team realized the deal would also cost them a third-round […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals rarely make a trade at the deadline, which is why it was somewhat surprising that a trade was reported on Tuesday when they (briefly) acquired Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles. However, the trade seems to have dissolved behind the scenes after the team realized the deal would also cost them a third-round compensatory pick they are hoping to receive from Trey Hendrickson signing with the Ravens. Then, for the rest of the deadline, no more moves were made, although it is unknown if any more trades were attempted or if they elected to stand pat once the Ebiketie deal fell through. The attempted trade for Ebiketie, though, is a clear indicator that the Bengals are not happy with the depth of their defensive end room. Cashius Howell is on IR for an unknown amount of time, and Shemar Stewart is getting few snaps and was even a healthy inactive for a game. With all of that, the failed trade, and no more trade possibilities, the Bengals could target the position through one of the free agents still available on the market, so let’s take a look at the top available defensive ends. Joey Bosa The 31-year-old Bosa was one of the top edge rushers in the NFL for most of his career; he last played in Buffalo in 2025 on a one-year, $12 million deal. In the offseason, he was in the discussion for many fanbases, but no rumored meetings or potential signings popped up, and in the summer it was hinted he may have even quietly retired, with Adam Schefter saying he may have played his final snap. However, in the last month there has been more buzz about him possibly coming back and joining a team for a run to the Super Bowl, mainly his previous team, the Bills, or joining his brother Nick Bosa in San Francisco. It is not impossible to imagine, though, a world where he wants to join his close friend Joe Burrow in Cincinnati for a title run as well, and the Bengals should not hesitate to call and see if it is possible. Leonard Floyd The 34-year-old Floyd is another older pass rusher who was productive relatively recently, now getting a lot of buzz as a potential addition for teams looking to make a Super Bowl push. On a one-year, $10 million deal in 2025, Floyd had a decent year and can still get involved as a pass rusher. The Bengals should be a desirable destination for any free agent edge rushers with their talented offense and impactful interior, giving edge rushers a lot of one-on-one matchups in obvious passing situations. As a rotational pass rusher, Floyd would fit exactly what the Bengals need. Haason Reddick The 32-year-old Reddick was one of the best pass rushers in the league for several years and was a double-digit sack player with Philadelphia. His production in recent years has really taken a nosedive, but the Bengals could sign him with the hope that he has fresh legs, not playing most of the year, and could be effectively deployed in a limited capacity to keep him fresh. If Reddick could find something even close to his 2023 form, he could be extremely impactful. Yetur Gross-Matos The youngest player on the list by a long shot, 28-year-old Yetur Gross-Matos signed a two-year deal with the 49ers in free agency in 2024. During that contract, though, he missed roughly half of his games with the team and wasn’t a consistent performer in the games he did play in. Gross-Matos did have flashes, and with him now either healthy or very close to it after a knee injury last year, he could be one of the more intriguing options, since he is still young and could have several years of impactful football ahead of him. The Bengals have quite a few options available if they want some fresh legs and some help in the pass-rushing department. If they were willing to spend a sixth-round pick, they should be more than willing to spend a few million dollars if it is the difference-maker in getting the Super Bowl win. What free agent defensive end would you target?

title: Browns have a penalty problem: All the stats and details- where does the blame fall?
summary: If the 2026 Cleveland Browns were a 1970s TV sitcom, on Monday’s game review they would have been saying, “Marsha! Marsha! full_text: If the 2026 Cleveland Browns were a 1970s TV sitcom, on Monday’s game review they would have been saying, “Marsha! Marsha! Marsha!” But instead, the Browns are a professional football team, and as the game film continued, the coaching staff could be heard saying, “Penalties! Penalties! Penalties!” (or so we would assume). The fact of the matter is, Cleveland is the most penalized team in the league. And that’s no laughing matter. RELATED: RECENT LOSSES – WHICH IS MORE DISAPPOINTING? At the halfway point of the schedule, Cleveland is ranked #1 in team penalties. 82, to be exact, for 563 yards. That averages out to 9.1 penalties per game. 97 total flags, which also ranks #1. 13 declined, which is tied for #1. What is this called? The “best at something?” Part of the problem is that the Browns’ offensive line is a collection of five new starters. Has that ever happened before in the league’s history? Probably, but wow, it stands out. This is a critical aspect of this year’s roster. Yes, the offensive line is five athletes, but more importantly, it is considered one group instead of a handful of individual players. An offensive line works more on cohesiveness rather than single-man stats. Tytus Howard up to three false start penalties today. — 𝚂𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎𝚛 𝙶𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚊𝚗 (@Spencito_) September 27, 2026 OT Tytus Howard came from the Houston Texans during free agency. Another free-agent signing was OG Zion Johnson, inked from the Los Angeles Chargers. OT Spencer Fano and OG Austin Barber are rookies. C Elgton Jenkins was signed away from the Green Bay Packers. This means none of these guys were on the Browns roster last year. And none of them have played together at any point until they showed up for Browns training camp. This means they had to get to know each other and find a way to communicate during a game. Even in camp, there was no certainty about who the starting five would be, so this group didn’t get a chance to become cohesive right away. Two holdovers from last year’s group, OT Dawand Jones and OG Teven Jenkins, have barely seen the field. In Jenkins’ case, he was penciled in at right guard before he started having back issues. He never started a game this year. On October 24, he was placed on IR. Jones was expected to become one of the offensive tackles, but came out of camp as the backup and is more considered the “swing tackle,” meaning he can come in at any point and play either side. He has played with the offense in just three games, but is on the kick teams, so he has played in every game as a blocker. What has this group contributed as far as team penalties? For starters, the Browns are ranked as the most penalized offense in the league. Yeah, there’s that. This unit features 17 false starts and 12 holding calls across the roster. Great googly moogly. A whopping 41 pre-snap flags is leaps and bounds greater than any other team. Is this because these five guys are still trying to figure each other out? Is it because there are two rookies starting? Is it because of the coaching style of OL coach George Warhop or his assistants? Is it because these players just aren’t very good? It has to be something, right? Nobody seems to be able to place a finger on the exact issue, though. It’s a major problem and is keeping this Browns’ offense from reaching its potential. One thing everyone knows: It just keeps happening. Now it’s time for individual stats: RT Tytus Howard: 10 total (7 false starts, 1 ineligible downfield, 1 holding, 1 declined) RG Austin Barber: 6 total (2 false starts, 4 holding) C Elgton Jenkins : 1 total (1 ineligible downfield, 1 declined) LG Zion Johnson: 9 total (2 false starts, 1 ineligible use of hands, 6 holding, 1 declined) LT Spencer Fano: 6 total (1 ineligible downfield, 5 holding, 4 declined) OT Dawand Jones: 2 total (2 ineligible formation, 1 declined) C Luke Wypler: 1 total (1 false start) This accounts for 35 of the 97 total flags. In the Top-20, Cleveland is listed twice. title: Browns vs. Texans: Week 10’s matchup could decide the 2026 season’s direction
summary: With the bye week looming, the Cleveland Browns return home after a strenuous road trip. The team has had some highs and many lows this season, but for the first time since 2023, they’re playing somewhat meaningful games in the middle of the season. Sunday’s tilt with the Houston Texans will be the first of […]
full_text: With the bye week looming, the Cleveland Browns return home after a strenuous road trip. The team has had some highs and many lows this season, but for the first time since 2023, they’re playing somewhat meaningful games in the middle of the season. Sunday’s tilt with the Houston Texans will be the first of four straight at home, but this matchup feels more important than the previous ones and is set to impact playoff odds greatly . If you were to ask who’s the biggest disappointment of the season so far, it would be the Texans (or the Los Angeles Chargers). Going into the season, many experts had this team penciled in as a favorite to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl. Considering the talent on both sides of the ball, an argument could be made that they are better than last year’s roster. It hasn’t been anything close to that. Considered one of the best in the league, Houston’s defense has been anything but. Overall, the unit has been a disappointment. Their run defense has been leaky, and they have been vulnerable to giving up explosives in the passing game. The Texans defense looked better last weekend against the Chargers, but anyone can have a get-right game against the winless LA team. The Texans haven’t looked like contenders at all this season. The defensive regression has more to do with their scheme not evolving, and the team is prone to letdown performances. Offensively, Houston appears to be clicking at a high level. Quarterback CJ Stroud has pretty much played himself into a new contract extension. While the Texans are essentially in playoff mode, the Browns are somewhat entering it. With the team at 5-4, going into the bye week with a 6-4 record could be big. Cleveland will probably not be favored in any of their games for the remainder of the season, but their schedule is somewhat favorable. Could the Browns beat the Texans this Sunday? Yes, but they are also prone to getting blown out if they aren’t careful. Sunday’s game against the Houston could be as close to a playoff atmosphere for Cleveland, and it will be interesting to see how they look.
