title: Browns roster foundation: Built for long-term success or missing too many key pieces
summary: The Cleveland Browns have spent many years in rebuilding mode while trying to establish their identity as a team. While this season has had its ups and downs, this is one of the first years where it feels like the team has more young foundational pieces than you can build a team around. There are […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns have spent many years in rebuilding mode while trying to establish their identity as a team. While this season has had its ups and downs, this is one of the first years where it feels like the team has more young foundational pieces than you can build a team around. There are a lot of first- and second-year players to be extremely encouraged by. On the offensive side of the ball, playmakers like Harold Fannin Jr. , KC Concepcion , and Denzel Boston have all shown flashes of greatness. They have each had standout performances and found success regardless of whether Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders is taking snaps at quarterback. It would be interesting to see what those young players could do with even better play from the quarterback and offensive line. On the defensive side of the ball, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has shown great flashes in the secondary. Carson Schwesinger has put together two consecutive impressive seasons. Players like that should be a staple of the franchise for years to come. On the other hand, there are still gaps in the roster at key positions such as quarterback and a pass rusher who can bend the edge continually. Despite that, there are many reasons to be excited about this team in the future. title: Browns defense starting to show some cracks in the armor
summary: The Cleveland Browns defense has been feeling the pressure through the first nine weeks of the season. Following the complete team meltdown in Week 1 against Jacksonville, the defense has carried more than its share of the water each week.  It has become a familiar script: the defense keeps the Browns in the game while […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns defense has been feeling the pressure through the first nine weeks of the season. Following the complete team meltdown in Week 1 against Jacksonville, the defense has carried more than its share of the water each week. It has become a familiar script: the defense keeps the Browns in the game while the offense bumbles its way through the first three quarters, only to catch fire when it appears all hope is lost to pull out a win. At least that is how it has played out with Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback. Unfortunately for the Browns, Watson was sidelined for last week’s game against the New Orleans Saints with a concussion, so no winning comeback was to be found. While everyone knows that playing the way the Browns have through the first nine games is not sustainable, most weeks it felt that way given the way the defense was playing. But the strain has started to show on the defense over the past few weeks; in the previous three games, they have allowed an average of 24.7 points and 167 rushing yards per game. So what can the defense do to get itself right and help the Browns avoid heading into the bye week on a three-game losing streak? staying disciplined pic.twitter.com/Qd3eov0HhA — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 12, 2026 When asked about it on Thursday, defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg said it comes down to facing the challenge head-on and finding that extra bit of energy to make a difference : “No one drive defines a game, and I think that’s important for the whole team to know, and that’s what Monk always talks about. Whether it’s starting fast, finishing faster, making the play at the end of the half, going in, getting a three and out after halftime. Each little six-second play defines the game. “And then of course at the end of the game, great defenses try their butts off to finish. And during the week, I’m not going to get into what we do, but what I can promise you is we are always addressing whatever came up head-on, honestly, together, and figuring out the best ways, whether it’s in a meeting, whether it’s out at practice, whether it’s a drill. We do all that, and our guys are bought into that, and it’s really cool to see.” But what about the run defense? While the Browns have never really been stout against the run, being ranked No. 27 against it (130.6 yards per game) this season doesn’t make life any easier. we are the engine pic.twitter.com/4mDb0ZASSM — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 12, 2026 The Texas don’t present a daunting challenge as they are ranked No. 29 in rushing (87.1 yards per game), but neither did the Saints, and they ripped off 141 rushing yards. Rutenberg went back to his standby answer when asked about what the coaches can do this week to get things back on track : “Every week, whatever it is, we address it, like I always say, because that’s just what football is. And in terms of the run defense, great run games are based on violence, which is what we’re built off of. Discipline fits and straining of the ball. And we’ll continue to preach our style of strain and violence and our style of the mind to do our best in the fits, practice it like we’ve been doing it, and continue to, whatever it is, take that approach in everything we’re trying to fix.” The joy of being 5-2 and first in the AFC North has started to slip away over the past two weeks, and the defense has played a role in that. This week presents another challenge, and if the Browns hope to enter the bye with a victory, they are going to need the defense to get back to its particular strain of violence when the Texans have the ball. summary: The Cleveland Browns take on the Houston Texans this Sunday. full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns take on the Houston Texans this Sunday. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley’s unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers’ league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who’s allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud’s other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston’s lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns’ permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans’ team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won’t matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that’s going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he’ll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That’s a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland’s defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns’ early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who has 25 tackles the last two weeks, helps Cleveland stick around at home. Below are our Week 10 NFL staff picks:

title: Cleveland Browns news: Silencing the QB noise
summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is still new to town, so he can be excused for not understanding how things work around here when it comes to quarterbacks. Every decision relating to the position must be questioned and defended on a daily basis. It does not matter how many names are on the infamous […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is still new to town, so he can be excused for not understanding how things work around here when it comes to quarterbacks. Every decision relating to the position must be questioned and defended on a daily basis. It does not matter how many names are on the infamous quarterback jersey; the mob always wants another one added to it. Because where is the fun of simply knowing who the starter is and practicing for that week’s opponent? Monken appears to be catching on, however, as he showed during Wednesday’s announcement that quarterback Deshaun Watson would be back as the starter for this week’s game against the Houston Texans after missing one game with a concussion. It is the type of standard move that NFL teams make all the time. A starter misses a game (or games) with an injury, and once healthy, they return to their former status. Maybe the fact that Monken is trying his best to run the Browns like a real NFL team is throwing people off. After all, despite not playing well for a full game yet this season, Watson has been instrumental in helping the Browns stay relevant into November, which is a rare feat around these parts. Why would Monken want to go away from that, especially after watching the same script play out against New Orleans only to end with a crucial loss instead of a key win? The answer, as it has been since the start of the season, is that he never wanted to, and it was only Watson suffering a concussion that brought a conversation no one wanted to have back into the light. Now that Monken has answered the question, the team can focus on getting ready for the Houston Texans and attempt to avoid going into the bye week on a three-game losing streak. We have spent enough time on all this; let’s get rolling with today’s edition of the Daily Dawg Chow. title: Commanders help Cowboys’ NFC East hopes with TNF win over Giants
summary: The NFC East just became a tiny bit easier for the Dallas Cowboys. They owe the Washington Commanders big time. On Thursday night there was an NFC East tilt that went down to the wire. When it looked like the New York Giants (5-3-1) were going to take a serious step forward, a leap to […]
full_text: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images | Getty Images The NFC East just became a tiny bit easier for the Dallas Cowboys. They owe the Washington Commanders big time. On Thursday night there was an NFC East tilt that went down to the wire. When it looked like the New York Giants (5-3-1) were going to take a serious step forward, a leap to be honest, in the NFC East race, Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs to give Washington the late lead that held until the end. In case you are unaware, a Giants win on Thursday night would have just about sealed the NFC East race. Nothing is ever official obviously, but it would have given them six wins to date and with the tie from their previous matchup against Washington that would have put them at 6.5 in an effective sense. New York’s remaining schedule suggests that they should come close to finishing around 9-10 wins. Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks Cleveland Browns at Detroit Lions at Dallas Cowboys Philadelphia Eagles Given that the Cowboys currently own a 4-5 record, and that they play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, envisioning them finishing with 10 or 11 wins to clear New York’s potential total with the tie is difficult, and obviously the lower the bar the more ideal the situation. The Cowboys’ remaining schedule: San Francisco 49ers Tennessee Titans Philadelphia Eagles at Seattle Seahawks at Los Angeles Rams Jacksonville Jaguars New York Giants at Washington Commanders Dallas still gets to play New York one more time so they can at least impact things in a direct sense that one time. They are far from out of the woods, but this outcome made a division title, and therefore playoff appearance, a little bit less silly to talk or dream about. For what it’s worth, the Commanders (3-5-1) are also now a factor. Their remaining schedule could see them find a way, too. Cincinnati Bengals at Arizona Cardinals at Tennessee Titans Houston Texans Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings at Jacksonville Jaguars Dallas Cowboys The dream lives another day. As you were.

title: Understanding the Cowboys and their lack of motion
summary: “Motion” is one of those buzzwords that has been talked about a lot with the Dallas Cowboys as of late, specifically about how the team is not incorporating it as often as people would like. How much would you like, even? Well, more than the current rate. This is the general sentiment to be clear. […]
full_text: “Motion” is one of those buzzwords that has been talked about a lot with the Dallas Cowboys as of late, specifically about how the team is not incorporating it as often as people would like. How much would you like, even? Well, more than the current rate. This is the general sentiment to be clear. Football fans look at modern offenses and how they are running things and they see a lot of motion. They see the statistical findings that list the top offenses deploying it at high rates. So when Cowboys’ offensive play-caller Brian Schottenheimer is not utilizing it all too often, especially after pledging to when he got his current job, people notice. Very recently, after the loss to the Arizona Cardinals, Schottenheimer was being grilled on his motion rates and noted that falling behind in games changes the calculus for him. This was an interesting answer and not one that I had ever personally heard a coach give before. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer on why Dallas' motion usage rate hasn't been the same this season: "We certainly have them in. I think without having the list in front of me, we believe in moving and shifting and motioning and things like that. Sometimes you don't do it when… pic.twitter.com/aXnceSKRjS — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) November 4, 2026 Brian Schottenheimer cites playing from behind as one of the main reasons why they haven't used as much motion in 2026. The Cowboys led all of Week 8 until the Cardinals' game-tying touchdown in the fourth quarter. Out of 28 teams to play last week, Cowboys ranked 18th in… — Mauricio Rodríguez (@MauNFL) November 4, 2026 It stood out a bit, clearly. Why abandon motion when you are behind? What is the thought process behind that? Motion is hardly an advanced concept, but there may be advanced reasoning. When I had the chance to speak to FOX’s Greg Olsen earlier this week, thanks to AWS and Next Gen Stats, I asked him about Schotty’s stance on the matter. You can watch our entire conversation below. Regarding Olsen’s thoughts on Schottenheimer’s quote on not being able to run motion as often when you are trailing in a game, here is what he had to say: “I don’t know if it’s necessarily like just that black and white like A and B. I do think there is an element to if you look at the teams that use motion at really high rates it’s a very specific style right. It’s under center. They’re more condensed formations. It’s in the play action game. It’s in the run game. There’s pre-snap movement horizontally at the snap. You know, you, the offenses you think of are like the Shanahans and like that style right. So when you get to shotgun spread just wide numbers to numbers, formations, shotgun, one back, right. Whether it’s 11 or 12 but let’s just say it’s 11. There are a lot of teams from a protection standpoint and just from a coverage identification standpoint they don’t like changing strengths.” “They don’t like bringing CeeDee Lamb from a three by one. He’s the number 2 receiver and all of a sudden we motion him to the left and now we’re in 2 by 2. Well we just moved the nickel. We just changed where the safety was. The offensive line now started this is a three by one now it’s a two by 2. What are our pass set rules? So there is a conversation a lot of quarterbacks feel this way a lot of coordinators feel this way in more of those gun pass.” “Now so if the assumption is “Hey we’re losing,” getting under center and running play pass all game doesn’t really help us ’cause they’re gonna just play pass as we play catch-up. That certainly makes sense to me if that’s what. Again I don’t know the quote from Schotty, I’m just going off what you said there is. So that would probably be my answer. If you feel like you’re coming from behind and I just gotta operate 11 personnel, put Dak in the gun, CeeDee on one sid,e George on the other side, mix and and just go play pass offense. 7 on 7 to go win the game, maybe change of strength doesn’t really have the effect it does under center run play pass.” “’Cause what you’re trying to do under center run play pass is you’re trying to change gap responsibilities of the defenders in real time and oftentime the guy I’m bringing into the run fit I have guys running routes in his pass coverage responsibility. So you don’t really have that when you’re in 2minute mode spread gun play from behind. So outside of motion just undressing man zone motion getting a free release where they can’t come up and jam me. Like there’s elements to that but it probably doesn’t have the greater effect it does in that other style of play which you wouldn’t probably do when you’re losing.” To be honest, this was way more of a justification than I thought was possible. It was very interesting to hear Olsen, justify may be the right word, but explain the potential rationale that Schottenheimer might be operating with these days. As noted, Olsen took time to chat with us thanks to AWS and Next Gen Stats which now offers NFL League Trends as a result of their work and technology. This tool, Next Gen Trends, powered by AWS, is free to use for all fans and is a ton of fun to play around with: You can access it right here . What do you think about the point regarding Schottenheimer and motion? Is it fair? No? Somewhere in between? Let us know in the comments below.

title: 2026 Week 10 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: The Cowboys’ victory over the Colts last week, despite all of the frustrations that came with it, allowed them to keep hope alive in the NFC East and improve in the NFC wild card race. As improbable as playoff contention feels right now, the win in Indianapolis preserved enough mathematical possibilities that we’ll keep looking […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys’ victory over the Colts last week, despite all of the frustrations that came with it, allowed them to keep hope alive in the NFC East and improve in the NFC wild card race. As improbable as playoff contention feels right now, the win in Indianapolis preserved enough mathematical possibilities that we’ll keep looking at things with unabashed optimism. Sitting 13th in the NFC standings before last week, Dallas rose three spots as the Buccaneers, Cardinals, and Falcons all lost and fell to 3-6. Arizona and Tampa’s head-to-head wins over the Cowboys make it especially important that they stay firmly behind us. Still, the NFC playoff scene looks pretty exclusive right now. The top five teams are easily San Francisco and the entire NFC North. Whichever teams come out of the NFC East and South are likely fodder for their eventual wild card opponents, even with home games. That said, many fans would still love to see the Cowboys rally and make the playoffs, however brief their postseason run may be. Here’s how they’re currently situated in the big picture. Current 2026 NFC Playoff Standings 1. San Francisco 49ers 7-1 (4-1 vs NFC) 2. Chicago Bears 7-2 (5-2) 3. New York Giants 5-2-1 (3-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers 3-5 (3-3) 5. Detroit Lions 6-2 (4-1) 6. Minnesota Vikings 6-2 (4-1) 7. Green Bay Packers 6-3 (4-3) _______________________________ 8. Seattle Seahawks 5-4 (2-3) 9. Los Angeles Rams 5-4 (3-2) 10. Dallas Cowboys 4-5 (2-4) Unfortunately, there’s little chance of Dallas building momentum this week as they host the conference-leading 49ers. Barring a total stunner, the Cowboys’ probable drop to 4-6 could allow some of those 3-6 teams to creep back above them in the standings. It’s only Week 10, though, so there’s still ample time to rectify it. Aside from Dallas shocking the world with an upset over the Niners, what else should Cowboys fans be rooting for this week? NFC East teams Commanders d. Giants The last time these two met, it ended in a tie in Washington. The rematch in New York is predicted to go the Giants’ way, but it wouldn’t be a huge surprise if the Commanders pull it off. Between the NFC East race and a motivational boost before their own game, Washington’s success would be a beautiful thing for the Cowboys. The Eagles are on a bye this week, putting their disastrous season on a much-needed pause. NFC vs. NFC Vikings d. Packers Panthers d. Saints Cardinals d. Rams Minnesota at Green Bay is mostly a toss-up. Both are at six wins and helping build the NFC North’s wall around playoff spots. But the Packers’ first-round pick makes for an easy tiebreaker, with the hope that they eventually fall out of the tournament and keep the Cowboys’ likely draft position no worse than 18th. Someone has to win the NFC South (seems like we say this every year), so it might as well be Carolina. The best thing for Dallas is that they get hot and put losses on all of their division rivals, especially Tampa Bay, to keep them off our backs. While Arizona does have that pesky head-to-head avantage over us, the Rams are actually between us and a wild card spot right now. Los Angeles is more like to find a late-season groove, so they’re the bigger threat. NFC vs. AFC Patriots d. Lions Chiefs d. Falcons Raiders d. Seahawks Easy interconference picks this week. Detroit and Seattle are hurdles to jump in the Wild Card race, and Atlanta is right behind at 3-6. While having a vested interest in New England losing, given the seventh-round pick they owe us, a Lions loss could be more beneficial. AFC vs. AFC Jaguars d. Titans If you’re going to pay attention to any all-AFC games this week, the Titans are the Cowboys’ next opponent. Their season is already trashed at 1-7, and we’d like them to stay deflated when they head to Dallas next Sunday. With Chicago and Tampa Bay also on byes, it’s a light week for the NFC. The Cowboys are up against it with Niners, so hopefully the other Week 10 action helps to mitigate the likely damage.

title: How the Cowboys offensive line matches up with the 49ers defense
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have a tough task this week when they host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys plan to launch an upset, they will need a balanced offense that gives Dak Prescott time to work. Here is how the Dallas offensive line matches up with the 49ers defensive line. Trench Dashboard Here […]
full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have a tough task this week when they host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys plan to launch an upset, they will need a balanced offense that gives Dak Prescott time to work. Here is how the Dallas offensive line matches up with the 49ers defensive line. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 53% (8th) Run Block Win Rate – 69% (31st) Pressure rate allowed – 30% (15th) Sacks allowed – 14 (4th) Last three-week trend: Run game finding life The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Nick Bosa is back, and Terence Steele should expect attention The season statistics can be misleading with San Francisco. The 49ers have only 15 sacks, ranking 27th in the NFL. That does not sound particularly frightening. But the defensive front Dallas faces Sunday is not the same one that produced most of those numbers. Nick Bosa returned against Las Vegas after missing five games with knee and calf injuries. He immediately played 39 defensive snaps and produced two pressures. San Francisco also brought DeForest Buckner back in a trade with Indianapolis. Bosa currently has an 89.6 overall PFF grade in his limited action this season. Before suffering the calf injury, he had generated six pressures on only 41 pass-rush snaps and was winning 20% of his rushes. That brings Terence Steele into focus again. Steele’s current 58.6 PFF overall grade ranks 59th among 70 qualifying tackles. Before Indianapolis he had allowed 17 pressures and two sacks. Bosa moves around, so Tyler Guyton will see him as well. But whenever San Francisco puts Bosa over Steele, that is the matchup Dallas should worry about. Steele winning enough one-on-one snaps could decide how aggressive Dallas can be offensively. PRESSURE POINT: San Francisco suddenly has an intimidating interior rotation DeForest Buckner was playing for Indianapolis only two weeks ago. Buckner currently has 21 pressures and six sacks, with a 72.9 pass-rush grade. San Francisco can now rotate him alongside former Cowboy Osa Odighizuwa. Odighizuwa produced three pressures against Las Vegas last week and led all 49ers defenders with an 84.4 pass-rush grade. He now carries a 51.6 overall season grade after the game. That creates a very different problem from simply stopping Bosa. Dallas has Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker at guard, with Cooper Beebe between them. That is arguably the strongest part of this Cowboys offensive line. San Francisco is going to test it anyway. Buckner is huge and can use his length to keep blockers away from his body. Odighizuwa wins more with quickness and already knows many of the Cowboys linemen extremely well after spending five seasons in Dallas. Dallas cannot allow pressure from the middle to combine with Bosa attacking from outside. If that happens, Prescott will have nowhere to move. Where to Attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the 49ers soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Use the screen game against San Francisco’s aggression Trying to simply run through San Francisco may be the wrong answer. The 49ers are allowing only 81 rushing yards per game, second-best in the NFL, and their 3.33 yards allowed per carry ranks first. Over their last six games, opponents have averaged only 70.5 rushing yards at 3.1 yards per carry, and Las Vegas managed just 24 rushing yards at 1.6 per carry last week. Dallas cannot spend Sunday repeatedly running straight into that wall. This is where screens become important. San Francisco has allowed running backs to catch 6.8 passes per game, the highest in the league. That gives the Cowboys an opportunity to use the 49ers’ aggression against them. Suddenly the defenders charging toward Prescott are on the wrong side of the play. GREEN LIGHT: Make the 49ers prove the upgraded rush can finish San Francisco’s defensive line looked much more dangerous against Las Vegas, but it still produced zero sacks. The 49ers generated plenty of disruption but they could not bring the quarterback down. Their sack rate sits around 5%, also near the bottom third of the league. Dallas has allowed 14 sacks, ninth-fewest, and its 3.8% sack rate allowed ranks fifth. That is where the Cowboys have to trust themselves. If San Francisco sends four rushers, Dallas should be willing to protect with five meaning they do not automatically keep extra players in protection because of the names standing across the line. Dallas needs as many receiving options as possible against Fred Warner and a talented 49ers secondary. The Chaos Report Here are the San Francisco 49ers defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 15 (28th) Pass Rush Win Rate – 49% (20th) Run Stop Win Rate – 29% (22nd) QB Pressure Rate – 27% (22nd) Last three-week trend: Front is fully loaded Matchup of the week Terence Steele vs. Nick Bosa There really is only one choice this week. When Bosa lines up opposite Steele, watch them. Steele is coming off one of his better run-blocking performances of the year against Indianapolis, earning an 81.7 PFF run-blocking grade, but pass protection still remains the concern. Bosa does not need five sacks to ruin the afternoon, one quick pressure can end a drive on third down. Steele’s job is simple to describe but extremely difficult to execute, keep Bosa outside. If Steele can survive without constant help, Brian Schottenheimer can send tight ends into a route instead of leaving him to help the tackle. Best Route to Success Dallas does not need to try and prove they can overpower the NFL’s best run defense. That would be playing directly into San Francisco’s hands. Dallas should still run the football. Williams is coming off a big game and the offensive line just produced one of its better run-blocking performances of the season, but this week requires more variety with screens, quick passes, counters, and play-action. Injury Updates: Dallas has quite the lengthy injury report so far this week, but none of the starting offensive linemen are on the list. Jake Ferguson’s injury situation is the biggest injury among potential blockers. The biggest confirmed San Francisco injury up front is Gracen Halton. The rookie defensive tackle suffered a fractured and dislocated ankle against Las Vegas and is expected to undergo surgery and move to injured reserve. C.J. West is also trying to return from IR after a knee injury he suffered in September.

title: 49ers coaching excellence spotlights the Cowboys recent struggles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have lost four straight games to the San Francisco 49ers, and that fact alone isn’t even really the main reason the Cowboys are seen as significant underdogs for the latest rematch. That would be more due to the 49ers being tied for the league lead with seven wins while making no excuses […]
full_text: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have lost four straight games to the San Francisco 49ers, and that fact alone isn’t even really the main reason the Cowboys are seen as significant underdogs for the latest rematch. That would be more due to the 49ers being tied for the league lead with seven wins while making no excuses for the rash of injuries they always seem to overcome. The 49ers started the season 6-0 with wins over all three of their division rivals in the books by week five, beating the Rams in Australia in week one, the Cardinals in week three, and Seahawks in Seattle in week five. A winning standard and a high level of effort and execution have been evident from the 49ers under Kyle Shanahan for a very long time now. The Cowboys have come into these matchups against the49ers with talented rosters, even home field advantage as well, but different iterations of coaching staffs that haven’t stacked up. This has led to lowlights like a season ending on Ezekiel Elliott playing center and snapping the football, or Dak Prescott having to fight both the 49ers defense and the sun in his own stadium. Throw in the Green Bay Packers, and they along with the 49ers tell the complete story of Cowboys playoff failures in recent times. The last Cowboys playoff loss to a team that wasn’t one of these sides was in 2018, to the Rams. Their last one before that was 2009, to the Vikings. Despite the Packers having the more recent playoff win against the Cowboys at JerryWorld, it’s the 49ers that give the peak behind the curtain into the failures of America’s Team. Each loss from the 2021 playoffs to the 2024 regular season loss (the only one of the current streak against the 49ers that came in Santa Clara) can be attached to a season where the Cowboys made coaching changes in the offseason. The Cowboys beat the 49ers at home in Mike McCarthy’s first season back in 2020, but missed the playoffs. Making the tournament the following year, despite losing in the Wild Card at home 23-17 to these 49ers, was seen as enough progress from year one to two under McCarthy to keep the brain trust of Kellen Moore as OC and Dan Quinn as DC in place for 2022. The Cowboys matched the 49ers in a lot of ways in that 2021 playoff loss statistically, but threw the ball 43 times compared to 21 rushes at just 3.7 yards per carry, and also committed 14 penalties. The same coaching staff and same 12-5 Cowboys the next year had to earn their trip to the 49ers by winning a Monday night Wild Card game at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Even having this momentum on their side did little to help how they came out against the 49ers, still looking overmatched and losing 19-12. The Cowboys defense didn’t allow a touchdown until the fourth quarter when Christian McCaffrey broke a 9-9 tie with the score that proved to be the game winner. This time around, Kellen Moore didn’t survive the loss, as the Cowboys moved on and hired Brian Schottenheimer as OC, while Moore went to the Chargers. After all the unforgettable toxic back and forth about Moore no longer being the right fit because he didn’t run the football enough to “rest the defense”, year one under McCarthy and Schottenheimer ended with the team falling behind 34-10 at home in the playoffs and having to throw the ball 60 times. That year’s Cowboys also lost 42-10 to the 49ers on primetime in week five, the worst loss to the 49ers in franchise history. This time around, Quinn was the coordinator that did not survive the embarrassment, and the Cowboys hired Mike Zimmer as defensive coordinator. All this got the Cowboys was a closer regular season loss to show against the 49ers in week eight, losing on the road again 30-24. By season’s end with no playoff berth in sight, McCarthy was not brought back, making way for Schottenheimer to become the current head coach. The bar to clear of expectations is low for Schotty in his first head coaching matchup against Shanahan and the model of consistency 49ers, which is ultimately the first problem with how standards have slipped in Big D. Just giving his team a chance to win by doing what Jerry Jones said earlier in the week it would take, stitching together the absolute best of what the Cowboys have done all at different times in all three phases, would be a huge win – even if that doesn’t manifest on the scoreboard. Anything short of an actual win in the books though would leave the Cowboys with even more dirt to dig out of to make the playoffs, backed into the familiar position of searching for their first back-to-back wins deep into November around Thanksgiving time again. The Cowboys are not in good company with the Jets, Dolphins, Titans, winless Chargers, Commanders, Saints, and Cardinals as the only other teams to either not have consecutive wins at any point this season. Meanwhile, the 49ers have already secured a six-game winning streak to start this season for the second year in a row, and have had a streak of six games or longer in all but one season since 2022. The 49ers have earned the right to look at this as any other game and come in with confidence to separate from the Cowboys early before thinking about the Vikings, Seahawks, and Rams in three of the next four weeks. The Cowboys have the unenviable task of coming out with their hair on fire and pulling out all the stops to score an upset, looking to do so against an opponent they’ve been outclassed by four times in a row. This applies to both on the field and on the sidelines, and how each side either helps or hurts the Cowboys this Sunday is something to bookmark as a potential turning point for the entire organization yet again. A win would be the Cowboys first against an opponent with a winning record since Week 12 of last season against the Eagles, a comeback from down 21-0 that carries a lot of weight when it comes to finding an example of a Schottenheimer-led team showing fight and winning. That too could be at jeopardy with a bad loss to the 49ers, as the more recent examples of the Cowboys having to fight came by way of trying to not blow a lead against the Cardinals and failing, and just hanging on against the Colts. Interestingly enough, the 49ers also had a 14-0 lead against the Cardinals this season and saw Arizona cut it to 29-27 in the fourth quarter, but unlike the Cowboys, they closed it out with another touchdown to win it on their terms. The only other common opponent coming into this game favors the 49ers on all fronts too, as they had to deal with four full quarters of Jayden Daniels when hosting the Commanders, something the Cowboys only got one half of. The 49ers flexed in primetime and led 23-3 in the third quarter, winning 23-17. A Cowboys loss would see the 49ers tie the Cardinals in beating the Cowboys for a fifth straight time, and both teams would trail only the Broncos for longest active streaks against the Cowboys. The Broncos have beaten the Cowboys eight straight times, and you guessed it, are another team these 2026 49ers have beaten 24-14 this season. There’s a lot working against the Cowboys this week, injuries included, and if coaching is yet again one of them in a big way to doom this team to a similar fate of 2025, we could very well be talking about the 49ers as catalysts for change in Dallas on this front by season’s end.

title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 10
summary: Fresh off a thrilling 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, the Dallas Cowboys return home on Sunday to host the red-hot San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys want to record their first winning streak since last November, they’ll need to bring their A-game against one of the league’s best teams. Before the two teams square […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a thrilling 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, the Dallas Cowboys return home on Sunday to host the red-hot San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys want to record their first winning streak since last November, they’ll need to bring their A-game against one of the league’s best teams. Before the two teams square off on Sunday, here are two players the Cowboys should use more in the matchup. 1) EDGE James Houston One pain point for Dallas’ defense this season has been their inability to consistently take down the opposing quarterback. While the Cowboys defense is tied for fifth in the league in pressure rate (32.8%), they have accumulated only 17 total sacks as a team, tied for the sixth-fewest. One change the Cowboys made in the past few weeks to help their struggling pass rush group was activating 27-year-old edge Jame Houston for their last three matchups. Houston, who played just 13 defensive snaps before Dallas’ Week 8 matchup against Arizona, made a big impact in his first outing with increased opportunities. In that game against the Cardinals, Houston recorded two pressures and a sack on just 11 pass-rush snaps. The former sixth-round pick had a 27.3% win percentage in that contest, the highest of any Cowboys defender, to go with a PRP of 13.6. After an impressive performance, Dallas rewarded him with more chances against the Colts. Houston played a season-high 31 defensive snaps with 18 pass-rush opportunities. While the 27-year-old couldn’t quite replicate his pass-rush success from a week prior, he recorded a 69.3 pass-rush grade on true pass sets, with a 12.5% TPS win percentage. If the Cowboys want the best chance to improve their pass rush, they need to keep increasing Houston’s usage on defense. Dallas should give Houston some of Donovan Ezeiruaku and Von Miller’s snaps to see if he can continue his upward trajectory. 2) S Alijah Clark The Cowboys defense got some unfortunate news after Sunday’s win. Safety P.J. Locke suffered a concussion and has already been ruled out for this week’s matchup against the 49ers. If the Cowboys are going to continue to play Caleb Downs primarily in the slot, Downs played 35 snaps there on Sunday; they’ll need someone to replace Locke as their second primary safety. Dallas’ coaching staff has shown an affinity for giving Markquese Bell chances when they had injuries to both starting safeties early in the year, but given how poorly Bell has performed, it’s time to give Alijah Clark the nod. Clark played 40 defensive snaps against the Eagles a few weeks back, allowing just one catch for nine yards in coverage. While Clark may not be as sure of a tackler as Bell, he is without a doubt more skilled in coverage. Dallas should give Clark the job to start alongside Malik Hooker and see if he can perform better than Bell has.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Cowboys have weapons to challenge the 49ers
summary: The Cowboys moved to 4-5 with a dramatic 27-23 win over Indianapolis and now return home for one of their toughest tests of the season. San Francisco is 7-1, but Dallas enters Sunday having won two of its last three and is coming off a very productive offensive yardage performance. Sure, the Dallas offense had […]
full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys moved to 4-5 with a dramatic 27-23 win over Indianapolis and now return home for one of their toughest tests of the season. San Francisco is 7-1, but Dallas enters Sunday having won two of its last three and is coming off a very productive offensive yardage performance. Sure, the Dallas offense had issues scoring which was hampered by penalties and two critical turnovers, but they still produced 508 total yards. Dallas outgained the Colts 508-271 yards on offense, producing 329 passing yards and another 179 on the ground. The Cowboys averaged 7.2 yards every time they snapped the football. CeeDee Lamb was almost unstoppable in Indianapolis. He caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown, his second-highest receiving total in an NFL game. He now has 904 yards and seven touchdowns this season. San Francisco also left its latest game with cornerbacks Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir both day-to-day with injuries. If either is limited, Prescott should waste no time looking toward Lamb. Javonte Williams also reached the century mark against Indianapolis, carrying 20 times for 101 yards and the game-winning touchdown. He now has 629 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns this season. Keeping that balance is crucial against the 49ers. It slows down the pass rush and prevents San Francisco from simply attacking Prescott every down. On the 49ers defense, Nick Bosa returned against Las Vegas, while DeForest Buckner made his return to San Francisco. Yet the 49ers finished the game with zero sacks. San Francisco have only 15 sacks entering that game, which is fourth-fewest in the NFL. The 49ers have dangerous names up front, but Dallas has reason to believe Prescott can be protected. As for San Francisco’s offense, it’s dealing with a major injury problem. Christian Kirk has been placed on injured reserve. Mike Evans is not expected to be ready for this week, while Deebo Samuel is only expected to return to practice Wednesday after missing time with a hamstring injury. That doesn’t mean San Francisco lacks weapons. Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle remain major problems. But taking established receivers away from Brock Purdy makes the job easier for a Dallas secondary that has struggled this season. If Dallas wants to beat San Francisco, slowing McCaffrey has to be near the top of the list. The encouraging part is what happened last Sunday. Jonathan Taylor entered the game as Indianapolis’ biggest offensive weapon. Dallas held him to just 46 rushing yards. That was one of the Cowboys’ best run-defense performances of the season. McCaffrey presents a different challenge because of his receiving ability, but Dallas has at least shown it can stop a high-level running back from controlling a game. So sticking with the Cowboys defense, Quinnen Williams forced a fumble last week, and rookie safety Caleb Downs grabbed his first NFL interception to seal the victory in the final minute. That comes after the defense produced five sacks and two takeaways against Arizona. The 49ers are the heavy favorite, but the Cowboys have weapons that give the team at least a puncher’s chance.

title: Broncos eager to use bye week to prepare for the stretch run
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos head into their bye week in a really good spot. After a great road win in Charlotte against the Carolina Panthers, the Broncos sit at 7-2. The bye comes after a gauntlet of a start to the season, in which Denver played some of the best teams in […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on against the Carolina Panthers during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos head into their bye week in a really good spot. After a great road win in Charlotte against the Carolina Panthers, the Broncos sit at 7-2. The bye comes after a gauntlet of a start to the season, in which Denver played some of the best teams in the NFL. For now, the Broncos lead the AFC West standings, are near the top of the AFC playoff seedings for home-field advantage, and are clearly one of the best teams in the league. Now, with some injuries and guys dinged up, the bye comes at a great time. We’re in a really good spot, obviously where you want to be,“ Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media after the win over the Panthers. ”You want to be first in your division. You want to be winning football games. We’ve played a really tough part of our schedule. At 7-2, we feel really confident, but at the same time, there’s a lot of things that we could get better at. We’ve said this every week, and some weeks we’ve gotten better at other things; some things we still got to clean up. “But overall, we’re finding explosive plays, doing better on third down today, stayed out of the third-and-long situations like we’ve been wanting to do. At the end of the day, we scored enough to win the game, and that’s what’s important going into the bye.” At least for Nix, he loves the bye week. As he said after the Panthers win: “You get stuck in Groundhog Day over time doing the same thing over and over every week. I can tell you exactly what I’m doing every day of the week, so this will be a good break, good rest for us. We all feel really good about it, feel like we need it, our coaches. We’ll get some rest. Players will get some rest, and then we’ll start right back up next week with our next opponent. It’s just going to be a good time to relax and also debrief and look back at a few things and just have a great breakdown and sort of digest where we’ve been and what we’re doing and where we want to go.” Since coming to Denver, Sean Payton knows how to handle the bye week and has the post-bye week figured out. The Broncos are 3-0 coming out of the bye under Payton. A big reason why is the time off he gives the players. What waits for Denver after the bye is the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 22 at home. “I think I told you guys this. I went two or three years practicing on Wednesdays and Thursdays, and we were OK. I can’t recall the year, but I called (Kansas City Chiefs head coach) Andy (Reid) one year in Philly. He was 9-0 after the bye … and he just said I get them out of here, and I see them the next Monday. And ever since we’ve done that, we’ve been pretty good after the bye as well. So, they’ll rest. The guys getting treatment will be in, and everyone else will. At some point, we’ll get a jump start on Vegas.” Given how close the Broncos like to play and win their games, the bye comes at a great time for the fans, too. Broncos links

title: NFL picks and predictions: Week 10 of the regular season
summary: Welcome back to the tenth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 9, I did extremely well. I was 14-1 with my picks, with the only loss being from choosing the New England Patriots who wound up getting obliterated by the Green Bay Packers. In all my years of doing […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Devon Key #26 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after defeating the Carolina Panthers 26-21 at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the tenth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 9 , I did extremely well. I was 14-1 with my picks, with the only loss being from choosing the New England Patriots who wound up getting obliterated by the Green Bay Packers. In all my years of doing this, the perfect slate of games remains elusive. With last week’s picks, I’m up to a 90-47 record on the season. That helped boost my pick accuracy up to 66-percent. This week there are just 14 games with the Denver Broncos, Chicago Bears, Philadelphia Eagles, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers all on their bye weeks. Washington Commanders at New York Giants — Thursday Night Football This week kicks off with an NFC East rivalry game on Thursday Night Football . The Giants have a multi-lead game in the NFC East with a 5-2-1 record. The Commanders are third place in the division at 2-5-1. This is a huge game for the Giants, who have a huge shot at extending their division lead with a victory. I feel confident they can take care of business at home. Winner: Giants New England Patriots at Detroit Lions — Sunday (Morning Game) The Patriots were walloped by the Packers in Week 9 and the Lions were able to defeat the lowly Miami Dolphins. I have a feeling this will be a close game, but Detroit needs to find a way to rattle Drake Maye who is coming off a three-interception performance. I like the Lions in this one. They need this win to keep pace in an ultra-competitive NFC North. Winner: Lions Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints — Sunday (Early Game) The Panthers had the Broncos on the ropes last Sunday but faltered in the fourth quarter and came up with a loss. Meanwhile, the Saints were able to squeak out an overtime victory over the Browns. Both of these teams sport a 3-5 record. Oddly enough, it’s a gridiron affair whose winner will become the top team in the division. I’m going to roll the dice and take the Panthers on the road. I liked what I saw from them against the Broncos and feel they will find a way to rebound in Week 10. Winner: Panthers Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennesee Titans — Sunday (Early Game) Jaguars General Manager James Gladstone went all in trading a bounty of picks to land multiple players to improve their defense in pursuit of a Lombardi Trophy. At 6-2, they have a commanding lead in the AFC South and have a chance to strengthen that with a win over the 1-7 Titans. I expect that to happen. Winner: Jaguars Buffalo Bills at New York Jets — Sunday (Early Game) The Bills are riding a four-game winning streak, and the Jets have dropped four in a row. I don’t think this AFC East battle will be close at all. I fully expect Josh Allen and Buffalo to take care of business on the road and hold onto the top seed in the AFC playoff race. Winner: Bills Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons — Sunday (Early Game) The Chiefs have a chance to pull to 7-2 alongside the Broncos in the AFC West if they can take care of business on the road against the Falcons. They made a trade for wide receiver Josh Downs to bolster their passing offense which has been hit-or-miss throughout the season. I like the Chiefs here, but their defense will have to play well and slow down Bijan Robinson in order to win on the road. Winner: Chiefs Miami Dolphins at Indianapolis Colts — Sunday (Early Game) The Colts were clearly sellers before and at the deadline and will be certainly looking to rebuild their team and identity this season. However, they did choose to keep running back Jonathan Taylor, who was pursued hard by multiple teams before the trade deadline. Neither of these teams are playing well, but I’m feeling like the Dolphins can find a way to win this one. I’d imagine the pulse in the Colts’ locker room right now is a bit vacant given the departure of so many players. Winner: Dolphins Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers — Sunday (Early Game) The Vikings have dropped two in a row, and their quarterback play is a big reason for it. On Tuesday, they sent off a third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders to bring back a familiar face—Kirk Cousins. Whether that addition will be good enough for them to compete in the NFC North down the stretch remains to be seen. I bet against the Packers last week but won’t be doing that this weekend. Jordan Love is on a heater right now. I’m anxious to see how he does against a great Vikings defense. Winner: Packers Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns — Sunday (Early Game) CJ Stroud and the Texans were able to ignite on offense against the woeful Los Angeles Chargers in Week 9. Stroud had an incredible game throwing for nearly 400 yards and torched the Chargers’ defense for five touchdowns. I don’t expect as much success against Cleveland, but they need a win to keep their playoff hopes alive. I believe they’ll pull through with a big road victory here. Winner: Texans Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders — Sunday (Afternoon Game) With Kirk Cousins in Minnesota, top pick Fernando Mendoza now will now be the man to lead their team the rest of the way out. His first NFL start won’t be easy going up against a top-tier Seahawks defense. I expect him to struggle in his first outing given such. I’ll be taking the Seahawks on the road here. Winners: Seahawks Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Rams are now 5-4 on the season after winning three in a row. Their last loss was in mid-October versus the Cardinals. Even though they are banged up, I don’t expect the same result this time. Myles Garrett was phenomenal last week, and I think their defense will be able to hold down rookie Carson Beck, who will get his first NFL start on Sunday. Winner: Rams San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The 49ers added veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline Brock Purdy another weapon on offense. Their wide receiver corps is incredibly banged up. Even though the 49ers have endured a ton of injuries this season, they are still 7-1 and one of the best teams in the NFL. Dallas has really struggled this year and are underperforming preseason expectations. I like San Francisco on the road in this one. Winner: 49ers Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals — Sunday Night Football This AFC North rivalry game on Sunday Night Football will decide who is the top team in the division. Both are riding four game winning streaks, and the Steelers have had an extra week to prepare for this matchup. Even so, I’ll be taking the Bengals here due to their elite offense that has already posted 240 points this season. I don’t think the Steelers can keep up with that. Winner: Bengals Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens — Monday Night Football The Chargers continue to scrape the bottom of the barrel and are still winless on the season. It’s uncertain whether or not Justin Herbert will play on Monday Night Football due to a hand injury suffered in last week’s loss to the Texans. It’ll be up to Jacoby Brissett to lead the Ravens to victory in primetime with Lamar Jackson being on injured reserve. This will probably be a messy game, but I expect the home team to win. I’ll take Baltimore here. Winner: Ravens

title: Will the Broncos make any changes to the starting lineup over the bye week?
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are 7-2 and hold the AFC West lead for now. That record is impressive all things considered. If you would have told me that would have been their record before the bye, I would have respectfully disagreed given the gauntlet of opponents they have played to date. There […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Ben Powers #74 of the Denver Broncos jogs off of the field during halftime of an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are 7-2 and hold the AFC West lead for now. That record is impressive all things considered. If you would have told me that would have been their record before the bye, I would have respectfully disagreed given the gauntlet of opponents they have played to date. There is no doubt the Broncos have a lot of room for improvement. They haven’t been at their best but are certainly trending in the right direction. Over the next week, Denver will have the opportunity to rest, recuperate, and also do some reflection on what they’ve accomplished this season. Moreover, what they need to do moving forward to have the best shot at earning the franchise’s fourth Lombardi Trophy. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton spoke with Colin Cowherd on the status of the team. If you haven’t had a chance to watch the interview, you certainly should at the link above. One of big questions was Cowherd asked for was Payton’s assessment of the offense in the first half of the season. “The cool thing about the bye right now is you really get a chance and zoom, and look really close what’s been going well, what hasn’t, and why hasn’t it been—and let’s not be kidding ourselves,” stated Payton. He went on to exert extreme confidence in Bo Nix. The third-year quarterback hasn’t made the huge jump fans were expecting this year. Nevertheless, Payton was adamant that the team has the right signal caller behind center. Despite some struggles, he is happy with what he has seen from Nix going up against some very tough defenses. Payton went on to talk about what they can do to set up Nix for better success in the second part of the season. Without hesitation, he discussed a position group that has experienced some regression this season at a few positions—the offensive line. “I’m watching the cutups from the game we just played [versus the Carolina Panthers]. We didn’t block them very well. I’m just being honest—that has to improve. We have plenty of depth on the offensive line. During this bye, we’re going to look at all those little things closely,” added Payton. I’m certainly not an offensive line expert by any means. Though I think it’s safe to say the Broncos have only had two consistent starters in their offensive trenches. Those would be left tackle Garett Bolles and right guard Quinn Meinerz. When it comes to center Luke Wattenberg, left guard Ben Powers, and right tackle Mike McGlinchey—all three have struggled and haven’t been at their best this season. I’d be skeptical that the Broncos would consider benching McGlinchey. I also find it hard to believe they would bench Wattenberg for Alex Forsyth. However, I wouldn’t be surprised if Powers was replaced. Last season when he got hurt, Powers was replaced by Alex Palcewzki and he performed admirably. Well enough for Denver to give him a multi-year extension this offseason. Powers had a restructure that lowered his base salary significantly but upped his guarantees. As noted in a feed post yesterday, Powers has struggled this season. In nine games, Powers has been credited with 14 blown blocks per SIS Data Hub . Ten of those have been pass blocks with four of them credit against the run. Though based on the eye test, I’d say they are drastically underestimating his issues paving lanes for the Broncos’ backs in the run game. We’ll just have to wait and see if the Broncos wind up making a change on their offensive line. Based on Payton’s discussion with Cowherd, that seems like a legitimate possibility. Denver certainly has to be better up front in the trenches if they want to be top-level competitors the rest of the way. What do you think, Broncos Country? Should Denver make a change on the offensive line? If so, what position and who do you feel should be inserted into the starting lineup. Sound off in the comments section and let me know. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Detroit Lions vs. New England Patriots preview, prediction: On Paper
summary: The Detroit Lions and New England Patriots are in Germany for a big international matchup. The Patriots are a bit desperate for a win, sitting at 5-4 and clinging to the final playoff spot in the AFC. The Lions are a little more comfortable in the fifth spot of the NFC playoff race, but if […]
full_text: Nov 12, 2026; Munich, Germany; Detroit Lions hats with 2026 NFL Munich Game patch at the NFL Shop Munich. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions and New England Patriots are in Germany for a big international matchup. The Patriots are a bit desperate for a win, sitting at 5-4 and clinging to the final playoff spot in the AFC. The Lions are a little more comfortable in the fifth spot of the NFC playoff race, but if they want to contend in a competitive NFC North, they need this game, too. So which team has that statistical advantage and will come out on top Sunday morning? Let’s dive into the numbers with our Week 10 Lions vs. Patriots On Paper preview and prediction. Note: Stats may be a little lighter this week because one of my bigger resources—NFL Pro—is not available in Germany. Lions pass offense (12th in DVOA) vs. Patriots pass defense (15th) The Detroit Lions had their worst passing offense performance last week against a bad—but improving—Dolphins defense. Offensive line struggles were the lowlight of the performance, headlined by the “suspension” of left guard Christian Mahogany and inconsistent play of rookie right tackle Blake Miller. Mahogany is back in the lineup, and that should help the Lions’ passing offense which has remained near a top-five unit for most of the season. They rank: Fourth in passer rating (106.5) Seventh in yards per attempt (7.8) Fourth in dropback EPA (0.237) Fourth in dropback success rate (51.0%) And despite the poor offensive performance, the Lions offensive line is still grading out well as a unit. Though they rank 17th in sack percentage (6.5), they’re fifth in pressure percentage allowed (19.4%), second in PFF pass blocking grade (75.1), and seventh in pass block win rate (54%). The Patriots pass defense started off strong, but has struggled as of late, even against some of the most medicore-to-bad passing offenses. For the season, they rank: 27th in passer rating (100.2) 25th in yards per attempt (7.9) 24th in dropback EPA (0.151) 25th in dropback success rate (48.4%) For comparison’s sake, all of these rankings except for dropback EPA are below the Lions’ pass defense. So whatever you think of Detroit’s ability to defend the pass, the Patriots have been worse. But much like Detroit’s pass defense, the one place they thrive is pressuring the opposing quarterback. Thought they’re just 19th in pressure percentage (22.4), they’re sixth in sack rate (8.0%), 11th in pass rush win rate (52%), and second in PFF pass rush grade (82.8). While EDGE Elijah Ponder leads the team with 7.5 sacks, it’s really New England’s interior pressure that causes havoc. Look out for Christian Barmore (78.1 PFF pass rush grade) and Milton Williams (20 pressures) to give Detroit’s interior offensive line some issues. But New England’s second is very beatable. Christian Gonzalez is having a down year (50.4 PFF grade) and the Patriots will be down Carlton Davis. Player to watch: Amon-Ra St. Brown. This isn’t just a Germany thing, St. Brown should thrive against the Patriots’ zone-heavy defense. Brown is the Lions’ best weapon when it comes to recognizing the soft spot in zones, just like last week’s eight-catch, 86-yard performance. Advantage: Lions +2.5. The Patriots’ pass rush does have a chance to disrupt Jared Goff like the Dolphins did last week, but for most of the day, the Lions quarterback should be picking apart this poor secondary. Lions run offense (4th) vs. Patriots run defense (10th) The inconsistency of this rushing attack is still very frustrating to watch, but putting things into perspective, it’s still a very decent run game in Detroit. For the season, they rank: 10th in yards per carry (4.4) 12th in rush EPA (-0.073) Third in rush success rate (46.0%( Negative plays remain a huge problem, with Detroit’s 20% stuffed rate ranking 25th in the NFL. They are improving in short-yardage situations, though, climbing to 18th in power success rate. Still, the offensive line—though still plagued by some mental mistakes—appear to be moving people. Detroit ranks fourth in adjusted line yards, eighth in run block win rate, and, as a whole, the Lions entire team is fourth in PFF’s run blocking grade. Detroit will face a formidable test this week against a run defense that has allowed 100 rushing yards just three times this entire season, and each of their last five opponents have been held at or below 4.0 yards per carry. Though last week’s performance against the Packers’ worst rushing attack in the league should provide at least some hope. For the season, the Patriots rank: Ninth in yards per carry allowed (3.9) 10th in rush EPA (-0.123) 11th in rush success rate (36.9%) Interestingly, the Patriots run defense appears more efficient than the sum of their parts. They rank just 16th in adjusted line yards allowed, 16th in run stop win rate, and 21st in PFF run defense grade. One thing they do thrive in, however, is limiting explosives. They’ve only allowed six rushing plays of 15+ yards (third fewest) and just a single run of 20+ yards (t-fewest). But they’re just okay in short-yardage situations. They’re 10th in power success rate allowed (59%), but sport just a 16% stuffed rate (23rd). Player to watch: LB Christian Ellis. While the Patriots are not particularly strong up the middle in run defense, Ellis sports the eighth-best PFF grade against the run (82.3), providing a strong second level of defense. The Patriots’ secondary is also active and strong against the run. Advantage: Lions +0.5. Detroit hasn’t been as explosive as expected running the football this year, but they have found some consistency running for gains of 5-10 yards, and that could be exactly what we see on Sunday. Patriots pass offense (6th) vs. Lions pass defense (24th) Despite a horrible start to the year, Drake Maye has seemingly righted the ship—outside of last week’s performance against a very solid Packers pass defense. For the entire year, the Patriots pass offense ranks: 11th in passer rating (96.2) Third in yards per attempt (8.4) 10th in dropback EPA (0.162) Third in dropback success rate (51.0%) Essentially, if the Patriots could stop turning the ball over, they’d be a top-five passing attack. But turnovers have been a serious problem. Maye’s 11 interceptions leads the league and his 4.0% interception percentage is third-highest in the NFL. To sport that dishonor and still produce the 10th-highest dropback EPA is pretty crazy. So what’s causing the high interception rate? It’s a little bit of everything. An injured offensive line that ranks 21st in pressure rate (23.6%) and 18th in sack rate (6.6%), a quarterback who is still young and figuring things out, and a receiving corps that lost Romeo Doubs for the season and hasn’t had a lot of A.J. Brown available. But, again, the Patriots passing attack remains pretty dang efficient despite those problems. I’m still hesitant to believe in Detroit’s defensive improvement through the air. Much of that appears based on simply playing a bunch of poor passing attacks, but the one aspect they have seriously improved on is explosive plays allowed. In the first four games, the Lions allowed 20 passing plays of 20 yards (most in NFL). In the last four games, the Lions have allowed 14 (still t-10th most). For the season, Detroit still only ranks: 24th in passer rating allowed (97.5) 18th in yards per attempt (7.2) 26th in dropback EPA (0.177) 24th in dropback success rate (48.3%) The pass rush (eighth in sack rate, seventh in pressure rate) remains solid, despite an ever-decreasing blitz rate (26.3%, 18th). Detroit will be without top cornerback D.J. Reed for at least another week, but Brian Branch’s return has allowed them to have a little more flexibility in their coverages, and it has calmed some things down (a little). Player to watch: Hunter Henry. While Henry is far from 100% as he deals with a foot injury, he remains the biggest threat to Detroit’s…

title: Before the Roar: Previewing Detroit Lions vs. New England Patriots
summary: After a gritty, grind-it-out win in Week 9 over the Miami Dolphins, the 6-2 Detroit Lions are set to cross the Atlantic for a Week 10 clash with the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. As part of the NFL’s continuing efforts to grow the league’s popularity on a global scale, this trip for Detroit […]
full_text: After a gritty, grind-it-out win in Week 9 over the Miami Dolphins, the 6-2 Detroit Lions are set to cross the Atlantic for a Week 10 clash with the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. As part of the NFL’s continuing efforts to grow the league’s popularity on a global scale, this trip for Detroit feels as though it has been in the works for a while—especially given the roots of All-Pro receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. To preview the inter-conference matchup, my good friend Meko Scott and I are back with the newest iteration of “Before the Roar.” For starters, we dive into the play of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Simply put, Maye is an ascending player with all the athletic upside a team could want in a modern-day NFL quarterback. At the same time, New England’s offense has been a boom-or-bust unit for most of the season, and Maye is at the center of many of those turnover struggles. From there, we discuss how New England will adjust to losing their top two running backs and what the Lions’ defense can do to make Maye’s trip to Germany one he’ll soon want to forget. On the defensive side of the ball, we highlight New England’s stout run defense and how Detroit can counter their aggressive front seven. We also highlight some of the struggles the Patriots have been dealing with in their secondary. Cornerback Carlton Davis III has already been ruled out, and Christian Gonzalez has struggled since returning from injury earlier this year. To catch the whole episode, you can watch here , as well as listen wherever you get your podcasts. If you haven’t already done so, please be sure to like and subscribe to the Pride of Detroit YouTube channel so you can stay up to date on all of the content we are putting out, including our annual charity drive taking place in November.

title: Discussion: Which NFL trade do you wish the Detroit Lions had made?
summary: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Detroit Lions made just a modest move. They sent a 2029 sixth-round pick for depth safety Andre Cisco. While Cisco had been taken out of the starting lineup for the New York Jets—who are sporting a solid duo of Dane Belton and Mikah Fitzpatrick at […]
full_text: Lions GM Brad Holmes speaks to the media on Tuesday, Jan.11, 2022, in Allen Park. Lions | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Detroit Lions made just a modest move. They sent a 2029 sixth-round pick for depth safety Andre Cisco. While Cisco had been taken out of the starting lineup for the New York Jets—who are sporting a solid duo of Dane Belton and Mikah Fitzpatrick at the position—he comes to Detroit with plenty of playing experience and a knowledge of their system, having played under Aaron Glenn. It appears Cisco will have a role quickly with the team. “We would like to get him going ASAP,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said Wednesday. “We’d like to get him going. He’s obviously going out to Germany with them. Our plan is to get him going in this game and let him help us a little bit. How much? That’s not quite there yet, but we do have a plan for him to help us.” For many fans, that move wasn’t enough to move the needle for the Lions. They were hoping for a bigger splash, and potentially some help at the linebacker and cornerback positions. So today’s Question of the Day is: Which move made at the NFL trade deadline do you think the Lions should have made? My answer: First, let me explain why I asked the question this way. Many people are mad that the Lions didn’t go out and get a player like Riq Woolen, Zack Baun, or Donte Jackson. But it’s hard to get mad at a move no one made, because we don’t know what conditions were required to trade for those players. Were they even available to trade for? Did the Lions try aggressively to acquire one, but the team wasn’t offering them at a reasonable price? Did the Lions ignore those players completely because they didn’t view them as scheme fits? It’s impossible to informatively critique the Lions for failing to make a move when we have zero reliable knowledge on what it would’ve taken to acquire those players. Those conversations feel like a waste of time and energy. However, we do know the conditions it took to trade for players who were moved over the last few weeks. We know for certain that they were available for trade, and we know (around) what it would’ve cost Detroit to acquire said player. So, among the moves that were made over the past few weeks, which one appeals to you the most? YOU CAN SEE THE FULL LIST OF TRADES MADE IN-SEASON HERE IN OUR TRACKER Interestingly, since the Joey Porter Jr. trade over a month ago, there have only been a few defensive trades made: Bears trade for DT Jeffery Simmons 49ers trade for DT DeForest Buckner Jaguars trade for DT Davon Godchaux Jaguars trade for S Jessie Bates Bills trade for S Amani Hooker Lions trade for S Andre Cisco Then two trades that were agreed upon fell through: Bengals trading for EDGE Arnold Ebiketie and Broncos trading for LB Daiyan Henley. So, essentially, zero trades were made at positions of need for the Lions. I saw many wishing they had traded for Henley (Broncos were going to spend a fourth and 2028 fifth-round pick for him), and at this point, it’s unclear why the trade did not go through. I will say, I’m intrigued by the other safety moves that were made. I think Jessie Bates is a game-changer, but a second-round pick for a half-season rental is a bit pricey for a Lions team that is getting healthier at the safety position right now. Hooker is a younger option who is signed through 2028 and comes with reasonable price tags of $9.57 million in 2027 and $11.8 million in 2028. If the Lions don’t believe Kerby Joseph will be around beyond this year, this could’ve been a very savvy move for what amounted to a second-round pick with a fifth-round pick in return. However, the trade I keep going back to is the Joey Porter Jr. one. I still think that’s a move I would’ve made (cost the Cowboys a sixth and a 2028 second-round pick). While Porter has struggled with injuries with Dallas, his play on the field has been as advertised. I thought he was a great scheme fit, and a potential long-term option for a position Detroit has struggled to find consistency at. I wrote more about why I thought the Lions should’ve traded for Porter Jr. back in October . Which trade deadline move, that was actually finalized, do you think the Lions should have made? Share your thoughts in the comment section below.
