title: Vikings sign former Green Bay Packer
summary: The Minnesota Vikings signed running back Damon Bankston, a former Green Bay Packer, to the team’s practice squad this week. Bankston spent Weeks 1- 7 with Green Bay, over two stints, before the team needed space on their own practice squad. This addition is interesting, as Bankston could have some info on how the Packers […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings signed running back Damon Bankston, a former Green Bay Packer, to the team’s practice squad this week. Bankston spent Weeks 1- 7 with Green Bay, over two stints, before the team needed space on their own practice squad. This addition is interesting, as Bankston could have some info on how the Packers want to attack the Vikings’ pressures. As we all know, Minnesota blitzes at a crazy rate. According to Pro-Football-Reference , they have the Vikings down with a 67.6 percent blitz rate, with the next highest team in the league being the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 37.2 percent. Because of the extra blitzers, many offenses allocate extra blockers to face the Vikings, most notably running backs. Bankston was not only in Green Bay when the team prepared to play Minnesota in Week 1, but he could also have information on the adjustments the protections made coming out of that game. If I were defensive coordinator Brian Flores, I’d want to pick the brain of the new addition, wouldn’t you? The Packers made a similar addition to their practice squad ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Vikings — which could be viewed as gamesmanship. Green Bay signed safety Kahlef Hailassie, who has been with Minnesota since 2025, ahead of the season opener. Hailassie is no longer with the Packers. We’ll have to see how long Bankston sticks with the Vikings, or if they only wanted his services for this particular week.
author: Justis Mosqueda

title: Will the NFC North Teams All Win 10 Games?
summary: In NFL history, no division has ever seen a last-place team win 10 games. It sort of almost happened in the NFC North last year, as the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions all finished with 9 wins, and in 2023 the Cincinnati Bengals finished last at 9-8 (and had several chances to […]
full_text: (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) In NFL history, no division has ever seen a last-place team win 10 games. It sort of almost happened in the NFC North last year , as the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions all finished with 9 wins, and in 2023 the Cincinnati Bengals finished last at 9-8 (and had several chances to get to 10), but that’s kind of it for close calls. Prior to 2002, the NFL had 5-team divisions, and so this was functionally impossible. And since the league went to a 17-game season in 2021, it is much more likely now. The four teams of the 2026 NFC North are all quite good , and all have at least six wins as we enter week 10. No team is perfect, but the Lions have an outstanding offense, and their defense has improved with some players like safety Brian Branch getting healthy. The Vikings have a truly elite defense and have now re-added quarterback Kirk Cousins for the stretch run. The Bears and Packers have both been quite good on both sides of the ball, with the Packers slowly fixing their offensive line, and the Bears adding defensive lineman Jeffrey Simmons to help shore up their defense. These teams will all continue to win games. In short, there’s a great chance that this division winds up with every team at 10-7 or better. I put together a very, very simple projection for the rest of the season (I want to stress how simple this was; it’s ugly, in Excel, and I made it primarily to work through what happens based on who wins the remaining division games, because I kept messing this up), and every team finishes with 10 wins in 30% of simulations. Every team finishes with 11 in almost 5%! (Yes, it is mathematically possible for every team to finish with 12, but it’s extremely unlikely.) Weird hypothetical projections you made while Outlook was down are one thing, so let’s try to be more concrete. The Bears have seven wins in the bag, and while they have some very tough games against Buffalo and Jacksonville, they also get the Saints and Dolphins, which almost surely gets them to nine. They would then need just a single division game (of their four remaining, two against Detroit, one each against Minny and the Packers) to get it done. The Vikings have six in the bag, with games remaining against the Commanders, Jets, Falcons, and Panthers. That might get them to ten without any additional help, but they also have three division games left, one against each North team, in addition to a tough battle with the 49ers. The Lions also have six in the bag with non-division games against the Giants, Titans, Falcons, Bucs, and Patriots, teams that range from “meh” to “atrocious. Even if they fail to win four of those, they still have the Bears twice, and the Vikings and Packers each once. And our Green Bay Packers, who sit at six wins, get the Rams without receivers Davante Adams or Puka Nacua, the Saints, the Dolphins, and the Texans, in addition to a tough matchup with the Bills. They will also face the Vikings in Kirk Cousins’ first game back, and one more each with the Bears and Lions. When you look at it like this, you can really see how the ten-win scenario is really pretty likely, and how the eleven-win scenario is downright plausible. Even in this analysis, I focused primarily on the out-of-division games. Remember, someone HAS to win the in-division games, too; they are not just hypothetical. Let’s take a look at a fairly negative scenario for the Packers as an example. Let’s assume the Bears and Lions split their remaining division games, each going 2-2, with the Vikings going 2-1, and the Packers finishing 1-2 in their remaining division games. That means, before accounting for any of the aforementioned trash out-of-division games, the Bears are 9-4, the Lions are 8-5, the Vikings are 8-3, and the Packers are 7-5. This puts the Packers in the worst spot, but still needing just three wins between New Orleans, Miami, Houston, an undermanned Rams team and Buffalo. It’s pretty likely! And in the event the Bears drop an additional division game or two, bolstering the Packers/Lions/Vikings, remember they have a one-game lead. So, unless the division falls apart, this is VERY likely to happen. The Packers have the misfortune to play in one of the best divisions in the history of football. And I, for one, cannot wait to travel to the 7-10 NFC South champions for the first round of the playoffs.
author: Paul Noonan

title: Packers Injury Report: Trey Smack was a full participant on Thursday
summary: Before Thursday’s practice, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said part of why the team had only a jog-through instead of a full practice on Wednesday was the number of players banged up on the roster. The good news? The team had a full practice on Thursday. The only change in the Packers’ participation […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before Thursday’s practice, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said part of why the team had only a jog-through instead of a full practice on Wednesday was the number of players banged up on the roster. The good news? The team had a full practice on Thursday. The only change in the Packers’ participation today was that kicker Trey Smack, who was estimated to be a limited participant on Wednesday, was a full participant on Thursday. Here were all the players who were non-participants today: S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee) LB Zaire Franklin (shin) RB Josh Jacobs (finger) C Sean Rhyan (ankle) EDGE Lukas Van Ness (back) TE Josh Whyle (concussion) LaFleur said that Jacobs hasn’t had his surgery on his right ring finger yet. He also stated that defensive lineman Warren Brinson, currently on the injured reserve, is about five weeks out from his calf surgery. If the Packers are down just those six players from their 53-man roster, they’ll only have 47 spots filled for the 48-man game-day roster on Sunday. That’s assuming that the team does some weird stuff with their roster, too, like keeping 10 offensive linemen on the game-day roster. My guess? They think a couple of these non-participants are going to be able to go. If not, the Packers are going to need to shut down players via the injured reserve just to piece together a game-day roster with practice squad call-ups this week. Javon Bullard missed today's practice with ankle/knee injuries. Here's what he said after practice: "I ain't missing no game, man. I care about this team. I care about my brothers, man, so I'm definitely going to play Sunday." — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) November 12, 2026 Safety Javon Bullard is already adamant that he’s going to be playing on Sunday. He, along with Lukas Van Ness, was able to finish the game against the New England Patriots last week, despite not participating in the last two practices for the Packers. The following players were limited participants today: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip) RB Chris Brooks (ankle-IR) OL Travis Glover (knee) LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness) WR Skyy Moore (ankle-IR) ED Micah Parsons (knee/illness-PUP) WR Savion Williams (groin) OL Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps) In total, 11 players were either non-participants or limited on Thursday, not including the 14 players already on the team’s injured reserve or physically unable to perform lists. The bye week is going to be much needed.

title: Green Bay Packers news: Packers ground game may be turning a corner.
summary: Ladies and gentlemen. It took 9 games. But we did it, Joe. For the first time in the 2026 season, the Green Bay Packers accumulated more than 100 rushing yards in a game. Please clap. Sarcasm aside, Sunday’s 129-yard performance against New England was indeed an encouraging development. But how did it happen? And can […]
full_text: (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) Ladies and gentlemen. It took 9 games. But we did it, Joe. For the first time in the 2026 season, the Green Bay Packers accumulated more than 100 rushing yards in a game. Please clap. Sarcasm aside, Sunday’s 129-yard performance against New England was indeed an encouraging development. But how did it happen? And can the Packers build on it? Perhaps the biggest boon was the long awaited emergence of shadowy veteran guard Kevin Zeitler, who finally took his first real snaps since signing with the Packers in late September. Coach Matt LaFleur has been cagey for weeks about why Zeitler hadn’t played yet and when fans could expect to see him. On Sunday, Zeitler stepped in to relieve an injured Aaron Banks, was benched for a short time as Banks attempted to return to action, but ultimately was re-inserted back into the lineup. For what it’s worth, it almost felt like a soft benching for Aaron Banks. With Zeitler in, Laken Tomlinson shifted to left guard, and the overall impact was immediately noticeable, particularly in the running game. As Rcon wrote earlier this week, Green Bay averaged 4.93 yards per carry on Zeitler’s 15 run-blocking snaps, compared to just 3.18 without him. And not to cherry pick stats (insert cherry-picked stat), if you remove the garbage time snaps with Tyrod Taylor on the field, the Packers actually averaged 6.25 yards per carry with Zeitler on the field. It’s a minuscule sample size, but the film showed a veteran doing exactly what Green Bay needs from its interior offensive line: winning assignments, creating space and giving runners somewhere to go. Speaking of runners, let’s talk about Kaleb Johnson. With Marshawn Lloyd out and Josh Jacobs leaving early with a fractured finger, Johnson took advantage of an expanded opportunity, finishing with 68 yards on 14 carries and his first career touchdown. It wasn’t a banner day, but in an otherwise juiceless backfield, Johnson showed he has at least some juice. And not for nothing, but in almost every game he’s played in, he’s broken off one explosive run play. One game doesn’t solve Green Bay’s rushing problems, but I do think it’s shown that being better than the worst run game in the league is not only possible, but perhaps even likely. It’s a low bar, but a guy can dream. Do the Packers finally have an answer at running back? After months of ineptitude, the Packers averaged 4.0 yards per carry against the Patriots. Much of the productivity was led by second-year running back Kaleb Johnson. ICYMI: Kevin Zeitler looked like Kevin Zeitler on Sunday It’s time for Matt LaFleur and company make the permanent switch at the right guard position. Brenton Cox is outplaying his price tag Edge defender Brenton Cox, a former undrafted player, has thrived under Jonathan Gannon and will hit unrestricted free agency for the first time in 2027. LISTEN: Toyotathon is on, and Jordan Love is balling One can’t help but admire how well Jordan Love continues to play in the face of consistent pressure and with no help from the run game. Why Packers’ Jordan Love is the 2026 midseason MVP Love is doing more with less and doing it better than every other quarterback in the NFL through nine weeks of the 2026 season Packers discussion in the Feed Kirk Cousins to Minnesota was inevitable. Now that it’s happened, how worried do you feel about Sunday’s matchup against the Vikings? The Feed is the place for you to share whatever it is you want to talk about, big or small. Head over to the editor to start writing today! Go Pack Go—wherever you go! title: Are the Houston Texans ascending or pretending?
summary: Life as a fan of the Houston Texans is all about tempering expectations. They don’t seem to bump along the runway forever, but can’t seem to maintain cruising altitude either. We’ve all seen them light up an opponent one week, then struggle and fall the next. This begs the question: which version of the Texans […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 8: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans gestures during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Melina Pizano/Getty Images) | Getty Images Life as a fan of the Houston Texans is all about tempering expectations. They don’t seem to bump along the runway forever, but can’t seem to maintain cruising altitude either. We’ve all seen them light up an opponent one week, then struggle and fall the next. This begs the question: which version of the Texans takes the field against the Cleveland Browns this Sunday? Do you think this team is about to go on a winning streak that ends in the playoffs? Or, will they pull out the old-reliable jumbo offense, forgot-how-to-tackle defense and let former Texans quarterback Deshawn Watson lead his Brownies to a win? Vote: Are the Texans ascending or pretending? | Battle Red Blog Personally, I think the Browns are going down. We told you so! First off, for all the people out there who raged about C.J. Stroud over the off-season. For the ones who called him trash, wanted him gone, swore up and down he was the worst QB on earth: you were so, soooo wrong. So wrong. After the absolute clinic he put on last weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers, throwing 35 passes for 21 completions, 384 yards, 125.5 passer rating, 5 touchdowns and only 1 interception, Stroud took home his 2nd AFC Player of the Week honor. He’s now the only player in the league to win it twice this season. AFC Players of the Week! (Week 9) @CJ7STROUD | @StoneColdJones | @cameronglittle pic.twitter.com/Ep3ACjpuu5 — NFL (@NFL) November 11, 2026 Still not convinced? Think Stroud’s game was a fluke? Doubling down on your silly belief that he isn’t all that? How about this: QBs to throw 350+ yards and 5+ touchdowns in multiple games at age 25 or younger: – C.J. Stroud – Dan Marino – Patrick Mahomes – Matthew Stafford Stroud is also the first Texans QB in team history to have multiple games of 350+ yards and 5 TDs. ( @NextGenStats ) — Jacob Barzilla (@JacobBarzilla) November 9, 2026 CJ Stroud this season: 2,251 Passing Yards 16 TD 2 INT Patrick Mahomes, Aaron Rodgers, Drew Brees, and Tom Brady are the only other QBs in NFL History to record or exceed these numbers with 2 or fewer interceptions through 8 games. pic.twitter.com/xl0PibQPxR — Bradeaux (@BradeauxNBA) November 9, 2026 C.J. Stroud is the best QB in the league against the blitz by a wide margin pic.twitter.com/dPi7GpKStX — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 10, 2026 C.J. Stroud gets it done on the CRITICAL down pic.twitter.com/gvdgIPxC9v — PFF (@PFF) November 10, 2026 Before you write off what Stroud did because the Chargers were 0-7, look at what Stafford, Mahomes and Allen did against that same defense. They threw for one touchdown combined. Stroud threw for five. Give him, Caley and the offense some credit. Or don’t. 😂 https://t.co/VOY2JVzm53 pic.twitter.com/ttD7x2t2x4 — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) November 9, 2026 Now that we’ve established Stroud is clearly not the problem, let’s take another minute to bask in the glory of it all: NICO COLLINS, ARE YOU KIDDING ME?!? 🤯 (via @HoustonTexans ) pic.twitter.com/zv7Zrgbuf0 — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 8, 2026 These angles of the 63 yard TD from C.J. Stroud to Tank Dell 🤌🏻 🎥 @HoustonTexans TT, @SomosTexans IG pic.twitter.com/BREkF4tTNW — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) November 8, 2026 C.J. Stroud and Kayshon Boutte with a 63-yard TD 👏 HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d6CjZxnTHH — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 TRENDING: Video compilation of Houston #Texans Pro Bowl quarterback C.J. Stroud’s five-touchdown performance against the Los Angeles #Chargers in Week 9. What do you notice about Stroud…? 👀👀👀 pic.twitter.com/Pm7PcmCZEC — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 9, 2026 Ok, now that we’ve settled that. Time to look ahead. Houston Texans vs. Cleveland Browns The Cleveland Browns are currently 5-4, have the 29th ranked offense, 17th ranked defense and lost a nail biter last weekend to the New Orleans Saints 22-23. At first glance, it seems like this should be a close game, particularly with Watson facing the team that dumped him in Cleveland with no bus fare back to H-Town. However, the Browns offense doesn’t have the stroke to stop Will Anderson Jr. and 10 of his best friends. Spencer Fano and (former Texans) Tytus Howard are currently ranked as #1 and #2 worse tackles in the NFL. For every Juice Scruggs who leaves the Nick Caley system to overachieve elsewhere, there’s a Tytus Howard who makes Caserio look like a genius for shedding him as one of the last vestiges of Bill O’Brien’s GM incompetence. Anderson Jr. is currently the NFL’s leading sack-master, with 9.5 on the season. Browns left tackle Fano has given up 8.5 sacks. Watson was sacked 62 times in his 2018 campaign with the Texans. While a lot of those were poor blocking and bad scheming, quite a few were on Watson for holding the ball too long. Hold the ball too long this Sunday, with Fano trying to ward off Anderson Jr. as Howard looks to stop Danielle Hunter, Sheldon Rankins and/or Jadeveon Clowney and Watson is going to have a long, long day. Here's a look at the worst 10 starting tackles in the NFL right now when it comes to pressures allowed. And man, do I have bad news for the Browns… pic.twitter.com/Mby8wczjTd — Henry McKenna (@henrycmckenna) November 11, 2026 DE Will Anderson Jr., DE Jadeveon Clowney and DT Sheldon Rankins have become the first Texans trio to each record at least 2.0 sacks in a single game in franchise history. — Houston Texans PR (@TexansPR) November 8, 2026 It’s honestly possible for the Texans defense to top last week’s 8 sacks when facing off against the Browns’s tackles. The 8 qb drops ties a team record. Could Deshaun Watson go down (pun intended) in the history books as the most sacked QB in a game vs the Texans? That would certainly feel right. 9 sacks? 10? The front 7 has to be drooling at the prospects… The Texans tied a franchise record with 8 sacks in a single game against the Chargers on Sunday. Here’s a cutup of all 8: pic.twitter.com/qYpdXqCEs7 — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) November 9, 2026 Will Anderson Jr. leads the NFL with 9.5 sacks through nine weeks, and up next? 👀 The Cleveland Browns, who have allowed an NFL-high 38 sacks this season. For perspective, the next closest team is Philadelphia with 31. pic.twitter.com/HKPBjvRJSf — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) November 11, 2026 What might stop the good guys from bringing home another dub? Despite Stroud’s amazing effort last week, the Texans still have no run game and no answer at tailback aside from Woody Marks. They let the trade deadline come and go without landing a starting level running back, which also means Caserio didn’t overpay for one. Rumor has it the Indianapolis Colts were holding their breath for a 1st round draft pick in exchange for Jonathan Taylor. Regardless, the Texans head into Cleveland with a smash mouth run game that lacks the capability to smash any mouths. Another X-factor is the defense. Did Coach Ryans’ back-to-basics tackling drills help refocus this crew? They held the Chargers to only 9 points through the first 3 quarters. LA only made 14 first downs and converted a measly 5 third downs into firsts. For perspective, the Chargers entered last week’s game with the 32nd ranked offense and 20th ranked defense. Marginally worse than the Browns are this week. Will Caley have a running game or rely solely on Stroud again? Will the defense continue their return to 2025 form or backslide? How these things play out will certainly impact the Monday mood. Which takes us back to the opening question: are the Texans ascending or pretending? From the looks of things, we’re climbing the hill. Hopefully we’ll still feel that way come Monday morning. #GoTexans

title: Texans stats 2026: How effective have Houston’s pass catchers been this season?
summary: There are any number of ways to look at the effectiveness of an offense or defense. We have been alternating throughout the season on Thursdays to look at one unit or the other. Sometimes the numbers within the numbers reveal things that the overall numbers do not. For instance, when we look at the offense […]
full_text: Photo by Melina Pizano/Getty Images | Getty Images There are any number of ways to look at the effectiveness of an offense or defense. We have been alternating throughout the season on Thursdays to look at one unit or the other. Sometimes the numbers within the numbers reveal things that the overall numbers do not. For instance, when we look at the offense we see that it is succeeding in a number of ways. Obviously, we have looked at the lack of a run game over and over again, but when we look at the overall numbers we see something different. Points per game: 26.1 (9th) Total Yards per game: 356.5 (11th) Yards per play: 5.8 (8th) Turnovers: 4 (1st) Sacks: 16 (10th) So, essentially the Texans are a top ten offense when you look at scoring, total yards, turnovers, and sacks allowed. They are only really deficient in terms of running the ball. However, there are some cracks in the veneer and they came to the forefront when Nick Caley appeared before reporters for his press conference during the bye week. He was asked about tendencies and it became very obvious that he was not aware of them. Self scouting is always the most important scouting. This seems natural in baseball which has always been my first love. One player hits .300 and the other hits .250. Obviously there are numerous other numbers to come to the forefront, but in general you play the more effective player. This can be seen when we look at the pass catchers on the Texans. We can look at just catches, yards, and touchdowns, but we can also look at snaps, targets, catch percentage, yards per target, and success rate. In other words, who is getting the most playing time and who should be getting the most playing time. We will look at snaps on passing plays only since we are including tight ends and running backs. Snaps Targets Catches Yards Catch% YPT Success Nico Collins 203 39 28 384 71.8 9.8 59.0 Xavier Hutchinson 207 45 24 287 53.3 6.4 46.7 Tank Dell 33 10 5 148 50.0 14.8 40.0 Marvin Harrison Jr. 34 11 6 60 54.5 5.5 54.5 Kayshon Boutte 200 28 19 319 67.9 11.4 64.3 Dalton Schultz 219 47 35 364 74.5 7.7 57.4 Foster Moreau 70 14 11 72 78.6 5.1 57.1 Woody Marks 160 21 15 98 71.4 4.7 38.1 No single number is the holy grail here. All of these numbers work together in concert. For instance, Tank Dell obviously has a lower catch percentage and success rate but he also has the highest yards per target. Obviously, he is valuable as a down the field threat and should probably be on the field as much as possible even given his low catch percentage and success rate. Those measurements don’t account for how much bang the Texans get for their buck and it doesn’t account for how his presence impacts the other receivers. However, there is something glaring that many people have noticed outside of Kirby. Xavier Hutchinson leads the wide receivers in passing down snaps and targets. So, obviously Hutchinson should be the best receiver on the Texans. Unfortunately, the numbers don’t bare that out. He is fourth among wide receivers in catch percentage, fourth in yards per target, and fourth in success rate. I might be nuts, but I’m not seeing exactly what Hutchinson brings to the table. This is the difference between looking at basic numbers and looking at the more advanced numbers. He is on pace to have 51 catches and over 600 yards receiving. He could have four or five touchdown catches at that pace. That feels like a pretty good season for a guy that is a second or third wide receiver. He is likely to be second on the team in catches at that pace. So, of course he is a solid wide receiver right? Except Boutte is a better down the field threat as well and Marvin Harrison Jr. looks like he could be a better possession receiver once he gets acclimated. Not only that, but Hutchinson was getting more snaps than Jaylin Noel who had very similar numbers to Tank Dell before he went down. Obviously there is more to football than just numbers, but it seems logical that you would want the players on the field that are going to be the most successful the most often. That has never been Xavier Hutchinson. Even when you go back to the last game you go back to Hutchinson leading the wide receiver group in snaps. That just doesn’t make a whole lot of sense. We realize that Harrison is still adjusting, but Boutte has been here all season and he clearly is more effective. Moving forward you could justify Harrison as WR5 given the numbers, but you could also surmise that he will get better as he gets acclimated to the offense. Moving forward Hutchinson should really be WR4 at the very best. Obviously, Dalton Schultz should be on the field as much as possible too as an underneath or intermediate target if you are going to go with Boutte and Dell as the other two wide receivers. A part of the art of running the most efficient offense possible is putting the best eleven guys on the field as much as possible. That means knowing what you have been doing and whether it has worked or not.

title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 10): Colts fan confidence falls again, down to 17%
summary: The latest SB Nation Reacts survey delivered another troubling update on the state of fan sentiment in Indianapolis, with just 17 percent of Colts fans saying they are confident the team is headed in the right direction. It is another slight drop from last week’s 19 percent mark, and it reinforces just how little confidence […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest SB Nation Reacts survey delivered another troubling update on the state of fan sentiment in Indianapolis, with just 17 percent of Colts fans saying they are confident the team is headed in the right direction . It is another slight drop from last week’s 19 percent mark, and it reinforces just how little confidence remains in the current state of the franchise. At this point, the result should not come as much of a surprise. The Colts have lost five straight games, fallen to 2-7 on the season and spent the last several weeks making major roster changes ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs have all been moved, while other notable players such as Jonathan Taylor, Grover Stewart and Daniel Jones remained with the team despite speculation surrounding their futures. Taken together, it has been a clear sign that Indianapolis is no longer focused on salvaging this season, but instead trying to position itself for a longer-term reset. That does not necessarily mean every fan opposes the direction the organization is taking. In fact, some of this low confidence may simply reflect how painful the current stage of the process looks rather than outright disagreement with the moves themselves. The Colts have finally started making the kind of difficult decisions that a struggling team often has to make, but that does not make the short-term product any easier to watch. Losing games, trading recognizable veterans and entering the second half of the season with significant uncertainty at quarterback, wide receiver and along both lines is not exactly a recipe for immediate optimism. What this number really shows is that Colts fans are still waiting for a reason to believe. The franchise may have started its rebuilding process in earnest, but rebuilding alone does not inspire confidence unless there is a clear sense that the team knows where it is going. Right now, that part still feels uncertain. Chris Ballard is gone, the roster has been reshaped, and the next general manager will inherit a team with more draft capital, but also plenty of holes and no obvious path back to contention in the near future. For now, the fan base remains deeply skeptical. Until the Colts start showing signs of a coherent long-term plan, or at the very least begin putting a more competitive product on the field, it is hard to imagine that confidence number rising in any meaningful way. title: January can’t come quickly enough for the Colts and their fans.
summary: The white flag has already been waived, and now we can simply hope that our remaining players stay healthy enough to fight another day. If they can improve a little along the way, that would be great as well. With the passing of the trade deadline, It is unlikely that the Colts make news nationally, […]
full_text: The white flag has already been waived, and now we can simply hope that our remaining players stay healthy enough to fight another day. If they can improve a little along the way, that would be great as well. With the passing of the trade deadline, It is unlikely that the Colts make news nationally, unless CIG gives Steichen an ultimatum to sit Jones and Shane refuses. Then we would get a new interim coach to toss into the mix and give the talking heads some material. I’m surprised that we are apparently going to finish the season with lame duck coaches. It seems like you would get maximum effort from a coach who wanted to get some experience? I would guess that at minimum, they would be willing to veer from the approach of their predecessor. It could be that they had a different idea of what the call should be in any given situation and could now be allowed to see if they would have any success. They might try some different players or game plan in a different way, or maybe just be willing to sit players that are not performing. This year isn’t much about winning and losing anyway. Some have said that they hate to see the Jets get a top 5 pick, but does it really matter? If they choose a QB, they’ll muck it up anyway. I also do not think the difference between say, 35 – 40, is all that large and I do not know how we could slide past 40 in the 2nd round. This season is seeing what upper level management thinks about their roster, and it’s professionalism and fight. What Carlie should most be concentrating on, is what kind of identity that she believes serves the Colts best, the day after the GM is hired. It should be the main factor in her choice and should become apparent as soon as the GM names a coach. If she has leaned as much as hoped, she knows what she wants to see, and chooses a leader that assembles a roster accordingly. Identity needs to be more of the focus than what sort of offense or defense we will be running. What is our current identity or the one we have taken over during Ballard’s term? Starting with the positives: Ballard was always considered loyal to Colts players. He also had a good reputation among agents as being fair in negotiations. We didn’t do much public airing of anything from the complex. We generally had good citizens and avoided a lot of negative press for player conduct. You might say that the entire building tried to do things the right way. Maybe you do not see all of these as positives. As for the negative: Historically bad starts. Struggles with finishing games and seasons. Prone to laying an egg against weaker competition. A long line of poor defenses, with a reputation for being pushed around. We have extended periods of poor tackling and have had a gap in the intermediate to deep middle for some time now. On offense, other than a brief period last year, we have trouble getting receivers open. We’ve not been able to run screens. We spend a lot of time in shotgun and we don’t have much of a chance if we can’t run the ball. For all of the attempts to play bully ball, it has had only limited success. Oh, the elephant in the room: The inability to find a franchise QB, without the assistance of the first pick of the draft. Since Luck’s retirement, we have banked on an offensive minded coach, far more than letting a QB have much control of the offense. Rivers’ brief run last year, was one of the few times we let the QB react to what the defense was showing. We have won some games, but how often has it been solely based on the play of the QB? For this reason, I’m hoping that a new regime finds a HC that doesn’t really have a hand in the offense, or the defense for that matter. Watch the game and get a sense of adjustments that need to be made, then relay that to your coordinators. I’d like it if the HC that doesn’t come in with a predetermined alliance with either side of the ball, In other words, don’t come in and say we need a shutdown defense and an offense that doesn’t get in the way. Or, a star wars offense, with a defense that just needs a couple of stops or force a couple of FGs to get a win. Spend your time on both sides of the ball in practice and know your personnel. Loyalties can be good, but let the coordinators know that if you think someone needs to be off of or on the field, you will be making that call. Lastly, lets hope that the new GM will hire someone with coaching experience, preferably with positive results. Keep your unproven “genius” types for the coordinator position and let them do what they do. The GM and the HC need to be in lock step, when identifying the QB (and all players for matter) that will lead the Colts to the other side of this rebuild. So, as much as we want to do mock drafts ad nauseum, the important part of the rebuild will happen when CIG and her team steps to the podium and announces our next GM/Personnel Director. From there, we can start building a new identity.

title: After trade speculation, Colts RB Jonathan Taylor ‘moving on’ to get ready for Miami
summary: The NFL’s Tuesday trade deadline came and went, and while other longstanding veteran pillars of the franchise were dealt, Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor somewhat surprisingly remained. Now, the consensus national reporting leading up to the last 72 hours or so before the trade deadline was that unless the Colts were ‘blown away’ by […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs the ball for a first down during the third quarter of the game against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s Tuesday trade deadline came and went, and while other longstanding veteran pillars of the franchise were dealt, Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor somewhat surprisingly remained. Now, the consensus national reporting leading up to the last 72 hours or so before the trade deadline was that unless the Colts were ‘blown away’ by either a ‘Christian McCaffrey’-esque trade package or even a first round pick in an offer for Taylor, that their star workhorse would remain in Indianapolis. That being said, when Taylor was asked whether he wanted to be traded, after seeing All-Pro teammates Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner both recently moved elsewhere, he was rather vague on Thursday in his answer—only responding that he was focusing and getting ready to play the Miami Dolphins at home this weekend: #Colts RB Jonathan Taylor was asked if he wanted to be traded Tuesday, but he didn’t give a clear answer. “Just regular scheduled programming Tuesday. It’s all water under the bridge now. That’s why I was excited to come see you guys … (and) talk about the Miami Dolphins.” pic.twitter.com/AnYwgDwjTs — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 12, 2026 While Taylor had previously indicated that he wanted to retire as a member of the Colts before signing a contract extension in early August, and that he had not requested a trade only a few weeks ago, it’s unclear if his mindset or desires changed once the Colts began a fire sale two weeks ago—and have now launched their ongoing rebuild. On the season, Taylor has 161 carries for 656 total rushing yards (4.1 ypc. avg.) and 8 rushing touchdowns during all 9 starts. He is currently the Colts franchise’s all-time leader in rushing touchdowns (77) and trails only Hall of Famer Edgerrin James as the organization’s career rushing yards (8,254) and carries (1,712) leader respectively. Even though Taylor remained a Colts for the remainder of the 2026 campaign, it’ll be interesting to see if he still is a member of the franchise this offseason—especially closer to the NFL Draft next spring. While he’s the Colts best player right now and remains an elite Top 5 player at the running back position, it’s a fair question with turning 28-years-old in January of whether he still has the prime career longevity left to outlast an Indianapolis rebuild that could (ideally) take only 2-3 years to complete if all goes to according to plan. As it relates to Miami defending Taylor, they’re exactly an average run stopping defense, coming in at 16th league-wide with opposing offenses averaging 111.8 total rushing yards per game.

title: Grading the Colts’ trade deadline: Which moves helped the rebuild and which could backfire?
summary: The Indianapolis Colts were among the NFL’s busiest teams leading up to Tuesday’s trade deadline, parting ways with four established players while electing to retain several others who had generated considerable interest around the league. With the team sitting at 2-7 and preparing for a significant rebuilding period following the dismissal of general manager Chris […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - MAY 06: Indianapolis Colts Assistant General Manager Ed Dodds watches a drill during the Indianapolis Colts rookie camp practice on May 6, 2023 at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts were among the NFL’s busiest teams leading up to Tuesday’s trade deadline, parting ways with four established players while electing to retain several others who had generated considerable interest around the league. With the team sitting at 2-7 and preparing for a significant rebuilding period following the dismissal of general manager Chris Ballard, the organization made it clear that its priorities have shifted toward the future. Over the past several weeks, I examined the potential trade values of Jonathan Taylor , DeForest Buckner , Quenton Nelson and Josh Downs , before taking a closer look at which players Indianapolis should actually consider moving . The Colts ultimately traded three of those four players, along with veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen, while deciding to hold onto Taylor despite receiving multiple offers involving significant draft capital. In total, Indianapolis acquired six draft selections while surrendering one seventh-round pick, leaving the organization with 10 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and another eight in 2028. That is a substantial amount of ammunition for whoever takes over as general manager, particularly with the Colts still lacking their first-round selection in 2027 following the Sauce Gardner trade. However, accumulating draft capital does not automatically make every decision a good one. Some of the trades were necessary and provided excellent returns, while others were considerably more difficult to justify given the players involved and the potential impact on the team’s next competitive window. The same applies to the veterans Indianapolis decided to keep, especially those whose contracts expire after the season. With that in mind, here is how I would grade each of the Colts’ major trade deadline decisions. DeForest Buckner Traded to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick Of all the decisions Indianapolis made ahead of the deadline, trading Buckner was probably the easiest to justify. The 32-year-old defensive tackle remained one of the team’s most productive players, but with his contract expiring after the season and the Colts potentially several years away from returning to contention, retaining him for another eight games offered very little long-term benefit. Buckner had also appeared increasingly frustrated with the organization’s continued struggles, something that was evident throughout his recent interviews. After spending more than six seasons in Indianapolis without experiencing sustained postseason success, an opportunity to return to San Francisco and compete for another championship made sense for both sides. The Colts were unlikely to retain him on another expensive multiyear deal, while Buckner could potentially spend the final productive years of his career playing meaningful football for a contender. Perhaps the biggest reason I supported this trade was the emergence of Adetomiwa Adebawore. The former fourth-round pick has developed into an extremely disruptive interior pass rusher this season, and Indianapolis has since rewarded him with a two-year, $35 million extension. His increased opportunities following Buckner’s departure should provide the organization with an opportunity to evaluate whether he can become a long-term cornerstone of the defensive line, while also allowing the Colts to begin building around a much younger player. In my previous article, I projected that Buckner would fetch a 2027 fourth-round pick, which is exactly what Indianapolis received. That is excellent compensation for a 32-year-old defensive tackle approaching free agency, particularly when considering that any potential compensatory selection would not arrive until 2028 and would depend on several factors outside the organization’s control. The Colts secured a guaranteed draft pick, created additional opportunities for a promising young player and allowed a respected veteran to pursue a championship elsewhere. I have very little criticism of this decision. Final grade: A Quenton Nelson Traded to Seattle for a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick Nelson’s departure is considerably more difficult to evaluate because, unlike Buckner, there is a legitimate argument that he could still have been an important contributor when the Colts eventually return to contention. At 30 years old, Nelson remains one of the NFL’s premier offensive guards and has shown little indication that his performance is beginning to decline. He could reasonably continue playing at a high level for another three or four seasons, meaning he would likely still be a quality starter if Indianapolis manages to build a competitive team by 2028 or 2029. There was also little indication that Nelson wanted to leave, making his departure particularly disappointing for a player who has spent his entire career with the organization. However, the compensation Indianapolis received was undeniably strong when compared with the historical trade market for guards. Kansas City received only a fourth-round pick for Joe Thuney in 2025, despite the veteran coming off another All-Pro season. Nelson is younger and arguably has more productive years ahead of him, but his expiring contract limited the number of teams likely to surrender significant draft capital. Getting a third-round selection and a future fifth is therefore an excellent return from a pure trade-value perspective, particularly considering that Nelson was scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent following the season. My biggest concern is what Indianapolis has actually lost. Nelson was one of the few players capable of consistently dominating his individual matchup, and his presence helped hold together an offensive line that has experienced considerable turnover throughout the past several years. Replacing that level of production will not be easy, and losing him also makes life more difficult for Jonathan Taylor and whoever eventually becomes the Colts’ next franchise quarterback. There is always the possibility that Nelson could return to Indianapolis in free agency, either next offseason or later in his career, although I certainly wouldn’t build the organization’s plans around that scenario. His attachment to Indianapolis makes the idea worth considering, but there is no guarantee he would be interested in returning after establishing himself in Seattle. Ultimately, I understand the reasoning behind this move and believe the Colts maximized his current trade value. However, considering his continued elite production, potential longevity and desire to remain with the franchise, there was an argument for extending him and keeping him. Final grade: B- Keenan Allen Traded to San Francisco for a 2027 sixth-round pick This one is relatively straightforward. Allen was 34 years old, playing on a one-year contract and was never going to factor into the Colts’ long-term plans. The veteran receiver provided some reliability and experience to an offense that has struggled considerably this season, but his presence offered little meaningful value to a team that is no longer realistically competing for a playoff spot. Allen finished his Colts tenure with 40 receptions for 351 yards and one touchdown, demonstrating that he could still contribute as a possession receiver even if he was no longer capable of consistently producing at the level that made him a six-time Pro Bowler. His route running and experience against various defensive coverages remained useful, but Indianapolis had little reason to retain him for the remainder of a lost season when younger receivers could benefit from additional playing time. Getting a sixth-round pick for an…

title: Jaguars Defensive Coordinator Anthony Campanile Talks Trade Deadline Success, Player Fit
summary: On Thursday morning, Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile spoke to the media with a grin as wide as his face would allow. Earlier in the week, Campanile was the recipient of the biggest and boldest series of trade deadline moves the Jaguars had ever undertaken. The Jags spent big but walked away with veteran […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JUNE 10: Defensive Coordinator Anthony Campanile of the Jacksonville Jaguars looks on after Mandatory Minicamp at Miller Electric Center on June 10, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday morning, Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile spoke to the media with a grin as wide as his face would allow. Earlier in the week, Campanile was the recipient of the biggest and boldest series of trade deadline moves the Jaguars had ever undertaken. The Jags spent big but walked away with veteran safety Jessie Bates, defensive tackle Davon Godchaux and, the crown jewel, defensive tackle Jordan Davis. General manager James Gladstone made it clear across the league landscape that he thought his team was close to a Super Bowl. And the man inheriting three top-level players to get said team to the Super Bowl was Campanile. “Obviously really fired up about it,” Campanile said of the deadline acquisitions. “Any time you get three great players, three great people, I couldn’t be more excited about it. The team itself feels the exact same way. They’re working really, really hard. They’re working tirelessly. They’ve been everything everyone said they were.” Coach Camp was quick to mention character fit as much as scheme fit when it came to the trio. Anyone can be traded around at any time, but their willingness to play within a set system with already set players makes a big difference. The second year DC said the three players Gladstone traded for are already immediate culture fits in Jacksonville. “It’s a good fit,” Campanile said. “They’re going to fit in well. And the guys on the team are excited about that. We want to make sure we’re bringing in competitive people and guys that are great teammates and we feel like we did that.” One of those immediate culture fits has been Bates , who was the first domino to fall in the trade deadline haul. Bates was a second-rounder back in 2018 and has been a consummate pro since his drafting. He has earned three Second-Team All-Pro honors along the way, most recently in 2025 with the Atlanta Falcons. Since Bates arrived in Duval County, Campanile isn’t positive his new safety has spent any time at home. “I don’t know if he’s left since he’s been here,” Campanile said. “He’s part of the coaching staff, I think. He loves football. He has a great way about him. It’s like having a coach on the field so he will fit right in with a lot of the other guys here.” Every Jessie Bates interception/forced fumble as a member of the Atlanta Falcons A great player and one of my favorite Falcons ever pic.twitter.com/fHRlEm6Atk — Arkesh Ray (@arkeshrayyyy) November 9, 2026 Campanile noted in Bates’ time in the league, and even in college, he had been coached well. The 29-year-old safety comes to Jacksonville already established with a good foundation, which is something Campanile said of the two defensive tackles as well. The so to say “least flashy” of the three acquisitions was Godchaux, who was with Campanile and the Miami Dolphins in 2020. While he may not have the accolades of Bates or the pedigree of Davis, Godchaux is someone Campanile knows can do the exact job they need him to do. “I have always admired the way he played,” Campanile said. “When we were getting into building things in Miami, he was a really big part of that. When you watch him play, a lot of people can appreciate the technique he plays with. He’s a throwback football player. Super skilled and drilled. I’m very happy he’s here.” Physicality upfront 😤 📺 NFL + | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/u0c8f2AY7E — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 12, 2026 Godchaux fills the run-stopping role left by DaVon Hamilton’s injury. Built almost exactly the same, save about 30 pounds, Godchaux does the dirty work that sets up someone like Davis to come in and finish things off on a crucial third down. Getting a guy like Davis to wreak havoc when needed was a month-early Christmas present for Campanile. “I think he’s phenomenal in every facet,” Campanile said. “He’s been good in every element of being a defensive lineman. He’s a pro’s pro. He’s another guy who’s a skilled technician. I’m fired up to have the guy here. We have high expectations for him.” Despite never having coached Davis previously, Campanile is actually familiar with someone who has: Vic Fangio. Fangio was the DC for the Dolphins in 2023 when Campanile was the linebackers coach. The football-lifer Fangio is about as good as it gets in the NFL, so Camp knew he was getting yet another player who was coached well all along his journey. Fangio served as Davis’ defensive coordinator for his past two seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles. Some run game film from new Jaguars defensive tackle Jordan Davis pic.twitter.com/7A4B1OWTNU — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) November 9, 2026 Both defensive tackles bring something a little different to Jacksonville, but both slot in as perfect puzzle pieces inside Jacksonville’s defense according to Campanile. “It’s hard to imagine getting two better guys that are a better fit for everything we do,” Campanile said. Davis’ new locker sits between former UGA teammate Travon Walker and franchise sack leader Josh Hines-Allen. Between Walker and Hines-Allen, Campanile said he has never been worried they wouldn’t hold their team to the highest standard. The thought is both of them will instill in Davis, along with Godchaux and Bates, the way things are done in Duval. The first such look at the new, vaunted defense will be Sunday when the Jags play the 1-7 Tennessee Titans. Despite the record and the fact the Jags are the only double-digit favorite over the weekend, the Titans are no slouches statistically as of late. Tennessee has scored 20 or more points in three straight games, including 36 in a close overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Even with all his fancy new toys, Campanile won’t be allowing the Jags to overlook their next opponent. “You would be hard-pressed to say they aren’t playing well,” Campanile said of the Titans. “They’re playing offense at a very high level. Their offense has continued to get a lot better. They’re scoring a lot of points and you can see why.” Jacksonville and the Titans kick off Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. If all goes well with the new players learning the verbiage of Jacksonville, Sunday should be when Jags fans see all three new acquisitions and even potentially the addition of defensive end B.J. Green. B.J. Green II brought the McDonald’s at home analogy to the Jaguars’ defense conversation 🤣 #Jaguars #duuuval @MiaOBrienTV pic.twitter.com/VD6NezUJ1z — Action Sports Jax (@ActionSportsJax) November 11, 2026 Comment down below what new Jag you’re most excited to see and why. Can Titans quarterback Cam Ward go another game without an interception? Or will the new-look Jaguars defense smother him into oblivion? Let us know and stay tuned for more Jaguars news and content at bigcatcountry.com .

title: 5 Questions About Jordan Davis: Jaguars Got ‘A Good Vibes Addition’
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jordan Davis! To learn more about Duval’s newest defensive tackle, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Brandon Lee Gowton, who covered Davis’ time with the Philadelphia Eagles over the past four and a half seasons for SB Nation’s Bleeding Green Nation. Question 1: Did […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis (90) runs onto the field against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jordan Davis! To learn more about Duval’s newest defensive tackle, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Brandon Lee Gowton, who covered Davis’ time with the Philadelphia Eagles over the past four and a half seasons for SB Nation’s Bleeding Green Nation . Question 1: Did the Eagles’ decision to trade Davis surprise you? Why did they feel comfortable making the move? I can’t say it was expected after the Eagles just signed him to a contract extension back in March. But pretty much no one would’ve thought that it was possible to get a first-round pick AND a second-round pick for him. The Eagles felt comfortable moving on because the value was simply too good to turn down. In addition, the Eagles reportedly have interest in signing fellow defensive tackle Moro Ojomo to an extension. Keeping Ojomo wouldn’t have been possible with the Eagles having both Davis and Jalen Carter on the books. Now they have a more realistic path to retaining Ojomo. Davis is a good player. But the Eagles making him the eighth-highest paid interior defender in the NFL wasn’t really jibing with how little they trust him to play, especially on pass rush downs: Jordan Davis Snaps played on obvious passing downs (3rd/4th down & 4+, 5+ DBs on field) 2022 : 4/186 (2.2%) 2023 : 19/188 (10.1%) 2024 : 6/208 (2.9%) 2025 : 33/161 (20.5%) 2026 : 10/92 (10.9%) total : 72/835 (8.6%) Davis has 1.5 sacks and 6 pressures on these plays. #Eagles https://t.co/rouXbyXao6 — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) November 9, 2026 Question 2: Jaguars GM James Gladstone has made it clear he’s searching for “intangibly rich” players. What can you tell us about Davis as a person? It’s impossible not to enjoy Davis as a person. He’s very much a good vibes addition to the Jags’ locker room. He’s charming, funny, accountable … the list goes on. His teammates voted him as a team captain this year for a reason. Jags fans will find it very easy to enjoy his personality. With a couple of clicks you can visit Dawgs By Nature and learn everything you need to know about this week’s opponent! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Question 3: Now, for Davis as a player. How would you describe his impact on defense, and where on the field does he play at his best? At his best, Davis is an impactful run defender. He was especially good in this regard last season. His presence as a nose tackle has allowed the Eagles to defend the run from lighter boxes. I’m guessing this is the vision for him in Jacksonville, as well. But he hasn’t exactly been a dominant run defender this year. Perhaps in part because he’s been playing through some injuries. And, as previously noted, he’s not going to provide much in the pass rush department. Though I’m interested to see if the Jags give him more opportunities in that capacity. He’s incredibly athletic, so, maybe there’s still some untapped potential. But he doesn’t always play with great pad level, making him easier to block. I do think it’s fair to say that his impact goes beyond the box score. At the same time, he has 1.5 sacks, 5 TFLs, and 3 QB hits in his last 14 games. You’d like to see a bit more production than that, especially relative to the investment made in him. Question 4: What’s something you learned about Davis during his time in Philadelphia? Off the field? The big man can sing! On the field? His hustle has stood out at times. I think back to his second season in 2023 when he helped to force Josh Allen out on a key play in the game: Or his field goal blocking ability: EAGLES BLOCK THE KICK AND JORDAN DAVIS SCORES A TOUCHDOWN BECAUSE WHY NOT pic.twitter.com/XNcYthVUMm — NFL (@NFL) September 21, 2025 Question 5: If you could describe Davis to Jaguars fans in one word, what would it be? title: 5 Questions About Jessie Bates III: Jaguars ‘Hit the Jackpot’
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jessie Bates III! To learn more about Duval’s newest starting safety, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Jeanna Kelley, who covered Bates’ time with the Atlanta Falcons over the past three and a half seasons for SB Nation’s The Falcoholic. Question 1: Did the […]
full_text: Dec 29, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III (3) does an interview after a victory over the Los Angeles Rams at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jessie Bates III! To learn more about Duval’s newest starting safety, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Jeanna Kelley, who covered Bates’ time with the Atlanta Falcons over the past three and a half seasons for SB Nation’s The Falcoholic . Question 1: Did the Falcons’ decision to trade Bates surprise you? Why did they feel comfortable making the move? I was not surprised by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates. He is still playing at a high level right now, but he’ll be 30 in February, and he’s in a contract year. From a business standpoint, trading Bates—while he still offers so much to a competitive team like the Jags who look ready to win NOW—and getting quality draft capital in return makes a lot more sense than holding on to him in a lost season (sure, the Falcons COULD still win the disaster that is the NFC South, but if you’ve watched any of their losses you’ll understand why I think this is a long shot) and getting absolutely nothing for him. Don’t get me wrong — I’m not happy about the trade. Bates has a defensive touchdown in four consecutive seasons, and the intensity of his preparation and play have set the standard for Jeff Ulbrich’s defense. He will be a wonderful addition for the Jags. Question 2: Jaguars GM James Gladstone has made it clear he’s searching for “intangibly rich” players. What can you tell us about Jessie Bates as a person? If James Gladstone is looking for “intangibly rich” players, he hit the jackpot with Jessie Bates. Bates may be a better leader than player, and he’s an outstanding player. Many young players in Atlanta are better pros because of Bates’ influence. He leads by example, and you won’t find many players in this league with a stronger work ethic or leadership abilities than Bates. Get ready for game day with SB Nation’s new app! SB Nation’s NEW game chat feature in the app is perfect for keeping the latest Jaguars updates and conversations at your fingertips. With a couple of clicks you can visit Dawgs By Nature and learn everything you need to know about this week’s opponent! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Question 3: Now, for Jessie Bates as a player. How would you describe his role on defense, and where on the field does he play at his best? Bates was a game-changer for Atlanta’s defense. His football IQ is off the charts, and he was able to elevate the play of everyone around him. He’s always been solid in coverage, but his big-play potential is off the charts — case in point, those four defensive touchdowns over the past four seasons. So far this season, Bates has 35 tackles, 3 forced fumbles, a pick and this season’s defensive touchdown, and that level of production has stayed consistent through his Falcons tenure. I’m sure time will eventually catch up to Bates, but I definitely don’t see it happening this season. Question 4: What’s something you learned about Bates during his time in Atlanta? Jessie Bates is obsessed with film study. He carries two iPads around the facility — one from the team with that week’s game plan information loaded on it, and his personal device for taking notes and looking up specific plays, etc. From Bates, via AtlantaFalcons.com : “Film study has always been my way of separating from other players,” Bates said. “That’s what I love. That’s the part a lot of people don’t see every day – the grind, the amount of time that you put into film to shine and make plays on Sunday.” Question 5: If you could describe Bates to Jaguars fans in one word, what would it be? I’ll give you two words: Outstanding addition. Jessie Bates is a fantastic fit for the Jags’ defense, and Jaguars fans are going to love him. title: Jaguars vs. Titans: Matchup History Through the Decades
summary: Following their win last week during Thursday Night Football, the Jags will be on the road this Sunday in Nashville. Football has been fun lately, so it pains me to talk about the Tennessee Titans (fuck ‘em). They’re like taxes: you know it’s happening every year and dread it, but persevere. The two teams have […]
full_text: NASHVILLE - NOVEMBER 11, 2007: The line of scrimage during the NHL game of the Tennessee Titans against the Jacksonville Jaguars at the LP Field on November 11, 2007 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following their win last week during Thursday Night Football, the Jags will be on the road this Sunday in Nashville. Football has been fun lately, so it pains me to talk about the Tennessee Titans (fuck ‘em). They’re like taxes: you know it’s happening every year and dread it, but persevere. The two teams have crossed paths 63 times, and the bad guys currently lead the series 35-28. While we hope we get another iconic Trevor stiff-arm moment, let’s revisit the Titans losing at home against the Jaguars throughout the decades. The 1990s Week 10 on November 2, 1997 Final score: Jaguars 30 – Oilers 24 Attendance: 27, 208 The Titans were the Tennessee Oilers at this point in time, and this was their first loss to the Jags after leaving Texas. Chris Hudson, Pete Mitchell, and Mark Brunell scored touchdowns. Brunell completed 17 out of 31 attempted passes for 169 yards and was sacked three times for a loss of 14 yards. James Stewart led the team with 99 rushing yards, and Jimmy Smith led with 50 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made the three attempted field goals. Chris Hudson had a six-yard interception, and Steve McNair was sacked twice for a loss of 16 yards. The 2000s Week 10 on November 11, 2007 Final score: Jaguars 28 – Titans 13 Attendance: 69,143 I’m attempting to manifest another Week 10 win in Tennessee. Greg Jones, Maurice Jones-Drew, and Fred Taylor scored touchdowns. Quinn Gray completed 13 out of 23 attempted passes for 101 yards and was sacked once for a loss of five yards. Maurice Jones-Drew led the team with 101 rushing yards and 28 receiving yards, averaged 14.50 yards in kickoff returns, and averaged 14.00 yards in punt returns. Mike Peterson and Brian Williams intercepted two of Vince Young’s passes. Reggie Hayward, Clint Ingram, and Jeremy Mincey sacked Young four times for a loss of 27 yards. The 2010s Week 13 on December 5, 2010 Final score: Jaguars 17 – Titans 6 Attendance: 69,143 Rashad Jennings and David Garrard scored touchdowns. Garrard completed 14 out of 19 attempted passes for 126 yards and was sacked once for a seven-yard loss. Maurice Jones-Drew led the team with 186 rushing yards, and Marcedes Lewis led with 36 receiving yards. Josh Scobee made one of the three attempted field goals. Derek Cox and William Middleton recorded interceptions. Jeremy Mincey recorded a sack on Kerry Collins for a loss of six yards. Rashean Mathis and Daryl Smith led the team with five combined tackles each. The 2020s Week 13 on November 30, 2025 Final Score: Jaguars 25 – Titans 3 Attendance: 54,098 The Titans scored their only points during the first quarter, and it was all Jacksonville football afterwards. Jakobi Meyers answered with a touchdown after a 50-yard catch-and-run brought the Jags to the five-yard line. Special teams forced a fumble and recovered the ball. Lawrence found Brenton Strange for another touchdown, then Trevor ran the two-point conversion in himself. In the second half, we saw a Tuten touchdown and a loose ball recovered by the Jags. Another game with Big Ham filling in at long snapper. summary: The Kansas City Chiefs cut their starting punt returner of three years, Nikko Remigio, earlier this week. full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs cut their starting punt returner of three years, Nikko Remigio, earlier this week. He posted a thoughtful goodbye message to Chiefs Kingdom on Instagram, ending with a note that he is signing with the Houston Texans ’ active roster. On Thursday, special teams coordinator Dave Toub told local media that he and Remigio shared a tearful goodbye and said Remigio was like a son to him. The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Texans Sign WR/KR Nikko Remigio | Pro Football Rumors The Texans have signed wide receiver/returner Nikko Remigio, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 reports. Remigio will join the Texans’ 53-man roster. After going undrafted out of Fresno State in 2023, Remigio signed with the Chiefs and went on to spend his first three-plus seasons in the organization. Even though Remigio had been the Chiefs’ primary returner since 2024, they cut him on Wednesday to open up a roster spot for newly acquired receiver Josh Downs. Kansas City Chiefs Tap Clark-AECOM JV for New Stadium | ENR The National Football League’s Kansas City Chiefs franchise has named a joint venture of Clark Construction Group and AECOM as construction team for its planned stadium in Wyandotte County, Kan. The team in July selected MANICA as lead architect, HNTB as architect of record and CAA ICON as owner’s representative for the $3-billion enclosed stadium. The 70,000-seat venue is envisioned as the anchor of a mixed-use development and entertainment destination. “As we finish the overall design, Clark | AECOM will help us advance the project further by identifying more certainty around project scope, budget and scheduling,” said Chiefs President Mark Donovan in a news release. ‘Another guy to help us get after the quarterback’ — Kansas City Chiefs second-year DT Omarr Norman-Lott nears injury return | A to Z Sports “Yeah, I watched him one-on-ones last week,” Spagnuolo said. “I thought he looked more like Omarr (Norman-Lott). I think he still got a little ways to go. Now I’m just going to trust the trainers on that. But they got him out there working and hopefully get him to the point where he can help us. But you know, we’re not there yet.” As things stand, Norman-Lott doesn’t look likely to return in Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons, but Week 11’s game against the Arizona Cardinals appears to be the target return date. The Chiefs are still kings of TV ratings after first half of NFL season | The Kansas City Star Of the NFL’s six most-watched games this season, three involved the Chiefs. That includes the top two. 1. Chiefs at Raiders, Oct. 4, 28.449 million viewers (CBS) 2. Chiefs at Broncos, Nov. 1, 28.175 million viewers (CBS) 3. Commanders at Cowboys, Sept. 20, 27.215 million viewers (Fox) 4. 49ers at Seahawks, Nov. 11, 26.698 million viewers (Fox) 5. Bills at Raiders, Oct. 18, 26.370 million viewers (CBS) 6. Chiefs at Seahawks, Oct. 25, 26.287 million viewers (NBC) That Chiefs game in Seattle is the highest-rated prime-time game of the season to date. Eric Bieniemy Breaks Silence on Sideline Tirade With Emmett Johnson | Heavy Sports Despite his tough and, as Bieniemy describes it, “colorful” approach to coaching, his players consistently praise him. Bieniemy does a good job of teaching a lesson after emotions calm down, which is what he went on to explain. “Everybody has a job to do,” Bieniemy continued. “The right tackle has to do his job, that’s where it starts. Emmett has to have a feel and do his part. Am I blaming him for anything? No, not at all. Things happen throughout the course of a season. If those things don’t present themselves, they don’t become those valuable lessons that need to be taught and learned.” Around the NF L Commanders stun Giants in final minute to save their season; what now in NFC East? | The Athletic While the Commanders (3-5-1) still have work to do to climb back into the race and catch the 5-3-1 Giants, this was a game they had to have to keep their faint playoff hopes alive. The victory also might take a little heat off coach Dan Quinn after a series of losses and questionable game-management decisions. The Commanders get to take advantage of a minibye, as they don’t play again until Nov. 23, a “Monday Night Football” game against MVP candidate Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals. Chargers’ Jim Harbaugh frustrated with Broncos after nixed Daiyan Henley trade | ESPN When asked if teams should be able to renegotiate a deal beyond the deadline, Harbaugh said Thursday, “It shouldn’t be, but apparently it is. “But that’s why it’s a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that. I mean, it’s a medical grade. It’s a pass-fail for a medical grade, and they told us they weren’t going to pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. And they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a fill-in-the-blank. And that was, I don’t know what to call that, but that’s what it is.” Rams place WR Puka Nacua on IR | Pro Football Talk McVay said “roster semantics” would keep Nacua on the 53-man roster, with every team getting only eight designated-to-return slots during the season. The Rams have used three of their designations and have Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson and now Nacua on IR with hopes of returning. But with Nacua set to miss “extended time,” as McVay said Wednesday, with MCL and PCL sprains in his knee and turf toe, the Rams opted to move him to the IR list. Nacua will miss at least the next four games, with the Cowboys game on Dec. 20 the earliest he can return by rule. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Protector of the Year The Chiefs’ run game has been revitalized this year, and Smith has been a key factor in the push up front. Kansas City ranks 10th in ESPN’s run-block win rate (74%), despite two games in which starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched. The Chiefs rank 12th in pass-block win rate as a unit, and Smith does not grade as highly in pass blocking as Humphrey or Suamataia, according to ESPN , but Smith has allowed just seven pressures (two quarterback hits and five hurries) over 307 pass-blocking snaps; Suamataia has allowed seven pressures (one sack, three hits and three pressures) in just 221 pass-blocking snaps, according to Pro Football Focus . title: Throwback Thursday: The time Tony Gonzalez was almost traded
summary: With the NFL Trade Deadline passing this week, it’s a good time to remember an era when the Kansas City Chiefs were more often sellers than buyers at this time of year. Wednesday morning, on “The Dan Patrick Show,” Fox Sports NFL Insider shared a story about former Chiefs tight end Tony Gonzalez nearly being […]
full_text: With the NFL Trade Deadline passing this week, it’s a good time to remember an era when the Kansas City Chiefs were more often sellers than buyers at this time of year. We ask @JayGlazer about the craziest trade that never happened. 👀 pic.twitter.com/Z14VL98lUR — Dan Patrick Show (@dpshow) November 11, 2026 Wednesday morning, on “The Dan Patrick Show,” Fox Sports NFL Insider shared a story about former Chiefs tight end Tony Gonzalez nearly being traded midseason. He reminisced about negotiations between Kansas City and two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles , led by head coach Andy Reid, and the Green Bay Packers , led by Mike McCarthy. “Tony Gonzalez wants to get traded from the Chiefs, right?” Glazer remembered. “At the time, Carl Peterson was the GM; he had two deals: one with the Eagles and one with the Packers. Andy Reid and the Eagles were offered a [third-round pick] and LJ Smith, their tight end, and the Packers were offered a three and whoever their tight end was.” Glazer is most likely referring to the 2008 season, a lost year in Kansas City that featured a 2-14 record. The year before, the Chiefs went 4-12. The Packers tight end he was likely referring to was Donald Lee, but Green Bay also had 21-year-old Jermichael Finley on the 2008 team. “This is Tony: he talked to the Chiefs. He wanted to finish his career on a contender,” Glazer recalled. “He wanted to go somewhere else, and they agreed. So they’re really going back and forth, and it’s really up to him.” “Maybe 20 minutes before, Carl Peterson changes it from a three to a two, and there just wasn’t enough time to do it, right? I got a text from Andy Reid like, ‘I knew this wasn’t going to happen.’ I got a text from McCarthy: furious.” Glazer told Patrick that Gonzalez lost it when hearing that the trade didn’t go through. He was ready to put the Chiefs on blast for not letting him leave town: “Get your pen out!” “He wanted to do a story that there was no way we could ever publish in the history of life,” Glazer said. “I never do stories where someone is just emotional… he was like ‘I’m never playing!‘” “He calmed down — might’ve taken a couple of days off — and went out and finished with Kansas City,” Glazer finished. “Eventually, him and Scott Pioli and Todd Haley were horrible, and they traded him to Atlanta.” Gonzalez was traded to the Atlanta Falcons the following spring in 2009, and finally won a playoff game in the Divisional Round of the 2012 season. If the trade had gone through with Green Bay, Tony G could’ve had his Super Bowl ring with the 2010 Packers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Too bad.
