title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Top Offensive Rookie
summary: There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one […]
full_text: Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. So far, we’ve awarded: Most Improved Player : DB Chris Roland-Wallace Top Defensive Rookie : CB Mansoor Delane Protector of the Year : RG Trey Smith In this post, we’ll reveal the top offensive rookie. OT Kahlil Benson VOTING: Kahlil Benson (6), RB Emmett Johnson (3) It’s certainly not flashy for an offensive lineman to be the team’s top rookie on offense. The stats may not be there, but because of his availability and exceeding expectations, undrafted rookie offensive tackle Kahlil Benson brings home the award at the midpoint of the season. Entering training camp, much of Chiefs’ Kingdom may not have even known who Benson was. An undrafted rookie from the national-champion Indiana Hoosiers, Benson entered training camp as depth on the offensive line, or as a potential challenger for the starting right tackle role. Forced into the lineup after left tackle Josh Simmons suffered a back injury, Benson has been a steady presence on the line, protecting the blindside of quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Never starting at left tackle in college, Benson has started all eight games at the position for the Chiefs. Even more impressive, he has played all 510 of the team’s offensive snaps. He is Kansas City’s player to play every offensive single snap. According to Pro Football Focus, Benson has allowed 22 pressures, 13 hits, and no sacks on the quarterback so far this season. He is currently ranked 53rd out of 71 qualifying tackles with an overall grade of 61.8 on the season. His run-blocking grade (70.9) is significantly better than his pass-blocking grade (46.7). Benson’s role could change in the coming weeks. If Simmons returns to the lineup at left tackle, Benson would either slide to his more natural position at right tackle or serve as valuable depth as a swing tackle along the line. But based on his play so far in 2026, Benson clearly has a future role in the Chiefs’ offense. It’s not often an undrafted player has this important a role on a football team. The Chiefs have half a billion dollars invested in Mahomes, and all their postseason hopes riding on him staying upright for 17 games. Because of Benson’s steady presence on the offensive line and his more-than-admirable play in this role, he is a very deserving recipient of Arrowhead Pride’s Midseason Offensive Rookie of the Year.
author: Dakota Watson

title: Dave Toub says Chiefs are hoping Harrison Butker starts a streak
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are showing strong loyalty to kicker Harrison Butker this week after a missed 51-yard field goal in Week 9, his seventh miss of the year. With Justin Tucker on the practice squad, the Chiefs are standing their ground, believing it’s all about pushing Butker out of a slump. It started Wednesday, […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are showing strong loyalty to kicker Harrison Butker this week after a missed 51-yard field goal in Week 9, his seventh miss of the year. With Justin Tucker on the practice squad, the Chiefs are standing their ground, believing it’s all about pushing Butker out of a slump. It started Wednesday, when head coach Andy Reid said the team is “sticking with” him . During his press conference on Thursday, special teams coordinator Dave Toub reiterated that faith in the team’s longtime placekicker. “He’s going to come through it,” Toub said. “I’m confident that he will; we’re just going to keep practicing him and keep working on little things; he’s looked good in practice. There’s a reason why he’s still our kicker.” The miss against the New York Jets was Butker’s fourth consecutive game with a missed field goal; two of them featured multiple missed kicks when including point-after attempts. It’s likely the worst stretch of Butker’s nine-year career in Kansas City. “It bothers him, it bothers him a lot,” Toub said. “It’s hard for somebody that has kicked at the level that he has kicked at to have this happen in front of 70,000 people. He hears it, he knows it, the pressure is on him, but I have confidence.” “There’s a weight on him,” Toub continued. “We have to get a 100% day, and then we have to put the second one in and the third one and the fourth one.” To give an example of a veteran kicker that has come out of a slump, Toub pointed to Buffalo Bills kicker Tyler Bass, who missed five extra points and five field goals in 2024 and didn’t play in 2025. “He’s got like 25 in a row right now,” Toub pointed out about Bass. “He was struggling last year. So we’re sticking with [Butker], and we’re hoping that he starts a streak this weekend.” As the Chiefs stand behind Butker, working with Tucker off to the side at practice to make sure he’s ready, the coaching staff is honest about Butker’s issue. “It’s a mental thing,” Toub noted. “You just have to be more aggressive, put the ball down the middle and take a shot. Don’t try to be perfect with the targets. Those are little things that we’re working on, and he just has to power through this thing and get a little streak going right now.” “Attack it, instead of trying to be perfect.”

full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. So far, we’ve awarded: Most Improved Player : DB Chris Roland-Wallace Top Defensive Rookie : CB Mansoor Delane In this post, we’ll reveal our top offensive lineman so far . RG Trey Smith VOTING: Trey Smith (5), Kahlil Benson (2), Creed Humphrey (2) The NFL now gives out the “Protector of the Year” award, so we will too. Right guard Trey Smith is the winner at the midseason point, playing 506 of 510 possible snaps and starting in all eight games. The Chiefs’ run game has been revitalized this year, and Smith has been a key factor in the push up front. Kansas City ranks 10th in ESPN’s run-block win rate (74%), despite two games in which starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched. The Chiefs rank 12th in pass-block win rate as a unit, and Smith does not grade as highly in pass blocking as Humphrey or Suamataia, according to ESPN , but Smith has allowed just seven pressures (two quarterback hits and five hurries) over 307 pass-blocking snaps; Suamataia has allowed seven pressures (one sack, three hits and three pressures) in just 221 pass-blocking snaps, according to Pro Football Focus . The intensity Smith brings is the cherry on top of his reliable presence on the line. He isn’t a perfect blocker, but he’s been Kansas City’s most consistent offensive lineman in a season where the unit’s depth is already being tested. Center Creed Humphrey’s low snaps likely hurt his chances at winning the poll, but rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson deserved some love; he has played every snap possible at left tackle this season. Is Smith the Chiefs’ top offensive lineman so far this year? Let us know in the comments.

title: Patrick Mahomes doesn’t expect a long learning period for Josh Downs
summary: On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs executed a trade with the Indianapolis Colts to bring in wide receiver Josh Downs in return for a pair of Day 3 draft selections. Now that the move is official, the process of integrating Downs into the offense begins. Speaking before Wednesday’s practice, quarterback Patrick Mahomes did not foresee […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs executed a trade with the Indianapolis Colts to bring in wide receiver Josh Downs in return for a pair of Day 3 draft selections. Now that the move is official, the process of integrating Downs into the offense begins. Speaking before Wednesday’s practice, quarterback Patrick Mahomes did not foresee a problem. Mahomes expects his new target to be on the field as he learns Kansas City’s offense. “It is realistic,” Mahomes explained, “because we do a great job of kind of moving guys in and out of every single position, and so guys know the entire concepts of the plays. We’re very detailed with how we call the plays in the huddle, which will help him out a ton. Then when he doesn’t know, being able to talk to me in the huddle or talk to the guys as they’re breaking the huddle, and that usually helps when the guys like each other. “It’s good to have a guy that you can tell everybody’s going to like and that he has his head on the right way and he’s going to make sure that he’s going to do whatever it takes to win.” Mahomes has no question about what Downs brings to the Chiefs. Daniel Jones dropped it in the bucket for Josh Downs @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pqCXVQd3Yg — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 “He does a great job of winning one-on-one matchups,” observed Mahomes, “which is always important. He runs routes really well. He sets them up really well, where he will run a route early in the game that he sets up for another one later in the game. “Then he has really good feel,” Mahomes said. “Obviously, playing in the system that he has — he has a lot of read-type routes, and you can tell he knows how to get himself open, settle in the right zones, and win versus man when he can. So, I think it will be an easy transition for him to kind of do that stuff in our offense. Then with how we do things, he can play a lot of different positions as we move receivers and tight ends around.” Speaking after Mahomes, Downs explained the obvious answer to how he will work himself into the system. “When [Mahomes] throws me the ball, just catch it,” he remarked, “and keep making plays when he throws it to me and do anything I can to learn the offense as fast as possible. “I don’t want to be a guy that’s asking everybody what the play is or what the formation is,” Downs pointed out. “I feel like that’s when you kind of get left behind. So, I want to do everything I can to learn as fast as possible.” Mahomes elaborated on the learning ahead of Downs, who he believes is up for the challenge after seeing his attention in Wednesday’s walk through. “The entire offense will probably take a couple weeks,” he predicted, “but I think what I’ve learned just from meeting Josh is he’s very intelligent. He has a good feel for playing in the NFL, and their scheme is similar to our scheme. Obviously, verbiage and everything like that, but we can utilize him in his role in his spots. At the end of the day, when you get guys in the building, and they’re picking up stuff like we were at walkthrough earlier and he’s picking up stuff quickly, then you can kind of give him more and more. And so, he’s definitely a smart football player, and I think it won’t be a long time until he’s really getting utilized in the offense.” One of Downs’ new teammates believes the adjustment will be easier than expected. “It’s not really hard to understand what Pat’s thinking on the field,” wideout Rashee Rice declared on Wednesday. “Once you love the game of football and you’re doing everything you can to get open, Pat’s going to do everything he can to get you the ball. So, as long as you separate and make some room to make sure he can make the throw, which he will. So, as long as he does that, it’ll be easy for him to prepare for the plays.” Other recent wide receiver trades for the Chiefs — such Kadarius Toney and DeAndre Hopkins — ultimately underwhelmed despite flashy moments. Neither was in Downs’ position, and he has proven himself while still playing for a second contract. “He’s done it,” Mahomes reiterated of Downs. “You can see that he’s made plays against some of the best defenses in the league and teams that we’ll go up against this season and in the playoffs. Whenever he’s put that on tape, then you know that that is there and so now it’s about us utilizing his skillset within the other guys on the team in order to make the offense even better than we’ve been so far.”
author: Jared Sapp

title: Week 10 AP NFL Power Rankings: The entire NFC North resides in the top 10
summary: Remarkably, half of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. Time sure does fly. The Arrowhead Pride Power Rankings saw one new entrant in the top 10, with the Green Bay Packers joining the rest of their NFC North brethren. If quarterback Jordan Love continues to be an absolute surgeon with the football, they […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Remarkably, half of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. Time sure does fly. The Arrowhead Pride Power Rankings saw one new entrant in the top 10, with the Green Bay Packers joining the rest of their NFC North brethren. If quarterback Jordan Love continues to be an absolute surgeon with the football, they will remain in the top 10 for some time. The Kansas City Chiefs exited the Top 10 to make room for the Packers. Although they came out of Week 9 with a win, their problems dropped them in the rankings. While all four teams of the NFC North are in the top 10, the extremely-mid NFC South ranks from 18-24 in the rankings. The NFL changes on a dime, and it truly is a “what have you done for me lately” business. Many teams have moved up or down the rankings drastically since the beginning of the season. With it being the halfway point of the season, we’ll also look back at where the Arrowhead Pride staff ranked the teams following Week 1. Biggest risers: Green Bay Packers and Houston Texans +3 Biggest faller: Baltimore Ravens -5 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Caleb James, Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. Buffalo Bills (1st, initially 3rd) The Vikings’ offense made the Bills’ defense look like the ‘85 Bears. 2. San Francisco 49ers (3rd, initially 4th) It just feels like this team is a shoo-in for the NFC Championship game. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (5th, initially 10th) This team is going all in for the postseason. Three big defensive trades a day before the deadline. 4. Chicago Bears (2nd, initially 8th) The only reason the Bears won despite Caleb Williams throwing four interceptions is the fact that they played a team that couldn’t even complete a pass the week before. 5. Denver Broncos (7th, initially 12th) I don’t want to hear a word from a Broncos fan about the officials favoring the Chiefs. 6. Cincinnati Bengals (8th, initially 6th) I’m starting to get a little concerned about the potential of seeing this team in January. 7. Minnesota Vikings (4th, initially 16th) What’s old is new again. Kirk Cousins returns to lead the Vikings. How happy is Justin Jefferson to have a QB that can at least convert a first down? 8. Seattle Seahawks (6th, initially 1st) The Super Bowl hangover may be real for the Hawks. If the season ended today, they’d be on the outside looking in at the postseason. 9. Detroit Lions (10th, initially 13th) The Lions have quietly won four in a row. 10. Green Bay Packers (13th, initially 17th) I dream of the Chiefs having a deep passing attack like the Packers. 11. Kansas City Chiefs (9th, initially 5th) Josh Downs undoubtedly improves the wide receiver room. But can he kick the football? 12. Pittsburgh Steelers (12th, initially 18th) 4-0 at home and 2-2 on the road. Notch a win against the Bengals in Cincinnati, and they’ll have to be taken more seriously. 13. Los Angeles Rams (14th, initially 11th) That was the Myles Garrett the Rams traded for. 14. New York Giants (15th, initially 15th) The Giants stood pat at the trade deadline, making no moves. This makes me think they will not be moving far up or down in the AP Power Rankings for the remainder of the season. 15. New England Patriots (11th, initially 14th) An absolute beatdown at home. The Patriots allowed the most points in their history at Gillette Stadium. 16. Cleveland Browns (16th, initially 32nd) Might as well let Shadeur Sanders play the rest of the way. He may or may not be the future, but they have to know Deshaun Watson is not. 17. Houston Texans (20th, initially 7th) A game against the Chargers will right a lot of wrongs. 18. Carolina Panthers (19th, initially 26th) They lead the NFC South with a record of 3-5… 19. Las Vegas Raiders (17th, initially 27th) The Fernando Mendoza era has arrived. 20. Atlanta Falcons (21st, initially 28th) Drake London would have looked fantastic in a Chiefs’ uniform. 21. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (22nd, initially 21st) Wonder if they’re regretting that Baker Mayfield contract? 22. Dallas Cowboys (23rd, initially 19th) An unserious football team. The Colts are actively trying to lose games, and they almost beat the Cowboys. 23. Baltimore Ravens (18th, initially 2nd) Without Lamar Jackson or Snoop Huntley at quarterback, the Chargers-Ravens game next week should be aired on Comedy Central. 24. New Orleans Saints (25th, initially 23rd) Win or lose, this is just an entertaining football team. 25. Washington Commanders (24th, initially 25th) Jayden Daniels will be seeing Myles Garrett in his nightmares. 26. New York Jets (27th, initially 29th) Head coach Aaron Glenn is on borrowed time. He played not to lose at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday. Repeatedly kicking field goals instead of going for it deep in the red zone is not going to win many games against Patrick Mahomes. 27. Arizona Cardinals (26th, initially 22nd) Ouch. Rough week losing wide receiver Michael Wilson and backup quarterback Gardner Minshew for the season. 28. Tennessee Titans (29th, initially 31st) Onto 2027. Trading Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker certainly does not improve the roster for 2026. 29. Philadelphia Eagles (28th, initially 9th) They didn’t go full seller mode at the trade deadline. But their moves also signal they do not plan to compete in 2026. 30. Indianapolis Colts (31st, initially 24th) I’m surprised Shane Steichen still has his head coaching job. 31. Miami Dolphins (30th, initially 30th) Respect the fight this team continues to display. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (32nd, initially 20th) As a Chiefs fan, it’s great news the Chargers were not major sellers at the trade deadline. Run it back!

title: Rams place Puka Nacua on IR
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without star receiver Puka Nacua for at least four games, as the team placed him on injured reserve on Thursday. Head coach Sean McVay had previously just said on Wednesday that Nacua would avoid going on IR — mostly for technical roster-related reasons — but the Rams found a […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will be without star receiver Puka Nacua for at least four games, as the team placed him on injured reserve on Thursday. Head coach Sean McVay had previously just said on Wednesday that Nacua would avoid going on IR — mostly for technical roster-related reasons — but the Rams found a way to do it anyway. Nacua injured his PCL and MCL when McVay called an end around for him on the final offensive play of Week 9’s win over the Washington Commanders. It is a decision that McVay instantly regretted. The Rams signed Brennan Presley to the active roster in a corresponding move. Rams placed WR Puka Nacua on injured reserve due to his MCL injury. HC Sean McVay has said he expects Nacua to miss “extended time.” pic.twitter.com/XAR4rutM0Q — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 13, 2026 Nacua is in a league of his own on the Rams roster. The Rams will be without Nacua and Davante Adams for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals, leading into their Week 11 bye. McVay said on Wednesday that the team hopes to get Adams back against the Packers the following week, but nothing is certain when it comes to L.A.‘s timeline for players returning. Myles Garrett was not supposed to be “that hurt” in the preseason and then he missed seven games. Terrance Ferguson was supposed to be back last week, but he’s out at least two more weeks. The Rams were not supposed to place Nacua on IR. Nothing is guaranteed except the present.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Myles Garrett still plans to lead the NFL in sacks this season
summary: Myles Garrett had three sacks in his first game back from a two-month stint on injured reserve and the L.A. Rams edge rusher says that he plans to get a lot more than that. In fact, Garrett told Rich Eisen that he will specifically be looking to cross off the names ahead of him in […]
full_text: Myles Garrett had three sacks in his first game back from a two-month stint on injured reserve and the L.A. Rams edge rusher says that he plans to get a lot more than that. In fact, Garrett told Rich Eisen that he will specifically be looking to cross off the names ahead of him in sacks this year week by week and that he believes he can win Defensive Player of the Year in 2026 despite already missing seven games. Given that he had 23 sacks last season, are Garrett’s goals that crazy? "Absolutely. … There's nothing to stutter about." 😮‍💨 @Flash_Garrett 's thoughts on if he can still win Defensive Player of the Year 👀 (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/QAr2wzHrJz — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 12, 2026 The NFL leader in sacks is Will Anderson, who currently stands at 9.5. “I don’t plan to make it easy for (Anderson),” Garrett said on the Rich Eisen Show on Thursday. Anderson’s league-leading total is 1.5 sacks more than Gregory Rosseau and Chase Young in second place with eight each. There are 11 players who have at least six sacks, which is twice as many as Garrett right now. However, Garrett had three sacks last week. If he has three sacks this week against the Cardinals — a team starting Carson Beck in his NFL debut — he will already be knocking on the door of the top-10 heading into L.A.’s bye week. Garrett would then have seven more games left in the season. Over Garrett’s best seven-game stretch of 2025, he had 16 sacks with the Cleveland Browns. Of course, if Garrett gets 19 sacks over his last eight games, starting this Sunday, he will obviously be in the running for Defensive Player of the Year, like he plans to be. Garrett made a stunning claim on the Rich Eisen Show. What’s more amazing is that he doesn’t sound crazy.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Byron Young’s ‘breakout season’ is breaking down
summary: The Los Angeles Rams finally paired Myles Garrett with Byron Young, their second-best outside linebacker, last week and the results were great. For Garrett. Although Young looked to be having a breakout season with 3.5 sacks in his first four games, he has since been much harder to notice during the five games since, recording […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams finally paired Myles Garrett with Byron Young, their second-best outside linebacker, last week and the results were great. For Garrett. Although Young looked to be having a breakout season with 3.5 sacks in his first four games , he has since been much harder to notice during the five games since, recording just one sack and quickly sliding down the rankings among the top outside linebackers in the NFL. Young is a 2027 free agent, which at one point made it seem like he would be very expensive and difficult for the Rams to re-sign. But if Young doesn’t have a strong second half of the season, L.A. might not try to re-sign him at all and instead will attempt to get a compensatory pick back from free agency. Byron Young’s Season Weeks 1-4: 22 pressures, 3.5 sacks, and a 22.6% pressure rate Young also had 0 missed tackles in the first four games. Weeks 5-9: 13 pressures, 1 sack, and a 9.4% pressure rate Young has since added three missed tackles to his tally over the last five games. So for anyone who thinks that Young’s “pressure rate” more accurately reflects his pass rushing value than sacks, that number has been more than cut in half since he was dominant in Week 4 against a decimated Eagles offensive line. Young had 2.5 sacks and a season-high eight pressures against Philadelphia. Since then he hasn’t had more than four pressures in any of the last five games. He has had one sack, which came against the Raiders. That sack came on 2nd-and-16, an obvious passing situation, and Las Vegas lost zero yards on the play. According to PFF, Young has an above-average pass rushing grade, ranking roughly 20th-30th at the position in the league. But a below-average run defense grade, below at least 50 or 60 other players: DE/EDGE grades stopping run and in pass rush pic.twitter.com/qGigyW22hg — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 11, 2026 We have a much larger sample size now than we did after Week 4. It’s becoming harder to justify an extension for Young when he either needs Myles Garrett to be successful or hasn’t proven that he can be consistent without Garrett. Young’s total season has a 14.9% pressure rate, which ranks 58th among linebackers . It’s much better if you only look at edges with at least 100 pass rush snaps — roughly 15th — but what if we look at the sub-10% pressure rate he’s had for most of the season? That’s simply not special. In fact, Josaiah Stewart has had a higher pressure rate and has been more productive, generating 12 pressures (in fewer snaps) and 2 sacks in the last five games . While someone may argue that Garrett’s three sacks in Week 9 proves that Young is “quietly” proving to be a good teammate, that’s hardly enough proof for the price of a veteran edge rusher when that same player is perhaps only a replaceable starter. Fans always so quick to trade me…wild. https://t.co/c7NRZNfZwR — B.Y. (@byron_97) November 11, 2026 Byron Young’s 2027 free agency With the emergence of Stewart as a player at the same position who is at least as productive recently, the justification to extend or re-sign Young looks much weaker. The Rams having “a lot” of cap space next year is a complete mirage . With so many free agents on both sides of the ball, and special teams, the Rams will surely run out of money fast. They also have to decide what to do with Puka Nacua and a franchise tag for the receiver would cost roughly $30 million. That’s a huge chunk of their available space compared to an extension, which would be much more team-friendly. And if they don’t re-sign Nacua, then they have to replace him and likely Davante Adams. That won’t be cheap. The going rate for a good free agent outside linebacker in his 20s (Young will be 29 next year) could be upwards of $20 million per season. It really depends on how the league sees him. 2026 free agent Boye Mafe got a three-year, $60 million contract from the Bengals despite not having a great season in 2025. A desperate team out there might see Young as a $20 million AAV player. That might be an understatement. Can the Rams really afford a $20-$25 million per year for a 29-year-old linebacker who might not be as good as Stewart, a very cheap 23-year-old linebacker? The only way for Young to force their hand would be to play a lot better — as a pass rusher and a run stopper — over the next eight games. He now has the NFL’s best edge-rushing linebacker on the other side. It won’t get any easier than this for an edge in the league. He’ll never be better than Garrett. But can he be better than he’s been recently?

title: Rams reportedly tried to trade for a receiver
summary: There are reports that the Los Angeles Rams tried to trade for Jerry Jeudy from the Cleveland Browns. However, the Browns apparently wanted “premium picks” and the Rams weren’t willing to part with them. I have also seen some rumblings that the Rams maybe wanted to trade for Ladd McConkey from the Los Angeles Chargers. […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 23: Jerry Jeudy #3 of the Cleveland Browns warms up prior to an NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Los Angeles Rams at Huntington Bank Field on August 23, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images There are reports that the Los Angeles Rams tried to trade for Jerry Jeudy from the Cleveland Browns. However, the Browns apparently wanted “premium picks” and the Rams weren’t willing to part with them. I have also seen some rumblings that the Rams maybe wanted to trade for Ladd McConkey from the Los Angeles Chargers. That didn’t happen either. So, rumors, reports and speculation suggest the Rams tried to trade for a receiver, but it didn’t work out. Either other teams were asking for too much, or the Rams didn’t want to give up what was being asked. Both things can be true. Remember, the Rams made their moves in their offseason. They traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. They made a move for Tutu Atwell too. So, the Rams pushed their chips before the season started, and now they are holding what chips they have left, and hoping their current pot is big enough to make a push. It’s not that the Rams didn’t try to make a move at the deadline, it’s more like a move didn’t happen. Browns Get Jerry Jeudy Trade Call From Familiar Team (sports.yahoo) “The two teams already completed one of the offseason’s biggest deals, sending Myles Garrett to Los Angeles for Jared Verse and three draft picks. Now, the Rams have another reason to contact general manager Andrew Berry. Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot reported Monday that the Browns would consider trading Jeudy for premium picks, but no such offer had arrived by Sunday. Cleveland was not shopping him. It leaves the desperate Rams needing to make an offer strong enough to change the Browns’ position.“ Rams’ failed trade pursuit of Chargers WR surfaces after NFL trade deadline (nypost.com) “The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry. Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call,” Graziano wrote on Wednesday. “Overall, though, the Rams didn’t seriously consider a receiver move because they expect both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to return this season,” he added. “The Rams trading for Los Angeles Chargers star receiver Ladd McConkey would have been one of the biggest trades made this season, despite McConkey’s disappointing campaign. The 24-year-old former Georgia Bulldogs star has 17 receptions for 286 receiving yards and one touchdown this season. That output leaves a lot to be desired, but the 0-8 Chargers’ entire offense has been abysmal, and McConkey’s production has taken a hit as a result.“ Rams Spark Tyreek Hill Speculation With Latest Roster Moves (heavy.com) “The Rams created $3 million in cap space by restructuring the contracts of Pro Bowl running back Kyren Williams and safety Kamren Curl, ESPN’s Field Yates reported on X. The details came from Spotrac. Los Angeles turned $2 million of Williams’ salary into a signing bonus and added two void years to his deal, which freed up $1.7 million. The Rams did the same with $1.7 million of Curl’s salary, which cleared another $1.3 million. Williams and Curl are both under contract through 2028. With the void years, both will now stay on the Rams’ books through 2030. It didn’t take long for Rams fans to connect the dots to free-agent wideout Tyreek Hill. “That seems like a Tyreek Hill move to me,” one fan replied.“ Sean McVay: Rams optimistic WR Davante Adams will return ‘sooner than later’ (espn) “LOS ANGELES — One of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams did not trade for a wide receiver before the NFL trade deadline, coach Sean McVay said, is because Los Angeles is “optimistic” that Davante Adams will return from his hamstring injury “sooner than later.” McVay initially said Adams, who ruptured his semitendinosus late in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, was expected to miss six to 10 weeks with the injury. McVay said Wednesday that Adams returning after the Rams host the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 is a “realistic timeline for him.” Los Angeles is currently without wide receiver Puka Nacua , who injured his right knee and toe in Sunday’s road game against the Washington Commanders . McVay said Wednesday that the Rams will not place Nacua on injured reserve related to roster mechanics, “but he still is going to be out for an extended period of time.” Battered, bruised and out for revenge: Can the Rams survive another Cardinals showdown? (nypost) “The Los Angeles Rams are beginning to resemble the Black Knight from “Monty Python and the Holy Grail.” Their arms have been chopped off, their legs are missing, and they’re bleeding all over the battlefield. Yet Sean McVay is still standing on the sideline screaming, “’Tis but a scratch!” Welcome to Rams-Cardinals Part Deux, where the only thing longer than the injury report is the list of excuses neither team wants to hear. Five weeks after Arizona stunned Los Angeles with an 18-16 walk-off victory at SoFi Stadium, the NFC West rivals reunite Sunday at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz., for a rematch that could determine whether the Rams enter their bye week riding a four-game winning streak or reliving their most embarrassing loss of the season.“ LA Rams injury report: Puka Nacua, 4 others sit out Wednesday (sports.yahoo) “The full details of their Wednesday injury report are below. Starters are noted with an asterisk. They have already activated three players and have eight others eligible. Head coach Sean McVay said Nacua he will be out “for an extended period of time.” Rams Receive Encouraging Davante Adams News After Puka Nacua Injury (athlonsports) “By our count, Adams and Nacua have drawn 142 of the Rams’ 337 targets this season, 42.1%. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games with 16.0 yards per catch, according to ESPN . The 5-4 Rams have won three straight, but they face a tough closing stretch . Getting Adams back for the Chiefs game would give Stafford his top deep threat again before the toughest part of the schedule.“ Rams avoiding IR stint for Puka Nacua is less promising than it seems (ramblinfan) “We’re not going to put him on IR, just because of some semantics with the roster and things like that, but he’s still going to be out for an extended period of time. It wasn’t like any sort of new information,” McVay told reporters Wednesday. Perhaps the greater concern, though, is that the Rams are chewing through the eight players league rules allow them to designate for return from IR. title: Is there a quick fix to the Las Vegas Raiders’ defensive woes?
summary: Immediately after his football team lost to the San Francisco 49ers 38-17 this past Sunday, Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was naturally asked about potential changes to a defense that’s now given up 30 or more points in six straight games. “We will look at the film, and we will make our decisions […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Immediately after his football team lost to the San Francisco 49ers 38-17 this past Sunday, Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was naturally asked about potential changes to a defense that’s now given up 30 or more points in six straight games. “We will look at the film, and we will make our decisions when we have cooler heads,” the rookie head coach said combating the need to make any rash decisions. Cooler heads prevailed and on Monday, Kubiak expressed confidence in his chosen rookie defensive coordinator Rob Leonard and emphatically shut the door on any changes in that regard. “No, I don’t. In fact, I see us doing the things we said we were going to do better. Stand behind Rob (Leonard). Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players,” Kubiak said during his Monday media availability. “And I think the world wants someone’s head on a platter every time things don’t go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason, to get a job done and develop players for the long haul, and that’s where we’re going.” Kubiak’s decision to stand behind Leonard, the defensive staff, and the players on that side of the ball likely draws mixed feelings from Raider Nation. After all, Las Vegas tied a modern-era NFL record of six-straight games allowing 30 or more points and team is ranked dead-last out of the 32 teams in: Points allowed (268), yards allowed (3,469), rushing yards yielded (1,361), and first downs given up (208). #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said they won’t be making changes to their defensive staff “I’m standing behind Rob, I’m standing behind our defensive staff, I’m standing behind our players. I think the world wants someone’s head on a platter every time things don’t go right…” Said… pic.twitter.com/nSlyXHTo06 — Jesse Merrick – Silver & Black Sports Network (@JesseSBSN) November 9, 2026 Being the caboose in the league in those categories isn’t a recipe for success, it’s a blueprint in ineptitude. Which beckons a question: Is there a quick fix to the Silver & Black’s defensive woes? An emphatic no, is the answer. Even if Kubiak decided to part ways with Leonard nine games into his initial tenure as an NFL defensive coordinator, the underlying issues remain — no matter who is promoted to interim play caller status. The cauldron of misery is a mix of both schematic and roster issues and it continues to simmer in a piping hot boil. There’s a glaring lack of talent — particularly in the trenches at defensive tackle — and no matter what play calls Leonard deploys to make up for that — more man coverage and blitzing — the results are there for everyone to see. The Raiders are gashed by the run and are habitually beaten through the air. Now it isn’t all bad. Leonard’s group showed sharper execution and focus in the second half in both Weeks 8 and 9 by rising to the occasion against the New York Jets and the San Francisco 49ers this past Sunday. But the moments of efficiency are too fleeting. And this shouldn’t be a surprise for folk who watched the offseason. Yes, the Raiders are in rebuild mode. Yes, the talent gaps weren’t going to be filled in one offseason. And yes, it’ll take the coaching staff time to truly integrate their philosophy on a roster that’s going through natural turnover during this early phase of the Kubiak era. But the expected growing pains shouldn’t absolve folk of criticism — from Kubiak, Leonard, and general manager John Spytek and Co. The ownership of a historically woeful defense is a beast of burden that multiple Raiders share. After the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers, Quay Walker talked about how slow starts on defense are a big reason they have allowed 30+ points for the sixth straight week. pic.twitter.com/oKwV5tZblS — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) November 9, 2026 Listening to linebacker Quay Walker above is encouraging. And it’s true all 11 defenders need to be on the same page on the field — ditto for the coaches and other defenders on the sideline. Unfortunately for the Walker — the 26-year-old free agent catch who inked a three-year, $40.5 million deal with the Raiders in the offseason — he’s a culprit of not playing as one, communicating, or executing properly in a glaring play against the Niners that left running back Christian McCaffrey wide open for a walk-in touchdown pass. It was a sequence that saw both defensive tackles Tonka Hemingway and Adam Butler dropping into zone coverage, with the former the “closest” defender to CMC. “It was. Yeah, we did not peel on the halfback,” Kubiak said of the play in particular , noting that play was a situation where another player just had an execution issue. “That was not those guys’ (Hemingway and Butler) job, though.” That defender is most likely Walker who should’ve have peeled back to cover McCaffrey instead of moving towards San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy. But amongst the myriad of lowlights, there were highlights from Leonard’s Raiders defense in Week 9. Edge rusher Maxx Crosby dropped Purdy for his fourth sack of the season just before halftime. The play showcases what is possible when all three levels of Las Vegas defense is on point — rush, second level, and backend coverage. As does the interception by rookie safety Treydan Stukes early in the third quarter. Kubiak waxes poetic about the culture and standard that he’s continuing to instill upon his Raiders. Former starting quarterback Kirk Cousins — who was traded to the Minnesota Vikings before the NFL trade deadline this past Tuesday for a 2027 third-round pick — helped foster the high-level of play that’s expected to permeate throughout the Raiders’ building. One can argue keeping Leonard in place creates a lack of accountability as the play under the defensive coordinator falls well below what Kubiak expects from his football team. Maxx Crosby with the SACK 😤 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xvZEgltKmI — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 On the other hand, Kubiak backing Leonard avoids the toxicity of canning a first-time defensive boss that’s growing into the role much like the head coach who chose him. Publicly backing his much-maligned defensive play caller showcases the head coach’s ability to back an assistant threw serious growing pains. And that’s what Kubiak will do through the rest of the 2026 campaign. Live with his choice and see if Leonard rises to the occasion or wilts under the pressure. We don’t know what’s being said behind closed doors, perhaps Leonard is on the receiving end of some harsh criticism from Kubiak that never leaves Raiders’ HQ? Leonard is given a chance to work through the schematic issues. The talent and depth limitations are an offseason item — at the earliest. Las Vegas could dig into the practice squad and elevate 2026 seventh-round pick Brandon Cleveland to the active roster at some point to see if the 6-foot-4 and 315-pound 22-year old can bolster the defensive tackle position, for instance. But until free agency next March and the 2027 NFL Draft a month later — shoot even a full offseason where Kubiak can scour potential replacements for Leonard — true reinforcements are far beyond the horizon. In the meantime, a focus on fundamentals with defenders being in position to make plays, execution, and the continued grind is what’s there for Leonard and Kubiak. Las Vegas still ranks in the upper echelon in terms of takeaways with 14 — good for sixth best in the NFL. And that was the difference maker last Sunday when the 49ers forced turnovers to thwart the Raiders’ offensive attack. Leonard has his reprieve from Kubiak. We’ll see if he can become the coach the head coach believes he can be or if he continues to fumble a golden opportunity away.

title: Fernando Mendoza faces top-ranked Seattle Seahawks’ defense in 1st start for Las Vegas Raiders Week 10 key matchups
summary: Week 10 is the official beginning of a new era for the Las Vegas Raiders, as rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is set to make his first start against the Seattle Seahawks. Meanwhile, the Raiders are still in the playoff picture, and general manager John Spytek made it clear that trading Kirk Cousins and turning the […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 10 is the official beginning of a new era for the Las Vegas Raiders , as rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is set to make his first start against the Seattle Seahawks. Meanwhile, the Raiders are still in the playoff picture, and general manager John Spytek made it clear that trading Kirk Cousins and turning the reins over to Mendoza isn’t a sign that the team is punting on its postseason aspirations. Taking down the defending Super Bowl Champions will be no easy task for Las Vegas, as we dive into this week’s key matchups. Mendoza/Kubiak vs. Seahawks’ Defense Normally, I stay away from broad key matchups like this one because a quarterback and offensive play caller against the opposing defense is significant every week. However, a rookie making his first start against the NFL’s top-ranked defense isn’t a typical circumstance that can be ignored. How good is Seattle at shutting down its opponents? Not only does the unit lead the league in yards per game allowed ( 244.2 ), but it’s over 35 yards per game better than any other defense. For context, the difference between second (Minnesota Vikings at 280.0) and third place (San Francisco 49ers at 291.9) is a little less than 12 yards. The Seahawks dip to tied for fourth in points per game (18.0), but that’s still a top-five unit, and they rank fourth in EPA per play allowed (-0.14), according to Sumer Sports . Diving even deeper, they’re also giving up the fewest passing yards per game (155.1) and are tied for third in EPA per pass allowed (-0.17). That’s the result of having legitimate difference makers on all three levels of the defense between defensive tackle Leonard Williams, linebacker Ernest Jones IV and cornerback Devon Witherspoon, just to name a few. But that also speaks to head coach Mike Macdonald’s scheme and play calling, as his system can create a lot of confusion for young quarterbacks. For example, Macdonald is 6-0 in games where a rookie quarterback attempts at least one pass as the Seahawks’ head coach, per Sumer . So far, the Tennessee Titans’ Cam Ward (256 yards and one passing touchdown) is the only first-year passer to throw for more than 130 yards and a touchdown against Macdonald. But what could give Mendoza an advantage over the other signal callers is that Raiders head coach and offensive play caller Klint Kubiak should know Seattle’s defense well, having spent last season as the Seahawks’ offensive coordinator. That should help Kubiak scheme up some easy throws to help the young quarterback exploit a potential weakness in the scheme, especially early in the game to get him in a groove. Also, the No. 1 pick has been running the scout-team offense against Rob Leonard’s defense, and Leonard’s scheme is similar to Macdonald’s. Granted, Vegas’ defense executes it at a much lower level, but Mendoza should at least have some familiarity with the confusing looks Seattle can present. In other words, there probably isn’t a worse defense for a rookie quarterback to make his first start against. But the 2025 Heisman Trophy Winner does have a great cornerman to assist in navigating the fight. Raiders’ IOL vs. Seahawks DTs As mentioned above, Williams is a big key to Seattle’s top-ranked defense. He was listed as the best defensive tackle in the NFL in Jeremy Fowler of ESPN’s poll of executives, scouts and coaches, with one coordinator noting that Williams “was the most important player on that Super Bowl team”. This season, the three-time Pro Bowler has picked up right where he left off. According to Pro Football Focus , he ranks tied for eighth among defensive tackles in pressures (26) and is tied for fifth in run defense grade ( 77.9 ). Part of the reason for the latter is that Williams has racked up 12 ‘ defensive stops ’ at a 9.8% rate against the run, with both figures ranking in the Top 25 at his position. [Editor’s note: Williams missed last week’s game with a stinger and is considered questionable for this Sunday at the time of writing.] But what makes Seattle’s front even scarier is that Byron Murphy II is just as productive. Murphy is sixth among interior defenders in pressures ( 28 ) and tied for 13th in run stops ( 14 ) at an 8.9% rate. Additionally, Seattle’s third defensive tackle, Jarran Reed, doesn’t offer much as a pass-rusher but is a quality run defender, currently sitting in the top 40 for the position with nine stops against the run. Part of the problem with Williams and Murphy is that those two will line up at several spots on the defensive line. Of Williams’ 358 snaps, 100 have come as a left defensive tackle, 67 have been at right end, 65 at right defensive tackle and 42 at left end, per PFF . Meanwhile, Murphy typically doesn’t play wider than the guards, but he’s registered 252 snaps at both DT spots combined and 80 at nose tackle. So, there will be no breaks for the Raiders’ interior offensive line on Sunday, and the unit needs center Tyler Linderbaum to be at his best. While Linderbaum has faced scrutiny for not living up to the massive contract he signed in the offseason, the free agent addition has picked it up in the last few weeks. He’s only given up two pressures on 108 opportunities and has a 73.7 PFF run-blocking grade during that time frame. For context, his overall mark of 65.3 ranks 14th among centers for the entire season, but he’s tied for sixth at 74.9 in Weeks 7-9 . Meanwhile, the Raiders have a big question mark at right guard. Rookie Trey Zuhn III has been solid in his first two starts during the team’s last two games, giving up just two pressures and posting an above-average 64.7 run-blocking mark. However, Zuhn is in concussion protocol after exiting last Sunday’s contest in San Francisco early. If he can’t go, that likely means either Jackson Powers-Johnson or Caleb Rogers starts, both of whom have been benched already this year. At left guard, it’s hard to know what version of Spencer Burford Las Vegas will get. Since Week 4, he’s followed a trend of earning a PFF grade well above the 60.0 baseline mark in one game and then being well below it in the next. He’s yo-yo’d from an 80.2 mark to 23.4 , 72.0 to 50.1, and 77.4 to 43.6 during that timeframe. That suggests Week 10 will be a strong outing for the fifth-year pro; however, the Seahawks have the best collection of defensive tackles the Raiders have faced this season. Bowers vs. Witherspoon It’s been well-documented that Brock Bowers is a unique offensive weapon who commands the attention of an opponent’s best coverage defender, especially since the Silver and Black’s offense isn’t exactly flush with talent at wide receiver. Raider Nation doesn’t need that to be rehashed here. This week, Bowers should expect to see cornerback Devon Witherspoon often. Witherspoon became the NFL’s highest-paid corner this offseason (until Christian Gonzalez surpassed him a few weeks later), signing a four-year, $132 million ($33 million per year) contract extension. That’s a good indicator of how impactful he is on the Seahawks’ defense, and he’s been used all over the secondary this season. per PFF , 181 snaps have been at slot corner, 147 snaps on the right boundary and 141 on the left. That sets up well to shadow Bowers. Production-wise, the three-time Pro Bowler hasn’t made many plays on the ball this season, with no interceptions and just three passes defended . Also, he’s allowing a 73.3% completion percentage when targeted, per PFF . However, that can be chalked up to having the sixth-lowest average depth of target (5.9 yards) among corners, and no player at the position has made more impactful tackles in coverage with 19 ‘defensive stops’. The latter is six more than any other cornerback. That has allowed Witherspoon to rank ninth at his position in yards per catch allowed (7.5) and could help limit Bowers’ YAC ability. But the 6-foot-4, 240-pound tight end should have an advantage when it comes to contested catches against the 5-foot-11,…

However, quarterback Sam Darnold has dealt with injuries and the Seattle lost Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker in free agency and their running backs room has been dealing with injuries. The constant from last season’s Seattle offense has been wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He has 71 catches for 1,036 yards and nine touchdowns. He won the NFL Offensive Player of the year award last season as he had 119 catches, 1,793 yards and 10 scores. Kubiak helped Smith-Njigba achieve that success last season. Sunday, he must help trying to stop the star receiver.

title: Ashton Jeanty struggles in both running and receiving game in Week 9
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-17 loss at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick saw his play time increase after he played a career […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 38-17 loss at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Seattle Seahawks. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick saw his play time increase after he played a career low 40 percent of the snaps in Week 8. Jeanty played 64 percent of the snaps at San Francisco. Yet, his production remained low. Jeanty had 25 yards on six carries. He has 98 yards rushing on 36 carries in the past five games. Jeanty has been effective as a receiver, but not in Week 9. He has five catches for minus-5 yards Sunday. Jack Bech: The second-round pick played 17 snaps, he fewest in a game this season he finished healthy. He had one catch for nine yards on two targets. Bech has six catches for 57 yards in five games this season. Darien Porter: The third-round pick played 52 percent of the snaps and started after he missed almost all of Week 8 with a groin injury. Caleb Rogers: The benched starter finished the game when he replaced rookie Trey Zuhn at right guard in the third quarter. Zuhn has a concussion and he could miss the Seattle game. Thus, Rogers, a third-round pick, could start this week. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense as usual. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, has been on the 53-man roster for two games and he was inactive for both games. Not great. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 33 snaps, the fourth most by Raiders’ defensive tackles against the 49ers. He had been the leading snap getter at the position most of the season. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the fourth time this season. He played 13 defensive snaps. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 18 snaps on special teams, which is his norm. He has played just three defensive snaps this season.

(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are preparing for their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts, which kicks off at 1 p.m. Eastern on Sunday. The game features two teams in contention for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, though the Colts do not hold a first-round pick this year. Instead, as part of their trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year, that pick belongs to the New York Jets. Could this game decide who holds the keys to the draft in the spring? This game will also feature the Dolphins making multiple roster adjustments after injuries to quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. Kyle McCord is expected to start in Willis’s place, his first regular-season opportunity after the Philadelphia Eagles selected him in the sixth round in 2025. Willis is out for at least four weeks, though season-ending surgery is still possible if his goin injury does not respond to rest. Sieler tore his biceps muscle on the first play of the team’s Week 9 game against the Detroit Lions, but played through the injury for the remainder of the game. He will need surgery and around six months of recovery time before he is cleared to return to football activities. The Dolphins may also be without starting center Aaron Brewer, who missed Wednesday’s practice with a concussion. He will have to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol before he is cleared to play. title: Jakobe Thomas’ Price for Number 8 Has a Lot of Zeros
summary: At his press conference to reintroduce himself to the Twin Cities media on Wednesday, new Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins was asked about what uniform number he would be wearing with the team. The number that he wore his first time with the Vikings, the number 8, is currently being worn by rookie safety Jakobe […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Jakobe Thomas #8 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images At his press conference to reintroduce himself to the Twin Cities media on Wednesday, new Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins was asked about what uniform number he would be wearing with the team. The number that he wore his first time with the Vikings, the number 8, is currently being worn by rookie safety Jakobe Thomas, who the Vikings took in the third round of this year’s NFL Draft. Cousins said that he hoped that he and Thomas could have a reasonable discussion about getting the number back. Well, apparently that discussion has been had, and Thomas has named his price. That price? Zero dollars and zero cents. (Hey, that’s three zeros. . .that’s kind of a lot.) Jakobe Thomas said he got a text from Kirk Cousins about No. 8 yesterday, and gave Cousins the number back with no negotiations. “No money needed,” Thomas said. “I just need him to come here and win games. A lot of fans have his jersey anyway, so they could pull him out of the… — Ben Goessling (@BenGoessling) November 12, 2026 “No money needed,” Thomas said. “I just need him to come here and win games. A lot of fans have his jersey anyway, so they could pull him out of the closet and put him back on. So that’s all it is. Kirko’s got a lot more memories and history in that number than I do, and it’s rightfully his. So I just gave it back to his rightful owner.” That’s a nice move from Thomas, who probably could have gotten a decent chunk of change from Cousins for the number had he wanted to go that route. . .I mean, it’s not like Cousins couldn’t afford it or anything. But he’s got respect for Cousins, so he was kind enough to just give the number over. Thomas will now wear the #6, which was the only number between 0 and 20 that was left available for anyone on the team to wear. So, to borrow a phrase, get your #8 jerseys out, folks, starting this Sunday at Lambeau Field. You won’t even have to put any tape on the back of it or anything.

LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. title: Patriots mailbag: What’s going on with Christian Gonzalez?
summary: The New England Patriots have landed in Germany where they hold a pair of practices before taking on the Detroit Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday. So, let’s get into this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. Like a lot of people, I was mightily disappointed (to say the least) in the recent performance […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have landed in Germany where they hold a pair of practices before taking on the Detroit Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday. So, let’s get into this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. Like a lot of people, I was mightily disappointed (to say the least) in the recent performance of our resident highest-paid cornerback in the league. But I find myself wondering if he’s the only one deserving blame. When he repeatedly lines up in such soft coverage, not pressing at the line of scrimmage — indeed, giving the receiver an obscenely huge cushion to release — that’s not entirely HIS decision, right? Isn’t that pre-snap alignment dictated by the coaches and their game plan, at least much of the time? How much of the problem do you think lies with coaching schemes that play away from Gonzalez’s strengths? – BriGuy301 What happened to Gonzalez last game and why? Was it a one-off, or did the Packers figure something out that other teams might be able to emulate? – fdsafdsa Gonzalez is certainly not blameless and needs to play better. However, he is also being asked to do a lot within a Patriots secondary that leans heavily on disguising coverages. While the All-Pro cornerback is at his best pressing receivers at the line of scrimmage and playing man coverage, he has been asked to handle a variety of responsibilities, including off-man coverage, inverted Cover 2 (where he is responsible for the half-field safety), playing the deep third in Cover 3 and more. The question here is whether the Patriots have leaned too heavily into those disguises and reached a point where simplifying things would benefit the defense. New England has a talented secondary that is playing well below its capabilities as they rank dead last in the league in zone coverage EPA per dropback. Opposing offenses like the Bears and Packers have also appeared to be one step ahead with coverage beaters and using tools like quick snaps to catch the defense out of position and generate explosive plays. At some point, the Patriots may need to prioritize letting their defensive backs play more straight up and to their strengths. With all the pressure that Maye faces each game, and especially against teams like the Packers who blitz a lot (46.5% of his drop backs against Green Bay), why do we not see more hot reads or short patterns? It looks like the Patriots rely predominantly on mid- to long-range routes, which take more time and require the Offensive Line to hold up longer. I would think that Pop or Chism – who both have short-area quickness – would be great at those routes, especially given that they seem to run a lot of them during the preseason. So I’m curious if A) they’re doing it but I just don’t see it? And/or B) is there a good reason to not run quick slants and crossers and hot reads? – PatsFanFromNH The Patriots’ offense does feature sight adjustments and hot routes. Earlier this season, players credited opposing defenses for dropping defenders off the line of scrimmage to take away those routes. New England will need to find ways to counter those adjustments or develop other answers against the pressure packages that have repeatedly given the offense trouble. In recent weeks, both the Bears and Packers have found success attacking the Patriots’ offensive line with overload pressures, sending two defenders off the same side of the formation and dropping defenders off the line of scrimmage on the other side. In both games, New England struggled to pick up those pressures early before settling down and finding answers as the game progressed. Moving forward, the Patriots need to determine how they want to handle those situations out of the gate, whether that means identifying the right protection calls before the snap or trusting Maye and his receivers to make plays after. Finding those answers earlier in games will be critical to avoid early deficits. Brian, if the Patriots lose to the Lions to fall to 5-5 with 4 very difficult games left, is it time to switch gears and root for draft position? It’s been a tough year full of injuries. That happens in football, and the draft is supposed to be a good one. On the other hand, if they pull off the upset in Germany, it’s full speed ahead going for the playoffs, with a bye week plus the Chargers game to get healthy. – New England Guy Sunday’s game against the Lions feels like an inflection point on the season, so it will be interesting to see which Patriots team shows up in Germany. As for the playoffs, 10 wins has historically been a good benchmark for securing a postseason spot. If the Patriots take care of business against the winless Chargers, Jets and Dolphins, they would need just two more wins from their remaining matchups against the Lions, Vikings, Chiefs, Bills and Broncos to reach that mark. And looking at the current AFC landscape, the threshold could be closer to nine wins. There appears to be a relatively clear-cut top seven in the conference unless the Houston Texans catch fire during the second half of the season. Why didn’t the pats trade for a nose tackle, 3rd safety, or/and a 3rd outside cornerback? Any one, two or all 3 of these positions were a must have to right the ship! – sjamesbossports After investing significant draft capital in A.J. Brown and looking to avoid taking on a major financial commitment, the Patriots were never likely to make a significant addition at the trade deadline. You could certainly make the argument for adding defensive depth in exchange for late-round draft capital, but the lack of movement at those positions around the league suggests there wasn’t much of a market at those spots. A question more long term :what are your thoughts about next year patriots cap big moves renegotiation with major players (or potential cut or trade) to absorb anticipated Maye super contract ? – 7i165 Who do you think will be the cap casualties next year? Onwenu, Barmore, Davis, Hunter, Byard, DeVitto, Moses, Landry? I know they are a veteran core, but almost all of them don’t produce to what they are being paid at, so we might need to cut bait. How much would we gain from trading or letting them walk? – Maxxwell The Patriots did not sell at the deadline as they still can be a competitve team especially as they get healthier on offense. It will be a different conversation this offseason as there is definitely an argument for the team getting younger and adding draft capital. Among the names mentioned, I would imagine the team moves on from Christian Barmore, Harold Landry, and potentially Carlton Davis as the veterans have no guaranteed money remaining. Byard’s play has not been worthy of a second contract while the guess would be Moses retires. Henry was extended this offseason while there’s no rush to move off DeVito. All the moves would free up a substantial amount of salary cap space. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: ‘Elite pocket passer’ Jared Goff not being underestimated by Patriots
summary: No matter where you go on Al Gore’s internet, whenever there is a list of the NFL’s best quarterbacks you find familiar faces near the top. Mahomes, Allen, Burrow, sometimes — when he has his turnover tendencies under control — Maye. Jared Goff, on the other hand, typically resides further down the list. It can’t […]
full_text: No matter where you go on Al Gore’s internet, whenever there is a list of the NFL’s best quarterbacks you find familiar faces near the top. Mahomes, Allen, Burrow, sometimes — when he has his turnover tendencies under control — Maye. Jared Goff, on the other hand, typically resides further down the list. It can’t be due to a lack of production, at least this year: Goff has been one of the most efficient quarterbacks in football while leading the Detroit Lions to a 6-2 record. But while fans and analysts might be underestimating the 32-year-old, his next opponent sure is not. The New England Patriots are well aware of the damage he has done, and is capable of doing this Sunday in Munich. “I think Jared’s playing at a high level,” said head coach Mike Vrabel. “Continued the last three years, he’s been at a high level.” “He’s an elite pocket passer,” linebacker Robert Spillane added. “He loves to step up in the middle of the pocket and deliver the ball downfield. Really can do it all. First overall pick for a reason, who just continued throughout his career to show why he was a first overall pick. Somebody who’s going to get the ball to all of his guys.” Distributing the ball to the weapons mentioned by Spillane, as well as to NFL scrimmage yards leader Jahmyr Gibbs, Goff has played some of the best football of his career so far in 2026. The numbers show it, too. In eight games thus far, he has completed over two thirds of his passes (185 of 273) for 2,134 yards, 15 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Whether you use traditional metrics or advanced ones such as EPA or CPOE Goff typically finds himself in the top 10 if not close to the league lead. He might not be the same big-play hunter as the quarterback the Patriots faced last week, Green Bay’s Jordan Love, but Goff has been steady and operating well within Detroit’s offensive system. “The quarterback runs the show very well,” said defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr. “He gets them into plays for the whole unit, and he kind of has the freedom to do that.” There might not be one particular part about Goff’s game or his physical abilities that stands out relative to other quarterbacks, which might contribute to his perception. However, that does not mean he cannot put intense pressure on any defense. A large part of that is his willingness to disperse the football, and the chemistry and experience he has built with the players surrounding him. “He’s a great quarterback,” said safety Kevin Byard. “He does a great job when he’s able to stand in the middle of the pocket, he can fire across the middle of the field, deep, with obviously the weapons that they have with Jameson Williams, a guy who can stretch the field, and obviously Amon-Ra St. Brown, who’s a guy who can work the middle of the field, work the intermediates and things like that. And Sam LaPorta’s a really good tight end.” “He loves [Jameson Williams] down the field. He loves Amon-Ra underneath, LaPorta all over the field,” added Spillane. “We know we have a huge challenge for us ahead.”

title: Patriots vs. Lions weather forecast for NFL Week 10
summary: Drake Maye won’t have to worry about slippery conditions this time around. Beyond just playing his first international game two years ago, the New England Patriots’ then-rookie quarterback also needed to get used to the grass surface at London’s Wembley Stadium. To make matters worse, he had to do all that in rainy conditions. “One […]
full_text: Drake Maye won’t have to worry about slippery conditions this time around. Beyond just playing his first international game two years ago, the New England Patriots’ then-rookie quarterback also needed to get used to the grass surface at London’s Wembley Stadium. To make matters worse, he had to do all that in rainy conditions. “One of the biggest things is getting used to the playing field, seeing what the grass is like,” Maye told reporters at the FC Bayern Munich training facility on Thursday. “I remember in warmups … in London. It was raining and it was open in Wembley, and I was slipping and worried about cleats.” Luckily for Maye and the Patriots, no rain is in the forecast for this Sunday’s international game against the Detroit Lions: according to Bayerischer Rundfunk , the chance of precipitation has been calculated at 0%. Temperature at kickoff will be around 48°F and not drop out of the 40s throughout the game. The Patriots’ most recent overseas contest was a 32-16 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2024. Despite the lopsided final score and challenging footing, Maye completed 26 of 37 pass attempts for 276 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Kickoff between the Patriots and Lions at Munich’s Allianz Arena is set for 3:30 p.m. local time or 9:30 a.m. ET.

full_text: And just like that we are on the back nine. The 10th week of the 2026 regular season will feature the New England Patriots take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday. Besides that game, 13 others are taking place this weekend. Here’s who t root for in those. Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET Washington Commanders (2-5-1) at New York Giants (5-2-1) : Go good game! Two teams with no direct ties to the Patriots’ standings going against each other to kick things off in Week 10. | Prime Video Sunday 1 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) at Atlanta Falcons (3-6) : Go Falcons! Your classic case of NFC team over AFC team. | CBS Houston Texans (3-5) at Cleveland Browns (5-4) : Go Texans! While this might be a dangerous pick given that the Texans have shown some signs of life lately and are still only two games back from the Patriots. At the time being, however, they still have the worse record among the two AFC teams. | FOX Minnesota Vikings (6-2) at Green Bay Packers (6-3) : Go Vikings! At least in theory, a Vikings win could end up having a positive impact on the Patriots: they still might beat them in Week 14 to improve their strength of victory tiebreaker. | FOX Miami Dolphins (1-7) at Indianapolis Colts (2-7) : Go Dolphins! We have done it, folks, we have reached the point where we start thinking about draft positioning. And so, we are picking the Dolphins in this one to help possibly mess up their spot close to the top of those standings. | CBS Carolina Panthers (3-5) at New Orleans Saints (3-5) : Go Panthers! The Patriots own New Orleans’ sixth-round pick in next year’s draft — Ja’Lynn Polk’s parting gift, if you will. The more Saints losses there are, the better for the position of that pick. | FOX Buffalo Bills (7-1) at New York Jets (2-7) : Go Jets! If the Patriots somehow want to retain their AFC East crown, they need the Bills to start losing some more games. What better way to start than a division game. | CBS Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-7) : Go Titans! Go team with the worse record! | FOX 4:05 p.m. ET Seattle Seahawks (5-4) at Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) : Go Seahawks! NFC over AFC, once again. | CBS Los Angeles Rams (5-4) at Arizona Cardinals (3-6) : Go good game! This contest has no true impact on the Patriots. | CBS 4:25 p.m. ET San Francisco 49ers (7-1) at Dallas Cowboys (4-5) : Go good game! Another game with no direct ties to New England and its standing in the AFC. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) at Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) : Go Steelers! Somebody has to win this one — we are not fantasizing about ties here for a moment — so it’s preferable to go with the team that at least the head-to-head disadvantage against the Patriots. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) at Baltimore Ravens (4-5): Go Chargers! Welcome to the “Will Patriots vs. Chargers get flexed out of primetime in Week 12?” bowl. We are rooting for L.A. not because ot scheduling, however, but simply because it has the worse record. | ESPN

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 8: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball against the Green Bay Packers during an NFL football game at Gillette Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots held a walkthrough at the FC Bayern Munich training ground upon arriving in Germany. There were no non-participants left for it on Thursday after head coach Mike Vrabel’s side ruled out running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III in the hours leading up to the overseas flight. But 11 practiced in a limited capacity, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown, as the Detroit Lions await. Here’s the second injury report ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena. DID NOT PARTICIPATE Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) G Ben Brown (knee — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) Lions RB Sione Vaki (ankle) C Cade Mays (ankle — out) CB D.J. Reed (hip — out) Seven Patriots had been sidelined from Wednesday’s sendoff session in Foxborough. And with three staying back, that resulted in perfect attendance for those in Germany. An illness has kept Henderson away from practice since late October and will now keep him off the field for a third consecutive game. In addition to the No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, knee injuries saw starters on the interior line and in the secondary ruled out. Last weekend’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers ended 31 offensive snaps in for Ben Brown. As for Davis, the perimeter cornerback was held to 35 defensive snaps in his second game back from a neck injury that forced him to miss time over the previous two months. The Lions have also since ruled out two players for the Munich matchup. LIMITED PARTICIPATION Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) WR A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) TE Hunter Henry (foot) TE Cameron Latu (back) OT Morgan Moses (foot) G Walter Rouse (concussion) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) CB Charles Woods (hamstring) S Kevin Byard III (chest) S Brenden Schooler (hamstring) Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) Despite facing a reported multiweek absence due to a knee tendon issue, Stevenson made the trip across the Atlantic Ocean. New England’s starting running back proceeded to return to practice in a partial capacity on Thursday. He stands with 657 yards and four touchdowns from scrimmage through 128 touches in 2026. And with a light still left on to face Detroit. Out wide, back-to-back limited practices have been booked by A.J. Brown while working back from a knee issue of his own. Shelved since late October, the June trade acquisition missed the previous two weeks worth of practice as well as two starts. To date, his inaugural Patriots campaign includes nine receptions for 101 yards while also working back from a high ankle sprain. Latu at tight end, Rouse at guard and Schooler on special teams upgraded to limited following Wednesday absences, while the 21-day activation windows remain open for two veterans on injured reserve. A spot on the 53-man roster remains open, too. FULL PARTICIPATION Patriots QB Drake Maye (right shoulder) Lions QB Jared Goff (chest) RB Jacob Saylors (neck, hamstring) DE D.J. Wonnum (concussion) S Brian Branch (hip) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return, out) Both starting quarterbacks move forward among the group of full participants. And while Maye’s throwing shoulder has been listed since the initial weeks of the season, no game designations have followed for the 24-year-old Patriots captain. The reigning AFC Offensive Player of the Month threw three touchdowns and three interceptions in last Sunday’s blowout at Gillette Stadium before taking a seat in the final quarter. That was the case after beginning the calendar with a comeback win spanning four incompletions, two passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown at Hard Rock Stadium.
