title: NY Giants-Washington Commanders not quite ‘for all the marbles’, but it’s big
summary: Week 10, beginning with Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders, is a massive one for the New York Giants. What happens will tell us a great deal about how difficult the Giants’ path to their first NFC East title since 2011 will be. Team Rankings gives the 5-2-1 Giants a 69.5% chance of winning […]
full_text: John Harbaugh and Dan Quinn | Getty Images Week 10, beginning with Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders, is a massive one for the New York Giant s. What happens will tell us a great deal about how difficult the Giants’ path to their first NFC East title since 2011 will be. Team Rankings gives the 5-2-1 Giants a 69.5% chance of winning the NFC East. The 4-5 Dallas Cowboys are at 24.0%, and the 2-5-1 Commanders are at just 6.4%. The Giants are 1.5-point favorites to beat the Commanders Thursday night, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The Cowboys host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers, and Dallas is a 4.5-point underdog. If the Giants win and the Cowboys lose, the NFC East standings will look like this: Giants 6-2-1 Cowboys 4-6 Commanders 2-6-1 The Giants will have a 3½-game lead. In that scenario, if the Giants go a reasonable 3-5 over their final eight games, they would finish 9-7-1. Dallas would have to go 6-1 to get to 10 wins, which is what they would need to win the division since the Giants’ tie with the Commanders counts as half a victory. I doubt even the most ardent of Cowboys fans would feel good about Dallas’s chances of pulling that off. If the Giants lose Thursday and Dallas upsets the 49ers, this is what the NFC East would look like: Giants 5-3-1 Dallas 5-5 Washington 3-5-1 Dallas would be just 1.5 games back, and the Commanders would be back in the hunt with eight games remaining. So, this week could provide a massive swing for the Giants. Giants head coach John Harbaugh was speaking specifically about the Commanders when he said the following, but the idea he was getting at applies to the week and the division as a whole: “This is for all the marbles. It’s a tie right now. This is the tiebreaker. It’s like going to the second half tied, you have a chance to go win the game right now and be one up on these guys for the rest of the season. So, it’s a big game.” Here are the schedules for the Giants and Cowboys after Week 10: Week Giants Cowboys Week 11 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Tennessee Titans Week 12 at Indianapolis Colts vs. Philadelphia Eagles Week 13 vs. San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks Week 14 at Seattle Seahawks BYE Week Week 15 vs. Cleveland Browns at Los Angeles Rams Week 16 at Detroit Lions vs. Jacksonville Jaguars Week 17 at Dallas Cowboys vs. Giants Week 18 vs. Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders Here are a few more things I am thinking about entering the game. Dealing with Daniels The unscripted quarterback run has hurt the Giants all season, never more than it did in Week 5 against Washington when Jayden Daniels ran for 38- and 26-yard touchdowns. After that game, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said those runs “should never have happened.” The difficulty for the Giants, especially with Wilson dialing up as much pressure as he has been in recent weeks, is that they play a lot of man-to-man in the secondary. That means the defensive backs don’t have eyes on the quarterback. They have also only used a spy on the quarterback sparingly. It will be interesting to see how the Giants adjust their approach on Thursday night. Or, if they adjust it at all. Another slop-fest The Week 5 game in Landover, Md. was a slop-fest played on grass in rainy, miserable conditions. This one promises to be a slop-fest played on Field Turf in rainy, miserable, cold conditions. This is the Thursday night forecast for East Rutherford, N.J. from the National Weather Service: Rain. Low around 40. North wind 9 to 11 mph, with gusts as high as 23 mph. Chance of precipitation is 80%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half an inch possible. The Giants lost a chance to win that game when a glove-less Skattebo fumbled away a scoring opportunity in overtime. The Giants have fumbled 14 times this season, losing six. Four teams have more fumbles than the Giants, with the Packers, Patriots, Chargers, and Saints all having 15. Ball security will be at a premium Thursday night. That has, obviously, not been a Giants’ strength this season. Thus, it is worth paying attention to. Considering the likely conditions, it is also worth remembering that rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada went just 2 of 5 on field-goal tries against Washington the first time, missing from 50, 57, and 46 yards. Cam Skattebo revenge game? I wrote on Wednesday about Skattebo’s reaction to all the trade chatter about Jonathan Taylor . Skattebo is a player who thrives on emotion, and he has a laundry list of things to fuel him against the Commanders: The highly publicized, and now failed, Taylor trade discussions. The reality that the NFL world knows the Giants have been looking for an upgrade from Skattebo as RB1 pretty much since John Harbaugh got the head-coaching job. The Giants were in on Kenneth Walker in free agency. They were connected to Jeremiyah Love in the draft. They aggressively pursued Taylor. They even made a call about Bijan Robinson. Missing Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles, which would have marked his return to the place where he suffered his dislocated ankle in 2025. His costly fumble against the Commanders in Week 5, which led to his pseudo-benching in Week 6. Let’s see if he can use all of that to jump-start a running game that clearly missed his presence on Sunday against the Eagles.

title: NFL Week 10 games: Eagles rooting guide
summary: The tenth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 10 games. EAGLES GAME No Philadelphia Eagles game this week; the Birds are on their bye. The 2-7 Eagles have a 0.4% chance (so, you’re saying there’s a chance?!) of making the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 27: Sam Okuayinonu #91 of the San Francisco 49ers sacks Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys during the game during the game at Levi's Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Cowboys 30-24. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The tenth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 10 games. EAGLES GAME No Philadelphia Eagles game this week; the Birds are on their bye. The 2-7 Eagles have a 0.4% chance (so, you’re saying there’s a chance?!) of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy . You can no longer bet on the Eagles to make the postseason on FanDuel; they and the Arizona Cardinals are the only two NFC teams off the board. So, yeah, it’s time to be interested in the Eagles maximizing their positioning in the 2027 NFL Draft. Current 2027 NFL Draft order of non-playoff teams via Tankathon : NFL DRAFT CONSIDERATIONS WASHINGTON COMMANDERS at NEW YORK GIANTS: Big Thursday night matchup between two NFC East teams. The Commanders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Also, the Giants losing makes it harder for them to run away with the division lead, which the Eagles should prefer since they play New York in Week 18. The Eagles shouldn’t want the Giants to be resting their starters in the regular season finale since a Philly win in that spot could mess up Philly’s draft positioning. Root for the Commanders. JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS at TENNESSEE TITANS: Thanks to the Jordan Davis trade, the Eagles own the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Jags to lose as much as possible. The Eagles also want to move ahead of the Titans in the draft order, so, Tennessee winning would be very preferable. Root for the Titans. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at DETROIT LIONS: Thanks to the A.J. Brown trade, the Eagles own the more favorable of either New England’s or Chicago’s 2027 fifth-round pick. However, the Pats are currently the No. 7 seed in the AFC playoff picture. And the Eagles should want to see the Jags fall out of playoff position. That becomes more possible with New England winning here. Root for the Patriots. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS at BALTIMORE RAVENS: Two reasons to root for the Bolts: 1) the Eagles want to move ahead of LAC in the draft order and 2) thanks to the Cam Jurgens trade, the Eagles own Baltimore’s fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Root for the Chargers. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS at ATLANTA FALCONS: The Eagles want to stay ahead of the Falcons in the draft order. Root for the Falcons. HOUSTON TEXANS at CLEVELAND BROWNS: Based on current draft position, the Texans are the bigger threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order. Also, Houston has the best chance of any non-Jags team to win the AFC South. And the Eagles want the Jags to not win their division. Root for the Texans. MINNESOTA VIKINGS at GREEN BAY PACKERS: The Vikings probably have a higher chance of bottoming out and going on a losing streak due to their questionable offensive outlook, even after the Kirk Cousins trade. So, could be good to see them win here, though it doesn’t look like it currently matters much. Root for the Vikings. MIAMI DOLPHINS at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS: The Dolphins have the fifth-toughest remaining strength of schedule while the Colts have the fourth-easiest schedule. Comparatively speaking, this is a rarer opportunity for Miami to get a win that can help move the Eagles above the Dolphins in the draft order. Root for the Dolphins. CAROLINA PANTHERS at NEW ORLEANS SAINTS: Whichever team you think has the lower floor, you want them to win, because they’re the bigger threat to moving ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. I think that’s the Saints, who are worse by point differential/DVOA/weighted EPA per play. Root for the Saints. BUFFALO BILLS at NEW YORK JETS: The Eagles want to stay ahead of the Jets’ own selection (currently No. 6, one spot behind the Birds) in the draft order. Root for the Jets. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS at LAS VEGAS RAIDERS: The Raiders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Raiders. LOS ANGELES RAMS at ARIZONA CARDINALS: The Cardinals are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Cardinals. SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS at DALLAS COWBOYS: I know it’s not fun to see the Cowboys win. But Dallas, which owes the more favorable of two first-round picks (either their own, most likely … or Green Bay’s) to the Jets, is the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Also, I think Eagles fans can agree it would be nice to see the Niners not get the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoff picture. And, once again, it’s preferable for the Giants to not just run away with the NFC East since they might be able to rest starters against the Eagles in Week 18. Root for the Cowboys. Then take a shower. PITTSBURGH STEELERS at CINCINNATI BENGALS: The Jags are currently No. 3 in the AFC playoff picture with a conference games win percentage tiebreaker over the No. 4 Steelers. Pittsburgh plays the Jags later this season, however, so there’s still a chance for the Steelers to earn a head-to-head tiebreaker over Jacksonville. The Bengals, meanwhile, already lost to the Jags. Since it could be easier for the Steelers to move ahead of the Jags in the playoff picture, it’s best to see them win in this spot. Root for the Steelers. title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 10 Edition
summary: Now that Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 08: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni looks on during the game between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles on November 8, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Now that Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 10 POWER RANKINGS 1 – Chicago Bears (Last Week: 1) – Tired: Turning the ball over five times is bad. Wired: Turning the ball over five times in a win is actually pretty impressive. Chicago doesn’t even need to be near their A-game to emerge victorious. The bad news for the Bears is that they play the NFL’s most difficult remaining schedule, in no small part due to the NFC North being loaded. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – The Niners bounced back from their sole loss with a decisive win against a scrappy Raiders team. They’re either going to be the No. 1 seed or the No. 2 seed in the NFC playoff picture. 3 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 3) – There’s no denying the Bills have benefited from their opponents dealing with bad injury lucky, especially at quarterback. Their defense faced pass attempts from Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer over the past two weeks. To their credit, they beat their weakened competition. 4 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 4) – The Chiefs rolled the Jets, as expected. 5 – Detroit Lions (LW: 5) – Make that four straight wins for the Lions. Detroit’s defense has improved … while their offense has cooled off. 6 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 7) – I might be underrating the Jags here; they’re the No. 1 team by DVOA and point differential. And the difference between them and No. 2 in point differential is the same difference between No. 2 and roughly the halfway point between No. 5 and No. 6. The Jags also improved their roster ahead of the NFL trade deadline. They’re going to push for the first-round bye in the AFC playoff picture. 7 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 8) – Pretty strong defense, below average offense. Very good but not great team. 8 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 9) – Drake Maye led the NFL with a 113.5 passer rating last year. Joe Burrow is currently ahead of that mark at 114.8. 9 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 6) – Kirk Cousins offers a level of quarterback competency the Vikings did not have prior to trading for him. They owed it to themselves to try to improve their offense since Brian Flores’ defense is so good. But this feels like a half-measure as opposed to trying to get really aggressive. They paid to be a team that might win a playoff game instead of paying to be a team that can more likely contend for a Super Bowl win. 10 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 11) – The Rams have won three in a row. It helps that they played the Raiders, Chargers, and Commanders. 11 – Denver Broncos (LW: 12) – Did you realize the Broncos have seven wins this season? Doesn’t seem right. Accordingly, they have the worst point differential of the four seven-win teams. They’re at +12 while the others are +79, +69, and +57. 12 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 14) – The Packers are 5-1 in their last six games and the one loss came on the road in Detroit by a field goal. They’re ascending. 13 – New England Patriots (LW: 10) – The Pats have mostly failed to hang with the big boys this season; they have losses to Seattle, Jacksonville, Chicago, and Green Bay. 14 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 13) – By trading Kirk Cousins, the Raiders are finally turning the page to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. The rookie quarterback’s first NFL start will come on the road in Seattle. Big test! 15 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 15) – The Stillers return from their bye for a big AFC North matchup against the Bengals in Cincy. Pittsburgh must win to retain their division lead. 16 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 17) – Dallas failed to cover the spread in a close win over the Colts. Impossible to take them seriously. 17 – New York Giants (LW: 18) – The G-Men are 5-2-1 after winning in Philly for the first time since 2013. New York has benefited from the NFL’s easiest strength of schedule (.346) by far. 18 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 16) – The Ravens are hoping to tread water with Jacoby Brissett until Lamar Jackson can return. Fortunately for them, their schedule does lighten up a bit after losing four straight. 19 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 19) – Back-to-back losses have damaged the Browns’ chances of winning their division. Could still be in the mix for a wild card spot, though. 20 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 20) – The Bucs are 3-6 but they’re looking like the most threatening team in the lowly NFC South at the moment. 21 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 21) – The Panthers had an opportunity to run away with their division and they failed to do so after three straight losses. We’ll see if they can stop the bleeding with a win over the Saints. 22 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 24) – The Saints can make a push for the NFC South crown if they can beat the Panthers. 23 – Houston Texans (LW: 25) – The Texans got a free win by playing the worst team in the NFL. 24 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 22) – The Falcons followed up a win over the 49ers with a shutout loss and a three-possession defeat. Not a very relevant team. 25 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 23) – With Gardner Minshew getting hurt, it’s Carson Beck time out in the desert. 26 – Washington Commanders (LW: 26) – Thursday night’s game against the Giants is a must-win for Washington. Even then, it might be too little, too late. But the Commanders can at least pretend to still be alive for the NFC East while holding a head-to-head tiebreaker over New York. If they lose, Dan Quinn’s fate should be sealed. 27 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 27) – Former Eagles draft pick Kyle McCord is now the starting quarterback in Miami. Given how weird and mismanaged Philly’s QB situation has been, it only feels fitting that he’ll ball out for Kevin Patullo. 28 – New York Jets (LW: 28) – People love to pretend Geno Smith is good for some reason. He’s 4-20 in his last 24 starts. 29 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 29) – After starting the season 2-0, the Eagles have lost seven straight. It couldn’t be more obvious that Nick Sirianni has no answers. The good news is that Howie Roseman is doing his part to put the team in a position to rebound beyond this season. The Jordan Davis trade was an absolute heist. 30 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 30) – The Titans return from their bye to take on the Jags in the first of two meetings over three weeks. More losses are coming. 31 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 31) – Despite losing five straight, the Colts are 3.5-point home favorites against the Dolphins in Week 10. Could be their first win since October 4. 32 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 32) – There’s a real chance this team goes 0-17.

title: Eagles News: Cowboys fans jealous of Philadelphia stockpiling draft picks
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Even in a season where the Eagles are 2-7 and worse than the Cowboys, Dallas fans still wish their team could be more like the Birds. It’s delicious to see how fans of Philadelphia’s NFC East rivals know that the Eagles […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 05: A Philadelphia Eagles fan celebrates next to a Dallas Cowboys fan during the second half of an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 5, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Even in a season where the Eagles are 2-7 and worse than the Cowboys, Dallas fans still wish their team could be more like the Birds. It’s delicious to see how fans of Philadelphia’s NFC East rivals know that the Eagles won’t be down for long. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … The Eagles Have a Plan. The Cowboys Have Jerry Jones. – Blogging The Boys The Eagles are having a down year, and Howie Roseman is doing what smart front offices do. He’s looking ahead, making trades and stockpiling draft picks to reload with 7 picks in the first two rounds of 2027 and 2028. Meanwhile, in Dallas, Jerry Jones and company continue to convince themselves they’re just a player or two away from contending. Spoiler alert: They’re not. Yet they’ve traded away valuable future picks to prop up a team that isn’t nearly as competitive as they seem to believe. NFC East Mixtape VOL. 206: The biggest week yet – NFC East Mixtape The biggest week of the season is here for the NFC East and it is big because of what is happening on Thursday night! The Washington Commanders are set to take on the New York Giants in a game where the latter is trying to take a firm grip on this thing while the former is trying to save their season. Given the importance of the game Scott Bair and Ed Valentine join RJ Ochoa and Brandon Gowton to discuss the matchup and everything encircling the only division where everyone has won the Super Bowl. Oh, and the Dallas Cowboys are also playing a football game this week. You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Eagles aren’t rebuilding. They’re retooling, with the immense draft capital as the backbone. – BGN The NFL trade deadline came and went for the Philadelphia Eagles, with the lone move in the days leading up to the deadline being the departure of Jordan Davis. Surprising? Not really, it’s hard to sell players off in the NFL — even for a team with a 2-7 record. It’s even harder to negotiate with a general manager like Howie Roseman, a savant at holding onto his players until he can deal them at the right price. See Davis and Cam Jurgens, the other in-season deal the Eagles made prior to the deadline that some seem to (already) forget about. The Eagles got a 2027 first-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick, and 2029 second-round pick for Jurgens and Davis — two players drafted in 2022 that clearly weren’t going to be part of the next era of Eagles football. Philadelphia also gave up a 2027 seventh-round pick in the Jurgens deal, and almost recouped a higher pick if the Arnold Ebiketie deal didn’t fall through. Add in the 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-round pick in the A.J. Brown deal five months ago and the Eagles are set for the future. The Eagles have a massive haul of draft picks coming their way over the next three years in the first three rounds — 13 in total. Game Review – NYG 19, PHI 11 – Iggles Blitz My biggest frustration with the game wasn’t the loss, but rather the amount of dumb mistakes the team made. Riq Woolen had a block in the back penalty on a punt return. It was blatantly obvious and put the offense in terrible field position. There were a lot of missed blocking assignments in the run and passing games. There was a completely blown coverage in the end zone. Elijah Mitchell had a pair of brain dead moments. I seriously wonder if he understands the game of football. When you are overwhelmed with injuries, the healthy players must play smart football and do the little things rigt to give the team a chance to win. That just isn’t happening with this team. 2026 NFL midseason report: Questions, stats for all 32 teams entering second half – ESPN Second-half storyline: Can Nick Sirianni save his job? He has built up equity after making the playoffs in each of his first five seasons, complete with a Super Bowl title. But things are a mess, particularly on offense — the side of the ball where his expertise lies. Turnover is coming to the offensive staff. Will Sirianni help oversee the changes, or will he be a part of them? Eagles midterm grades by position at the bye week in 2026 – NBCSP It should be no surprise to see the Eagles’ coaching staff gets the worst grade out of everything. This is a poorly coached team right now. The offense is directionless under Sean Mannion, the OL is a wreck under Chris Kuper, the defense has regressed under Vic Fangio and special teams has regressed under Michael Clay. Ultimately, it all falls on Nick Sirianni, who will have to coach for his job the rest of the season. Maybe he gets a mulligan in a season with a bunch of injuries, including one to his starting QB, but there’s a real chance he’s not back for a seventh season in 2027. 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Chargers land Jeremiah Smith, Dolphins find their quarterback in Drew Mestermaker – PFF 5) Philadelphia Eagles: ED Dylan Stewart, South Carolina. Philadelphia’s edge rushers have disappointed this season, and it’s extremely unusual for the team to rank 29th in the NFL in pass-rush grade. Stewart has rebounded from injury to post an elite 90.8 pass-rush grade and an excellent 18% pass-rush win rate. He’s the exact type of high-ceiling rusher the Eagles can develop as they rebuild in the trenches. […] 25) Philadelphia Eagles (via JAX): OT Carter Smith, Indiana. Smith has been Indiana’s starting left tackle for four seasons and continues to play consistently sound football for the Hoosiers. He has allowed just one sack this season after surrendering two in each of the previous three campaigns. Whether he projects as a right tackle or a guard in the NFL, Smith would provide valuable versatility for a Philadelphia team that needs to bolster its offensive line. NFL Power Rankings, Week 10: Jaguars reach season high; Vikings, Patriots slide after lopsided defeats – NFL.com 31) EAGLES. Philadelphia’s turn to Joe Milton III helped the Eagles hold a temporary lead Sunday before giving it away and losing an ugly game to a division rival. The Eagles’ willingness to trade Jordan Davis to Jacksonville tells us everything we need to know about this team in 2026. Zac Taylor offers apology on behalf of Duke Tobin for botched trade with Eagles – Cincy Jungle “Obviously, we tried something yesterday. Duke (Tobin) was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed, and I’m not comfortable doing it, but I’m gonna do what he asked,” said Taylor. “We did make an effort to put some depth in there in place of Cashius (Howell). As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. Duke is really apologetic about it and wants to make clear Philly was a great trade partner and it was on our end, and that’s just the way things go.” NY Giants-Washington Commanders not quite ‘for all the marbles’, but it’s big – Big Blue View The Giants are 1.5-point favorites to beat the Commanders Thursday night, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The Cowboys host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers, and Dallas is a 4.5-point underdog. If the Giants win and the Cowboys lose, the NFC East standings will look like this: Giants 6-2-1, Cowboys 4-6, Commanders 2-6-1. The Giants will have a 3½-game lead. In that scenario, if the Giants go a reasonable 3-5 over their final eight games, they would finish 9-7-1. Dallas would have to go 6-1 to get to 10 wins, which is what they would…

title: Bengals sent Zac Taylor to clear the Eagles’ name in failed Arnold Ebiketie trade
summary: The Eagles and Bengals thought they had a deal in place to send Arnold Ebiketie from Philadelphia to Cincinnati, but just an hour after the trade was announced, it had reportedly been canceled. Insiders like Adam Schefter were quick to report that the trade falling apart was not due to a physical or performance concern, […]
full_text: LAS ROZAS, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 06: Zac Taylor, head coach of the Cincinnati Bengals, attends during the NFL Madrid 2026, week of game, between Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at Ciudad del Futbol on November 06, 2026, in Las Rozas, Madrid, Spain. (Photo By Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images The Eagles and Bengals thought they had a deal in place to send Arnold Ebiketie from Philadelphia to Cincinnati, but just an hour after the trade was announced, it had reportedly been canceled. Insiders like Adam Schefter were quick to report that the trade falling apart was not due to a physical or performance concern, and it was eventually revealed to be a miscalculation on what Ebiketie would cost the team. Initial trade terms was sending a sixth-round draft pick to the Eagles in exchange for the OLB, but since Ebiketie was a compensatory free agent, trading for him would negate the Bengals future third-round comp pick from the Trey Hendrickson trade. Adding in the loss of a third-rounder, in addition to the agreed upon sixth-round pick, made the trade to expensive for Cincinnati, so they bailed on the deal. Instead of speaking to reporters about the incident himself, Bengals GM Duke Tobin sent a message via head coach Zac Taylor about the situation — who admitted he didn’t really feel comfortable with the specific way Tobin wanted things portrayed —, but wanted it to be clear that Howie Roseman and the Eagles were good trade partners. #Bengals HC Zac Taylor, speaking for GM Duke Tobin, says he’s very apologetic about how the Arnold Ebiketie trade fell apart. “Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end.” pic.twitter.com/kHjzf7UWE6 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 11, 2026 Mike Garafolo said that the vibes inside the Eagles building were very angry, and how teams move in these situations can absolutely affect future trades and team’s willingness to do business together. Taylor shouldn’t have been the messenger, but it was important for Tobin to clear the air and make sure this move wouldn’t even further affect the Eagles in a negative way.

full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line has been the most pleasant surprise of the season so far. Pittsburgh has one of the best rushing attacks in the entire league through nine weeks, averaging 117.9 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s offensive line is finally turning the corner and emerging as a serious strength of the team, and it all starts with their center, Zach Frazier. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell put together his midseason All-Pro team , with the Steelers center earning first-team honors. Frazier’s 79.5 overall PFF grade is first among centers this season. The center has posted his best grades as a run and pass blocker of his career this season. New column: My midseason awards + All-Pro team https://t.co/TywmDBPYUr pic.twitter.com/U1ckcuHeFm — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) November 12, 2026 As well as being named to Barnwell’s midseason All-Pro team, Frazier was also named a top contender for the Protector of the Year award. “With Creed Humphrey’s problems snapping the football becoming more conspicuous, Frazier has emerged for me as the best center in football,” Barnwell said. “The Steelers have quietly fielded one of the league’s most efficient run games this season, and so much of that is what Frazier is able to do as the pivot. Watch here, as he reaches and manhandles Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger to spring Jaylen Warren for a 24-yard gain. Frazier has also given up only one sack and four quick pressures all season, per NFL Next Gen Stats.” There is no denying that Frazier is putting together the best season of his career. The 51st overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft is due for an extension this summer that will almost certainly make him one of, if not the highest-paid center in the league. Frazier will continue to be one of the Steelers’ key building blocks for years to come, and he’s finally getting the attention he deserves. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Mike Tomlin finally reveals why he stepped down as Steelers head coach
summary: Mike Tomlin was head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers for 19 years before stepping down this past January. Months later, before Tomlin returns to the sidelines of a Steelers game as an analyst for NBC Sports this Sunday night as Pittsburgh takes on the Cincinnati Bengals, he opened up to Cam Heyward on his “Not […]
full_text: (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Mike Tomlin was head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers for 19 years before stepping down this past January. Months later, before Tomlin returns to the sidelines of a Steelers game as an analyst for NBC Sports this Sunday night as Pittsburgh takes on the Cincinnati Bengals, he opened up to Cam Heyward on his “Not Just Football” Podcast about his decision to step down. When asked if he knew that he would be retiring after the Steelers loss to the Texans in the wild card round in January, Tomlin admitted the decision was made quickly. “I did probably by the time I pulled in my driveway,” Tomlin said. Tomlin knew very quickly after the loss that he would step down, which suggests that he had been thinking about it for quite some time. “I never wanted to stay too long,” Tomlin continued “As a football lover, I was always really impressed by those that moved away or had the self-awareness to move away at what they deemed the appropriate time. I just always wanted to respect the game enough to be able to do that. To not overstay my welcome. That was a big component of me coming to the decision as anything.” The head coach always knew that he wanted to go out on his terms. His retirement shocked many, as Tomlin kept his decision to himself until it was time to step down. “I just thought we had the makings of a really good team, a team that is capable of competing for and winning a championship,” Tomlin said. “But when I really started thinking about it, man, my bags might slow that down. I thought that guys like him (Heyward) and T.J. were deserving of the optimism that comes with new regimes. I’ve been around that. I saw it in Tampa. I want that for those guys, even if it means it doesn’t happen with me.” The longtime head coach always had the reputation of being someone who had a special relationship with his players. Even when Tomlin decided that he was stepping away from coaching, he had his players in mind, whom he simply wanted to see succeed at the highest level. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers mid-season awards: Rookie of the Year
summary: This marks our final mid-season award for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Thus far, we have crowned Jaylen Warren as the team’s mid-season MVP and Offensive Player of the Year, while T.J. Watt was crowned as the Defensive Player of the Year. Our final award will be Rookie of the Year, taking both sides of the ball […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images This marks our final mid-season award for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Thus far, we have crowned Jaylen Warren as the team’s mid-season MVP and Offensive Player of the Year, while T.J. Watt was crowned as the Defensive Player of the Year. Our final award will be Rookie of the Year, taking both sides of the ball into consideration rather than splitting it into two separate awards. With that said, here is how our staff voted. Joey Bray – OT Max Iheanachor: Ever since Max Iheanachor made his first start in Week 3, the Steelers’ offensive line has shown massive improvement. The first-round pick has beaten the “project” allegations with exceptional play from his first start in the league. Iheanachor is going to be a huge piece of the Steelers offensive line for years to come. Austin Bechtold – WR Germie Bernard & S Robert Spears-Jennings: I couldn’t pick just one so decided to pick one on each side of the ball. Bernard has impressed and earned Aaron Rodgers’ trust, something close to impossible for rookie wide receivers to do. In eight games, Bernard owns 32 catches for 284 yards and one touchdown. He’s basically played six games after only a handful of snaps against Atlanta and only one catch against Cincinnati. Bernard has a more diverse route tree than DK Metcalf and I think is a better all-around receiver. The Steelers found a gem in the second round and no one is going to miss out on Makai Lemon. Robert Spears-Jennings has a serious case to win this award outright. The Steelers continue to rave about his ability and keep playing the defensive back after DeShon Elliott returned. He’s registered 20 tackles and his first career interception against Cleveland. Spears-Jennings is PFF’s fifth-highest-graded rookie (78.7) and the highest-graded rookie tackler (82.7) in football. The former seventh-round pick looks like a starter for years to come. Spears-Jennings has helped solidify a veteran, but very vulnerable secondary. Ryan Parish – OT Max Iheanachor: Another race with several valid options. Seventh-rounder Robert Spears-Jennings has a case, as does Germie Bernard and Daylen Everette. But as one of the lone voices that was celebrating getting Iheanachor over Makai Lemon on draft weekend, I’m thrilled that he’s playing so well. The Steelers’ offense was unquestionably and definitively improved beginning the week Iheanachor took over as starter and the line as a whole is now a strength of the team. That locks up the award in my book. Ryland Bickley – OT Max Iheanachor: This was the easiest choice for me. The Steelers’ offensive success this season can be traced back to the moment Iheanachor and Brock Hoffman were inserted into the right side of the offensive line. Has Iheanachor been perfect? Far from it, but I’m not sure where the Steelers offense would be right now without the rookie tackle. Mike Nicastro – OT Max Iheanachor: While Germie Bernard and Daylen Everette will certainly receive consideration, my vote goes to rookie offensive tackle Max Iheanachor. After a 1-1 start, head coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to insert the rookie into the lineup. Since then, Pittsburgh has responded by winning five of their next six games and improving to 6-2. That’s not to suggest Iheanachor is solely responsible for the turnaround, but his presence has helped stabilize an offensive line that needed a spark. His physical tools, ability to hold up at the point of attack and continued development have made him an important addition to the starting lineup. Bernard and Everette deserve recognition for their contributions, but Iheanachor gets the nod because of the impact he’s made at a position where rookie adjustments can be particularly difficult. Jason Aponte – WR Germie Bernard: After logging just three snaps in Week 1, Bernard has run away with this award. Given the injuries to Michael Pittman, Jr and Roman Wilson, Bernard has gained the trust of Aaron Rodgers, and the duo evokes memories of Rodgers and Randall Cobb. The arrow is up for the rookie receiver, and regardless of the health of returning players should be involved all the way down the stretch. Jarrett Bailey – S Robert Spears-Jennings: The safety position has been a very thin one for the Steelers, but seventh-round pick Robert Spears-Jennings has been terrific this season. Of all safeties to play at least 100 snaps, he is 13th in lowest completion percentage allowed as the nearest defender, and his yards per coverage snap and yards per target are both in the top 20, as well. He has proven to be tremendous value after being selected in the final round of the draft, and someone who could end up being a growing piece of the defense, not just in 2026, but for seasons to come. Consensus Rookie of the Year: OT Max Iheanachor Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: The Steelers made zero trades – and that’s completely fine
summary: I don’t want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. When the NFL trade deadline came and went, I was vocal with my praise of the Jacksonville Jaguars for their “F—k them picks” approach and pushing all their chips to the middle of the table. Many Pittsburgh Steelers fans were hopeful that […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports I don’t want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. When the NFL trade deadline came and went, I was vocal with my praise of the Jacksonville Jaguars for their “F—k them picks” approach and pushing all their chips to the middle of the table. Many Pittsburgh Steelers fans were hopeful that general manager Omar Khan would make a big move(s) of his own after the Steelers were at the center of trade rumors for the better part of a month. Instead, Pittsburgh stayed put and didn’t make any trades before the 4:00 PM EST deadline on Tuesday, which led to many a Steelers fan to all but proclaim the season as over. I don’t know how I became the rational one as it pertains to the Steelers, but the front office not making any sort of trade doesn’t bother me in the slightest. Would I have enjoyed seeing a big-time safety like Amani Hooker or Jessie Bates head to Pittsburgh? Yes. The same can be said about a cornerback like Riq Woolen or Charvarius Ward. At the same time, though, the defense is phenomenal. They are fourth in fewest points per game allowed, seventh in yards per game, and their run defense has been the best in the NFL since Week 4. I’m all for a great unit getting even greater, and would have loved a trade for any of the aforementioned names, but I’m also not throwing my hands in the air about it. As it pertains to the receiver position, there were simply no needle-moving trades to be made. Brian Thomas Jr. was the golden goose and best available name at the position – the Jaguars opted to keep him, and that was probably the right move on their part. Who else were the Steelers supposed to try and get? Josh Downs isn’t a needle mover. Calvin Ridley certainly isn’t, either. They’ll get Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson back in the lineup before the end of the season, which will provide in-house aid to the group of pass-catchers. Yes, I love when a team goes balls to the wall and puts everything on the line to win a championship. I mentioned the Jaguars, and they are a perfect example of that. However, they are also in a very different position than Pittsburgh organizationally. They have a long-term answer at quarterback signed and locked up in Trevor Lawrence who is continuing where he left off in 2025 when he finished fifth in MVP voting. They have a group of three-five legitimate pass-catchers at receiver and tight end and a good run game. They are the only team in the league that is currently top five in offensive and defensive EPA. And while the Steelers are in the midst of a great season themselves, they don’t have that long-term answer at quarterback on the roster, making them (understandably) hesitant to part ways with draft picks to use in a potential trade up in the 2027 NFL Draft to select a signal-caller. So with that all in mind, let’s focus on the rest of 2026. What does the offense need to do going forward after keeping their group the exact same? For starters, spend more time under center. The Steelers are the 10th-best offense in terms of EPA since Week 4 when they go under center. Additionally, keep trotting out heavier personnel. Over that same time span, Pittsburgh is the best team in the NFL when they have three tight ends on the field. Bully ball is working. They need to lean into it more rather than try to make a largely ineffective passing game the star of the show. There are plenty of things we can be hard on the Steelers’ front office and ownership for. The trade and extension for DK Metcalf, then following that up with trading away George Pickens. The handling of the Joey Porter Jr contract (although, right now they look like they are actually coming out as the victors in that situation), the lack of long-term answer at quarterback since Ben Roethlisberger retired – all are fair to point at and ridicule. full_text: The Seattle Seahawks call it their ready squad… the league recognizes it as a practice squad. Seattle added veteran guard Cordell Volson to that group of 17 on Thursday. (A reminder that center Federico Maranges qualifies for the NFL’s IPP roster exemption) The Seahawks announced they’ve signed G Cordell Volson to their practice squad and released S AJ Finley to make room. Volson is a former starter for the Bengals and was college teammates at North Dakota State with Grey Zabel and Jalen Sundell. — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 12, 2026 The 28-year-old Volson made 48 starts in three years with the Cincinnati Bengals, missed all of last season with an injury, and this year has since spent preseason and practice squad stints with the Tennessee Titans and Green Bay Packers. After the blockbuster trade for Quenton Nelson , the Seattle Seahawks had to announce a minor medical procedure for the star lineman’s knee after one game. He is currently week to week, but should avoid IR. In his place, Anthony Bradford is off the bench and back in the lineup at RG, shifting Grey Zabel back to his most experienced pro position at LG. Behind those two, fifth-round rookie Beau Stephens provides depth. The addition of a former starter in Volson keeps Seattle’s bases covered when it comes to depth a week away from its bye week. Like Zabel and starting center Jalen Sundell, Cordell Volson played collegiately at North Dakota State. Volson is a former fourth-round pick by the Bengals, and has experience mainly at LG. When Stephens was getting playing time this year in place of Bradford, it was in a rotational role with Christian Haynes at RG. Haynes is gone to South Beach and the backup room may be shifting. The Seahawks have signed multiple former starters as depth pieces just this offseason. Names like Rodney Thomas II and Bobby Hart have seen action. It wouldn’t be surprising to see Volson get an immediate practice squad elevation for Sunday’s game against the Raiders, while Q-Nelson is out. Safety AJ Finley, who started in the Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders, has been released to make room for Volson.

title: Seahawks All-22 review: What the film tells us from Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks bounced back from their loss to the Chicago Bears, defeating the Arizona Cardinals at home to move back above .500. Beating Arizona wasn’t enough to restore all the confidence Seattle had lost or completely revive its playoff hopes. Still, with seven players ruled out, including Sam Darnold, Quenton Nelson, Charles Cross, Leonard […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 08: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks catches a pass in front of Baron Browning #5 of the Arizona Cardinals during the first half at Lumen Field on November 08, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks bounced back from their loss to the Chicago Bears, defeating the Arizona Cardinals at home to move back above .500. Beating Arizona wasn’t enough to restore all the confidence Seattle had lost or completely revive its playoff hopes. Still, with seven players ruled out, including Sam Darnold, Quenton Nelson, Charles Cross, Leonard Williams, Uchenna Nwosu and Rashid Shaheed, this was a game the Seahawks simply could not afford to lose. Despite facing an opponent that never looked particularly threatening, Seattle showed resilience and, more importantly, a few signs of improvement. The 17-3 victory wasn’t spectacular , but there were encouraging developments on both sides of the ball. Let’s take a look at the good, the bad, and what the All-22 tells us about Seattle’s performance. The Bad The offensive line still has a long way to go The Seahawks’ offensive line continues to struggle with consistency. Injuries certainly haven’t helped, and the anticipated impact of Quenton Nelson’s arrival has been delayed by a few weeks. Grey Zabel vs Quenton Nelson execution pic.twitter.com/lSXXC3T8Kg — Alexandre Castro (@alexcastrofilho) November 11, 2026 Speaking of Nelson, there was plenty of discussion about whether Anthony Bradford should remain in the starting lineup while Grey Zabel moved to the bench once Nelson returned. I think this game provided another reason why that shouldn’t happen. Bradford’s limitations remain evident, while Zabel still offers considerably more long-term upside. Here, Bradford’s immediate loss in pass protection (on the game’s first play, nonetheless) prevents Drew Lock from getting to any secondary reads. He’s easily beaten by Walter Nolen’s hand technique and has no opportunity to recover once the pressure gets through. You might argue that Bradford isn’t particularly good in pass protection, but at least he contributes to the running game. That’s true to some extent, but his run blocking has been far from consistent. He was thoroughly dominated by Walter Nolen and Andrew Billings throughout the game. On this play, his poor timing and angle leave the defensive tackle free to blow up the entire run. That doesn’t mean Zabel has been playing particularly well, either. I simply believe his potential is considerably higher than anything Bradford has shown so far. On this snap, Zabel fails to properly set up his pull block, missing the opportunity to create space and ultimately blowing up the play. Abe Lucas also hasn’t returned to his previous level of play. On this snap, he’s beaten by LJ Collier. There’s not much more to explain here: it’s simply a bad rep from the right tackle. As mentioned earlier, this isn’t a problem isolated to one player. We also see issues when the offensive line has to work together. Bradford is completely lost in his assignment here, but the bigger issue is that communication breakdowns have become a recurring problem for this unit. Here’s another communication breakdown. The protection slide appears to be directed toward the right, which means Zabel should be responsible for the more interior gap, especially considering Josh Jones’ movement. I also believe Sundell could have adjusted after seeing No. 50 move in the opposite direction. These are the kinds of technical, communication, and adjustment issues that need to be cleaned up. The defense still has room to improve The defense’s numbers were impressive. Seattle contained the running game, showed progress in the red zone and, for the first time this season, kept an opponent out of the end zone. However, against a dysfunctional Cardinals offense, there were still areas that need attention. Arizona finished with just 198 total yards, including 50 rushing yards on 18 attempts (2.8 yards per carry). Gardner Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards without a touchdown or interception, and Seattle recorded three sacks. After allowing a field goal on Arizona’s opening possession, the Seahawks shut the Cardinals out for the rest of the afternoon. They also forced a turnover on downs on Arizona’s final red-zone opportunity. That’s an excellent response, especially considering the absences of Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu. The edges of the defensive line remain one of the most vulnerable areas against the run. I’ve noticed a recurring tendency for the EDGE defenders to attack the more interior gap aggressively, while the rest of the defense fails to execute the necessary replacement responsibilities. This creates running lanes that opponents can exploit. It’s something that needs to be addressed with some urgency. Another issue has been the space between defenders and the way offenses manipulate Seattle’s second level. Routes attacking those areas have repeatedly found openings. This is something to keep an eye on, particularly with Brock Bowers coming up next week. Seattle plays man coverage against Arizona's empty formation, spreading out the defense. Thomas has a chance for an easy tackle but loses the rep to Minshew. If the QB doesn't give himself up, he might even have a path to the end zone. pic.twitter.com/yHhLd8Hob8 — Alexandre Castro (@alexcastrofilho) November 12, 2026 The Seahawks are playing man coverage against this Cardinals empty formation, designed to spread out the defense. Drake Thomas has a clear opportunity to make an easy tackle, but he loses the rep to Gardner Minshew. If the quarterback doesn’t give himself up, he might even have a chance to reach the end zone. Jobe's reps tend to follow the same pattern. When he wins at the line with his press technique, he can make plays. When he loses that initial battle, things go downhill quickly. Here, he's in trail position, but Minshew is sacked before he can throw. pic.twitter.com/m8ygRxfhPS — Alexandre Castro (@alexcastrofilho) November 12, 2026 Josh Jobe’s reps tend to be repetitive. When he wins at the line of scrimmage with his press technique, he has a chance to make a play. When he loses that initial battle, things usually go downhill quickly. Here, he ends up in trail position behind the receiver, but fortunately, Minshew is sacked before he has time to deliver the ball. The Good The Price and Charbonnet duo gives Seattle reasons for optimism This was the second game with Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet sharing the backfield, and there were some encouraging signs. Charbonnet finished with 16 carries for 77 yards (4.8 yards per carry), adding one reception for nine yards. Price recorded nine carries for 24 yards and made an even bigger impact as a receiver, catching all four of his targets for 54 yards. That gave him 78 yards from scrimmage, while Charbonnet finished with 86. Those performances offer some hope for greater consistency in the running game, particularly once Nelson returns and Seattle gets its offensive line closer to full strength. And speaking of consistency, the Seahawks have a running back who provides plenty of it. I don’t necessarily see Charbonnet as an explosive runner who will consistently threaten defenses with long gains, but he’s always looking for ways to keep the offense moving. Here, AJ Barner’s block gets beaten, forcing Charbonnet to make an immediate adjustment. Notice how he doesn’t waste time searching for some magical running lane. Instead, he finds a way to salvage the play and pick up positive yardage. He then runs through contact, continuing to fight for every extra yard. This is a highlight-worthy run. The design sends Charbonnet right behind the FB and OL, but he cuts back, forcing the center to adjust. Billings initially does a great job, yet Charbonnet escapes, breaks another tackle and picks up the first down to help seal the win.…

title: Seahawks defense presents a major test for rookie Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza
summary: The Seattle Seahawks’ next opponent is making a major change at quarterback. After trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, the Las Vegas Raiders are turning to Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, as their starter for Week 10. Mendoza has already made his NFL debut, completing six of […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks’ next opponent is making a major change at quarterback. After trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, the Las Vegas Raiders are turning to Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, as their starter for Week 10. Mendoza has already made his NFL debut, completing six of eight passes for 48 yards in garbage time against the New England Patriots. Sunday, however, will be a different challenge: his first career start against the reigning Super Bowl champions and one of the NFL’s most difficult defenses to prepare for. The Cousins trade also has implications beyond Las Vegas. Minnesota is strengthening its quarterback room with a familiar veteran, potentially improving the offense of a team competing in the same NFC playoff picture as Seattle. While the Vikings still have questions to answer, the move makes them a team worth watching in the wild-card race. For the Seahawks, though, the immediate focus is Mendoza. And if history is any indication, Mike Macdonald has a particularly uncomfortable welcome waiting for the rookie. A difficult matchup for first-year quarterbacks Macdonald has built his defensive reputation around disguise, pressure and forcing opposing quarterbacks to make decisions before they are entirely comfortable with what they see. That combination can be especially difficult for a rookie. Young quarterbacks are still learning how quickly NFL defenses close throwing windows, how protections should respond to different fronts and when a seemingly open receiver is actually being baited into a dangerous throw. Macdonald frequently uses simulated pressures and disguised coverages to complicate those decisions. A defense can show a threatening blitz before dropping defenders into coverage, or present what looks like a manageable protection before sending pressure from an unexpected angle. The objective is not just sending more rushers; it is to make the quarterback unsure of where the pressure is coming from and which areas of the field will remain open after the snap. That uncertainty creates two opportunities for Seattle. The first is hesitation: if the quarterback holds the ball while identifying the rush, the pass rush gets more time to reach him. The second is a rushed decision: if he anticipates pressure and throws early, he may deliver the ball into a coverage that looks different from the one he initially read. For an experienced quarterback, these situations are challenging enough. For a rookie making his first start, the margin for error is considerably smaller. The numbers against rookie quarterbacks Seattle’s recent matchups with rookie starters illustrate the challenge. Across the four games against Bo Nix, Caleb Williams, Cam Ward, and Max Brosmer, the quarterbacks combined for 642 passing yards, seven interceptions and 17 sacks. Those quarterbacks completed 89 of 142 pass attempts, for a combined completion percentage of 62.7%. The most striking numbers are the sacks and interceptions. Seattle averaged more than four sacks and nearly two interceptions per game in this sample. That is a demanding combination for any offense, especially one relying on a quarterback who has not yet experienced the full speed and complexity of an NFL defense as a starter. The passing-yardage average also tells part of the story. Although Cam Ward threw for 256 yards, the other three quarterbacks combined for just 386. The overall average was 160.5 yards per game, with the individual performances varying considerably. The results were equally notable: Seattle won all four games. Four games, four different challenges Bo Nix opened his rookie season against Seattle in September 2024. The Seahawks held him to 138 passing yards, intercepted him twice and sacked him twice in a 26–20 victory. Nix completed 26 of 42 attempts, but the volume did not translate into an efficient passing performance. Caleb Williams had an even more difficult afternoon. In a 6–3 Seahawks win, he completed 16 of 28 passes for 122 yards, threw an interception and was sacked seven times. The game demonstrated how a defense can disrupt an offense without needing to generate a large number of points itself. Cam Ward provided a different test in 2025. He completed 28 of 42 passes for 256 yards without an interception, but Seattle still recorded four sacks and won 30–24. His production showed that rookie quarterbacks can find opportunities against this defense, even when the overall matchup remains difficult. Max Brosmer’s experience was the most punishing statistically. In Seattle’s 26–0 shutout of Minnesota, he completed 19 of 30 passes for 126 yards, threw four interceptions (including an awful pick-six to Ernest JOnes) and took four sacks. The four games offer different lessons. Nix struggled with turnovers, Williams was overwhelmed by pressure, Ward produced yards but could not lead Tennessee to victory, and Brosmer endured a disastrous afternoon against a defense that consistently won the decisive plays. Mendoza will need to avoid all four outcomes. What this means for Fernando Mendoza Mendoza enters the matchup with an impressive college résumé, including a Heisman Trophy and a national championship at Indiana. But college accomplishments cannot eliminate the learning curve involved in facing an NFL defense. His most important task may not be producing explosive plays. It may be avoiding the mistakes that allow Seattle to control the game. That means getting the protection calls right, identifying where pressure could come from, trusting the answers built into the offensive scheme and knowing when an incompletion is preferable to forcing a throw. The Raiders will also need to help him with a credible running game and manageable third downs. If Mendoza repeatedly has to hold the ball while deciphering Seattle’s coverage, the Seahawks’ pass rush could take over. If he anticipates pressure and throws without confirming the post-snap picture, Macdonald’s disguises could create turnover opportunities. The Raiders cannot expect their rookie to solve every problem on his own. The coaching staff must put him in positions where he can make quick, defined reads rather than asking him to consistently win complicated passing situations. For Seattle, the plan is straightforward: make the rookie prove he can recognize the defense, protect the football and respond when the first option is unavailable. Final Thoughts Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start presents the Seahawks with an opportunity to test a rookie against a defense built to create uncertainty. Macdonald’s system does not rely exclusively on overwhelming quarterbacks with blitzes; it combines pressure with disguise, forcing passers to diagnose the play while the pocket is already changing around them. Seattle’s recent results against rookie starters are encouraging. Those numbers do not guarantee another dominant performance, but they establish a clear challenge for Las Vegas. For the Seahawks, the ideal outcome is to make the rookie hesitate, force him into difficult decisions and turn those moments into sacks, turnovers and stalled drives. If Seattle executes that plan, Mendoza could discover just how steep the learning curve can be when facing Mike Macdonald’s defense for the first time as a starter.

title: Recent history shows that 49ers-Cowboys is a ‘rivalry’ in name only
summary: The San Francisco 49ers head to Arlington to face off with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in what used to be a hotly contested rivalry. Yes, you read that right. Of course, both fan bases and the players dislike each other given the history, but a rivalry isn’t a rivalry until a team wins a […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers head to Arlington to face off with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in what used to be a hotly contested rivalry. Yes, you read that right. Of course, both fan bases and the players dislike each other given the history, but a rivalry isn’t a rivalry until a team wins a game. I’m referring to the 49ers owning the Cowboys. Despite numerous beatdowns, the Cowboys (Micah Parsons) players and organization have stated they will “have something” next time for the 49ers. Ok, when? One side does the winning; the other side does the yapping. Here is the recent history between Dallas and San Francisco. The 49ers lead the all-time series with a 21-19-1 record over 41 meetings. The last Cowboys victory was in 2020 over the Nick Mullens-led 49ers. 2021 Wild Card The two teams squared off in the playoffs for the first time since the 49ers defeated Dallas to move on to the Super Bowl in the 1994 NFC Championship Game. Jimmy Garoppolo and the 49ers narrowly escaped with a 23-17 score following a mental lapse by Dak Prescott, allowing the game to end before an attempted spike. Deebo Samuel was the engine of the 49ers’ offense and famously told Kyle Shanahan to get him the ball, and he “put the ball in the box.” 2022 Divisional Round In back-to-back seasons, the two franchises met, but this time at Levi’s Stadium. The entire game was tense and went down to the wire, with one of the more interesting play calls and formations for Dallas being Ezekiel Elliott snapping the ball alone and being asked to block the pass rush on the final play. With a 19-12 score, Brock Purdy and the 49ers did enough to advance to the NFC Championship Game in Philadelphia. The 49ers’ victory tied the all-time series at 19-19-1. 2023 Week 5 The 2023 49ers were a juggernaut. Dallas stood no chance against the 49ers offense, and George Kittle lit the Cowboys up for three touchdowns and proudly displayed a shirt that expresses every 49ers fan’s sentiments regarding Dallas. The 32-point margin was the largest victory over the Cowboys. Parsons would run to his podcast to complain about Kittle rather than stop him. That is typical Cowboy behavior. 2024 Week 8 Dallas actually led this contest at halftime, 10-6. The third quarter would see the floodgates open for the 49ers offense, and the team put up 21 in the quarter. Kittle would score again, and Dallas would close the gap with 3:32 left in the fourth quarter, but ultimately the 49ers would prevail. Anders Carlson was the 49ers’ kicker in this game and added three field goals. Just something funny to note. Unfortunately, until the Cowboys punch back, this rivalry has turned into a one-sided beef. It won’t happen Sunday. The rivalry has turned into an avalanche.
author: Jason Aponte

title: Where Keenan Allen fits in the 49ers offense, and the one Brock Purdy weakness he can fix
summary: Everybody’s calling Keenan Allen insurance for Mike Evans. I think that sells short what the San Francisco 49ers just bought for a sixth-round pick. Allen isn’t here to be Evans. He’s here to fix the one spot where Brock Purdy hasn’t been elite. Look at Purdy’s Independent Quarterback Rating from Sports Info Solutions. It’s passer […]
full_text: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) Everybody’s calling Keenan Allen insurance for Mike Evans. I think that sells short what the San Francisco 49ers just bought for a sixth-round pick. Allen isn’t here to be Evans. He’s here to fix the one spot where Brock Purdy hasn’t been elite. Look at Purdy’s Independent Quarterback Rating from Sports Info Solutions. It’s passer rating, graded on the throw instead of what happens after it, so a drop doesn’t count against the quarterback. On throws of zero to nine yards, Purdy sits at 107. On throws of 20-plus, he’s at 135. But on throws between 10 and 19 yards? A 79. That’s his worst zone by a mile. Now look at where Allen lives. His average target this season came 8.5 yards downfield. He dropped one ball all year. That’s third-and-7 country. That’s where linebackers and safeties sit in zone, and where you need a receiver who knows exactly where to settle and has the hands to finish it in traffic. Allen has made a career out of that. And don’t judge him by his work in Indianapolis. The Colts are 2-7, Allen was trailing Josh Downs and Laquon Treadwell in routes, and the ball wasn’t finding him in good spots. Put him with a quarterback who wins with timing and efficiency, and that changes. I saw video of him at practice. Let’s be honest, he ran a 4.71 coming out of Cal, and at 34, the 4.7 isn’t there anymore. Nobody’s asking him to run past anybody. But the movement is still there. He’s quick in and out of his breaks, and he’s strong at the catch point. He’s a grown man. He’ll block in the run game, and in this offense that matters. Here’s what I love most. On third-and-7, the 49ers don’t have to dig into the playbook for a creative call with extra motion and moving parts. Sometimes it isn’t about the scheme. It’s cat coverage: your cat versus my cat. And for the first time since Evans went down, the 49ers have a cat that can win that fight. Allen wins with footwork and release packages, and he knows where to sit against zone. That’s the piece the offense has been missing: a guy who can just win no matter what the defense calls. Is he a yards-after-catch guy? No. He averages 2.7 yards after the catch, and this offense lives on YAC. But that’s not his job. His job is to move the chains when the play breaks down. And the timing works. Dallas ranks 30th in defending intermediate throws, according to NFL Pro. Kyle Shanahan says he’ll reassess Allen on Saturday, so we’ll see how much he plays in Dallas. I’ve got a lot more to say about how Shanahan can use him, and we’re breaking it down on The Coaches Huddle this week. So what do you think, Faithful? Is Allen the piece that fixes Brock’s middle of the field, or just a nice veteran to have around?
author: The Coach

title: Why it’ll be tough for the 49ers to take Jordan Watkins off the field
summary: One player who has taken a big step in his development is Jordan Watkins. He’s growing up right before our eyes. Physicality kept Watkins off the field at the start of the season. Remember, he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. Watkins is still learning the ropes and figuring out what it takes to […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images One player who has taken a big step in his development is Jordan Watkins. He’s growing up right before our eyes. Physicality kept Watkins off the field at the start of the season. Remember, he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. Watkins is still learning the ropes and figuring out what it takes to block, but he’s much improved. With a banged-up wide receiver room in Week 9, Watkins led the way with 52 snaps, 17 more than any other wideout. He’s a player general manager John Lynch is “proud” of. Lynch walked us through Watkins’ journey from a rookie to today: He really stuck it out. We had a lot of high hopes for him when we brought him from Ole Miss. I remember Kyle and I being on the phone with Lane Kiffin, who was his coach there and saying, ‘Man, we see outstanding talent. Tell us about this young man.’ You know he was hampered a bit there by injuries at Ole Miss, but he’s got a lot of juice. I think what we’ve learned, and it’s been a little bit of a process. He’s had to fight a little to get himself out on the field. There were some good options at receiver. I think there was some frustrations on Jordan’s part. To his credit, he kept going out there and grinding. It would have been easy for Watkins to feel sorry for himself, make excuses, and be content with his situation. According to Lynch, a conversation with Kyle Shanahan helped Watkins correct his course: He did have a conversation with Kyle. And Kyle said, ‘Man, it’s nothing that you’re not doing. Just focus on the little stuff. Everyone sees the touchdown on a post. And that was a great play. But really, what got Jordan on the field was his toughness in the run game. And becoming that guy for us. You lose a big body in Stribling. And Demarcus Robinson goes down. Somebody’s got to block on all these tosses we run. Somebody’s got to block defensive ends. That’s not very fun when you’re a smaller body. But we needed someone to do it. Jordan, that’s the way he found his way on the field. His ability to go out there and help on special teams. Watkins had to learn that there’s more to being a wide receiver in the NFL than running routes and catching passes. Of the 52 snaps he played against the Raiders, 28 of those were on running downs. That’s the ultimate sign that he has Shanahan’s trust. There’s still plenty of room to grow, but we’re seeing Watkins progress in real time and respond to coaching. That explains why Lynch is proud of Watkins: So, I’m really proud of the young man. He fought his way out there. He earned it. And not it’s starting to pay dividends for himself, and for our team, in a big way. I’m really proud of Jordan. He grinded. And now he’s kind of creating a niche. Everything in this league is earned. It doesn’t always come easy. Not everybody starts and steps in on Day 1. If you earn it, and you find a way to get yourself on the field. Then you have an opportunity. And you can make a play. And now, it’s going to be hard to get Jordan off the field, because he’s earned that right. So, I’m really excited and proud of him. He was in the top five before this, but Watkins 60-yard touchdown catapulted him to No. 1 among all wide receivers in EPA/target. The majority of his 10 receptions have resulted in some impact play for the 49ers. Perhaps the biggest surprise is Watkins winning his 50/50 opportunities over the previous month—all the more reason to keep developing a player you may need to count on in the postseason. Lynch concluded, “I don’t see him coming off. You play like he has been playing. The nitty-gritty. The tough stuff. Hank [49ers WR coach/passing game coordinator Leonard Hankerson] has a saying that I love. ‘No block, no rock.’ And he’s been doing a lot of block. He’s been doing the little stuff. And that’ll get you on the field around here.”
author: Kyle Posey

title: John Lynch says the 49ers ‘focused’ on Josh Downs before Keenan Allen
summary: San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch told the backstory of how the team acquired Keenan Allen on KNBR Thursday morning. Lynch was watching another Colts receiver with Kyle Shanahan. He explained how focusing on Josh Downs led to a conversation about Allen: “Our personnel staff does a great job of bringing people to light […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Josh Downs #2 of the Indianapolis Colts lines up against the Minnesota Vikings during the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch told the backstory of how the team acquired Keenan Allen on KNBR Thursday morning. Lynch was watching another Colts receiver with Kyle Shanahan. He explained how focusing on Josh Downs led to a conversation about Allen: “Our personnel staff does a great job of bringing people to light that may be options. Really, we kind of focused on Josh Downs as an option we’d have some interest in. Kyle and I are kind of watching Josh. And in the process, Kyle’s like, ‘What about Keenan?’ I was like, you know, we haven’t given much thought to that, but like, let me ask about that. And so, there started a conversation about two and a half weeks ago. Really, when the DeForest talks. And you know, it’s always fluid. At a certain time, they didn’t wanna give up Keenan. It kind of wasn’t going to be on the table. We kept communicating. Ultimately, we got him. I think it’s a really good fit for us. We wanted to make an ad at receiver. He had a really good first day of practice. It’s just a start. He’ll fit in well. Really pleased to add him.” The 49ers chose the receiver who could add more to their offense for a better price. When we look back on both trades in a couple of months, don’t be surprised if Allen is the more productive wideout. Allen will need to get up to speed in a hurry. Grasping the nuances of the 49ers playbook is closer to a 501 course than a 101. Unlike the last time the Niners traded for a veteran wide receiver, Allen didn’t play for a coach in the Shanahan coaching tree. “I think Emmanuel [Sanders] had an advantage. Rich Scangarello had been their coordinator that year. So there was a lot of familiarity. He had been with us. Keenan doesn’t have that. It’s a struggle I watch install. And our game plans are robust. They’re difficult. And so I sit there and say, ‘My goodness.’ Just aligning in the formations and the motions we have.” Lynch acknowledged it’ll be a “tough task” to get Allen ready for Sunday. He likened it to the Christian McCaffrey trade, which happened on a Thursday and played a meaningful role the following Sunday. But that’s at running back. Here’s Shanahan on Wednesday discussing “Running backs are a lot easier because once you hand them the ball, they can just run. It takes a lot for receivers just getting lined up, knowing all the route tree, hearing the verbiage and everything on how to do it. Sometimes it’s easier. I mean, Emmanuel had a year with an old coach from us, so they had the same terminology for a year, which helped him, but it was still a challenge for him. You’ve got to work at it a ton and you know they can do it physically, but it does take some time to get really comfortable with it.” Lynch said there were “extra meetings” with Allen on Wednesday, who took his physical at 5:45 am PT. Allen “functioned well” at practice, but it’ll be a “race to Sunday to get him ready.” Lynch believes the Niners are getting healthier at wide receiver, with Demarcus Robinson returning last week and Deebo Samuel on track to return this Sunday. Mike Evans is “week to week” with an Achilles injury, according to Shanahan. Lynch didn’t get specific when asked whether Allen was an interim replacement for Evans. “No, we wanted to make an add there. Nonetheless, Stribling went out the first game. We’re hopeful to get him back late in the year. Ricky Pearsall, obviously, went out. You know, Christian Kirk. So, with all those things… that position is a tenuous one. We want to have the ample amount of guys in quantity, and then in quality, as well.”
